The core, landed unused at GH-376, was finished first: clipping management became the calendar's string vocabulary with `collected` as the default (GH-376 shipped `!!clippingsCollected`, so an absent value meant `returned` and silently halved P/K removal); traffic was removed from the per-nutrient path entirely, because the modifier scales the annual N upstream and removal already scales with N, so a second application would double-count it; sufficiency ranges became a required, caller-resolved input for all three methodologies, which removed the last `window.GilbaClassificationConstants` read and made the module fully pure; a nutrient with no soil reading is now returned as removal-only with `missingSoilData` set instead of being omitted (D-9); the ceiling comparison is `>=` on every methodology (D-8); and the below-floor lift target is the floor itself rather than 1.5x the MLSN minimum (D-6) — the one deliberate numeric move, aligning the export to the Plan page, which takes MLSN calcium on the dev sites from roughly 125 to 48 kg/ha and Burns 12th Fairway's P requirement from 21.5 to 14.1. `nutrition-requirement-engine.js` became a facade: its public `compute()` and the facility GP distribution are unchanged, and `_calculateNutrientRequirement`, `REMOVAL_RATES`, `MLSN_THRESHOLDS`, the pH ladders, the tissue gate and the clipping table are now lazy re-exports of the core's, so there is one copy of each in the product. The old `CLIPPING_COLLECTION_FACTOR = 2.5` is gone — uncited, MLSN-only, and the opposite polarity (it amplified on collected instead of reducing on returned); the legacy boolean `turf.clippingsCollected` is ignored rather than aliased, because it has no writer anywhere in `assets/` or `app/` and has therefore always arrived as false, so aliasing false to `returned` would have halved K removal for the old hub's panel and for every existing caller — ignoring it keeps the factor at 1.0, the number those callers already get. The new adapter is the only module allowed to read site config, sample state or the DOM for annual N, clipping, traffic, turf type, species, methodology, texture, CEC, pH and the sufficiency ranges, and it stamps a provenance source per field; `word-export.js`'s `_buildEngineInputs()` lost its 145-line AA-range IIFE (the GH-352/353/355/357/364/379 seam), its `GAIP_STATE.turf.clippingsCollected` and `GAIP_STATE.traffic.intensity` reads (neither field has ever had a writer) and its `.gaip-nutrition-annual-n` / `.gaip-n-program` DOM reads. That last pair was the cross-site annual-N leak: the hidden legacy input is filled by `restoreFromPersisted()` with the first restored site's `target_n` and then not refilled, so every later site in a multi-site Combined export inherited it — Burns samples printed 250 kg N/ha in a Test5-active export instead of their own 120. `word-export-combined.js`'s per-sample calendar branch now builds its inputs from the same adapter keyed by `r.siteId`, which also retires the `parseFloat(...) || 0` soil-ppm block that turned a missing reading into 0 ppm, i.e. maximally deficient against every floor — the failure GH-338 fixed on the Plan page and left standing in the export. A site whose inputs cannot be resolved is now skipped with a warning rather than computed against another site's configuration. The calendar persists `meta.annualNBase` (the pre-traffic figure) and `meta.inputSources`, and restores the Annual N input from the base rather than from the traffic-adjusted `adjustments.target_n`, which would otherwise compound the modifier on every regenerate; its two false comments — the clipping factors described as "not currently applied" when STEP 3 has always applied them — are corrected. `nutrition-requirement-core.js`, `nutrition-program-inputs.js` and (on Plan) `gaip-classification-constants.js` are enqueued on plan, reports/export, scenarios, forensic and hub, head-like on the four bundle pages so they execute before the deferred scripts. The Plan page's own arithmetic is unchanged in this ticket — `computeProgram()` still computes its own removal and correction; that is GH-384. Deliberately not done: the annual N shown on the Plan form is still only what the user typed, never seeded from Settings > Turf (D-4b's second half, declined); traffic derivation and persistence remain unwired (`deriveTrafficIntensity()` returns moderate/1.0 with `source: 'not-wired'`). New tests: `gh383-nutrition-program-inputs.test.js` (34), `gh383-clipping-uniform-all-methodologies.test.js` (17, reusing the stopped work's cases against the real modules), `gh383-input-contract-guard.test.js` (14, source-text guard on the retired reads); `gh376-nutrition-requirement-core.test.js` rewritten to the new contract (30) and `gh376-three-way-nutrition-parity.test.js` rewritten as a two-way surface comparison, with five assertions marked `test.failing` because they are the GH-384 gate. Ten red-checks recorded in the ticket's report, each breaking one decision and naming the test that caught it. **Live-verified**: `npm run test:e2e` 14/14 with the Test5 - NZ fixture at `clippingManagement: 'returned'` AND at `'collected'` — the `returned` state reported 12/14 before this change (K required 82 on the Plan vs 136.1 in the export, P removal 14 vs 33.9), which is the pure input divergence this stage closes. Also implemented from decision D-4b: when a site's annual N could not come from a generated programme, the Combined export prints a note above the Annual Nutrient Requirements table naming the site and the source it fell back to (Site Settings → Turf, or the species default) and saying that no programme has been generated — gated on the adapter's own `sources.annualN` stamp, so it can never claim a fallback that did not happen. The other half of D-4b was declined by the user and is not implemented: the Plan page's own Annual N field is still never seeded from Settings.
Full suite 1802 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 158 suites (baseline 1722 / 155), 120 PHPUnit unchanged.

**GH-384** D31 stage 2 — the Plan page's `computeProgram()` now delegates STEPS 2-5 (base removal, the clipping factor, the deficit/lift correction and the ceiling) to `assets/nutrition-requirement-core.js`, the same module GH-383 put the Word export on, so the audit's D31 finding — "two requirement engines, one product" — is closed: there is one implementation of the per-nutrient requirement, one range resolver and one input adapter behind both surfaces. What the calendar keeps is everything the core deliberately excludes: the traffic-adjusted annual N, the GP-weighted monthly distribution, the monthly N cap, the monthly programme build and the whole persisted output shape (`annual_totals`, `annual_removal`, `annual_lift`, `annual_totals_range`, `annual_totals_range_source`, `missing_soil_data`, `tissue_gate_applied`, `adjustments`, `meta`, `soil`, `program`), which the regional integrations, `plan-ui.js`, `word-export*.js` and `k-reconciliation-decision.js` read unchanged. `annual_totals_range` is built explicitly as `{min,max}` rather than handed the resolver's own object, which also carries a methodology label and a citation that are not part of that contract. Four settled decisions move Plan-page numbers, each re-derived by hand in the tests rather than read back off the new code. **D-5** — the generic (non-tissue) removal ratio is now the per-species `REMOVAL_RATES` table (Carrow/Waddington/Rieke 2001; Christians/Patton/Law 2017) instead of one flat set applied to every species (P 0.10 / K 0.55 / Ca 0.17 / Mg 0.08 / S 0.05, Turner & Hummel 1992, a single cool-season composition). P/N is 0.10 in every table row so P does not move; at N 200 perennial ryegrass K goes 110 → 111 (100/180 = 0.5556), fine fescue 110 → 120 (60/100 = 0.60), buffalo +14%, bentgrass −3%; Ca/Mg/S move on every site because tissue never governs them (at N 200: Ca 34 → 33, Mg 16 → 17, S 10 → 11). The retired numbers are kept in `CONFIG` under `_retiredNutrientRatiosToN_gh384`, unreferenced, as the record of what this page printed before. **D-6** — below the floor the lift target is the floor itself, which is what this page always did; asserted explicitly so the cutover could not silently adopt the engine's old 1.5× target. **D-7** — the MLSN P threshold gains the pH ladder (35/28/21/32/40 at pH ≤5.5 / ≤6.0 / 6.0-7.5 / ≤8.0 / above) that the engine has carried for years and this page never had; no stored dev sample sits outside the 6.0-7.5 band, so nothing moves today, and GH-382's correction note about this is now closed. **D-8** — a reading exactly at the ceiling applies zero, on all three methodologies, which is also what this page already did. Rounding: the core is canonical at 0.1 kg/ha and this page displays whole kg, at the same two points it always rounded, so a Plan total can differ from the export's one-decimal figure by 1 kg/ha — the residual is asserted at ±1 in the parity test, never absorbed by widening a tolerance. `calculateDeficit()` and `getThresholds()` remain exported for their direct callers but are no longer reached by `computeProgram()`. Also fixed: the Combined export's K Reconciliation caption still read "lift toward target × 1.5 over 2 years" after the arithmetic changed, which would have described the printed MLSN figure incorrectly to the client. Tests: new `gh384-plan-page-through-core.test.js` (16); `gh376-three-way-nutrition-parity.test.js`'s five stage-2 gates promoted from `test.failing` to plain assertions; `gh361`, `gh338`, `gh311`, `gh319`, `gh379`, `gh382` re-derived or re-pointed, with the arithmetic written into each. Four further red-checks recorded in the ticket's report. **Live-verified on three sites with three different methodologies, Plan page against the rendered .docx, not only the harness fixture**: Test5 - NZ (AA) 14/14 at `clippingManagement` `collected` AND `returned` — at `returned` the Plan's K required is 81 and the export's ANR "K req" 81.4, where before GH-383 they were 82 and 136.1; Burns 12th Fairway (MLSN, P 18 ppm below the 21 ppm minimum) 14/14, Plan P required 14 and export ANR "P req" 14.1, where the export printed 21.5 before decision D-6; New test - location "Putter Green" (SLAN, P 23.81 and K 19.31 both below floor) 14/14, Plan K 103 / P 14 / S 8 against export ANR K req 103.0 / P req 14.2 / S req 7.9. Two new fixtures (`e2e-parity-burns-12th-fairway-mlsn.json`, `e2e-parity-new-test-location-slan.json`) and four harness corrections the new fixtures exposed: the AU/UK product recommenders are hooked as well as the NZ one; the engine's resolved ranges are read from `ranges` (which covers all three methodologies) rather than the AA-only `aaRanges`; the ANR table's printed soil ppm is compared at whole-number precision because the renderer rounds it; and the Plan page's soil sample is now selected through its own picker, because on a multi-sample site the two surfaces were otherwise compared on different samples. **Two findings recorded, neither fixed here**: the Plan page's sample picker never restores a remembered selection — `soil-nutrition-analysis.js`'s `mountSampleDropdown` compares `samples[j].id === persistedId` with `===`, and the id from `/api/samples` is a number while anything read back from `localStorage` is a string, so the comparison is always false; and on Burns the Plan page and the Combined export select different product catalogues (Plan: ICL-SPORTSMASTER3 / SOL-AS / VAR-MAPTECH; document: MESA 30, Greenmaster Liquid, Wilbur Ellis GroMaxx 46, FoliMAX N-Hancer-N), a pre-existing regional-catalogue question in the GH-362/D30 family that the engine unification does not touch — the two new fixtures declare `productParity.asserted: false` with that reason in the fixture itself rather than the harness quietly skipping the rows. Also verified live on `/hub`: the old hub's Nutrition Summary panel renders through the engine facade with no page errors and the same figures. Full suite 1818 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 159 suites (baseline 1722 / 155), 120 PHPUnit unchanged. Still open by design: traffic derivation and persistence (stage 3) and the GP-weighted monthly distribution, which remains duplicated between the calendar and the engine (stage 4).

**GH-385** `snapshotConfig()` compared two different sites and threw both their nutrition programmes away on every site switch. `saveCurrentSiteConfig()` snapshots the site being switched AWAY from, but by the time it runs `GAIP_SampleManager` and the DOM already describe the site being switched TO — so the carry-forward block at the bottom of `snapshotConfig()` read `_configs[getActiveSiteId()]`, i.e. the ARRIVING site's stored config and its nutrition-programme coordinate stamp, and compared that stamp against `.gaip-lat`/`.gaip-lon`, which still held the DEPARTING site's coordinates. Two different sites on the two sides of one comparison: GH-371's "the coordinates moved, drop the cached programme" rule fired every single time, and the emptied result was then written into the departing site's slot. This is `REVIEW-GH349-onward.md`'s open question 11, latent since GH-371 and made load-bearing by GH-383 — the Word export now takes each site's annual N from that field, so a transient drop produced both a wrong annual N (Settings → Turf instead of the client's own target) and a client-facing note stating "no nutrition programme has been generated" printed on a site that has one. Reproduced live before fixing, on a two-site Combined export of Test5 - NZ + Burns with the browser instrumented: at t=0 both sites held their programmes (target_n 250 and 120), at t=1382 ms the switch to Burns left Test5 with none, and at t=5042 ms the switch back left Burns with none; the instrumented snapshot logged `coordinates changed for site <Burns> (-35.2285452,149.0022925 -> -36.8508827,174.7644881)` while `previousSiteId` was Test5 — Burns' stamp against Test5's coordinates. Fixed by giving `snapshotConfig()` an optional `forSiteId`: the carry-forward reads the config of the site the snapshot is FOR, and when that is not the active site the location comes from that site's own stored record rather than from a DOM describing somebody else — which is also what `saveCurrentSiteConfig()` substituted immediately afterwards (b35fix169), except that the staleness check runs inside `snapshotConfig()` and so never saw it. A site with no stored location gets an empty one rather than the active site's, because a wrong position drives the climate normals and the regional product catalogue. Every call site now names its site; most were already the active one, but several run inside `setTimeout` callbacks where the active site can have moved on before they fire. GH-371's real invalidation is unchanged and still fires when the ACTIVE site's own coordinates move, and when a named site's own stored coordinates have moved away from its stamp — both asserted. New `tests/gh385-snapshot-config-site-scoped.test.js` (10 tests) encoding the live reproduction verbatim; red-checked three ways (restore the active-site read: 2 fail, `Received: undefined` for the carried programme; restore the DOM location read for a foreign site: 2 fail, `Expected -35.2285452 / Received -36.8508827`; drop the `_previousSiteId` argument: the call-site guard fails). `tests/gh371-*` and `tests/gh377-*` pass unchanged (95 tests across the three files). **Live-verified**: the same instrumented two-site export now shows a single timeline entry — neither programme is ever dropped — and both engine calls resolve `annualNSource: 'plan-persisted'` with each site's own target (Burns 120, Test5 250, previously Test5 resolved `settings-turf`); the D-4b note correctly does not appear. ANR row unchanged at `12th Fairway 120 / P req 14.1` and `Soccer 250 / K req 136.1`. Full suite 1829 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 160 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 14/14 on all three fixtures.

**GH-386** Both sample pickers in `assets/soil-nutrition-analysis.js` — the Analysis page's zone selector and the reusable `mountSampleDropdown()` that Plan → Nutrition uses to choose which soil sample the Nutrition Program is generated for — stored the chosen sample's id in `localStorage` and then compared it back with `samples[j].id === persistedId`. `/api/samples` returns `id` as a JSON number and everything read out of `localStorage` is a string, so `123 === '123'` was false, the match never succeeded, and the picker silently reopened on whatever the list order put first. User-visible consequence: on a multi-sample site the Plan page opens on a sample the user did not choose, and Generate there computes and persists a nutrition programme against it with nothing on screen saying so. Found while adding GH-384's MLSN/SLAN E2E fixtures, where the Plan page sat on Burns' "Green 2" while the export used "12th Fairway". The canonical identifier was chosen deliberately rather than by whichever value was nearest: `samples.id`, the database primary key, compared as a string on both sides — it is what `/api/samples` returns, what `/api/samples/{id}/analyse` is addressed by, and it exists for every sample. `client_uid` was rejected because it is nullable (several tissue samples in the dev data have none), client-supplied rather than allocated, and not unique across sites; the Word export picker's own `data-sample-uid` scheme (`<siteId>::<client_uid | label | sample_<id>>`, built by `sample-persistence.js` for the offline store) answers a different question and is deliberately untouched — conflating the two would be worse than the bug. Both loops now route through one `_snSampleIdMatches()` helper, the write side stringifies explicitly at `_snSaveActiveId()` and at `nutrition-calendar.js`'s `onSelect`, and a missing id on either side is never a match, so "nothing remembered" cannot resolve to sample 0. Existing stored values are already the id stringified, so nothing needs migrating — a remembered selection starts working on the next page load. New `tests/gh386-sample-picker-remembers-selection.test.js` (9 tests) including the numeric-prefix trap (14 and 1411 must not match 141); red-checked twice (restore the strict comparison: `Expected true / Received false` and the list lookup returns −1 instead of 1; let one picker keep its own comparison: the "no raw `=== persistedId` survives" guard fails). The helper is attached after the module's export line rather than inside the object literal because eleven existing test files load this module by string-splicing on that exact line. **Live-verified on Burns, a seven-sample site, the same run before and after**: pick "Rye Nursery" (sample 53, soil K 7.6) → before the fix a reload came back on "12th Fairway" with K 195 and P 18, the list's first entry, while `localStorage` still held "53"; after the fix the reload comes back on "Rye Nursery" with K 7.6. The E2E harness still drives the picker through the UI to pin its fixture sample — that is what a user does, and with nothing remembered the default is list order regardless. Full suite 1838 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 161 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 14/14 on all three fixtures.

**GH-387** The Plan page and the Combined Word export handed their product recommender different SURFACE TYPES, so the same sample got different products out of the same catalogue. Reported after GH-384 as a regional-catalogue divergence in the GH-362/D30 family; establishing the root cause first showed that reading was wrong — every product involved (Sportsmaster WSF, Ammonium Sulphate Tech, MAP Tech on one side; MESA 30, Greenmaster Liquid Spring & Summer, Greenmaster Liquid High N, Wilbur Ellis GroMaxx 46, FoliMAX N-Hancer-N on the other) lives in the SAME Australian catalogue, and both pages resolved `isAustralia() === true`. Hooking the AU recommender on both surfaces for Burns "12th Fairway" gave identical monthly nutrient series (N 120.1, P 14.0, K 0.0 across 12 months), identical methodology and identical distributor filter, with exactly one input differing: `surfaceType` was `golf_greens` on the Plan and `golf` in the export. Root cause is GH-383's own rewiring of the Combined export's per-sample calendar inputs, which assigned `_siteInputs.turfType` into `perSampleInputs.surfaceType`. Those are three different things: `turfType` is golf/sports/lawns, `surfaceType` is the surface the calendar works in (greens, soccer, …), and the recommenders key on a canonical third form (golf_greens, tees, fairways, bowling_greens, cricket_wickets). The same defect was live in a quieter form on Test5 - NZ — export `sports` against the Plan's `soccer` — where it changed no products because the Prebble recommender's selection is insensitive to that value at those figures, which is precisely why it stayed invisible while the harness was green. Fixed in the shared input adapter, which now resolves both values once for both surfaces: `surfaceType` follows nutrition-calendar.js's own long-standing chain (a per-sample soil reading, then the site's sub-category, then its 'sports' default, including the cotula_bowling_green special case) and `recommenderSurfaceType` is the canonical key mapped from turfType + subCategory. `nutrition-au-fertiliser-integration.js`'s own `_mapTurfType` now delegates to that mapping, keeping its literal copy only as the fallback for a page that has not loaded the adapter, so one implementation answers for both pages. New `tests/gh387-surface-type-parity.test.js` (10 tests) pinning all three vocabularies, every rung of the mapping and the provenance stamp; red-checked three ways (restore the turfType assignment: both structural rows fail; break the golf-greens rung: `Expected "golf_greens" / Received "greens"`; stop delegating: the one-copy assertion fails). **Live-verified on Burns "12th Fairway", both surfaces, same run**: both now resolve `surfaceType: 'golf_greens'` and choose the identical three products — Sportsmaster WSF 20-0-0 + Seaweed, Ammonium Sulphate Tech (soluble), MAP Tech — and the rendered document's Annual Product Summary lists exactly those three. Test5 - NZ now resolves `soccer` on both surfaces (was `sports` in the export) with its product set unchanged: MESA Country Club 100%, Ammos 22 (Nitro 22), Pro Balance. The E2E harness's product-programme rows are now asserted for every fixture — GH-384's `productParity.asserted: false` opt-out is deleted along with the defect that justified it — which needed five harness corrections the AU fixtures exposed: an AU catalogue for assertion 14 (it previously checked Australian products against the NZ catalogue after matching "Hill Labs" in the text), a product roll-up from the monthly series so the Plan's enriched integration object and the export's raw recommender return are compared like with like, a header-indexed Annual Product Summary footer parse (the AU panel's header is Product | Applications | Total Rate | N | P | K, so the harness had been reading the application count as delivered N — 12 instead of 120), a name guard for AU annual-summary entries that key by product id, and a K Reconciliation section that is legitimately absent when the programme delivers no K at all. **Two findings recorded, neither in scope:** the K Reconciliation section is suppressed on Burns because the correct greens products carry no K and `_perSampleKDelivered()` returns null at zero — correct behaviour, but the client sees no K discussion at all on a site whose soil K is 195 ppm against a 55.5 ppm ceiling; and the AU Annual Product Summary's per-product N figures do not partition its own delivered total (113 + 7 + 5 = 125 against a printed 120, MAP Tech's 5.4 kg N appearing as a row but not in the total), identically on BOTH surfaces, so it is an AU-renderer inconsistency and not a parity defect — the harness's row-sum rows are therefore asserted for the NZ renderer only, with the reason written at the assertion. Full suite 1848 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 162 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 14/14 on all three fixtures with product parity now asserted.

**GH-388** Three leftovers from the D31 cutover, all the same shape — a second copy, or a rule delivered to one surface only. **(1) Dead duplicated arithmetic.** GH-384 routed `computeProgram()` through the shared core and the shared range resolver, which left `NutritionCalendar.calculateDeficit()`, `.getThresholds()`, `CONFIG.mlsnThresholds` / `.slanThresholds` / `.aaThresholds` and the whole `_collectAATexture()` / `inputs.aaTextureKey` plumbing unreachable: a second implementation of exactly the arithmetic and exactly the threshold tables D31 exists to de-duplicate, sitting inside the file whose own changelog claims the duplication is gone. Verified before removing — no caller anywhere in `assets/`, `app/` or `tests/`; the only references were prose in three test headers and one source-text assertion, now re-pointed at the core's equivalent. The behaviour they carried is unchanged one level down: the null-not-zero guard is the core's `typeof currentLevel !== 'number'` branch, the ppm→kg/ha conversion is its `ppmToKgHaFactor`, and the AA sands/others bucketing is the shared resolver's `aaTextureKey()` off the one texture chain. `CONFIG.clippingManagement`, `CONFIG.trafficModifiers` and `CONFIG.yearsToCorrect` are genuinely still used and stay. **(2) Decision D-4b, half delivered.** GH-383 printed the "annual N target came from Site Settings" note in the Combined export only; the single-sample export renders its own Annual Nutrient Requirements section and printed nothing, so a site with no generated programme received an unannotated document even though `annualNSource` was already on `engineInputs.turf`. Same wording on both paths now. **(3) The single export swallowed the adapter's fail-loud.** `resolveSiteProgramInputs()` throws when a site config cannot be resolved, deliberately, so that no surface computes against another site's configuration; `word-export.js` caught it, warned to the console and carried on with `_userN = null` — the engine then substituted `REMOVAL_RATES`' per-species N, `annualNSource` was null so not even the note could fire, and the client got a document full of confident figures scaled against a number nobody chose. It now nulls `engineInputs` and returns, which routes into b35fix329's established "no silent fallback" drop rather than inventing a second suppression path, and warns naming the site — the same shape `word-export-combined.js` already used. New `tests/gh388-calendar-dead-arithmetic-and-single-export.test.js` (12 tests), including a runtime check that the removed members are no longer exposed on the module and that the constants they held still exist once, in the core. Red-checked three ways: reintroduce a private threshold table and `getThresholds()` (3 fail, including `Received: [Function anonymous]` from the runtime check); suppress the single export's note with `if (false && …)` (the gate assertion fails — it matches the whole condition precisely so that leaving the note's text in place cannot satisfy it); restore the swallowed catch (2 fail). **Live-verified**: with a site's persisted programme temporarily removed, the export prints "Note — annual nitrogen target source: Burns (Site Settings → Turf). No nutrition programme has been generated on the Plan page for this site, so the annual N target every requirement below is scaled against was taken from the site configuration rather than from a programme. Generate the programme on the Plan page to base these figures on your own target." above the Annual Nutrient Requirements table, with the adapter resolving `annualN: 150` from `turf.nProgram`; the site's config was restored afterwards and verified byte-identical by MD5. The single-export note itself could not be exercised through the UI: every export from the new hub routes through the Combined pipeline regardless of how many samples are ticked (REVIEW-GH349-onward.md open question 7), so that branch is reachable only from the old hub — it is covered by test and by inspection, and that limit is stated rather than glossed. Full suite 1860 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 163 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 14/14 on all three fixtures.

**GH-389** The E2E parity harness gained the multi-site row the D31 plan's section 10.3 called for. Per-site annual N in a multi-site Combined export was GH-383's headline fix — before it, `word-export.js` read the target from `.gaip-nutrition-annual-n`, a hidden legacy input that `nutrition-calendar.js`'s `restoreFromPersisted()` fills with the first restored site's `target_n` and then refuses to refill, so every later site in the document inherited it — and it was protected only by one manual probe. The harness now ticks a second sample from a different site and asserts that each sample's ANR "N kg/ha" equals THAT site's own persisted `meta.annualNBase`, read from the page's per-site config store, plus that the two figures differ (equal targets would make a leak indistinguishable from correct behaviour) and that every engine call resolved its N from a generated programme rather than the Settings fallback. The fixture names the second sample, so the pairing is data rather than a hard-coded site: Test5 - NZ (target 250) with Burns "12th Fairway" (target 120). Done as a SEPARATE second export rather than a second tick in the existing one, deliberately — the Combined document's Annual Product Summary aggregates every ticked sample, so a two-sample run would silently change what every other comparison in the file means; only the ANR table and the engine calls are read from it. Red-checked by reintroducing the original defect (the pre-GH-383 hidden-input read) in `_buildEngineInputs`: the new row fails by name with Burns' 12th Fairway printing **250** — Test5's target — against its own 120, `"diff": -130`. Fixtures without a second site assert that they have none rather than passing silently. Harness now 15 tests; 15/15 on all three fixtures. Full suite 1860 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 163 suites, 120 PHPUnit unchanged.

**GH-390** The E2E parity harness reads its login from a git-ignored `tests/e2e/.e2e-credentials.json` (`{email, password, url}`; `.e2e-credentials.example.json` beside it is tracked and shows the shape) instead of requiring `GILBA_E2E_EMAIL=... GILBA_E2E_PASSWORD=...` in front of every run; the environment variables still override the file, so CI and one-off runs as another user are unaffected. Added `test:e2e:burns` and `test:e2e:slan` scripts so fixture selection is a fixed command rather than a `GILBA_E2E_FIXTURE=...` prefix. Two reasons, both practical: a command carrying inline assignments is a different string every time it is quoted or reordered, so a permission allowlist can never match it and every run prompts again; and a password on the command line ends up in shell history, process listings, transcripts and the allowlist rules that quote the command. Verified by running `npm run test:e2e` and `npm run test:e2e:burns` with no environment variables set at all — 15/15 each. Also added a project rule (`CLAUDE.md`): live checks and bug reproductions are written as test files run through jest, never as throwaway `node probe.js` scripts — a committed test is repeatable and re-runs when the code moves under it, and `node <script>` cannot be safely allowlisted because the caller authors the script it then runs.

**GH-391** The Australian recommender's strategic P application added only its P to the annual `delivered` accumulator, while the application it pushed onto the month declared its full `delivers: {N, P, K}` vector. Every surface builds its product rows from the monthly applications and its total from `delivered`, so the P source's nitrogen appeared in a row that no total contained: on Burns "12th Fairway" the Annual Product Summary read 113 + 7 + 5 = 125 kg N/ha against a printed 120, the 5 being MAP Tech (12-27-0, 45 kg/ha over 3 applications = 5.4 kg N), picked for its P. `delivered.N` now also takes `pProduct.nDelivered`, and `delivered.K` takes `kDelivered` — MAP carries no K so that line is inert on the usual pick, but netK's annual budget cap (GH-343) reads `delivered.K`, and a K-bearing P source would otherwise be spent twice. Not a display fix: `balance.N` is measured against `delivered.N`, so the missing 5.4 kg was reporting a genuine over-delivery as on-target. Burns' annual N target is also 120, which made the defect easy to misread as "the total is the target"; it is not, and the new tests hold the two apart explicitly. New `tests/gh391-au-p-supplement-nutrients-counted-in-delivered.test.js` executes the recommender and asserts `delivered` equals the sum of the monthly applications (5 tests). Harness gained two rows — the same invariant on both surfaces, and that the Plan's "Total Delivered" footer tracks `delivered` rather than `targets` — and GH-387's Australian opt-out from the row-partition assertion is gone with the defect it was documenting. Red-checked by disabling the two added lines: offline, `delivered.N` 143.9 against applications summing to 151.1; live on Burns, `delivered.N` **120.1** against monthly `delivers.N` summing to **125.4999…**, a gap of exactly **5.4** on the Plan page and in the export alike. Live-verified after the fix: the exported Annual Product Summary reads Sportsmaster WSF 20-0-0 + Seaweed 113 N / Ammonium Sulphate Tech 7 N / MAP Tech 5 N, and the Plan's Delivered N moved 120.1 → 125.5 against a Required of 120, so the over-delivery is now stated rather than absorbed. Also un-brittled two `tests/gh331-au-p-supplementation.test.js` assertions that sliced the source by a fixed character count and broke on the added comment; they now bound the block by its own section markers. Full suite 1865 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 164 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 17/17 on all three fixtures.

**GH-392** `mulders-interaction-checker.js` converted ammonium-acetate soil values that were never in cmol/kg. `normaliseToBasis()` branched on `methodology === 'ammonium_acetate'` and multiplied every cation by `atomic weight / valence × 10`. Nothing in this hub feeds it cmol/kg: `AmmoniumAcetateMethodology`'s bands are declared `unit: 'ppm'` (K sands 75–175, Ca 500–750, Mg 100–200); `HillLabsSampleTypes.getRangesPpm()` converts the certificate-native me/100g **thresholds** into ppm precisely so the comparison happens in ppm, so me/100g lives on the range side and never the sample side; `lab-report-parser.js` keeps any genuine me/100g reading under its own key (`K_me`, `CEC_meq100g`), distinct from the ppm `K` the checker reads; and the dev DB's only AA site stores soil ppm K 40 / Ca 803 / Mg 129 against a resolved certificate range of Ca 400–800 and K 78.2–195.5. The branch was scaling already-correct numbers — K 40 → 15 640, Ca 803 → 160 921, Mg 129 → 15 680 — and because the multiplier differs per element (K ×391, Ca ×200.4, Mg ×121.6) it distorted the very cation ratios the rules test (K:Mg inflated 3.2×), fabricating antagonisms rather than merely rescaling them. Removed, not made case-tolerant: the comparison missed only because `word-export.js` upper-cases the stamp, so matching the other casing would have made the export actively wrong instead of accidentally right, while the lowercase-key callers (the AU/UK integrations, `mlsn-progressive-disclosure.js`) did convert and are now correct. The `methodology` parameter is gone with the branch, so there is no argument left to branch on. New `tests/gh392-mulders-no-cmol-conversion.test.js` (19 tests) pins the basis to the input for every stamp and casing the hub emits, asserts the cation ratios are undistorted, and guards against reintroduction. Red-checked by putting the branch back: 8 of 19 fail, the behavioural ones printing the 15 640 / 160 921 inflation directly. Harness gained a `GilbaMulders.analyse` hook — the basis is the map every ratio divides and no surface prints it, which is how a unit error survived unseen — asserting on live page data that the basis is the readings themselves; green on all three fixtures including Test5 - NZ, the ammonium-acetate site. Full suite 1884 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 165 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 18/18 on all three fixtures.

**GH-393** The export and the live page resolve the Prebble recommender's methodology from different sources under different rules, and the P-deficiency threshold `methodology === 'mlsn' ? 21 : 30` is duplicated in three files fed by two of them. Three rules are live: `nutrition-calendar.js` starts at `soil.methodology` but treats a bare `'mlsn'` as the hub store's placeholder rather than an answer (GH-377's `_methodologyResolved`) and falls through to the DOM select then `GAIP_HUB_CONFIG.turfMethodology`; `resolveSiteProgramInputs()`, which the Combined export calls, takes `sample.methodology || turf.methodology || GAIP_HUB_CONFIG.turfMethodology` first-non-empty with no placeholder concept, so a raw `'mlsn'` beats the site config outright; and `NutritionPrebbleIntegration.getMethodology()` reads only the site config, never the sample, folding everything except `'slan'` to `'ammonium_acetate'` so it can never return `'mlsn'` and the live threshold is always 30. An NZ site whose soil stamp genuinely read MLSN would therefore get 21 in the document and 30 on screen for the same sample; before GH-379 the export's comparison matched neither, so both were 30 by accident. Not reachable today — NZ coordinates auto-select ammonium acetate and both dev NZ sites resolve to it on both surfaces. **Deliberately not aligned**, and handed back for a decision: adopting the page's rule would cement a fold that `normalizeMethodology()` and `prebbles-products.js` `generateProgram()` both contradict by preserving `'mlsn'` and folding only cotula/bowls, while adopting the shared resolver would flip NZ AA sites to MLSN because it has no placeholder concept and all 109 dev soil samples are stamped `methodology_snapshot = 'mlsn'` — plainly a default, not 109 choices. The hub cannot presently tell a genuine MLSN choice from that default, so what an NZ site with a genuine MLSN stamp should use cannot be settled without first deciding how a genuine choice is recorded. New `tests/gh393-prebble-methodology-source-divergence.test.js` (9 tests) documents all three rules and pins each one — the canonical resolver's preservation of `'mlsn'`, the page's two-value fold, the three copies of the 21/30 threshold and which source feeds each — so the divergence cannot widen or be "fixed" on one side alone without the suite saying so. Red-checked by making `getMethodology()` return `'mlsn'`: the fold assertion fails, printing the third return value it gained. Full suite 1893 Jest passed / 1 skipped / 166 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 18/18 on all three fixtures.

**GH-394** (D31 stage 3) The traffic modifier was inert: no UI wrote it and every site resolved `moderate` ×1.0. Settings → Traffic & Wear collected the match and training schedule and wrote it to `localStorage['gilba_traffic_state_<siteId>']` and nowhere else, so nothing reached the server, the Plan page's programme, the Word export or a second device. Both missing links are now in place. **Persistence**: the save handler PUTs `config.traffic = { schedule, savedAt }` to `/sites/{id}/config/gaip` alongside the localStorage mirror, and the form reloads from the config first so another browser sees it. Top-level `config.traffic` rather than `config.turf.*` because `snapshotConfig()` rebuilds `turf` from the legacy DOM on hub pages and would drop a turf field with no DOM twin — and for the same reason `traffic` joined `site-config-persistence.js`'s carry-forward list and its server-pull merge list, without which the first site switch on `/reports/export` would PUT a snapshot without it. It is not a programme, so a coordinate or species drift drops the cached programmes and leaves the schedule standing. `plan-ui.js`'s Recovery section and the Clegg restore both read the config first, so they work on a device that never saved the form. **Derivation**: `deriveTrafficIntensity()` in the shared adapter implements the settled rule — matches/week > 3 → `extreme`, > 1 → `high`, else `moderate`; an empty or unsaved schedule → `moderate`, so no existing site moved. Sports `turfType` only; golf, lawns, an absent and an unrecognised type are all ×1.0 whatever the schedule says, and the gate reads `turfType`, never `surfaceType`. The rule reads only the saved schedule: the Settings field is a placeholder, not a value, and the legacy `.gaip-matches-week` input (hard-coded `value="2"`) would have made every sports site `high`. Table `{low 0.85, moderate 1.0, high 1.15, extreme 1.3}`; `low` is unreachable by this rule and kept so a later rule needs no second table. **One live defect found and fixed with it**: `word-export-combined.js`'s per-sample calendar branch passed the adapter's already-scaled `annualN` as `annualNOverride`, and `computeProgram()` multiplies that by the modifier itself — so a Combined export would have applied it twice (1.3225 instead of 1.15) while the same site's ANR table applied it once. It now passes `annualNBase` plus `trafficModifier`, matching the Plan page. Inert before this ticket because every site was 1.0. New `tests/gh394-traffic-schedule-persisted-and-derived.test.js` (31 tests) pins every rung and both boundaries (exactly 3 is `high`, exactly 1 is `moderate`), the sports gate against four surfaceType values, placeholder immunity, and — through the real `computeProgram()` — that removal follows the scaled N once, with each figure derived by hand from the ratio table. Red-checked five ways: shifting the boundary to `>= 1` fails "exactly 1 is MODERATE" printing high/1.15; defaulting a missing count to 2 fails three named tests including GH-383's no-movement guarantee; opening the sports gate fails four; restoring the double application prints N target **159** where the adapter resolved **138**; and removing `traffic` from the carry-forward list, the config PUT or either reader fails its own named test. New `tests/e2e/gh394-traffic-live.test.js` (`npm run test:e2e:traffic`, 7 tests) drives the real stack: saves the schedule through the Settings UI, reads it back through the API, then opens a **fresh browser context with no localStorage** — Settings shows 2 matches, and the Plan page renders **N 138** against a base of 120 at ×1.15 `high`/`schedule`, removal P 12→14, K 67→77, Ca 20→23, Mg 10→12, S 7→8. Burns, a golf site given the identical schedule, stayed at **120** with `not-sports`; clearing the schedule returned Test1 to **120** with `no-schedule`. Both site configs were snapshotted, restored and the restore verified. The `test:e2e` scripts now name the parity file explicitly so the traffic run is a separate command. Full suite 1924 Jest passed / 2 skipped / 167 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 18/18 on all three parity fixtures and 7/7 on the traffic check.

**GH-395** Settings no longer offers MLSN as a soil-test methodology on a New Zealand site. The dropdown was not region-aware, so an NZ site could be set to MLSN, would save it, and would show it — while the two halves of the product then disagreed about what it meant: `getMethodology()` (`nutrition-prebble-integration.js`, reached only on NZ sites) folds everything except SLAN into ammonium acetate, so product selection ran on AA and used a P-deficiency threshold of 30, while the requirement engine read the raw `turf.methodology` out of the site config through the shared adapter and branched on MLSN thresholds — 21 in the export. Same site, two methodologies, no indication on screen that they differed. SLAN is deliberately still offered: it passes that fold untouched and both halves honour it, so an NZ site on SLAN is consistent today and removing it would have taken away a working option. Not to be confused with `Controller::effectiveMethodology()`, which does force AA for NZ coordinates but is called only by `SettingsController` for this page's own display value; the `$turfMethodology` reaching every other page is built in `AppServiceProvider` from the raw saved value, unforced, which is why saving `mlsn` really did reach the engine. A site already saved as `mlsn` is shown as Ammonium Acetate — that is what its product selection already runs on — with an amber notice saying so and inviting a save, rather than swapping the displayed value in silence or letting the select fall back to "— select —", which a later save of the whole turf form would have written as an empty methodology. Display normalisation only: nothing is written unless the user saves. Deliberately narrow. It was found alongside a wider defect — the methodology is stored in two places, and `sites.methodology_override`, which sample creation reads, is written by nothing but the API (null on all ten dev sites), so all 144 samples carry `methodology_snapshot = 'mlsn'` from the account default including samples of two pure-AA sites — but that is latent today (the export takes its per-sample methodology from the site config, and the stamp's only other reader places it behind the live value) and the rework was deferred; the analysis is recorded in `files/fixes/26-08-17-hoxton-v6/PLAN-methodology-storage.md` so it is not re-derived. New `tests/gh395-nz-methodology-gate.test.js` (7 tests) pins the option list, the NZ-only unset, the stored-`mlsn` normalisation and its notice, and the fold this gate exists because of — including that it still lets SLAN through, since if it stopped, removing SLAN would become correct too. Red-checked by disabling the NZ branch: two named tests fail. New `tests/e2e/gh395-nz-methodology-gate-live.test.js` (`npm run test:e2e:methodology`) renders the real page, because a correct blade can still emit the wrong options if `$isNewZealand` does not resolve as the source implies — **live: Test5 - NZ offers `["slan","ammonium_acetate"]`, Burns (Canberra) keeps all three.** Also added `npm run test:e2e:all`, restoring a globbed run that GH-394's explicit file naming had removed, so a future e2e file cannot be silently unreachable. **GH-521 update:** the sentence above about `effectiveMethodology()` being "called only by `SettingsController` for this page's own display value" was already out of date when it was written: the server's NZ rule was in force on seven pages through eight call sites, and it is removed by GH-520. The SLAN carve-out this entry describes is also gone — it rested on the client fold in `getMethodology()`, which GH-521 removed, and a New Zealand site is now offered Ammonium Acetate alone. A stored value the region does not offer is no longer displayed as AA; it is shown as itself, with a note saying the site still computes on it.


**GH-396** The Combined export's Annual Nutrient Requirements table now prints the Plan page's own columns, in the Plan page's own words: `Sample | Nutrient | Current (kg/ha, ppm) | Removal | Required | Delivered | Range | Balance | Status`, against the previous `Sample | N kg/ha | P ppm | P req | K ppm | K req | S ppm | S req`. No arithmetic changed — the two surfaces already agreed on every figure — and four presentation defects closed. **One measurement in two units**: the report printed soil K as 40 ppm while the Plan printed Current 56 kg/ha, the same quantity through the hub's own 40 x 1.4 x 10 x 0.1 conversion; kg/ha is now primary everywhere with the certificate's ppm in brackets (`56 (40 ppm)`), because the client cross-checks the table against a lab certificate written in ppm. **Two quantities under one name**: the report's `K balance` was Delivered minus Required (does the N programme's incidental K cover the requirement) while the Plan's Balance is Current + Delivered minus Removal (the projected soil level at season end). They cannot be collapsed — on Test5's phosphorus the first is zero, there being nothing to apply, while the projected pool falls from 56 to 17 kg/ha, 39% below the floor; one is about this season, the other about next. Both are now printed, and the report's column is renamed **Programme vs required**, along with its `K req` / `K delivered` neighbours, which become `Required` / `Delivered`. The Plan's column names are untouched: the report was brought to them, not the reverse. **A subset of the columns**: removal, delivered, range and status simply were not in the document, which is the real reason the two read as different data. b35fix316's samples-as-rows layout is kept — a 45-sample council report in the other orientation ran off the page — so the nutrients moved into rows and the table grows downward at a fixed nine columns. The nutrient set narrows from N/P/K/S to the Plan's N/P/K. **A false caption**: the AA caption claimed the figures were removal-replacement estimates and expressly not deficit closure, but below the sufficiency floor Required is removal plus that year's share of the lift — live on Test5, K Required 152.7 is removal 126 plus lift. Rewritten in both export files, since the single-sample export carried the same sentence; the Hill Labs S277/S81 sample-type templating survives, and the new Balance clause cross-references the K reconciliation table only when that table will actually render. To make the new columns the Plan's numbers rather than a second resolution of them, the per-sample `computeProgram()` result is stashed as `r._planParity` (`soil`, `annual_removal`, `annual_totals_range`, `missing_soil_data` — the exact four fields the Plan page reads) and the Plan's `classifyBalance()` moved to a new shared `assets/nutrient-balance-status.js`, which both regional integrations and the export now call; the two integrations had held byte-identical copies and the export had none. `_computeProgrammeKDelivered` became the `'K'` case of a new `_computeProgrammeDelivered(map, nutrient)` so the Delivered column cannot be one accumulator for K and another for N and P. A sample with no programme prints em-dashes in these columns rather than reconstructing them from a stand-in bulk density. New `tests/gh396-report-plan-vocabulary.test.js` (32 tests) pins the headers, the narrowed nutrient set, the retired captions, the delegation on both Plan integrations, the module's presence and load order in all five blades that render either table, and executes the classifier against the figures both surfaces actually rendered. Red-checked seven ways: reverting the Current header fails two named tests printing the old `K ppm` literal; restoring the false caption sentence fails two; re-inlining the classifier on the Plan page fails the delegation pin and GH-338's flag pin; dropping the module from `plan.blade.php` fails the load pin; splitting the K accumulator back out fails its own test; making the formatter print bare ppm fails with `40 ppm` where `56 (40 ppm)` was expected; and restoring the `K balance` header fails the rename pin. The parity harness's table parsing was updated for the new shape — parsing only, no expected value touched — and its Balance test gained the cross-surface check this ticket exists for: Current, Removal and Range identical on both surfaces, each surface's Balance equal to its own printed row, and the same Status verdict. Live on Test5 - NZ "Soccer", Plan against rendered .docx: N removal 288 / required 288.1 vs 288 / delivered 258.6 / balance -29.5 vs -29.4 / On Track; P current 56 vs `56 (40 ppm)` / removal 39 / required 0 / delivered 0 / range 28–42 / balance 17 / Deficit (-39%); K current 56 vs `56 (40 ppm)` / removal 126 / required 153 vs 152.7 / delivered 201 / range 109.5–273.7 / balance 131 / On Track. **Found and not fixed, reported instead:** on the SLAN fixture the Plan's P Delivered is 14.0 and the export's 14.5, so the same Deficit verdict prints as -7% and -5%. The export's product accumulator prefers each application's `delivers` vector when populated and falls back to analysis x rate, while the Plan always multiplies rate x splitCount x analysis. N and K agree to the last decimal on all three fixtures; P does not on that one. Closing it moves printed figures in the Annual Product Summary and the Purchasing Summary across all three regional integrations, so it needs its own ticket. Full suite 1967 Jest passed / 3 skipped / 169 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 18/18 on Burns and the SLAN fixture, 7/7 traffic, 2/2 methodology. Test5 - NZ is 17/18 both before and after this ticket, on a pre-existing failure it does not touch: that site now has a saved traffic schedule (2 matches/week, sports), so GH-394 scales its annual N 250 x 1.15 to 288, while the harness compares the printed figure against the site's pre-traffic `meta.annualNBase` of 250. The printed 288 is correct; the harness's expectation predates GH-394 and needs its own decision. **Resolved after this entry was written**: the schedule was cleared back to 0 matches on the site itself rather than by changing the harness, restoring Test5 to base 250 / modifier 1 and the fixture to 18/18. Test5 is the parity reference and is better kept with no modifier engaged; traffic behaviour is covered on Test1 - Sports by its own live check.

**GH-397** In the Combined export's Annual Nutrient Requirements table, only Balance and Status carry colour; Current and Required print in plain body text. GH-396 had introduced a second palette beside the Plan's: `_anrColor` painted Current and Required by the soil's MLSN/SLAN status band (red for Very Low/Low/Deficient, amber for High/Excessive, green otherwise) while Balance and Status used the Plan's verdict colours — two colour systems answering two questions in one nine-column row. Removed because Required is an instruction, apply this much, not a verdict on the soil: a red 152.7 reads as though the figure itself were wrong, when what is low is the soil. The soil's condition is already stated twice in the same row, by Range and by Status, so the colour carried nothing the reader did not have and competed with the palette next to it. The Plan page, which GH-396 made this table's reference for both vocabulary and presentation, colours nothing but Balance and Status either. `_anrColor` is deleted rather than left unreferenced — its only caller was this table, and a dead colour helper is what someone re-wires later without meeting the reasoning; the reasoning now sits at the assignment it replaced. Header wrapping ("Nutri ent", "Remova l") is left alone deliberately: nine columns will not fit otherwise, and narrowing the data cells to widen the headings would be the worse trade. New `tests/gh397-anr-colour-scope.test.js` (5 tests) pins the plain colour on both cells, the absence of any conditional in that assignment, that the helper has not returned anywhere in the renderer, that Balance and Status still read from the shared classifier, and that no local `statusColour` copy has appeared — the last being the thing GH-396 existed to prevent. Red-checked by restoring a conditional (`isN ? '111827' : 'DC2626'`): the plain-colour test fails by name. **Live-verified in the rendered .docx**, phosphorus row: `56 (40 ppm)` and Required `0.0` both `111827`, Balance `22.0` and Status `Deficit (-21%)` both `D97706`; nitrogen row Balance `-12.6` and `On Track` both `16A34A`. Full suite 1972 Jest passed / 3 skipped / 170 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 18/18 on all three parity fixtures.

**GH-398** (D31 stage 4) The GP-weighted monthly distribution — the last duplicated engine — is one implementation. `nutrition-calendar.js`'s `distributeByGP()` + `applyNCap()` (the Plan page's Monthly Nutrient Program: 0-11 indexing, three modes, a monthly N cap with overflow redistribution, raw values until display) and `nutrition-requirement-engine.js`'s `distributeNGPWeighted()` (the export's Monthly N Distribution: 1-12 indexing, GP-weighted only, **no cap**, GP rounded to 2 dp before weighting and each month to 1 dp after) both now call a new `assets/nutrition-monthly-distribution.js`, enqueued ahead of both engines in all five blades that load either. One document printed both series. **The cap was the live defect, not the rounding**: four of the ten dev sites carry a "Max N per application" of 15 kg/ha/month and it binds on all four, and the report printed the unclamped series for every one of them — Federal Golf's Plan page shows `[15, 15, 15, 12.7, 9.9, 0, 0, 0, 10.1, 12.3, 15, 15]`, five months clamped with the annual 120 preserved by redistribution, against a January of ~21 in its own document. The parity harness never caught it because its fixture peaks at ~35 against a cap of 50. `applyNCap()` moved across unchanged and both surfaces run it; the export's table states the outcome in the Plan page's own two banners rather than printing a clamped series with no explanation, including the case where the cap leaves nitrogen that fits nowhere and the months genuinely sum to less than the target. The heading is composed from the mode instead of reading "(GP-Weighted)" unconditionally, since the table now honours the site's own choice. Four further decisions are implemented as settled. **Rounding**: full precision through the calculation, rounding only at output — the Plan's convention; the pre-allocation GP rounding was worth up to 0.2 kg/month and moved Federal Golf's April/May/September to 12.6/10.0/10.2. **C3/C4**: the engine's per-month blend wins with its fractions untouched, so an overseeded sward is described by season instead of as pure C3 or pure C4 all year; exact for every other sward, since `GilbaGrowthPotentialEngine`'s `blend` computes `f × c3GP + (1 − f) × c4GP` and f = 1 IS the C3 curve, so no site without an overseed configuration moves. The four summer-intent fractions carry no external citation and are flagged for the agronomist. **Every nutrient** goes through `distributeProgram()`, so no second copy survives in the calendar; the document still prints N only. **`front_loaded` is carried across unchanged, defect and all** — it does not conserve the annual total (each active month takes total/10 and months 8-10 are then multiplied by 1.5) and its boost months are hard-coded southern spring; deferred deliberately, no site uses it, and both defects are pinned by test so neither is repaired by accident. The monthly cap and the distribution mode joined `nutrition-program-inputs.js`'s contract (`maxNPerMonth`, `distributionMode`, with `sources` entries), so `word-export-combined.js`'s two private reads — the cap off the site config, the mode off the persisted programme's meta — are gone; the 0-11/1-12 reindex GH-363 was an inline copy of now has one implementation, as do the two season tables and the 0.10 activity threshold, which existed in three places. New `tests/gh398-monthly-distribution-unified.test.js` (26 tests) works off Federal Golf as the database holds it and derives every expected figure by hand. New `tests/gh398-monthly-distribution-guard.test.js` (21 tests, modelled on `gh383-input-contract-guard`) fails if per-month arithmetic reappears in the calendar or either export file, or if a blade stops enqueuing the module. Red-checked nine ways, each by name: nulling the engine's cap prints `[21.2, 21.1, 17.5, 9.3, 2.7, 0, 0, 0, 3.1, 8.4, 16.4, 20.3]` where the stored programme is `[15, 15, 15, 12.7, 9.9, …]`; restoring the 2 dp GP rounding fails the raw-GP test and shifts three months; flattening the C3 fractions prints twelve zeros against `[0.1, 0.1, 0.4, …]`; distributing N alone drops five nutrients; re-inlining the weighting in the calendar fails three guard tests; rescaling `front_loaded` to the target gives 250 where 337.5 is pinned; and removing the script tag, the combined export's adapter reads or `word-export.js`'s `distribution` block each fails its own guard. **Live**, Plan page against the rendered .docx (whole kg in the document): Federal Golf `[15, 15, 15, 12.7, 9.9, 0, 0, 0, 10.1, 12.3, 15, 15]` vs `[15, 15, 15, 13, 10, 0, 0, 0, 10, 12, 15, 15]`, "Monthly N cap applied (15 kg/ha per month): peak months trimmed, 21.4 kg/ha redistributed to shoulder months. Full target of 120 kg/ha delivered.", ANR N Required 120 unchanged; New test - location `[14.5, 15, 14.9, 11.9, 6.4, 3.4, 2.5, 3.2, 7.1, 11.5, 14.6, 15]` vs `[15, 15, 15, 12, 6, 3, 3, 3, 7, 12, 15, 15]`; Test5 - NZ, uncapped, `[30.3, 30.3, 29.9, 26.2, 19.2, 12.4, 8.9, 9.9, 13.3, 17.5, 23.3, 28.8]` vs `[30, 30, 30, 26, 19, 12, 9, 10, 13, 18, 23, 29]`, annual 250; Burns `[16.7, 18.9, 18.6, 11.4, 3.3, 0, 0, 0, 3.7, 10.3, 17.8, 19.4]` vs `[17, 19, 19, 11, 3, 0, 0, 0, 4, 10, 18, 19]`. New `tests/e2e/gh398-monthly-distribution-live.test.js` (`npm run test:e2e:cap`) drives that comparison off the rendered cells and the document's own table, 6/6 on all four sites. Full suite 2019 Jest passed / 4 skipped / 172 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 18/18 on all three parity fixtures, 7/7 traffic, 2/2 methodology.

**GH-399** (delivery unification, stages 0-1) The requirement half of the nutrition calculation has been unified since GH-383…GH-398; the delivery half — how much of each nutrient the chosen products actually supply — never was, and **six** hand-maintained accumulators had drifted apart: the NZ Plan path recomputed totals and rows in two separate loops, AU did the same, UK printed the recommender's declared figures, the Combined export had a fallback that treated a declared `0` as "missing" and substituted `analysis × rate` while ignoring the application count, `_extractEntryNutrients` topped phosphorus up from analysis so the single export contradicted itself between its own product rows and its Delivered column, and the single export trusted a persisted `annualSummary` rather than rebuilding from `monthly`. Symptom on the SLAN fixture: the Plan printed P Delivered 14.0 and the export 14.5, so one verdict rendered as −7% on screen and −5% in the document. New `assets/nutrition-delivery-core.js` holds the one implementation; all six sites call it. **The rule it encodes**: the recommender's declared `delivers` wins where it declares one, and **a declared zero is a zero, not a missing value** — that specific confusion is what the export got wrong. Physical content (`mass × analysis`) is used only where nothing is declared, with `mass = rate × (splitCount ?? applications ?? 1)`; the old Combined fallback dropped the count. Amendments are excluded from catalogue totals, and the module does no rounding at all — each renderer rounds at its own output, which is where the remaining 0.1 differences live (GH-401). **Deliberate exception, documented in the code and pinned by test:** the UK integration's totals line still prints `program.delivered`, because that recommender rounds each `delivers` to 1 dp but sums the unrounded values (27.909 against 27.8 by rows), so switching it would make the panel disagree with itself by 0.1 kg P; fixing that belongs in the recommender and has its own ticket. **Live** (New test - location / Putter Green, Plan page against the rendered .docx): N 138.8 On Track on both; **P 14.0 Deficit (−7%) on both, where the document previously read 14.5 and −5%**; K 104.6 Deficit (−36%) on both; product rows identical on both surfaces (Greenmaster Liquid Spring & Summer 3/0/1, Long Paddock Rapid Uptake 3/0/3). The Plan's own figures did not move anywhere, as required. Test1 (12.1) and Canberra (22.6) are pinned offline against their real persisted programmes. **A side effect worth recording:** the old NZ loop summed into Delivered the amendment entries the export injects into `monthly` (b35fix323) — on Test5's persisted programme that was 38.2 kg K counted twice, 175.2 of catalogue plus 38.2 of amendment; the module excludes them and the single export now blends amendments in separately, so the double count is closed. New `tests/gh399-nutrition-delivery-core.test.js`, `tests/gh399-delivery-consumers.test.js` and `tests/e2e/gh399-delivery-live.test.js` (`npm run test:e2e:delivery`), plus six fixtures captured from the real persisted programmes of Burns, Canberra, New test - location, Test1 - Sports, Test5 - NZ and Test6 - UK; those fixtures deliberately carry `monthly` and `delivered` but **not** `annualSummary`, so a test cannot pass by copying the output of the accumulator it replaced. Red-checked: restoring `v !== 0` to the declared-value check fails 8 tests; dropping the application count from `mass` fails 6; including amendments in totals fails 2; and reverting either the AU or the NZ totals line to `program.delivered` fails the pin added for it — that last gap was found by the review, which showed the whole suite staying green without it, since the existing assertions only forbade the old `+=` shape and said nothing about where the totals came from. **Two honest limits.** Stage 0's harness rows were never observed red against the old code: the ticket was implemented in one revision, so that they would have failed is derived from the unit tests (14.5 against 14.0) rather than measured. **Westview's predicted move is now verified** — it was the one prediction left open, because that site had no fixture and its persisted programme predated GH-391, so it could not be reproduced. Regenerating it through the Plan page settles it: Delivered P comes out at **20.1**, exactly the figure the plan predicted the export would fall to from 27.2. The regeneration also cleared genuinely stale stored figures, and what moved is a record of this week's decisions rather than of this ticket: annual K **110 → 125**, Ca 34 → 38, Mg 16 → 20, S 10 → 13, with N and P unchanged — that is GH-383's per-species removal table reaching a buffalo site (K:N 0.625 against the retired flat 0.55), and P is unchanged because P/N is 0.10 in both. Federal Golf, checked at the same time, was already current and did not move. Full suite 2081 Jest passed / 5 skipped, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 21/21 on each of the three parity fixtures (18 plus the three new delivery rows), 7/7 traffic, 2/2 methodology, 6/6 cap, 7/7 delivery. Sample rows unchanged across every live run (144 rows, 58 live).

**GH-400** (delivery unification, stage 2) Australian liquid applications now count the phosphorus they carry. `au-fertiliser-products.js` pushed `delivers: { N, P: 0, K }` onto every liquid in the annual programme while the same objects' `analysis.P` held up to 2% — no comment justified the zero and none had ever been computed: the granular sibling has derived `pDelivered = rate × analysis.P / 100` since the file's first commit, and `selectFoliarNitrogen()` simply never returned the field. **Both halves are fixed, and the second is the one that changes anything.** The selector returns `pDelivered = rate × applications × analysis.P / 100`, and `delivered.P += liquidRec.pDelivered` feeds the annual accumulator that `netP` (GH-342's `annualTargets.P − delivered.P` cap), the strategic-P top-up's `annualPRemaining` and both P-delivery scorers read. Declaring without accumulating would have made the report honest while leaving selection working from a requirement inflated by exactly the phosphorus already applied — on Westview that half-fix prints product rows summing to 30.6 kg P beside an annual total of 20.1, which is GH-391's defect one nutrient over; a test runs that variant and pins the gap on all six sites. **This is the only piece of the delivery work that changes which products get chosen**, hence its own number. **Live**, Plan page against the rendered .docx, all four Australian sites regenerated through the Plan page: New test - location / Putter Green **P 18.7 on both surfaces, up from 14.0**, N 137.6, K 104.5, with Long Paddock Rapid Uptake's row moving 0 → 1 kg P, and Country Club IV 17-0-17 (172 kg) and the 10 kg MAP Tech top-up dropping out in favour of a second Country Club IV 18-9-18; Westview / Backyard N 224.8 / P 21.4 / K 154.1 with TPG Ratio and both MAP Tech (soluble) picks replaced by GTS Sport Series Colour Plus 20-0-16 and a second FoliMAX NRG-NK month — its sample carries a pH and nothing else, so that document has no Annual Nutrient Requirements section at all and the check falls to the Annual Product Summary, which matches the Plan row for row. Burns / 12th Fairway (125.5 / 12.3 / 0) and Federal Golf / Green 1 (135.1 / 13.2 / 73.4) are the controls: their liquid columns are Ammonium Sulphate Tech and Urea Tech, so nothing moves, and the offline suite asserts their twelve months are byte-identical before and after. Nothing outside the Australian recommender is touched — a guard fails if `GH-400` appears in any other file under `assets/`. Test1 - Sports (12.1 → 11.9, MAP Tech 15 → 7 kg) and Canberra (22.6 → 23.9, same product set) are pinned offline; neither site has a surviving soil sample to regenerate. New `tests/gh400-au-liquid-phosphorus.test.js` (32 tests) and `tests/e2e/gh400-au-liquid-phosphorus-live.test.js` (`npm run test:e2e:phosphorus`, 24 tests across the four sites), plus six fixtures holding each Australian site's twelve monthly requirement rows — the recommender's **input**, with no product, rate or total in the file, so a test cannot pass by copying what it is meant to derive. Red-checked six ways: reverting the accumulator fails 20 offline tests (rows 14.1 against a total of 12.1 on Test1, 30.6 against 20.1 on Westview) and, live on New test, prints 18.7 → 15.0 with both dropped products back; reverting the declaration fails 20; counting one application instead of `applications` fails 15 (Long Paddock 0.6 → 0.1); dropping the field from the return fails 17; removing it from the docblock contract and leaking a `GH-400` marker into `prebbles-products.js` each fail their own guard. **One finding, reported rather than repaired.** New test - location now over-delivers phosphorus by 4.7 kg against a 14 kg target, and it is not an artefact of a half-fix: the requirement the scorer sees is correct — 1.7 kg of the annual budget still outstanding in November — but `selectNitrogenSource` compares `effectiveMonthlyP = pAtRate / monthsCovered` against a `pRequired` that GH-342 already capped to the **annual** remainder, so Country Club IV 18-9-18's 6.4 kg reads as a 1.9× "moderate" overshoot (pScore 30) instead of a 3.8× one (pScore −20) and outscores the phosphorus-free alternative by 14 points. That units mismatch in the P scorer is a separate defect and is left for a decision. Full suite 2113 Jest passed / 6 skipped / 175 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 21/21 on each of the three parity fixtures, 7/7 traffic, 2/2 methodology, 6/6 cap, 7/7 delivery, 24/24 phosphorus. Sample rows unchanged across every live run (144 rows, 58 live).

**GH-401** (delivery unification, stages 3-5) The last three stages, and the delivery half is one implementation end to end. **Multi-application liquid volumes and counts.** A liquid sprayed four times in a month contributed ONE spray's volume to "Total Rate" and counted as ONE application, on the Plan page and in the document alike, while the Monthly Schedule two tables away printed "4x 7 L/ha" — and that column is the one the client orders fertiliser off. `applications` (the Australian recommender's word) now counts exactly as `splitCount` (the New Zealand one) always has, and GH-399's `liquidVolume: 'per-month'` escape hatch is deleted rather than defaulted, since no caller ever set it. **No nutrient total moves with it, and that is not luck**: an Australian liquid declares its `delivers` vector for all of its sprays together (Urea Tech 15 kg × 46% × 2 = 13.8), so only the volume and the count were ever short; every site is asserted to have the same annual N/P/K before and after, and a double count would fail that. **Live**, Plan page against the rendered .docx: New test - location / Putter Green — Long Paddock Rapid Uptake **1 application / 7 L/ha → 4 / 28 L/ha** on both surfaces, footer 10 applications and "77.7 g/m² + 49 L/ha"; Federal Golf / Green 1 — Urea Tech **2 / 30 kg/ha → 4 / 60 kg/ha**, still kg/ha and not L/ha, since a soluble listed in the liquid column carries kg/ha (b35fix282). Pinned offline against the real recommender run over each site's real requirement rows: Canberra (Urea Tech 15 → 30, Long Paddock 7 → 28, FoliMAX N-Hancer-N 20 → 40), Test1 - Sports (Long Paddock Sportsturf 15 → 60, X Factor 30 → 60), Westview (Greenmaster Liquid Advance Spring and Summer 80 → 240, FoliMAX NRG-NK 100 → 250 — the plan's predicted 417 → 657 was measured before GH-400 regenerated that site's product set). Burns and Test5 - NZ are the controls and nothing on either moves. **Round once.** All three regional integrations rounded a total to 1 dp for the Nutrient Delivery Summary and then rounded THAT to a whole number for the Annual Product Summary caption, so a true total anywhere in [n + 0.45, n + 0.5) printed as n + 1 — a caption disagreeing with its own rows for no reason a reader could see. One step now, from the raw sum, through one shared `GAIP_NutritionDelivery.roundAtOutput()` that the Word export calls too, so a figure cannot be 104.5 on screen and 104.4 in the document because one surface used `toFixed()` on a raw sum and the other rounded first. Delivered and Required print at 1 dp on the Plan for the first time ("14.0", not "14"), matching the document. **The brief's expected move did not happen and something else did.** Burns' footer was predicted to fall 126 → 125; it does not, because GH-399 already changed the Plan's source from the recommender's `program.delivered` (125.49999999999999) to the shared accumulator's total, which sums the same three figures to exactly 125.5 — so the caption rounds half up to 126 while its rows print 113 + 7 + 5 = 125. That row/total gap is real, is unchanged by this ticket, and is a different rule (sum-of-rounded-rows versus round-the-true-total); it is reported, not silently adjusted. What the stage did surface is **New test - location's potassium**: 48.3 + 29.8 + 12.5 + 1.1 + 2.8 + 10 is 104.5 in decimal and 104.49999999999999 in binary, so rounding the raw sum naively printed **104 against rows summing to 105** and a Delivered column reading 104.5. `roundAtOutput()` therefore carries a 1e-9 snap, stated in the code as a policy rather than hidden: it is `Math.round` of the value's own decimal reading, four orders of magnitude below the last digit any of these tables prints and far above the ~1e-13 of representation error on a sum of ten to thirty doubles. With it, no development site's printed figure moves at all — the artefact is removed for the band it inflates, and a test builds a programme that lands there (three declared vectors summing to 125.46) to prove the caption now prints 125 where the old two-step printed 126. **"Total Delivered" in the export's Annual Product Summary.** The Plan has had that bold caption since GH-316; the document's copy of the same table stopped at the last product, so neither a reader nor the parity harness could compare the two tables' bottom lines — the comparison this whole unification exists to make possible. One row now, catalogue-only, from the same `_computeProgrammeDelivered()` the Annual Nutrient Requirements Delivered column reads, so a document cannot contradict itself. Where the export injected a soil amendment the rows above deliberately do not add up to it, and a caption under the table says so instead of leaving the reader to find the discrepancy. **Live**: New test 138 / 19 / 105 on the Plan footer and in the document's new row, with Gypsum (837 kg/ha) and Epsom salts (108) outside the 826 kg/ha total; Federal Golf 135 / 13 / 73; Burns 126 / 12 / 0; Test5 - NZ 237 / 0 / 175. Both documents gain it from one edit — single and combined exports share `buildSections()`. New `tests/gh401-delivery-volumes-and-rounding.test.js` (65 tests) runs the real Australian recommender over the six persisted requirement fixtures and then **renders the actual Plan panel in a sandbox** and reads the printed cells, so the figures it pins are the ones a reader sees; it also renders the panel against a copy of the delivery module with the `applications` branch removed, so "what moved" is measured against the old code rather than transcribed. New `tests/e2e/gh401-delivery-volumes-live.test.js` (`npm run test:e2e:volumes`, 28 tests across four sites). The parity harness gained the row the plan reserved for stage 5 — the export's own total against its ANR Delivered and against the Plan's caption — and its export product-row reader now splits the caption out, since it counted every row as a product and would have reported "Total Delivered" as a foreign catalogue item. Red-checked six ways, each by observed output: removing the `applications` branch fails 21 offline tests (New test's footer prints 7 applications where 10 is pinned, Canberra's Urea Tech 1 where 2 is) and, live, the volumes revert; restoring the intermediate 1 dp pass in the Australian integration prints **126 where 125 is pinned**; removing the 1e-9 snap prints **104 where 105 is pinned** on New test's potassium footer, and fails the two arithmetic tests by name; deleting the export's total row leaves the offline pins green until a pin for the `push` itself was added, and live prints "(MISSING)" and fails three tests; making the total row include amendments prints 12 applications / 1771 kg/ha against 10 / 826 and fails the catalogue-only test live; and replacing a fail-loud module guard with a silent local fallback fails its own pin. **Folded in and reported, not fixed: the Required gap.** The Plan and the document disagree on Required by 0.1-0.2 on every Australian site — live, New test P 14.0 vs 14.2, Federal Golf P 11.9 vs 12.0 and K 63.9 vs 64.0, Burns P 14.0 vs 14.1, Test5 K 136.0 vs 136.1 — and it is **not** this ticket's double rounding: removing that moved neither figure. They are two different quantities under one column name. `nutrition-calendar.js` rounds the engine's `annualRequirement` to a **whole** kilogram before distributing it across the calendar and then rounds each of the twelve months to 1 dp; the Plan's Required is the sum of those twelve, i.e. what the programme actually schedules. The document prints the engine's `annualRequirement` itself, unrounded, at 1 dp — the requirement before it was made schedulable. Which of the two a column headed "Required" should show is a decision, so it is recorded with its cause pinned by test rather than resolved here. Full suite 2183 Jest passed / 7 skipped / 184 suites, 120 PHPUnit, E2E 22/22 on each of the three parity fixtures (21 plus the new total-row row), 7/7 traffic, 2/2 methodology, 6/6 cap, 7/7 delivery, 24/24 phosphorus, 28/28 volumes. Sample rows unchanged across every live run (144 rows, 58 live).

**GH-402** Importing a CSV no longer switches a site onto a different calculation model behind the user's back. b35fix371 turned multi-site turf **on** automatically whenever an imported file carried a species column; that call is removed from `sample-manager.js`, with the reasoning left in its place. What the mode does when on: per-sample turf profiles become live, so selecting a sample overwrites the site's own turf settings — type, species, variety, oversow — with the ones attached to that sample, and every figure downstream (removal rates, growth potential, product selection) is computed for that grass rather than the configured one. The product already answers "one site, several surfaces with different grass" a different way — a separate site per surface, each with its own turf settings — so this is a second, competing model for the same question, and whether it should exist at all is not settled. It is dormant meanwhile: no site in the database has the mode on, and the toggle that controls it is enqueued only on `/hub` and the three report pages, never in the new hub's Settings, so there is nowhere in the product a user actually works to see the mode or turn it off. **The danger was the silent arming, not the feature.** A client importing a lab file whose columns happened to include a species would have had the mode switched on, their samples given profiles, and their calculation quietly following the sample instead of their settings, with no control anywhere to notice it.
