Our own import templates (`files/samples/templates/soil_test_template.csv` and the rest) carry no species column, so only a hand-edited file could reach it — which is why this is disarmed rather than treated as urgent. Samples still receive `turfProfile` on import: it is inert while the mode is off, and the data is worth keeping if the feature is kept. The bulk-apply modal's own auto-enable is deliberately left alone — its button is hidden while the mode is off (`sample-switcher-ui.js` sets `display:none`), so the modal cannot be opened to reach it, and once the mode is on the call is a no-op. New `tests/gh402-no-silent-multisite-turf.test.js` (5 tests) pins that the importer calls no enable setter in any spelling, that the reasoning and its restore note survive in the source, that the profile is still written, that the bulk path stays gated, and that the shipped templates have no species column. Red-checked by reinstating the call: the guard fails by name. Full suite 2118 Jest passed / 6 skipped, no other test moved. **Not decided, deliberately:** whether the per-sample turf model should be kept and given a Settings toggle and modals on the working pages, or removed along with the profiles. Recorded in `PLAN-remaining-defects-RU.md`.

**GH-403** "Required" is one quantity on both surfaces, and the Annual Product Summary's caption now agrees with the rows above it. `nutrition-calendar.js` rounded the shared core's annual requirement to a whole kilogram before distributing it across the twelve months, and all three regional panels then re-derived Required by summing those twelve already-rounded rows — two roundings, not one, which is why the Plan read P 14.0 where the document read 14.2 (New test - location), 11.9/12.0 and 63.9/64.0 (Federal Golf), 14.0/14.1 (Burns) and K 136.0/136.1 (Test5 - NZ). **GH-401's diagnosis named only the first cause and called it the sole one; removing it alone fixes one of those five cases and flips New test - location to 14.3 against 14.2** — so `annual_totals` is the core's canonical 0.1 kg/ha figure now and the panels print it directly, through `GAIP_NutrientBalanceStatus.annualRequired()`, falling back to the old monthly sum for a programme persisted before this ticket; the twelve monthly rows keep their 1 dp display, since they are the schedule and nothing sums them into Required any more. Live, all four sites: Required identical string-for-string on the Plan page and in the generated .docx (120.0/14.2/103.0, 120.0/12.0/64.0, 120.0/14.1/0.0, 250.0/0.0/136.1), and one monthly cell moved by more than a single display step across the ten development sites — Westview's sulphur in January, 3.5 → 3.3, which is the arithmetic of an annual that was being scheduled as 13 against a true 12.5. **Second defect:** Burns' Annual Product Summary printed a Total Delivered of 126 kg N above rows reading 113 + 7 + 5; making the caption the sum of the printed rows was measured and rejected, because rounding-up bias accumulates with the row count (Test6 - UK potassium: rows 127 against a true 125.4, in a document whose Annual Nutrient Requirements table prints 125.4), so the rows gained the decimal instead — every nutrient cell in that table, on all three panels and in both exports, prints through one shared `GAIP_NutritionDelivery.formatDelivered()` at 1 dp, which reverses GH-318's whole-kilogram rule for this table and matches the two other tables that have printed this quantity at 1 dp all along. GH-399's one documented exception went with it: the UK panel's Delivered read `program.delivered` (27.909, printing 27.9) above its own rows summing to 27.8, and now reads the shared accumulator like everything else. New `tests/gh403-required-one-quantity.test.js` (130 tests) loads `nutrition-calendar.js` twice — once as it stands, once from a copy with the rounding put back — over a new fixture holding all ten development sites' real programme inputs, so the before/after is measured against the old code rather than transcribed; `tests/gh401-delivery-volumes-live.test.js` gained the plan-vs-document Required equality, the caption-equals-its-rows check on both surfaces and a read of the Plan's Annual Requirements cards. Red-checked seven ways by observed output: reinstating the whole-kilogram rounding fails 16 offline tests (burns P 14 where 14.1 is pinned, Test5 K 136 where 136.1 is); reverting the AU panel to `program.targets` fails 7 rendered-cell tests (14.0 where 14.2 is pinned); reverting the AU, NZ or UK caption or product row to a whole kilogram fails the rows-add-up test by name (125 where 125.5 is pinned, 163 where a decimal is required); reverting the export row and the UK totals line each fail their own pin. Full suite 2327 Jest passed / 8 skipped / 187 suites and 120 PHPUnit (both totals include GH-404's tests, landed in the same tree); E2E 104/104 across the seven live suites this ticket touches, 40/40 on the extended volumes suite, and 22/22 on each of the three parity fixtures. **Reported, not changed:** the document's Annual Nutrient Requirements table prints N Required at 0 dp ("120") beside P and K at 1 dp — same number as the Plan's "120.0", different precision in one cell of one column.

**GH-404** Settings will not save a site without coordinates. `sites.latitude` is a nullable column, `store()` and `update()` both validate it as `nullable`, and `syncRegistry()` creates a site without touching it — so a site could be saved, and used, with no location. Nothing downstream then failed: `climate-module-v2.js:682`, `disease-integration.js:376`, `hub-orchestrator.js:1455`, `irrigation-scheduler.js:263` and `hub-tissue-v3.js:385/2294` each substitute a hardcoded Sydney-ish latitude (-33.87 / -35 / -33) when they cannot resolve one, four of them on new-hub report pages, so the site received a full, confident report — climate, disease risk, growth potential, irrigation — computed for somewhere it is not, with nothing in the document saying so. For a UK or NZ site that is the wrong hemisphere and the wrong season. The Site form's submit handler now stops the save and names what is missing, in the same shape as the site-name check directly above it. **The gate tests the coordinates, not the Location field**, so clearing them by hand is caught as well as never setting them; the message points at the Location search either way, because picking a result is what fills the coordinate inputs and asking someone to type a latitude by hand invites the wrong number. The fields stay editable for a search result that is close but not exact. `required` is added to the Location input for intent and styling only — the form carries `novalidate`, so it does not gate anything on its own, exactly as with the site name. **Removing the fallbacks themselves is separate work and was not attempted**; this is the gate in front of them, in the one place a user sets a location. New `tests/gh404-settings-requires-location.test.js` (11 tests, including a pin that the fallbacks still exist so the reasoning cannot go stale unnoticed) and `tests/e2e/gh404-settings-location-required-live.test.js` (3 tests, `npm run test:e2e:location`). Red-checked three ways: gate stubbed to `&& false` (1 fail), gate deleted outright (4 fails, `Received: null`), `required` dropped from the blade (1 fail). **Live-verified on Burns**: clearing both coordinate inputs and submitting produced "This location has no coordinates yet. Pick a result from the Location search to fill them in — the climate, growth potential and disease calculations are all based on them.", `PATCH /api/sites` requests observed: 0, and the stored coordinates unchanged at -35.2285452 / 149.0022925.

**GH-405** The Annual Nutrient Requirements table prints nitrogen at the same precision as everything beside it. That column printed N at 0 dp and P and K at 1 dp — "120" next to "14.1" — while the Plan page printed "120.0" for the same quantity, so one number wore two precisions in one column and disagreed across the two surfaces for no reason but the format. GH-403 settled the rule for this table (figures that agree beat whole numbers); nitrogen sat outside that ticket's scope, not outside the rule. One line in `word-export-combined.js`: the N branch now rounds through `_round1dpForDisplay()` like its neighbours. The source is unchanged — still the programme's own annual total, not the engine's `annualRequirement`. `tests/e2e/gh401-delivery-volumes-live.test.js` had excluded N from its string-equality check precisely because of this; the exclusion is removed, so all three nutrients are now held to identical strings. **Live on all four sites**, plan against the generated `.docx`: New test 120.0/120.0, 14.2/14.2, 103.0/103.0; Federal Golf 120.0/120.0, 12.0/12.0, 64.0/64.0; Burns 120.0/120.0, 14.1/14.1, 0.0/0.0; Test5 - NZ 250.0/250.0, 0.0/0.0, 136.1/136.1. Red-checked by restoring `toFixed(0)`: 4 of 40 fail with `"what": "required disagrees"` on N, one per site. `tests/gh396-report-plan-vocabulary.test.js` also needed widening: it slices this source at a fixed 14000 characters, and the explanatory comment added here pushed `tableRows.push` past the end, failing an assertion whose subject had not changed. The window is now a named constant with the reason written beside it. Full suite 2327 Jest passed / 8 skipped, E2E volumes 40/40.

**GH-406** The Fertiliser Purchasing Summary says which unit each row is in. Its headers were hardcoded "Total kg" and "Total kg/ha avg" and the quantity was read as `p.totalKg || p.totalKgHa || p.totalLHa` — whichever field existed — so a true liquid's litres printed under a kilogram heading with nothing to tell them apart, in the one table a greenkeeper orders from. The Plan panel has always got this right per row rather than per column (`nutrition-au-fertiliser-integration.js:1047-1053`): a true liquid is L/ha, a soluble powder is kg/ha even though it is dissolved before spraying. Both rules are reused verbatim. **Not carried over: the panel's g/m² branch for greens.** That is an application rate for a small area; this table answers "how much to order", which is bought by mass and volume. Headers are now `Total` / `Rate avg` (and `Total rate` in the no-area variant) with the unit printed beside each figure. **No figure moves:** for a liquid the accumulator sets `totalKg` and `totalLHa` to the same number (pinned in `tests/gh401-...`, `totalKg === totalLHa === 28`), so the old chain was already reading the right value under the wrong name — this is a labelling fix, not an arithmetic one. There is no total row in this table to reconcile: each column aggregates one product across samples, and a product has one form, so a row never mixes units. New `tests/gh406-purchasing-summary-units.test.js` (7). Red-checked two ways: unit suffix removed (1 fail), form-aware read reverted to the flat `||` chain (1 fail). GH-401's structural pin on that chain was updated to the new shape with its claim intact, not deleted. **Not live-verified**, and the reason is on record from GH-401: the aggregator suppresses itself without a fresh soil sample, and no development site has both a fresh sample and a multi-spray liquid.

**GH-407** Neither setup wizard offers MLSN for a New Zealand location. GH-395 removed it from the Settings dropdown; the wizards have their own methodology step and were never changed — the likelier route, since a wizard is where a site is first configured. Reported from the UI: NZ coordinates entered by hand at step 1, MLSN still selectable at step 4. **There are two wizards with this step, and the first attempt fixed only the wrong one.** `onboarding-wizard.js` (`window.GilbaWizard`) is what the new hub shows, loaded by `dashboard.blade.php`, and is what the report was about; `site-setup-wizard.js` (`window.GaipSetupWizard`) is an older twin reached only from `/hub` and the report pages. The first pass changed the twin, and its live test drove the twin too, so the run went green while the wizard on screen still showed three buttons. Both carry the fix now, and both are asserted, structurally and live. Each step already knew the location was NZ — it adds Ammonium Acetate *because* of it, auto-selects it, and prints a note if you choose otherwise — it simply never took MLSN off the list, so it stayed one click away and that note was all that stood between a new NZ site and a methodology whose thresholds are not defined against the numbers NZ labs report (Olsen P, ammonium-acetate extractions). Warning and offering are not the same as not offering. MLSN is now spliced out when the NZ check passes, a selection made before the location was set is normalised to `ammonium_acetate`, and the swap is announced in the existing note rather than the button silently vanishing. The button grid drops from three columns to two for NZ, since it now holds two cards either way. Flags live on the wizard instance, never on the persisted data object, and reset when the location is not NZ. MLSN is untouched everywhere else, including the golf-greens auto-suggest. New `tests/gh407-wizard-nz-no-mlsn.test.js` (15, both files) and `tests/e2e/gh407-wizard-nz-live.test.js` (3, `npm run test:e2e:wizard`), which renders the dashboard wizard's real step into a detached host and reads back the `data-method` buttons. **Live-verified on /dashboard**: Auckland → `["slan","ammonium_acetate"]`, selected `ammonium_acetate`; Auckland with MLSN preset → same, normalised, note reads "MLSN is not offered for New Zealand locations…"; Canberra with MLSN preset → `["mlsn","slan"]`, selected `mlsn`. Red-checked by stubbing the splice to `if (false)`: the live run reproduces the reported symptom exactly — `["mlsn","slan","ammonium_acetate"]`, three buttons. The live test also caught a defect in its own first draft: it read a note element id that does not exist (`gaip-wizard-method-note`; the real one is `gaip-wizard-species-note`), reporting `note: null` for a note that rendered correctly.

**GH-408** The Word export scores a warm-season site on the warm-season growth-potential curve. `nutrition-requirement-engine.js`'s `compute()` hardcoded `{ isOverseed: false, baseIsC4: false, summerIntent: 'transition' }` as its default overseed config, and **no caller anywhere supplies `inputs.overseedConfig`**, so every site this engine served was scored on the C3 curve whatever grass was configured. The Plan page never had it: `nutrition-calendar.js` passes `isC4` into the same shared `monthlyC3Fractions()`. Both surfaces call the same `monthlyGP()` — they were handed different C3 fractions, so this is an input-side divergence, the same shape as the three D31 closed, not a second implementation. **Reported from the UI** on a Christchurch golf site set to Couch: the Plan printed GP 16% for January against the document's 90%, and the document went on to distribute the full 250 kg N/ha across nine "active" months a warm-season sward does not have at that latitude, while the Plan could schedule only 100 under the same monthly cap. `isC4Species()` already existed in this file, delegating to the same shared classifier the Plan uses; it simply was not consulted at that line. An explicitly supplied `overseedConfig` still wins, so a caller describing a real oversown sward is unaffected. Two of the eleven development sites are warm-season (Couch, Buffalograss), and couch is ordinary on Australian golf and sports turf — this was not an edge case. New `tests/gh408-warm-season-gp-parity.test.js` (7), which loads the real modules in a VM and **runs `compute()`** rather than pinning source: Christchurch January comes back Couch **15%** / Bentgrass **89%**, matching the Plan's 16% and the document's old 90%. Buffalograss is asserted to match Couch. Red-checked by restoring the hardcoded `false`: `Couch 89%, Bentgrass 89%` — the reported symptom exactly, `Expected: < 30 / Received: 89`. Full suite 2356 Jest passed / 9 skipped.

**GH-409** The document's product tables print the Plan page's columns and the Plan page's units. Two reports, one complaint: the `.docx` did not match the screen. **Columns** — the Annual Product Summary rendered `N | P | K | Mg | S` on one site and a different set on the next, because b35fix328 turned a column on whenever some product in the table happened to carry that nutrient above 0.05 kg/ha; the Plan has only ever had N, P and K. The set is now fixed at those three, phosphorus unconditionally, and the Fertiliser Purchasing Summary asks the same function — it imported it and then never called it, deciding its own columns off a second threshold that could disagree about the same products. Ca, Mg and S still accumulate exactly as before and are still printed in full by the Annual Soil Amendments table; only two tables' column lists changed. **Units** — on a golf greens site the Plan's "Total Rate" column reads `40 g/m²`, `90 L/ha`, `61.6 g/m²`, `2 g/m²`, `90 L/ha` and the document printed `400`, `90`, `616`, `20`, `90` under a header saying "Total kg/ha": ten times the figure, on every fine-turf site, in both tables. **THE SURFACE DECIDES THE UNIT** — not the region, not which integration draws the page: a true liquid is L/ha (litres do not convert to grams per square metre), a fine-turf surface is g/m² for every mass rate including powders, everything else is kg/ha. Four renderers each carried a copy of that rule — the New Zealand, Australian and UK panels and the Word export — and they disagreed about one cell: a SOLUBLE POWDER on greens was `g/m²` on the NZ panel and `kg/ha` on the AU and UK ones, because b35fix281's "solubles are powders — always kg/ha, never L/ha" guard sat on their g/m² branch as well as their L/ha branch. One row in a foreign unit in a table of g/m² rows is what the owner read as an error. Settled by the owner: the surface decides, so Urea Tech on Federal Golf's greens prints `6 g/m²` where it printed `60 kg/ha` — the same product, the same dose, the same amount to order. b35fix281's real point survives inside the shared helper's L/ha branch. The rule now has ONE implementation (`nutrition-delivery-core.js`: `usesGM2`, `isSolubleProduct`, `rateUnitFor`, `formatRate`, `productRate`, `programmeTotalRate`) and all four renderers read it. The soluble test is the union of theirs, which matters: the five Sportsmaster WSF products carry `form: 'soluble'` while their names do not say so, so the NZ panel's label-only test missed them and printed their kilograms as "L/ha". The document's header is the Plan's own "Total Rate" with the unit on each row, and the total row states litres after a `+` instead of adding them into the kilograms — it used to be one `Math.round` over every row's mass, litres and kilograms together. The surface comes from `program.meta.surfaceType`, the value the Plan panel itself branched on, falling back to the turf record and reporting loudly if neither resolves. GH-406's decision to keep `g/m²` out of the Purchasing Summary is reversed, at the owner's request, for the rate columns only; the absolute "Total" column stays in kilograms and litres, being a purchase quantity for a whole area rather than an application rate. A product applied on two surfaces of one site falls back to kilograms and is named under the table. **CONSUMERS THAT READ THESE CELLS AS NUMBERS** were the real risk and were swept: four live harnesses located the table by its old header; `ui-vs-export-parity` and `gh401-*-live` compared the cell against a per-hectare quantity and now convert through one `rateKgHa()` helper; `gh401-*-live`'s fixture gained `perHa` beside the printed `rate`, which are no longer the same number; the offline `gh401` rendered-panel test rebuilt the expected unit from the product's form and now reads it off the rendered row; `gh406`'s source pins were updated where they pinned the superseded shape. Nothing in the application re-parses a printed rate. New `tests/gh409-product-table-units.test.js` (31, over real persisted programmes in `tests/fixtures/gh409-product-rates.json`) and `tests/e2e/gh409-product-table-units-live.test.js` (12, `npm run test:e2e:units`), which compares the painted Plan cells with the cells of a generated `.docx`, string for string. **Live-verified** on `Test - GC - NZ - delivery` / 18th Green and `Test - GC - NZ - warm season grass test` / Main Oval (both tables, every row identical to the screen, headers `Product | Applications | Total Rate | N | P | K`), and on the four `gh401` sites: Federal Golf `Urea Tech 6 g/m²`, Burns `Ammonium Sulphate Tech 3.4 g/m²`, New test - location `Epsom salts 10.8 g/m²`, Test5 - NZ unchanged in kg/ha and L/ha. Red-checked three ways, each restored: the bare-number cell put back — document `400 / 90 / 616 / 20 / 90` against the Plan's `40 g/m² / 90 L/ha / 61.6 g/m² / 2 g/m² / 90 L/ha`, the reported symptom exactly; `Ca/Mg/S` forced on — 2 offline failures; the AU panel's soluble exception restored — live, `plan "60 kg/ha"` against `document "6 g/m²"`, the two surfaces disagreeing again. **Found and NOT changed**, needing a product decision: the Monthly Schedule below these tables has the same divergence one table lower (Plan `@ 20.0g/m²`, document `@ 200 kg/ha`), and its liquid column carries a second question — the Plan prints a soluble there in kg/ha even on greens, disagreeing with its own product table. The live harness prints both surfaces' cells on every run so the evidence is to hand. Full suite 2402 Jest passed / 10 skipped; all 10 live suites, 126 tests, plus both other parity fixtures.

**GH-413** The pH of the sample picked on the Plan page reaches the engine, and the document's Range column is read off the same floor its Required column was computed from. `applySample()` copied only a sample's nutrient ppm into `GAIP_STATE`, so `collectFromState()` resolved `pH` null on every generation and both pH-adjusted phosphorus floors — SLAN's Spencer ladder and MLSN's D-7 ladder — were dead on that page while the Word export applied them; separately, the Combined export overwrites every programme input per sample except `ranges`, so the document's per-sample programme (and the Range column it prints) came from the facility snapshot's pH rather than the sample's. Live on New test - location, Plan and document now identical string for string: Green 5 (pH 8.26) Required P 15.6 → **32.4** with Range `71.4–75.6` where it printed `37.8–75.6`, Green 4 (7.52) 12.0 → **15.7**, Green 2 (5.97) 12.0 → **14.5**; Green 11 (6.07) correctly did not move, its floor already being 27. **One MLSN sample moved with them and needs a data decision, not a code one:** Burns' 12th Fairway sample of July 2024 carries `pH` 6.6 and `pH_Water` 5.5, the two keys disagree on that row alone out of fifty, and the canonical-key rule (`pH_Water ?? pH`, which both surfaces already used) puts its phosphorus floor at 35 rather than 21 — Required P 16.2 → 26.0. Which reading is right for that sample does not follow from the code, and whether the importer can write a CaCl₂ figure into `pH_Water` has not been checked. New `tests/gh413-plan-sample-ph.test.js` (9) over `tests/fixtures/gh413-ntl-green5-ph826.json`.

**GH-414** One green is computed against one soil texture and one tissue analysis, on both surfaces. `resolveSoilTexture()` ranked `samples.soil_texture_snapshot` — stamped automatically at import — above the site's hand-set `soil_texture_override`, so Russley resolved `sand` on the Plan and `loam` in the document and the same green got the Hill Labs S279 certificate on one surface and the generic ammonium-acetate band on the other (decision D-2: the override wins); and the Plan paired tissue with soil by no rule at all, handing the site's single latest tissue analysis to every soil sample, where the export has matched by zone key since b35fix_greentissue. The Plan now runs that same match through one shared implementation (`GAIP_NutritionProgramInputs.matchSampleToZone`, which the export's `buildZoneMap` also calls) with no "only one on the site, use it" fallback, and says so — on screen, and in the document's Annual Nutrient Requirements caption — when a zone has none. Live: Russley Green 18 P `0.0` / K `119.0`, Range `7–21` and `109.5–273.7` on both surfaces where the document had printed P `20` / K `106.7` against `16.8–39.2` and `140–329`, and FoliMAX Phosphite+ is gone from it; Green 1 and Green 13, which have no tissue of their own, moved to the generic ratio (K `119.0` → `106.7`) as intended, and Green 1's phosphorus with it (`0.0` → `1.8`, the generic removal of 20 against a certificate ceiling of 15 through GH-415's maintain-floor branch). The document's Gypsum and Epsom salts rows stay: they are soil-amendment decisions on calcium and magnesium (100–220 ppm and 21–40 ppm on these greens), below every floor on either texture, so they were never an artefact of the fallback range. New `tests/gh414-zone-and-texture.test.js` (15) over `tests/fixtures/gh414-russley-green18-aa-sand.json`.

**GH-415** "Required 0.0" and "Deficit (-56%)" can no longer stand in the same row. Thirteen rows said both at once, and it was arithmetic rather than presentation: above the sufficiency ceiling the requirement was a flat zero, which is only safe while the range is at least as wide in kg/ha as the season's removal, and MLSN potassium on greens is a band of 25.9 kg/ha against a removal of 64. Decision B1, confirmed by the owner: Woods' `max(0, removal − (current − floor) × unit)` in that branch, identically on MLSN, SLAN and AA, so Required is zero exactly when Balance lands on or above the floor and the two models cannot disagree; the new `maintain-floor` intent is explained in the Delivery Summary popover and in the document's caption, and Woods inside the range (variant B2) was measured and deliberately not taken. Live, the audit harness finds **no row anywhere** printing Required 0.0 beside a Deficit, against thirteen before: the twelve Burns potassium rows move from `0.0` to `1.0…30.4` (Green 4 `0.0` → `29.0`, Delivered `0.0` → `28.2`, Deficit −56% → −2%) and Test5's phosphorus from `0.0` to `5.9`, and the potassium and phosphorus products those requirements pull in appear with them — the change of product selection the owner accepted when taking B1 before the release rather than after it. **Small requirements still go undelivered:** where the new figure is under about 6 kg/ha the Australian recommender finds no potassium source and says so only in the console, which is GH-418's subject and is not fixed here. **And it uncovered a Plan-against-document divergence that needs a product decision, not fixed here:** giving Test5 - NZ a phosphorus application to balance around made the two surfaces choose different balancing products (Plan 247.6 N / 180.7 K, document 249.7 / 163.5) off an identical requirement and an identical twelve-month series. Exactly one recommender input differs — `context.soilCEC`, Plan `8` against the sample's measured `5.9` — because `NutritionPrebbleIntegration.getSoilCEC()` reads a state slot nothing on the Plan writes, then a DOM field plan.blade.php does not render, then returns a hardcoded 8, while the export's hidden hub runner has the real value. Every New Zealand site on the Plan has been scored for leaching risk against that 8. Confirmed by patching the getter and re-measuring: with the sample's CEC the two contexts come back identical, and the distributor pool was eliminated the same way (both resolve `prebble`, 31 granular / 24 liquid). It is not fixed here because it changes product selection on New Zealand sites, which is the owner's call, and because one line is not the whole fix — `ui-vs-export-parity` reaches the Plan by a route that never touches the sample picker, so a complete fix reads the CEC the calendar itself resolved whatever route the sample arrived by. **Until it is decided, `npm run test:e2e` (the Test5 - NZ fixture) is red on it**; the Burns and SLAN fixtures are 22/22. New `tests/e2e/gh415-prebble-input-parity-live.test.js`, which names the field rather than a number three tables later and is red on it deliberately. New `tests/gh415-maintain-floor.test.js` (44) over `tests/fixtures/gh415-burns-green4-k-above-ceiling.json`.

**GH-416** A programme built without a soil test says so. Four development sites reach the recommender with no soil chemistry — two with no samples at all, two with a sample carrying nothing but pH — and all four produced a full seven-product programme with nothing on the Plan page to say the P/K/Ca/Mg/S figures behind it are removal estimates; in the document it was worse, because the Annual Nutrient Requirements and Monthly N Distribution tables both iterate one filtered list that excluded a pH-only sample, while the Annual Product Summary beneath them is not filtered. The Plan now shows "Built without a soil test…" whenever the engine reports no reading for both P and K, and the document prints both tables for a pH-only sample with the same "No Soil Data" rows the Plan shows; Generate is not blocked (decision D-5). Such a sample deliberately does not get a per-sample programme recomputed for it — the catalogue branch is chosen from coordinates and resolves to Australia for anything outside the New Zealand box, so recomputing would put Australian products in test4 - USA's document. Live: Westview's document now carries both tables and agrees with the Plan string for string (200.0/224.8 On Track, 20.0/21.4 and 125.0/154.1 No Soil Data), the banner appears on Canberra, Test1 - Sports, Westview and test4 - USA and on no site with a real soil reading, and test4 - USA — which has no product catalogue at all — prints its requirements and its "No Soil Data" verdicts with a dash for Delivered and Balance rather than an assumed zero. New `tests/gh416-no-soil-test.test.js` (10).

**GH-417** The "Strategic P application" note prints what the product delivers, not what was asked for; the phosphorus source it picks is rate-capped (MAP Tech at 20 kg/ha of product is 5.4 kg P/ha), so the note read "19.8 kg P/ha" above a product line supplying 5.4, and now reads "5.4 kg P/ha (of 19.8 requested)". **The plan's second half rests on a wrong premise and is recorded rather than acted on:** `recommendations.pDelivered` was expected to be a live counter whose correction would raise Delivered P on the New Zealand greens, but nothing reads that field — the accumulator the pacing decisions use is built from the applied products' own analysis, and the single application per year comes from `pApplicationMonth` plus `excludeStarters`. The field is corrected anyway, because a field called `pDelivered` must not hold a request, and `tests/gh417-strategic-p-note.test.js` (7) measures both halves by running the recommender twice from patched source: the note moves, the programme does not. Live on both New Zealand sites, every Required and Delivered figure byte-identical before and after (delivery 250/237.2, 25/10.6, 143.8/140.1; the Couch site 250/15.6, 25/5.4, 150/0.0), with the March note now reading `Strategic P application: 5.4 kg P/ha (of 19.8 requested)` and `… (of 25.0 requested)`.

**GH-421** The nutrition programme carries the cation exchange capacity it was computed against. `computeProgram()` stamps `soil.CEC` — the value `collectFromState()` resolved, whatever route the sample arrived by — so a consumer that scores on CEC no longer has to re-read the page for it. `null` where there is no reading, and it stays null: a soil measurement has no default. Inert on its own; GH-422 is what reads it.

**GH-422** The Plan scores New Zealand product selection against the sample's own CEC, and where the sample has none, both surfaces say so. `NutritionPrebbleIntegration.getSoilCEC()` resolved CEC by re-reading the page — `GAIP_STATE.soil.cec` (a slot nothing on plan.blade.php writes), then a `.gaip-cec` input (which lives in `partials/legacy-hub-markup.blade.php`, so it exists on /reports/export and never on /plan), then a construction-type guess, then a hardcoded 8 — so every New Zealand site reached the recommender with CEC 8 on the Plan whatever the certificate said, while the export passed the real figure. Both surfaces now read GH-421's programme field; the guesses and the 8 are gone and are not replaced, because a substituted soil figure is indistinguishable on the page from a measured one. Where there is no reading the getter returns `null`, the NZ panel's input row prints "CEC: no reading on this sample" with a banner naming what it costs, and the document's Nutrition Program section prints the same in prose — both stating that the recommender's own medium-CEC assumption (10 meq/100g, `prebbles-products.js`, not introduced here) applied. The same call fixes a second, latent bug on the export: the bare getter read the one hidden `.gaip-cec` input on the page, i.e. whichever sample was loaded into the legacy form rather than the sample of the iteration, so a multi-sample export scored every sample's leaching risk against one of them. **The ticket's premise — that this is why Test5 - NZ's Plan and document print different Delivered figures — is wrong, and is recorded rather than acted on.** CEC reaches product selection through exactly two functions, `getReleasePreference()` (bands <5 / <12 / >=12, crossed with irrigation frequency) and `estimateLongevity()` (bands <5 / <10 / >=10); 5.9 and 8 are inside the same band of both, so the recommender could not tell them apart. Measured live before and after across the eleven-pair audit harness: **every Required, Delivered, Balance, Status, product row and monthly cell is byte-identical on both surfaces, New Zealand included** — the Plan's recommender input moves 8 → 5.9 on Test5 and 8 → null on Russley, and no printed figure moves anywhere. Test5's Plan 247.6 N / 180.7 K against the document's 249.7 / 163.5 therefore still stands (the Plan takes Sportsmaster WSF High K where the document takes Lo Biuret Urea, and Ammos 22 at 50 L/ha against 45), `npm run test:e2e` on that fixture is still 18/22 red on the same four rows (Burns and SLAN 22/22), and the cause is still open. **A second input divergence was found, named and left red rather than chased.** `tests/e2e/gh415-prebble-input-parity-live.test.js` started its export before the page had resolved the site's annual N, so the per-sample recompute was skipped and the only "document" snapshot it could capture was the export page's own hidden hub panel — the same integration as the Plan's, agreeing with it by construction. With the annual-N wait the file compares `[CombinedExport b35fix426]`, the code that actually builds the .docx, the CEC row is green, and `context.soilTemp` shows Plan 13 against the document's 12.8: `getSoilTemperature()` prefers `window.climateMetrics.temperature.mean` (live, 12.8) and falls through on the Plan to the persisted analysis cache (13). Soil temperature feeds `getReleaseTechEfficiency()` and `estimateMonthlySoilTemp()`, so it is a product-selection input; it is not the same one-line reach as CEC (nothing carries it on the programme) and wants its own ticket. New `tests/gh422-soil-cec-input.test.js` (9, including the band measurement above) and `tests/e2e/gh422-soil-cec-live.test.js` (16, every New Zealand site on the development database — Test5 / Soccer 5.9, Russley / Green 18 none, GC-NZ delivery / 18th Green 8.5, GC-NZ warm / Main Oval 9.2 — read off the panel and out of the .docx, against 8 for all four before).

**GH-423** Test5 - NZ's two surfaces disagree because of `context.soilTemp`, and that is established by replay rather than by inspection. `PrebbleRecommender.generateProgram()` is a pure function of three things — the twelve rows of `calendar.program.monthly`, the `context`, and the `PrebbleProducts` pool — so the new `tests/e2e/gh423-nz-divergence-live.test.js` captures what each surface actually handed it and runs it again over every combination. The pool is identical, the twelve rows are identical **whole** (`temp`, `month_num` and `season` included, not just the month/gp/N/K/P summary that used to stand in for them), `docCalendar + planContext` reproduces the Plan exactly and `planCalendar + docContext` reproduces the document exactly, and of the three context fields that differ only one moves the output: swapping `soilTemp` alone turns 247.6 N / 180.7 K into 249.7 / 163.5, product for product. `soilPpm` and `muldersFlags` move nothing. **The mechanism is staleness, not a wrong formula.** Both surfaces read the same quantity from different places: the export resolves `window.climateMetrics.temperature.mean`, computed live (12.8 today), while on the Plan that object does not exist at all and `getSoilTemperature()` falls through to the persisted analysis cache (`GAIP_DASHBOARD_DATA.computed.climate.temperature.mean` = 13, written 2026-09-10). Both readings are real; they are a day apart, and 0.2 °C is enough to flip November's foliar product from Sportsmaster WSF High K to Lo Biuret Urea and January's balancing Ammos 22 from 50 L/ha to 45. The b35fix426 PRE snapshots now carry the whole monthly row, the calendar meta and the pool, so this class of difference is visible rather than summarised away. **The fix is measured and deliberately not shipped**, because it changes a New Zealand document: preferring the persisted cache over the live read makes both surfaces resolve 13, and live across the eleven-pair audit exactly one pair moves — Test5's document, Delivered N 249.7→247.6 and K 163.5→180.7, Balance -0.3→-2.4 and 110.5→127.7, the Lo Biuret Urea row replaced by Sportsmaster WSF High K ×2 and Ammos 22 (Balance) 45→50 L/ha — after which the document equals the Plan, `npm run test:e2e` on the Test5 fixture is **22/22** (18/22 before, red since GH-415), Burns and SLAN stay 22/22, and `calc-audit-export-parity-live` is 4/4. Nothing outside New Zealand moves and no Plan figure moves anywhere. The trade-off for the owner: the document would print the temperature from the site's last analysis run rather than today's, which is what the user saw on screen but can be arbitrarily old.

**GH-423 (harness integrity)** Three findings from asking what the parity harnesses can actually fail on. **One harness could not fail**, and it was the new one: `gh415-prebble-input-parity-live` identified its "document" side by a console tag (`b35fix426`) that two different producers emit, and started the export before the page resolved the site's annual N, so the per-sample recompute was skipped and the snapshot it compared was the export page's OWN hidden hub panel — the same `NutritionNzFertiliserIntegration` code as the Plan's, agreeing by construction. It was written during GH-415 and was that way for a day, not the week. Fixed under GH-422 (the wait) and GH-423 (it now asserts `path === 'combined-export-per-sample'` and throws if the export produced no recompute snapshot at all). **The main acceptance harness cannot fail this way, and that is measured rather than argued:** `ui-vs-export-parity` was run with its annual-N wait removed, reproducing the degraded export, and it went **10 failed / 12 passed** — its hard assertions on the document's Annual Nutrient Requirements table and on the export's own hooked `computeProgram` / engine / recommender calls catch it loudly. The file was restored byte-identical and re-run 22/22. **A real hole in the audit harness, now closed:** `calc-audit-export-parity-live`'s completeness test asserted `expect(Array.isArray(bad)).toBe(true)`, which is true of every array, while its comparison test skips any nutrient missing from either side — so a pair whose export degraded contributed no comparisons and still reported green. It now asserts the incomplete set equals a named list (`test4 - USA / Green 13`, which has no regional panel by design) and counts the nutrients actually compared per pair. Every export-touching harness swallows the annual-N wait with `.catch(() => {})`; that stays, because in every one of them the degraded document is caught downstream by an assertion on content the recompute alone produces.

**GH-424 (measurement, nothing shipped)** The product stands on two climate bases, and this measures what the live one costs. **Premise confirmed by reading both pages, not by argument:** all four New Zealand sites resolve `monthlyTempsSource: nasa-power`, "20-year … (January 2001 – December 2020)", per site coordinates, and those values *are* the `temp` field of the twelve rows the recommender is already handed — Auckland 19.8/20.4/19.1/17.0/14.7/12.6/11.4/11.8/12.9/14.2/16.0/18.2, Christchurch 17.5/17.1/15.1/11.9/9.2/6.6/5.9/7.1/8.9/10.8/13.3/15.8 — so option 3 needs no new fetch. Product selection instead anchors on `climateMetrics.temperature.mean`, the mean of the live hourly forecast window. **What that curve actually is:** `estimateMonthlySoilTemp()` is keyed 1–12 and is called with `month_num`, which `computeProgram()` writes 0-based, so January reads `pattern[0]` — undefined, `|| 0` — and every other month gets the *previous* month's deviation. Against Auckland's own normals the modelled curve is out by −7.0 °C in January, −4.6 in August, −4.3 in September; it is not merely offset but wrong-shaped, and that off-by-one is a defect in its own right. **The current reading is used as the ANNUAL MEAN, and that is the larger fault.** `const annualMean = currentTemp || 15;` — the whole twelve-month curve is one live reading plus a hardcoded seasonal shape, and the reading approximates the CURRENT month. So the same sample generated in a different month gets a different year: for Test5 the curve moves **bodily by 8.4 °C**, identically in all twelve months, between a January generation and a July one. Generated in February the model calls Auckland's February soil 27.4 °C (normal 20.4); generated in July it calls the same February 18.4 °C, and July itself 6.5 °C against a normal of 11.4 — near the bottom of the methylene-urea and polymer-coated-urea efficiency curves. Across the twelve possible months of generation the sample yields **2 distinct annual programmes**; under option 3 it yields **1**. (Precisely: `getReleaseTechEfficiency()` interpolates a piecewise-linear curve with breakpoints at 5/10/15 °C, so efficiency is continuous, not a step — the discreteness in the output comes from the candidate ranking flipping and from rounded rates. The curve is steepest between 5 and 15 °C, which is where these sites sit.) **How unstable the anchor is:** Auckland's next seven daily means are 12.3, 13.2, 13.4, 13.7, 13.1, 12.8, 12.7 (spread 1.4 °C); Christchurch's are 7.9, 8.0, 10.0, 10.5, 11.2, 11.7, 8.0 (spread 3.8 °C). Sweeping the anchor 8.0–20.0 °C in tenths gives Test5 **four** distinct product sets with boundaries at 8.6/8.7, 10.0/10.1 and 12.8/12.9 — band widths 0.7, 1.4, 2.8, 7.2 °C — and today's reading sits one tenth of a degree from a boundary, so running those seven real daily means through the recommender yields **two different programmes for the same sample in one week**, 3 days one way and 4 the other. **Option 3 measured live:** taking each month's soil temperature from that month's own normal makes the output independent of the anchor entirely (12.8, 13.0 and 19.0 give identical programmes), and across the eleven-pair audit exactly one pair moves — Test5's **document**, Delivered N 249.7→247.6 and K 163.5→180.7, `Lo Biuret Urea (soluble) ×1 20 kg/ha` replaced by `Sportsmaster WSF High K ×2 40 L/ha`, `Ammos 22 (Balance)` 45→50 L/ha, 13→14 applications — after which it equals the Plan. No Plan figure moves on any site; Russley and both GC-NZ sites move on neither surface; nothing outside New Zealand moves, and nothing can, because `prebbles-products.js` is the New Zealand recommender and the Australian and UK catalogues never read a temperature curve. `npm run test:e2e` is 22/22 on the Test5 fixture (18/22 before) and stays 22/22 on Burns and SLAN; `calc-audit-export-parity-live` 4/4. New `tests/gh424-soil-temp-basis.test.js` (9) over `tests/fixtures/gh424-test5-recommender-inputs.json` and `tests/e2e/gh424-soil-temp-basis-live.test.js` (3). The candidate was applied to measure and then removed; the tree carries the tests only.

**GH-425 (TEMPORARY — remove when the figures are signed off)** The Plan page shows how it reached the three figures in its Nutrient Delivery Summary. The client sets the agronomic rules this product implements and cannot judge a number whose derivation he cannot see, so a block under the summary prints the whole chain for nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium with the arithmetic visible: the soil reading and its conversion, the sufficiency range with its floor, ceiling and citation, the removal ratio and whether it came from this site's tissue analysis or the species table, the requirement branch that actually ran with the real numbers substituted into it (the lift shown as its own step, with its ppm gap, its kg/ha conversion and the years it is spread over; above the ceiling, `max(0, removal − headroom)` with both terms), the delivery accumulated application by application — rate × count = mass, then either the recommender's declared figure or mass × analysis% — and the balance as `current + delivered − removal` against the range in kg/ha. Then, once, **the inputs the page shows nowhere else**: methodology, annual N target, traffic, clipping factors, the monthly N cap and distribution mode, soil texture, sample pH and CEC, bulk density and depth with the ppm→kg/ha unit they produce, the tissue reading and whether the gate fired, years-to-correct, the twelve monthly normals with their provider and climatology window, the growth-potential series, and the recommender's soil temperature — each beside where it was resolved from. **It computes nothing.** Every figure is a field the engines now publish, and the two shared modules are called over the same programme object the panel above was drawn from rather than reimplemented; the block then compares all 21 of its headline figures against the summary cells they explain and prints a red warning if any disagrees. What was threaded out to make that possible is additive and permanent (the panel is not): `computeProgram()` stamps `requirement_detail` (the core's per-nutrient working — branch, floor/ceiling, removal ratio and source, clipping factor, unit, correction period, lift/headroom), `tissue_percent`, `soil.pH`, `soil.soilTexture`, `meta.monthlyTempsSource`/`monthlyTempsPeriod`/`maxNPerMonth`; `nutrition-requirement-core.js` publishes `ppmToKgHaFactor`, `yearsToCorrect`, `removalRatio`/`removalRatioSource`, `liftPpmGap`/`liftKgHaBeforeSpread`, `headroomPpm`/`headroomKgHa`, `maintainRaw`; `classify()` publishes `branch`, `unit`, `balanceKgHa`, `delivered`/`required`/`removal` and `pct`; the delivery ledger carries `analysisPct`. No printed figure moves anywhere — `npm run test:e2e:burns` and `:slan` are 22/22 and the full unit suite is green. **UI only, and only the Plan page: it is deliberately absent from the Word export (owner's decision) and from every other view, which `tests/gh425-calc-trace.test.js` asserts by walking `resources/views`.** One file, `assets/plan-calc-trace.js`, and one `<script>` tag in `plan.blade.php`; deleting those two removes it. New `tests/gh425-calc-trace.test.js` (26, including mutating an engine value and watching the printed figure follow it — a local recomputation could not) and `tests/e2e/gh425-calc-trace-live.test.js` (33 across five Australian sites, covering a sample with no phosphorus, a sample with neither P nor K, the below-floor lift branch on MLSN and on SLAN, and both above-ceiling outcomes; New Zealand sites are deliberately not opened). Two things the block surfaced and does not hide: the input adapter stamps methodology, species and surface type as coming from the "sample" on this page whatever their real origin, because the Plan resolves them before the adapter sees them; and `annual_totals_range_source` reads `certificate` under MLSN and SLAN by design, so the block names the published range for those rather than inventing a Hill Labs certificate.

**GH-426 (measurement, nothing shipped)** Should the recommender be fed SOIL temperature, via the hub's own air-to-soil model? **Both premises verified in the source.** The efficiency curves are specified against soil temperature and say so — methylene urea cites "Spencer 2008 Table 18; Cornell Turf BMP" with `Cornell: "little N released unless soil temp >50°F (10°C)"`, and its release is microbial, so air is wrong on the curves' own terms. And `estimateSoilTemp()` (climate-engine-v2.js) is a real model: `api` (reliability 85), an analytical heat-equation branch `model` (60) that damps the surface amplitude with depth using a texture-keyed diffusivity, and `crude` (30) = air − 1.5. **But the branch the app can reach monthly is `crude`.** The model branch needs a diurnal amplitude; `climate-normals-service.js` requests `parameters: 'T2M'` and nothing else, and there is no per-month API soil reading for a climatology — so "soil temperature" would reduce to a flat −1.5 offset at reliability 30, with no texture and no heat equation. It is closable: the same single NASA POWER request also serves `T2M_MAX`/`T2M_MIN` (fetched into `tests/fixtures/gh426-nz-monthly-normals.json`), so an amplitude is two parameters away. **The two reachable branches disagree about the SIGN of the air-to-soil step** — crude puts January Auckland soil at 18.3 against an air normal of 19.79, the model at 22.8, a 4.5 °C spread — because `estimated = mean + amp·exp(−d/L)·0.5` is phase-averaged, not mean-preserving. **And that settles the question:** the amplitude term is the diurnal residual, not a mean-level offset — evaluate the same formula at 2 m and it returns 19.79, the air mean, exactly. For a MONTHLY figure the heat equation's answer *is* the monthly mean air temperature, so plain option 3 is not an approximation of the soil conversion; at monthly resolution it is what the soil conversion reduces to. **Measured live on all four New Zealand sites, replayed through the recommender each page actually ran** (with the site's own distributor pool, checked against the pool ids the page recorded — a first pass that assumed Prebble reproduced neither surface on the three PGG/all sites and was thrown out): air normals and the soil model branch produce **identical programmes on every site**; soil-crude differs on exactly one, Test5, where it reproduces today's *document* (249.7/163.5) rather than today's *Plan* (247.6/180.7). Russley, GC-NZ delivery and GC-NZ warm are unchanged under all four options. So the soil conversion, done properly, buys no change in output, and done with the data available today it moves one site in the wrong direction. **The 0-based/1-based defect does not survive the change and does not need its own fix:** `computeProgram()` refuses to produce a programme unless all twelve `monthlyTemps` are real numbers, so every row's `temp` is a resolved normal and any option reading it never reaches `estimateMonthlySoilTemp()` — the function becomes dead code and should be deleted with the change rather than kept as an unreachable fallback. New `tests/gh426-soil-temperature-conversion.test.js` (8) and `tests/e2e/gh426-soil-temp-options-live.test.js` (3) over `tests/fixtures/gh426-nz-monthly-normals.json`. No production file was modified this round.

**GH-427** New Zealand product selection runs on the site's twelve monthly climate normals, and `estimateMonthlySoilTemp()` is deleted. The per-month temperature is now each calendar row's own `temp` — the NASA POWER 20-year climatology for those coordinates that growth potential already uses, carried on the programme and identical on both surfaces. What it replaced took `climateMetrics.temperature.mean`, the mean of the next few days' hourly forecast, and used it as the year's ANNUAL mean plus a hardcoded seasonal shape, with three faults compounding: a live reading drove an annual plan (Test5's own forecast moves 12.3–13.7 °C in a week across product boundaries at 8.65/10.05/12.85, so the same sample produced two programmes depending on the day); a current reading used as an annual mean moved the whole curve 8.4 °C between a January and a July generation; and the pattern objects were keyed 1–12 while the call passed a 0-based `month_num`, so January got no deviation and every other month got the previous month's — out by −7.0 °C against Auckland's own January normal. **The function is deleted rather than left as a fallback:** `computeProgram()` refuses to build a programme unless all twelve `monthlyTemps` are real numbers, so there is nothing to fall back to, and an unreachable known-wrong function is how it gets called again. **Live, eleven pairs, in a window certified quiet against the concurrent GH-425 work: exactly one pair moves — Test5's document** (Delivered N 249.7→247.6, K 163.5→180.7; Balance −0.3→−2.4 and 110.5→127.7; `Lo Biuret Urea (soluble) ×1 20 kg/ha` → `Sportsmaster WSF High K ×2 40 L/ha`; `Ammos 22 (Balance)` 45→50 L/ha; 13→14 applications) — after which it equals its Plan. No Plan figure moved anywhere, Russley and both GC-NZ sites moved on neither surface, and nothing outside New Zealand moved. `npm run test:e2e` is **22/22 on the Test5 fixture**, red since GH-415; Burns and SLAN stay 22/22; `calc-audit-export-parity-live` 4/4; `gh423-nz-divergence-live` reports "the two surfaces agree — no divergence to explain", with all four cells of its replay matrix equal. `gh415-prebble-input-parity-live` is green: `context.soilTemp` still differs between the surfaces (13 against 12.8) and is now vestigial — swept 8.0–20.0 °C in tenths it yields exactly one product set — so it is excluded there with that sweep as the evidence, and the three context objects that still carry it could drop it. **The air-vs-soil gap is a known property and is deliberately not surfaced** (owner's decision): the release-efficiency curves are written about soil temperature and these are air normals, recorded here and in the code, with no wording in the panel, the popover or the document. GH-426 measured the alternative and it is byte-identical on every New Zealand site. Tests reworked rather than deleted with the function they measured: the curves it produced are recorded in `tests/fixtures/gh424-test5-recommender-inputs.json` under `observed.beforeGH427`, and `tests/gh424-soil-temp-basis.test.js` (11) now asserts the inverse — one product set across the whole sweep, one programme across a week of forecast, one across twelve months of generation. Two harness faults found and fixed while doing it: `gh340-nz-k-catchup-pacing` pinned source text inside a fixed 2000-character window and went red because a comment grew above the line it looks for, now bounded on the end of the `monthContext` object instead; and the GH-426 option replays patched `estimateMonthlySoilTemp`, so once it was deleted they silently compared four identical options — they now apply the curve on the calendar rows, where the recommender reads it.

**GH-428** The Plan's calculation-trace block shows the twelve temperatures product selection actually ran on, and the dead outer soil temperature is deleted. The block's "Soil temperature (product selection)" row read `context.soilTemp` — one value the integration resolved before calling the recommender, which `generateProgram()` overwrites with each month's own climate normal before any selector sees the context — so it printed 13 degC on Test5 - NZ above a normals row containing no 13. **The ticket's premise that it fell through to a hardcoded 15 is wrong and is corrected here:** probed source by source on all four New Zealand sites, the first four live sources are null and the persisted analysis cache answers (Test5 13, Russley 10.4, both GC-NZ sites 9.6), so the figure on screen was a real reading from a real source — which is what made it hard to see. `getSoilTemperature()` and the `soilTemp` field are deleted from all three recommender contexts (`nutrition-prebble-integration.js`, `nutrition-nz-fertiliser-integration.js`, `word-export-combined.js`), on the same reasoning that deleted `estimateMonthlySoilTemp()` in GH-427. **Established before deleting, by instrumenting the consumers rather than reading the source:** `generateProgram()` is the recommender's only entry point from production code, and the three functions that read a temperature (`getReleaseTechEfficiency()` and the two product choosers) are only ever reached through the month context — they were handed 14.2 / 16 / 17 / 18.2 / 19.1 / 19.8 on Test5 and never 13. `prebbles-products.js` now publishes `program.soilTempSeries`, the per-month figure recorded as the loop hands it to the selectors, and the row reads that; only the New Zealand recommender has a temperature curve, so the field's absence is what makes the Australian and UK rows say the region takes none. `buildTrace()` no longer accepts a `context` at all — it was the recommender's INPUT object, and on New Zealand sites not even the one belonging to the programme on screen. **Nothing moved:** a full pre-change snapshot of all four New Zealand sites (summary table, every monthly product row and rate, annual tally, delivery totals) compares equal after; `npm run test:e2e` is 22/22 on the Test5 fixture and on Burns and SLAN; `calc-audit-export-parity-live` 4/4 over eleven pairs; `gh415`, `gh422`, `gh423`, `gh424`, `gh425` and `gh426` live all green, with `gh423` now reporting `soilTemp` gone from the context diff. New `tests/gh428-outer-soil-temp.test.js` (9, durable) and `tests/e2e/gh428-outer-soil-temp-live.test.js` (5).

**GH-428 (harness)** The trace block is now checked against what entered the calculation, not only against what the page displays. Its existing self-check compares its headline figures with the Nutrient Delivery Summary above it — displayed against displayed — and was green throughout GH-428, because the summary says nothing about soil temperature. `tests/e2e/gh428-calc-trace-provenance-live.test.js` wraps `computeProgram()`, the regional recommender's `generateProgram()`, and the functions that consume a temperature or a CEC, in the live page before Generate is pressed; it records each call's arguments and a deep clone of its return, and asserts all 23 input rows and every nutrient headline and delivery-ledger line against those recordings, at a named grade — **consumed** (recorded where a calculation used it, the only grade that catches a figure which is in the object and drives nothing), **entered** (an argument to `computeProgram()`), **produced** (the return, cloned at return time). Nothing in it reads `GilbaNutritionCalendar.program` or `GAIP_NUTRITION_PROGRAM`, so it cannot agree by construction the way two harnesses did this week. **It is proven to fail rather than argued to:** the run mutates the live objects the block reads — twelve plausible soil temperatures one degree off, an annual N seven kilograms up — remounts the block and asserts the same checker names exactly those two rows, while the block's own self-check still reports all 21 figures match. Re-pointing the row back at a single hardcoded value reproduces the original defect as `printed "13 degC" vs engine "consumed but not printed: 14.2 / 16 / 17 / 18.2 / 19.1 / 19.8"`. It covers every row the block prints and goes red if a row is added. **It belongs to the temporary GH-425 block and is listed in that block's removal instructions as step 3**, alongside `tests/gh425-calc-trace.test.js`; `tests/gh428-outer-soil-temp.test.js` is the half that outlives it. 7 tests, on Test5 - NZ and Burns.

**GH-429 (TEMPORARY block, GH-425)** The delivery ledger's note says why an amendment is excluded, in the reader's terms. It opened with "these lines add up to the total" and then contradicted itself in the same sentence, and it explained the exclusion as "added at export rather than by the programme" — our own plumbing, which tells an agronomist nothing about why a product he can see is not in the figure. It now reads: the total is the sum of the lines above; amendments — gypsum, lime, Epsom salts — are shown in the product table but not counted here, because they are applied to correct the soil itself and counting them towards delivery would cancel the deficiency that called for them. That is the real reason the exclusion exists (`word-export.js:1833`: counting an amendment would "self-suppress the very amendment that produced the entry"). The note is also now printed only when the ledger actually contains an amendment line; it used to appear on every nutrient, explaining an exclusion that was not there. Reported from the UI on Test - GC - NZ - delivery, where phosphorus carries no amendment and the note appeared anyway. Unit suite 2552 passed. **Not live-verified**: the samples stage-0 agent was working at the time, and a live run would have measured against a moving tree.

**GH-430** (lab samples, stage 0) `POST /api/samples/sync` no longer deletes a sample because the browser's push did not mention it. `reconcileMissingSnapshotSamples()` soft-deleted every row of a (site, sample_type) outside the keep-list each push built, treating the request as "here is my complete picture, make the database match" — and the push is never that picture, because samples restored from the server reach the store shaped as `values` while `sync()` reads only `rawData`, so a tab that has just saved one sample sends a keep-list of one. Reproduced live on a scratch site holding six samples before the change: one Capture answered `synced: 1, deleted: 6` and left one live row; the same action after it answers `deleted: 0` and all seven stand, as do an edit of a restored sample and a two-row CSV lab import. `clearSiteData` is untouched and is now the only deletion the endpoint performs. **Deletion is inert until per-record writes land:** removing a sample in the hub reached the database only through this same mechanism, so a deleted sample now returns on reload — accepted as the better half of the trade, and the reason stages 1–2 of `files/fixes/26-08-17-hoxton-v6/PLAN-samples-sync-FINAL.md` should follow promptly. Nothing already soft-deleted is resurrected by the change, and `samples` is unchanged at 147 rows / 87 soft-deleted across the whole run. New `tests/Feature/Gh430SamplesNoSnapshotDeleteTest.php` (4, three of them red before the change) and `tests/e2e/gh430-samples-sync-no-snapshot-delete-live.test.js` (7, `npm run test:e2e:samples`, self-cleaning); `SiteApiTest`'s `test_..._reconciles_deleted_samples` asserted the data loss as a feature and is inverted. PHPUnit 124/124, Jest 2552, `npm run test:e2e` 22/22 on Test5, Burns and SLAN.

**GH-430 (harness)** `tests/e2e/gh401-delivery-volumes-live.test.js` is green again on Test5 - NZ. Its Delivered/Total-Delivered pins read 237.4 / 0 / 175.2 and its Required phosphorus 0, against 247.6 / 14.9 / 180.7 and 5.9 on both surfaces: GH-415's maintain-floor took the phosphorus requirement from 0.0 to 5.9, which pulled a phosphorus product into the programme and moved the Plan's Delivered, and the document caught up at GH-427. Re-pinned to what the product prints, after confirming on the same run that the two surfaces agree — Required identical string for string, the document's total row equal to its own ANR Delivered, and no plan-against-document Delivered disagreement. 40/40 across all four sites.

**GH-431** (lab samples) A sample deleted on the Data page stays deleted. `saveSampleRecord()` looks its row up with `withTrashed()->firstOrNew()` and called `restore()` on it, and `POST /api/samples/sync` runs that for every pushed sample carrying `rawData` — so the Data page's own per-record delete (`DELETE /api/data/entry/{id}`, under a button reading "This cannot be undone") was undone by the next ordinary push from any browser whose localStorage still held the sample. Measured on the dev stack: delete → `deleted_at` set → one push → `deleted_at` NULL. GH-430's note said deletion was inert "until per-record writes land"; the per-record endpoint had already shipped in the new hub, which is what made the trade it described not the trade in force. `sync()` now passes an explicit allow-list and restores nothing outside it, reporting the refusals as `skipped`. The one exception is the Settings import: `clearSiteData` and the bundle arrive in the same request, and that request is a whole-site replacement by the owner's decision, so there the file is the new truth and any row it names is restored — including one deleted before the import began, which a narrower rule would have dropped on the floor while reporting it as written. `SiteApiTest`'s `..._can_restore_soft_deleted_sample` asserted the old behaviour and its own docblock predicted this flip; it is inverted. New `tests/e2e/review-sample-delete-resurrection-live.test.js` (3, red before), two PHPUnit cases for the refusal and for the import exception, and the GH-430 live pin `a row that was already soft-deleted is not resurrected` — which could not fail, because its subject was seeded before the browser loaded and was therefore in no push — replaced by one that deletes a sample the tab is holding. PHPUnit 127, Jest 2584, live `npm run test:e2e:samples` 8/8 with `samples` unchanged at 147 rows / 87 soft-deleted.

**GH-432** `POST /api/samples/sync` asks what the user may do with the site. It was the only sample-writing endpoint with no role check — `store()`, `update()`, `DataController::destroy()`, `SprayLogController::destroy()` and `SiteController::update()` all call `canEditSite()`, while this one filtered on `$user->sites()`, which is membership at any role. A viewer could upsert samples and, with `clearSiteData: true`, hard-delete the site's `spray_logs` and `field_log_entries`. Sites the user cannot edit are skipped rather than aborting the whole request, so one read-only site in a multi-site push does not fail it for the rest, and the count comes back as `forbidden`. New PHPUnit case.

**GH-433** The Nutrient Delivery Summary's info popover says what the table does. The legend was registered under one glossary key by BOTH `nutrition-prebble-integration.js` and `nutrition-au-fertiliser-integration.js`, with a comment in the Australian file recording that the duplicate was harmless because the two were "byte-identical twins". `Object.assign` replaces a key rather than merging into it, so that held only while the bodies matched — and GH-415 rewrote the New Zealand copy's Required line and left the Australian one saying "Required — Removal + Lift; 0 once soil >= ceiling." That file is loaded second in all five blade templates that load either, so the stale sentence won on **every** page, New Zealand included, directly above the non-zero Required figures GH-415 had just introduced. The entry now lives once, in `nutrient-balance-status.js`, the module that computes the quantities it describes and is loaded before both panels everywhere. The two GH-312 pins that should have caught this each asserted their OWN file's copy, so the pair recorded the divergence instead of detecting it; both now read the owner. New `tests/gh433-one-glossary-entry.test.js` (4) and `tests/e2e/gh433-glossary-live.test.js` (4), the latter counting the registrations on the live page rather than only reading the winner. Live before: two registrations, the popover showing the stale sentence; after: one, showing GH-415's.

**GH-434** The document's Monthly Schedule prints the surface's unit. GH-409 moved the Annual Product Summary and the Fertiliser Purchasing Summary onto the shared unit rule and left this renderer hardcoding `kg/ha` for granulars and `L/ha` for liquids, which made the document internally inconsistent where it had at least been uniformly wrong: on Test - GC - NZ - delivery the Monthly Schedule read `200 kg/ha` and `186 kg/ha` under an Annual Product Summary three paragraphs above, and a Plan page beside it, both saying `20 g/m²` and `18.6 g/m²`. Six rows on that site, on the table GH-401 records as "the one the client orders fertiliser off". New `applicationRate()` in `nutrition-delivery-core.js` handles a per-application row, as `productRate()` does an annual total; it takes the recommender's own pre-formatted string where there is one (the Australian and UK rows already carry `4x 7 L/ha`) and builds the New Zealand form otherwise, so each region's document matches that region's own Plan rather than a third convention. Two things this surfaced: the Plan page contradicted ITSELF on a soluble — `MAP Tech` printed `20 kg/ha` in the New Zealand monthly table and `2 g/m²` in the Annual Product Summary on the same page — which is fixed the same way, and the Monthly Schedule's liquid line still carries no application count. `tests/e2e/gh409-product-table-units-live.test.js` has printed both surfaces' cells since GH-409 under the heading "ALSO READ, AND NOT YET ASSERTED"; they are asserted now, 16/16 on both New Zealand greens sites.

**GH-435** The Australian "Strategic P application" note names the shortfall, as the New Zealand one has since GH-417. GH-417 recorded that the Australian twin "has always printed the delivered figure" — true, and the reason the caption was left alone; the figure is right and the caption around it is not. `selectPhosphorusSource()` rate-caps every source it can pick, so `Strategic P application: 4.1 kg/ha (annual requirement)` asserts that one capped application IS the annual requirement. On Burns the note now reads `4.1 kg P/ha (of 14.0 requested)` in October, `(of 9.9 requested)` in November and `(of 5.8 requested)` in December; where nothing was capped the old wording stands. The unit is spelled `kg P/ha` for the same reason it is on the New Zealand side. Also deleted here: `getSlowReleaseEfficiency(gp, soilTemp)`, never called from anywhere and the only thing in the Australian catalogue that read a soil temperature — which made the Plan trace's "this region's recommender takes no soil temperature" look wrong to anyone who grepped for one. New `tests/gh435-au-strategic-p-note.test.js` (6), including a run of the pre-change source that proves no product, rate or delivered figure moved.

**GH-436** Eight tests that could not fail. Each was rewritten and then shown failing on the defect it is supposed to catch. `gh424-soil-temp-basis` patched `estimateMonthlySoilTemp`, which GH-427 deleted and which the same file asserts is gone sixty lines above, so its three "option 3" runs were the baseline three times — and it PRINTED them as measurements the GH-424/426/427 planning quoted; it now varies the live anchor across its range and asserts the temperatures the selectors consumed. `gh403-required-one-quantity` read `printed[1]` inside a loop named `i`, asserting nitrogen three times and never phosphorus or potassium, on the fallback branch; it now checks all three against the figures that branch falls back to. `gh401-delivery-volumes-and-rounding` said in its own comment that it ran `_computeProgrammeDelivered` and then tested `Array.reduce`; it loads `word-export.js` and calls it. `gh387-surface-type-parity` asserted `body.toContain("'golf_greens'")` and an arity check repeated six times; it now evaluates the real fallback from its own source with the adapter absent and compares both mappings over twenty inputs. `gh365-gp-status-unit-explicit` had two negative assertions per file, so a call site that dropped `GAIP_GPStatus` entirely and inlined its own thresholds passed both; the positive is asserted now. `gh425-calc-trace`'s declared-contribution test ran zero assertions on every run — the only declared entry in its fixture is an amendment with `nutrients.N` of 0, so its `if (!declared) return` always fired — and now runs on a fixture with twelve. `gh368-two-engines-tissue-parity` loaded one engine and compared it with a transcription of the other, under a `toBeLessThanOrEqual(1)` tolerance; it compares the engine with the shared core, both loaded, exactly. `gh410-phosphorus-overshoot-probe` never set the `gap` it sorted on and printed, so its "worst overshoot first" table was unsorted and said `undefined`. A ninth, found while fixing the first: the two GH-312 glossary pins are corrected under GH-433.

**GH-437** The calculation-audit harnesses write their output to a gitignored directory. `calc-audit-results.json` (2.1 MB) and `calc-audit-export-results.json` were written to the repository root as tracked files, so every run put a large diff in `git status` beside whatever code change the run was measuring. Both old paths are also listed in `.gitignore` so a working copy still holding them stops reporting them; removing them from the index is `git rm --cached` and is left to the owner.

**GH-438 (TEMPORARY block, GH-425)** Three things the block said that were stronger or vaguer than what it knew. **The green self-check line** read "All 21 figures match the Nutrient Delivery Summary cell they explain", which reads as an independent verification; it is displayed-against-displayed over the same programme object, so it can only catch this block having been drawn from a different programme than the table, and GH-428 is the standing proof that it stays green while a row is wrong. The line now says what it covers and what it does not. **Bulk density and sampling depth** were sourced as "the selected soil sample, or the engine default where it carries none" — both possibilities, for the two numbers that make the ppm→kg/ha factor and through it every lift and headroom term. `computeProgram()` now stamps `bulkDensityDefaulted` / `soilDepthDefaulted` (deliberately NOT inside `meta.inputSources`, which the parity harness compares field for field across the two surfaces), and the row names the one that applies. That half is additive and permanent. Writing it surfaced a third: the row printed `soil.bulkDensity`, which `computeProgram()` leaves undefined when the sample carries none — the core substitutes its default at the point of use — so the row read "— g/cm3 / — cm" above "1 ppm = 1.4 kg/ha in this rootzone". It prints what the core recorded having used. Also corrected: the removal instructions were headed "in two steps" and listed three. New `tests/gh438-bulk-density-provenance.test.js` (6, durable).


**GH-439 (stage 0 of 5)** The server stops accepting a browser's copy of a site as the truth about that site. `POST /api/sites/sync` no longer writes the site name and no longer creates a site for an ID it does not recognise: its payload is the browser's own legacy registry, whose label falls back to the site ID whenever it has none, which is where both a live site renamed to its own UUID and the "sites I never created" rows came from. A new `PATCH /api/sites/{site}/config/gaip` takes the change rather than the state — a white list of top-level keys, one-level merge for object sections, absent means untouched, `null` refused in favour of an explicit `clear`, and the identity fields (`turf.species/methodology/turfType`, `location.lat/lon`) that cannot be emptied at all; GH-371's rules for the cached programme are reused unchanged, and every call is logged as `site-config.patch`. The whole-object `PUT` still answers, because the hub pages still send one in the background, and is now guarded: keys the payload omits are carried forward and emptied identity fields are put back, with a `site-config.put.blanked-fields` warning. Measured live: one load of `/reports/forensic` fires 14 background config PUTs across every site on the login, and the `wizard` section survives them now. The site time zone is derived from the coordinates (`DateTimeZone::getLocation()`, nearest reference point, no dependency) instead of the hardcoded `Australia/Sydney` both setup wizards sent, with the Settings field remaining a manual override; `sitePayload()` reports the derived value as `timezone_derived`. This is the server half only — the pages still push whole configs and still send state they hold, which is what stages 1-4 remove. New `GH439SiteConfigPatchTest` (18), `GH439PutGuardTest` (6), `GH439SyncRegistryTest` (6), `GH439TimezoneTest` (9), and `tests/gh439-no-client-state-writes.test.js` as six `test.todo` for the structural check the later stages make true. Two `SiteApiTest` cases that created their fixture through `sites/sync` build it directly instead. Live `tests/e2e/gh439-config-reset-live.test.js` 12/12, with B, H1b and H1c red on purpose (`test.failing`): a stale tab's methodology, the legacy form's `nProgram`, and its PGR defaults are all non-empty values the server cannot tell from a deliberate edit. **Review follow-up:** two of these tests could not fail and now can — the identity-field test was green through the null rule that answers first (it disables the two middleware that convert `""` to null, so the identity rule is the one under test, and asserts the message that tells them apart), and H2a/H2b were green having sent nothing at all (they require a push and print what its body carried; the 7 s delay H1 uses is what makes the page send one). Both were shown failing with the guard removed and passing with it restored.

**GH-440 (GH-439 stage 1 of 5; stage 0 shipped as GH-439)** The new hub's writers send what changed. Settings' four save paths (Site, Turf, Traffic, bundle import), `nutrition-calendar.js`'s two persistence paths, both setup wizards, the alerts panel and the dashboard's companion selector all `PATCH .../config/gaip` with the sections they own, and take the site's config back from the response instead of from what they sent; `site-config-persistence.js` gains `patchConfigOnServer()` and its three exported writers (`mergeConfig`, `setCompanionSpecies`, `setMultiSiteTurfEnabled`) route through it. `pushConfigsToServer()` still exists for the background snapshots (stage 2 removes those) but nothing here calls it. Scenario B of the GH-439 live suite is green: a Plan tab opened before a Settings methodology change, then pressed Generate, used to put the old methodology back on every press — it sent its whole load-time copy — and now sends only the programme keys it computed, having re-read the site's config first (`refreshSiteConfig()`, one GET on the button). Two things the plan could not know, both found live: an empty form field never arrives as an empty string (Laravel converts it to null, which the route refuses), so every writer states an empty control as a named `clear` and leaves the five identity fields out of the request entirely rather than trying to empty them; and a generated programme reaches the server as two writes — the calendar with its coordinate stamp, then `nutritionProgram` alone — so the second is matched against the stamp already stored, narrowly and only for that shape, since a stored stamp proves nothing about a newly-offered calendar programme. Client half of the time zone (contract 2.5): neither wizard sends `Australia/Sydney` any more, and the Settings select leads with `Auto — <derived zone>` (or `Auto — set location first`), which submits an empty value and lets the server derive. Also closed here, from the stage-0 review: `sites/sync` logs the IDs it skips, and a PATCH that moves a site no longer keeps a `nutritionProgram` computed for the old location when the patch replaces only the calendar programme. New `tests/gh440-writers-send-changes.test.js` (17) and new live scenario S1 (every config write from Plan and Settings is a PATCH of named sections; zero PUTs measured across the run). Six existing tests asserted the whole-object writes and are rewritten onto the patches. PHPUnit 169, Jest 2602, live `gh439-config-reset-live` 13/13 with H1b/H1c still red by design (stage 2), `sites` and `site_configs` byte-identical before and after the run. **Review follow-up:** the stamp fallback is gone.
