It was not as narrow as it read — the four regional integrations all send that shape, on page load as well as on Generate — and it reopened GH-371 from the other side: a stale tab's calendar was refused for being computed elsewhere, then the product programme built from that same calendar landed under the stored stamp, leaving a programme for one location beside a calendar for another, which no read path can see because every staleness check reads the calendar. Each integration now states its programme's origin (`NutritionCalendar.coordsFromCalendar()`, the calendar's own `meta.lat/lon`) and the server supplies a stamp for nobody. Also here: the structural "no PUT" case was matching the URL and the method on the same line, so it watched two files of six and missed both wizards — it pairs each `config/gaip` request with the method near it now, ignores comments, and records the one PUT still in `pushConfigsToServer()` as known until stage 2; and a failed pre-Generate re-read no longer falls through into a computation on settings the page could not confirm — it says so and stops. New PHPUnit case walks the stale tab's two writes end to end (red before), plus five Jest cases for the re-read states and two for the stamp's origin. PHPUnit 171, Jest 2611, live 13/13.

**GH-441 (GH-439 stage 2 of 5)** The browser stops writing state. `site-config-persistence.js` becomes a read cache: `pushConfigsToServer()`, `syncSiteRegistryToServer()`, `saveLocationToServer()`, `loadFromStorage()`, `snapshotConfig()` and the four DOM-snapshot listeners (`gaip:turf-profile-change`, `gaip:site-save-requested`, `gaip:config-save-requested`, `gaip:analysis-complete`) are deleted, along with the switch-away save, the location-bleed cleanup and the two one-time migrations that edited the cache in place. `GET /api/sites` replaces the cache whole — no savedAt negotiation, no per-field merge, a site the server does not mention is dropped — and the page-load restore now runs when that response arrives instead of on an 800/3000 ms timer, which is what used to make a slow page push its own form defaults. This is what closes the cross-site damage the stage-1 review measured live: the snapshot belonged to whichever site was last rendered into the legacy form, so one site's species and methodology reached another site's row, and no server rule could catch it because the values were real. Measured after: five hub pages opened against a 7 s-delayed `GET /api/sites` produce **zero** writes to `/api/sites*` and every `savedAt` in the database is unchanged (new live scenario S2). When the settings cannot be read the page says so — `gaip:site-config-failed` / `gaip:samples-persistence-error(sites-list)` raise one shared banner from `dashboard-ui.js` and the analysis does not start on the form's defaults (S3). `sample-persistence.js` stops pushing the site registry and stops rebuilding it from this browser's samples or config copy (`recoverSitesFromLegacyConfig()` deleted); `sample-manager.js` creates registry entries with no label rather than one made of the site ID. Every db-shell page now carries the active site's stored config and wizard record (one `layouts.db-shell` composer), so the setup wizard follows the database instead of `localStorage` — a clean browser no longer sees it on a completed site (S5) — and `location-preloader.js`, which wrote coordinates from the local copy over the server's, is removed from all five views. The `/hub` Save and Rename buttons go with the write paths they used (decision 9). Also here, from the stage-1 review: a refused config write is now visible on the Plan panel instead of leaving a programme on screen that the database does not have. Tests: `gh385-snapshot-config-site-scoped` (10) deleted with the function it described, the snapshot blocks in `gh371-d01` and `gh377` removed — the read-side staleness guards they shared are untouched and still assert — and the merge-rule cases rewritten for replace-wholesale. PHPUnit 171, Jest 2590, live `gh439-config-reset-live` 15/15 with no `test.failing` left in the file, `npm run test:e2e` red on exactly the one pre-existing row (tissue K, fixture vs both live surfaces, a sample edited 12.09 — not this work). The one config that changed across the runs is Test5 - NZ's, whose programme keys the parity harness rewrites by pressing Generate. **Review follow-up:** the failure state was half-built and in the wrong half. Clearing `GAIP_SITE_CONFIG_PENDING` on the failure branch opened both deferred-compute guards, so the analysis ran on the legacy form's defaults anyway — measured live on /reports/forensic before the fix (`computeAll triggered`, disease risk 79 from a form nobody had filled). Four places now read `GAIP_SITE_CONFIG_FAILED` and stop instead: the orchestrator's site-changed timer, hub-tissue's site-switch fallback and its 6 s auto-run safety net, and `auto-refresh.js`, which was the one actually starting the run. The banner moved out of `dashboard-ui.js` into `settings-unavailable-banner.js`, loaded by both layouts — it was invisible on /morning-briefing, a page a client opens, because that page sits on `layouts.app`. New live scenarios S4a (/morning-briefing) and S4b (/reports/forensic) assert the banner, the failed flag and the absence of any run trace; S4a also captures the screen. Five scenarios that counted writes could pass on a page that never rendered — `assertPageRendered()` now checks the navigation status and that a layout actually exists, shown failing against a 500. Measured and reported rather than changed: on /reports/export the setup wizard stays hidden even with no `wizard` record at all, because `gilba_turf_profiles` in localStorage (written by site-profile-bridge.js) short-circuits it before the injected flag is consulted — stage 4's wizard repair needs to know that. PHPUnit 171, Jest 2590, live 17/17, parity unchanged at 21/22 on the same pre-existing row.

**GH-442 (GH-439 stage 3 of 5)** The browser's copy of the configuration is deleted and the old write routes are closed. `site-config-persistence.js` keeps `_configs` in memory for the life of the page and nothing else: `saveToStorage()` is replaced by `forgetStoredConfigs()`, which removes `gilba_hub_site_configs` and its namespaced twin once on load, so a browser upgrading from an older version stops carrying a stale copy of someone's settings. Every remaining reader moved to the server: `hub-orchestrator.js` reads companion species from the cache, `gaip-field-log-analysis.js` reads the site config from the cache or the page's own injected config (its pre-flight no longer merges into localStorage, and the PGR bleed cleanup that repaired that copy is gone), `gaip-morning-briefing.js` drops its two-key localStorage fallback, `site-profile-bridge.js` builds TPC profiles from the cache rather than the stored blob, `settings-init.js` loses its three mirrors, and `gilba-storage-migrate.js` stops migrating a key that no longer exists. `location-preloader.js` is deleted outright — no view has loaded it since stage 2. Server: `PUT .../config/gaip` answers **410** for `gaip` (`gssh` keeps the endpoint, decision 7) and `POST /api/sites/sync` is withdrawn with `syncRegistry()`. Two things measured rather than assumed: the withdrawn sync path answers **405**, not the 404 the plan expected, because `/api/sites/sync` still matches `GET /api/sites/{site}` — nothing accepts the payload either way, and the test records the real answer; and the live suite's own setup had to stop using the whole-object PUT to seed a site's state, so it writes the row directly — test setup is not a client. The six `test.todo` placeholders written in stage 0 are now six real assertions in `tests/gh439-no-client-state-writes.test.js`, verified by putting each violation back and watching three of them fail. Tests moved with the routes: `GH439PutGuardTest` becomes the 410/405 suite, `GH439SyncRegistryTest` is deleted with its endpoint, ten PUT cases leave `GH371CoordinateInvalidationTest` (every rule they covered is asserted on the PATCH route), and two `SiteApiTest` cases move to PATCH. New live scenario S6 plants both storage keys, walks eight pages and finds them gone. PHPUnit 150, Jest 2596, live `gh439-config-reset-live` 18/18, parity unchanged at 21/22 on the same pre-existing row; `sites` identical before and after, and the only config that moved is Test5 - NZ's programme keys, rewritten by the parity harness pressing Generate. **Review follow-up:** an ordinary load of `/reports/export` and `/plan` was still writing, and scenario S2 could not see it — S2 stalls `GET /api/sites` by 7 s and the programme chain does not finish inside that window, so it measured the window rather than the product. Measured with no delay at all: two `PATCH config/gaip` per load, and the trail names the cause — `restoreFromPersisted()` dispatches the same `gaip:nutrition-calendar-generated` event as a real calculation, so the regional integrations rebuilt the product programme from a **restored** calendar and wrote it back. That is the page returning state it was just given, not an intent, and it moved `savedAt` on every plain page load. The two dispatches now say which they are (`restored: true/false`) and the four integrations write only a freshly computed programme; the same trail on a clean run reads "restored programme — not written back". New scenario S8 measures a plain load with no stall (zero writes, `savedAt` unchanged across all sites) and S2 is renamed to say what it actually covers. Dead code after the route closures: the unreachable `gaip` branch in `updateConfig()`, `guardWholeObjectGaipWrite()` and `resolveGaipConfigWrite()` are removed — `isBlankConfigValue()` sat between them, was removed with them by mistake, and eight PATCH tests caught it on the next run; it is back. Two GH-371 rules live on the PATCH route with no test there — a site's first programme when its coordinates start NULL (a regression that has happened once already) and a malformed stamp — now have one each, both shown failing with the rule removed.

**GH-442 (race, introduced by stage 1)** `patchConfig()` lost whole patches under concurrency, and the defect is this work's own. Stage 1 replaced one whole-config PUT with several small patches; `patchConfig()` reads the row, merges in PHP and writes the column back, so two patches that overlap each read the row before the other has written, and the second write -- built on content already stale -- replaces the first. Both answer 200 and nothing on screen says otherwise. Measured: six concurrent patches of six different keys, six 200s, **four keys in the database** (new live scenario S9, red before the fix). It is also what the flaky S8 was reporting: Generate sends three patches inside one second, and the first vanished whole -- calendar and the `maxNPerMonth` that travelled with it -- in three of the reviewer's four runs and two of mine. The read, the merge and the write now happen inside one transaction with `lockForUpdate()` on the config row, in `patchConfig()` itself, so every writer in the product is covered by one guard rather than by a rule each caller has to remember. A second read-modify-write on the same row -- `update()`'s GH-371 programme clear, which Settings fires *concurrently with* a config patch by design (`Promise.all`) -- gets the same lock; new scenario S10 sends that exact pair and asserts neither side is lost. Five consecutive S8 runs after the fix, all clean on the first read. Also removed: the dead `$siteSync` left in `updateConfig()` after the 410.

**GH-443** Two things on /morning-briefing, a page a client opens. A site card with no analysis behind it showed a **green** dot and a green header — the colour that means "nothing needs attention" — which is what the screen looked like while a red banner above it said the settings could not be read; a card with no data is grey now, and says "No analysis for this site yet." The same card's link read "Open in hub →" and its empty state said "open site in hub to run", pointing a client at `/hub`: the plugin-era interface that is a calculation runner, not a page. The link now opens the site's Dashboard. The literal colours are deliberate: this page also renders on the old layout, where the design-system custom properties are undefined and `var()` would resolve to transparent.

**GH-444** /morning-briefing named a site that does not exist. With a fully configured active site in the database, the page showed "My Site / Species not set" while /field-log, same login, showed the real site and its disease risk — because the card list was built from sample snapshots in `localStorage`, which this page never writes, falling through to a hard-coded placeholder. It reads `GET /api/sites` now, which answers both questions it has (what the sites are called, and what their configs hold), renders after that answer arrives, and says "Your sites could not be loaded" rather than inventing a list when it does not. New live scenario S7 asserts the real site name is on the page and the placeholder is not, on an ordinary load with no stall.

**GH-445** Emoji out of two client-facing pages. `/field-log` labelled its five type tabs, its recent-entry list and its photo button with emoji, and `/morning-briefing` its action rows; the project rule is inline SVG in the style of the neighbouring pages (13-16px, `currentColor`, 2.5 stroke, as `analysis.blade.php` uses) or nothing at all. Both draw SVG now, and the two CSS rules that sized those slots as text are updated with them. New live scenario S11 asserts no emoji remains in the rendered text of either page and that the icons were replaced rather than simply dropped.

**GH-446 (GH-439 stage 4a of 5)** `php artisan sites:repair-config` repairs the rows the old write paths damaged, and prints what it did. It writes exactly two fields, each where the damage has a signature no decision could produce. `config.wizard` is restored where the config has a species and the site has coordinates: a site in that state has been through the wizard by definition, and the record saying so was removed by a background snapshot (scenario H1), not by a person; a site that already has a wizard record in any form, including `skipped`, is left alone, and one missing a species or coordinates is reported with the reason rather than repaired — the wizard should open on those. `sites.timezone` is rewritten only where it is NULL or `Australia/Sydney`, because nothing in the product ever wrote any other value: NULL came from site creation, Sydney from four automatic writers (both wizards, `syncRegistry()`, and the Settings select showing its first option over a NULL). Any other zone could only have been typed by a person and is never touched — a consultant running a New Zealand site on London time is a legitimate choice. Even `Australia/Sydney` survives where it keeps the same clock as the derived zone (Melbourne, Canberra, Hobart run Sydney's time; renaming those would be a change with nothing behind it), which is checked by comparing UTC offsets on 1 January and 1 July through the same `SiteTimezone` helper the server writes with — extracted here from `Controller` so the repair cannot drift from the rule. Names that equal their own site id, sites without coordinates and empty unused sites are reported and never written: the first cannot be restored from anything, and deleting the third is irreversible and the owner's call. Everything runs in one transaction under a row lock; the report prints on every run and `--dry-run` prints the same thing without writing. Run on dev against the pre-work baseline (`archive/GH-439-baseline-dev-2026-09-16-RU.md`): 12 wizard records restored and 6 zones rewritten — `test4 - USA` to `America/Los_Angeles`, `Test6 - UK` to `Europe/London`, `Russley`, `Test - GC - NZ - warm season grass test` and `Test - GC - NZ - delivery` to `Pacific/Auckland`, `New test - location` from NULL to `Australia/Sydney` — exactly the six the baseline names, with the six matching sites untouched, `Test5 - NZ` among them. The baseline's list C is now empty, lists A, B and E are still zero, and a second run reports "Nothing to repair" and changes nothing. Each repaired row carries its own trace: `config.wizard.repaired = 'GH-439e'`, and `sites.attributes_json.gh439_repair.timezone = { from, to, at }`. New `GH439RepairConfigTest` (11).

**GH-447** One writer for the site config column, and a guard that says so. GH-442's race needed a transaction and a row lock in two places, and the second was found only because someone went looking -- so the lock stops being a rule each caller remembers and becomes the only door: `App\Support\SiteConfigWriter::mutate()` takes the row under `lockForUpdate`, hands the stored config to a closure and writes what comes back (returning null leaves the row alone), with `createEmpty()` for the blank row a new site starts with. Six call sites moved onto it: `patchConfig()` (whose merge is now a pure builder that returns what to store), `update()`'s GH-371 programme clear, `updateConfig()` for the stadium namespace, `store()`, the analysis cache, the magic-link and user-invite site creation, and the repair command. New `tests/gh447-one-config-writer.test.js` asserts the property that matters: **nothing but the helper writes the column** -- not "every mutation is locked", which a third hand-written-but-correct writer would satisfy. Shown failing against exactly that: a new controller method with its own transaction, its own `lockForUpdate` and its own `updateOrCreate` is caught on both of its lines. The single exemption (the helper itself) carries its reason in the file, because an exemption with no reason reads later as a place someone forgot.

**GH-448** Three things about the repair from the stage-4a review. `test_a_dry_run_changes_nothing_and_reports_the_same_thing` never checked the second half of its name -- the preview was compared with nothing, and that property is what the decision to run this on production rests on; the transition lines (`site_id | field | was | became`) of a dry run and of the write that follows are now parsed out of both reports and compared, shown failing by making the preview hide one row. The wizard repair's trace was poorer than the time-zone one and left nothing on the site row at all, so on a database where only some sites had a zone rewritten, `sites` was silent about the rest: both repairs now write `attributes_json.gh439_repair.<field> = { from, to, at }` through one helper, and the restored wizard record carries `repairedAt` and `repairedFrom` instead of a `completedAt` set to the repair's own date -- the real completion date is not recoverable, and stamping today's would read six months from now as a fact about the site. (The twelve dev rows repaired before this change keep the older shape: `completedAt` holding the repair date, and no `gh439_repair.wizard` on the row.) Also: the zone comparison looks at January and July of this year **and the next**, since a zone's rules can change between years; and the report-only test asserted three headings that print whether their lists have rows or not -- it asserts the counts now.

**GH-449** The config-column guard had a blind spot in the two forms Eloquent makes most natural. `tests/gh447-one-config-writer.test.js` looked for the query builder and for `->update(['config' => …])`, and matched neither `$row->forceFill(['config' => …])->save()` nor `$row->config = …; $row->save();` — both idiomatic, `forceFill` already in use in the same controller, so a third writer in either shape would have walked past the guard that exists to stop exactly that. Each form is matched on its own now, and each was shown catching a planted example separately (a planted pair also passed the old guard silently first, which is how the gap was confirmed rather than assumed). The report names which rule caught a line, so a future hit says what it is.

**GH-450** A deliberately skipped wizard counted as unanswered on page load. `site-setup-wizard.js` records `wizard.skipped` when the user dismisses it, and the client has always read `complete || skipped` — but only after a save; the flag the server injects read `complete` alone. Nothing surfaced because the localStorage profile gate was suppressing the overlay anyway, and GH-451 removes that gate: a site whose wizard had been skipped on purpose would have been asked again on every clean browser. Both layouts now take the answer from one expression in the `layouts.db-shell` composer (`injectedWizardAnswered`), and the live suite covers the `skipped` shape, which no scenario had touched before.

**GH-451 (GH-439 stage 4b of 5, last in the plan)** The setup wizard decides from the database and from nothing else. Two localStorage checks are gone from `site-setup-wizard.js`: `gilba_wizard_complete`, a per-browser copy of the answer the server already sends, and "any entry in `gilba_turf_profiles`" — a plugin-era heuristic for a returning user, written before the record existed in the database. That second one is what actually ran: the key is written by `turf-profile-controller.js` on any hub-page load and is one key for every site, so a browser that had opened a hub page once suppressed the wizard on every site whatever the database said. The four writes of `gilba_wizard_complete` (two in each wizard) go with it, and the key leaves the storage migration. The TPC profiles themselves are untouched — they stay the legacy controller's storage and merely stop being a gate. Precondition from stage 4a holds on dev: zero sites without a wizard record. **Measured, and it corrects the plan's premise:** the paired live scenario S5b runs the same three cases — no record, `skipped`, `complete` — in an ordinary browser (warmed through `/reports/export`, which writes the profiles; the test asserts they are there, or the half proves nothing) and in a clean context, and the two agree exactly: no record → overlay, skipped → none, complete → none. It runs on `/hub`, not on Reports, because `initWhenReady()` returns early on anything carrying `.db-shell` — this wizard never initialises on a Reports page at all, which is the real reason the stage-2 measurement saw no overlay there, rather than the profile gate. So what stage 4b changes is the behaviour on `/hub`, and only there: four views load `site-setup-wizard.js` (hub, reports/export, reports/forensic, reports/scenarios) and three of them are db-shell pages where it returns on its first line, while `/morning-briefing` and `/stadium` do not load it at all. The db-shell pages have their own wizard, and it already decides from the species the database holds. New `tests/gh451-wizard-gate-is-the-database.test.js` (5). PHPUnit 164, Jest 2604, live 25/25, parity unchanged at 21/22 on the same pre-existing row.

**GH-452** The parity harness's two tissue rows compared the wrong pair, and fixtures now state the scenario they are written for. `tissue N/P/K %` was asserted as `FX.tissuePercent` — a number written into the fixture on the day it was captured — against the export's input, so Plan never entered the comparison and what the row actually checked was "the database still holds the reading it held on 09.09". It went red when the owner moved sample 144 to a different scenario, which is a legitimate thing to do to a test site: the sample has been sufficient, deficient and normal in three weeks. The rows now compare `plan.program.tissue_percent` against `cal.inputs.tissuePercent` and `eng.inputs.tissuePercent`, exactly as the neighbouring soil rows have always compared Plan with the export (`summariseCalendar()` had to start carrying `tissue_percent`, which `computeProgram()` has stamped since GH-425 — that omission is why the rows had nothing from Plan to compare in the first place). Both directions shown: with the export's `_tissuePercentFromData()` shifted by 0.4 the rows go red (`plan 1.05` against `export 1.45`, and the K requirement with it, 84.1 against 106); with the sample moved in the database from 1.05 to 1.2 — a real edit, within the same scenario — the harness stays green, which is the whole point of the change. The precondition checks the database against the **declared state** now, not against a number, and prints what it found: `tissue K 1.05 in the database, declared irrelevant, band {lo 2, hi 3.42, criticalBelow 1.6}`. Fixtures carry a `scenario` block (`state`, `band`/`rule`, `value`, `why`) with `deficient` / `normal` / `sufficient` / `irrelevant`, added to the three that hold tissue inputs; new `tests/fixtures-scenario-consistency.test.js` (5) refuses a value that does not sit where its state says, shown failing on a fixture declaring `deficient` while holding 2.5. `gh361`'s docblock is corrected: 1.05 and 3.05 are two scenarios — the gate lowering K and the gate raising it — not two captures of a similar site. No sample and no fixture number was changed. `npm run test:e2e` is **22/22** for the first time in this work; Jest 2609, PHPUnit 164.

**GH-453** The four soil precondition rows moved to the same scenario form as the tissue ones, and the scenario guard's own blind spot closed. The rows asserted `plan.program.soil.ppm` and the printed ANR row against `FX.soilPpm`, so they carried the defect GH-452 had just removed from the other half of the inputs: they pass or fail on whether anyone has edited the sample since the fixture was captured. Identity is now Plan against the export's own ANR row (tolerance 0.5, because the renderer rounds ppm to a whole number), and the site's state is checked against the **declared scenario**, printing what it found: `soilK 40 ppm on the page, declared deficient, resolved floor 78.2 ceiling 195.5`. Seven more fixtures gained `scenario` blocks for their soil inputs. The guard in `tests/fixtures-scenario-consistency.test.js` only ever iterated fixtures that already carried a `scenario` key, so the one thing it could not catch was a fixture with none — it now walks every fixture, deep-walks for `tissuePercent` and `soilPpm`, and demands either a matching entry or a named exemption with a reason; shown red by deleting `soilK` from `e2e-parity-test5-soccer.json` (`"e2e-parity-test5-soccer.json (/currentInputs/soilPpm)"` reported as undeclared). Both directions shown on the live harness: sample 141 moved in the database from 40 to 44 ppm — a real edit, still below the floor, still `deficient` — and the run stays **22/22**; a value changed on the product path goes red with the numbers on screen (`plan 44, export 51, diff 7` in the ANR row, in the calendar inputs and in the totals). The sample and the file were restored afterwards, both byte-for-byte (payload MD5 `58f79989a84d41776fc241253d3f7cf3`, `updated_at` untouched).

**GH-454** The parity harness selected the export's engine calls by the fixture's numbers. `exportCalendarCall()` and `exportEngineCall()` filtered the captured calls on `num(c.inputs.soilPpm.K) === FX.soilPpm.K`, which is the same "fixture as the expectation" construction GH-452 and GH-453 took out of the comparisons — one level deeper, in the selection that feeds every comparison. Moving the sample in the database, even within the state the fixture declares, made both return null and six tests fail on `not.toBeNull()` with no number on screen to say why. The export run is already narrowed to one ticked sample (`checkedCount === 1`), so the call is now chosen as the last one whose soil reading matches what the **Plan page** resolved — product against product — falling back to the last call of its kind and printing what did not line up: `GH-454: no calendar call carries the Plan page's soil reading (K=44 P=40); the export ran 1 of them: K=51 P=40`. The fallback is deliberate: a divergence between the two surfaces is what this file exists to catch, and it has to arrive as a numeric mismatch in the comparison rows rather than as a null selector that hides which number moved.

**GH-455** The parity harness's Monthly Schedule expectation was written in the wrong unit. It built `g.name + ' @ ' + g.rateKgHa + ' kg/ha'` and searched the export's cell for that literal string, so on a greens site it looked for "83 kg/ha" in a cell reading "8.3 g/m²" and reported the export — `npm run test:e2e:burns` and `:slan` were red on it, `:soccer` (a sports surface, kg/ha) was not. The export is right: a fine-turf rate is grams per square metre whatever the region (GH-406/GH-409), and GH-434 carried this renderer over to the shared rule while the harness kept the pre-GH-409 half. The cell is now parsed into `{ name, rateText, rateKgHa }` entries and compared as a quantity through `rateKgHa()` — the same converter the Annual Product Summary rows already use — at tolerance 1 kg/ha, which is the resolution of one decimal of g/m². Parsing drops the split marker `applicationRate()` appends (` [×2]`), which `num()` would otherwise read into the number: "193 kg/ha [×2]" as 1932. Shown red by shifting the printed rate half a gram per square metre on the product path: `plan 83, export 88, diff 5, printedAs "8.8 g/m²"`, named per month and per product. All three fixtures are **22/22** for the first time. Two review findings closed on the same entry, because separately neither is visible and together they are a wrong number nobody sees. The tolerance was a flat 1 kg/ha borrowed from the rendered-rows check; the rule this file already follows is half of the last printed digit, so a cell printing one decimal of g/m² earns 0.5, whole g/m² would earn 5 and whole kg/ha earns 0.5 — 1 was right only for the documents the three fixtures happen to produce, and on the smallest rate in the set (15 kg/ha) it was 6.7%. The reader stripped a bracketed split marker and scanned whatever was left for digits, so a marker written without brackets ("12.5 g/m² x2") came back as 125.2 kg/ha against a true 125 — a 0.2 difference the flat tolerance absorbed in silence. Both now come from one anchored read of the printed form in `tests/e2e/schedule-cell.js`: the rate, the precision it was printed at, and the tolerance that precision earns; anything that does not match end to end is refused and reported as itself rather than guessed at, including the AU recommender's leading-count wording for liquids ("4x 7 L/ha") and a unit this cell should not carry. Neither rule can be shown on a live run — every rate in the three catalogues prints exactly, so no export this stack produces reaches the rounding boundary the tolerance exists for — so both are exercised directly by `tests/gh455-schedule-cell.test.js` (10), shown red twice: with the flat 1 restored, 83.6 against a printed 83 is called rounding; with the loose reader restored, "12.5 g/m² x2" reads 125.2 instead of refusing. The three fixtures stay 22/22 under the tighter tolerance. Two more review findings on the same entry, both about the tolerance rather than the rate. Half of the last printed digit collapses on a value carrying floating-point noise: applicationRate() writes String(value) with no rounding, so "8.300000000000001 g/m²" read as fifteen decimals and earned 5e-15 — the last bit of a double reported as the two surfaces disagreeing, a false red that reads as a parity defect and sends the next person looking for a fault that is not there. The tolerance is capped at one decimal place deeper than the precision the unit is actually printed to — two for g/m², one for kg/ha, from nutrition-delivery-core.js formatRate() — which is one rule rather than a test on the digits. A threshold on significant digits stood here first, drawn from what a double can carry, and it let through any residue with a short enough written form: "1666.67333332 kg/ha" is twelve significant digits, fewer than a double distinguishes, and collapsed the tolerance to 5e-9 just the same. The cap does not ask. It can miss a difference of half a printed digit where a cell prints finer than its unit's rounding plus one, which nothing in the current catalogues does; the other direction costs more. And numericMismatches() compared with `> tol`, which is false for every pair of numbers when `tol` is undefined — a broken wiring of the per-row tolerance would have returned an empty list and reported that both surfaces agree, on a comparison that never ran. It now refuses a non-numeric tolerance and names the rows. Shown red by removing the cap: "8.300000000000001 g/m²" earns `tolKgHa 5.000000000000001e-15` and "1666.67333332 kg/ha" earns `5e-9`, while every reference case holds across the change (8.3 g/m² 0.5, 12 g/m² 5, 193.6 kg/ha 0.05, 193 kg/ha 0.5); with the wiring broken deliberately, the run fails with `numericMismatches() needs a numeric tolerance, got undefined` naming the row, and the same breakage with the guard taken out passes 22/22 green.

**GH-456** Whether the harness compares tissue rows is decided by the Plan page, not by the fixture. `FX.tissuePercent` was the last live reader of `fixture.currentInputs` — add a tissue reading to a site whose fixture has none and the rows were skipped while the branch below demanded both tissue gates be off, which turns an edit to the data into a red run. The decision now reads `plan.program.tissue_percent` and prints which branch it took (`tissue rows: the Plan page carries a tissue reading (N/P/K), comparing it against the export`). Both directions shown: `tissuePercent` deleted from `e2e-parity-test5-soccer.json` and the run is unchanged at 22/22 on the same branch; `computeProgram()` stopped stamping `tissue_percent` and the branch flips, going red with `planGate true, exportGate true` against the `false, false` that branch asserts. `fixture.currentInputs` now has no reader in the harness at all — the numbers stay in the fixture files, where `tests/fixtures-scenario-consistency.test.js` checks them against the scenario each file declares. Both files were restored afterwards and both matched byte-for-byte (`assets/nutrition-calendar.js` MD5 `13cfc21af07f63ab7429089eadf0a4ba`, the fixture `2ff9110a2a16b6f5404a636216e926f2`).

**GH-457 (Q26 part 0 of 7)** Every Jest test must make at least one assertion. `expect.hasAssertions()` now runs in a `beforeEach` registered globally through `setupFilesAfterEnv` in `jest.config.js`, which closes class A of the Q26 pass — the test that reaches its end having checked nothing — for the whole corpus and for files written later, without reading any of them. Shown failing on a test whose body returns before its only `expect`, and passing on the same body with the return removed. The full run found **eight** such tests, all genuine class A and none of them the setting catching something legitimate: four in `nz-fungicides-registration-auth.test.js` (`if (product) expect(...)` — the product is not in the rotation, so "X is NOT classified as multi-site" proved nothing), two in `gh365-gp-status-unit-explicit.test.js` (`if (!quoted.length) return`, on the two files that have no inline fallback), one in `gh401-delivery-volumes-and-rounding.test.js` (the `burns` parameterisation, whose moves list is empty by design), and one in `ui-vs-export-parity.test.js` on the NZ fixture (`if (!prog.delivered || !footer.delivered) return`, where the "Total Delivered" footer check silently skips; burns and slan reach the assertions). All eight were then rewritten to assert what they had always claimed, each shown failing on its own cause. The four in nz-fungicides read the reason off the entry or off `null` when the product is absent, so the claim "not classified as multi-site" is asserted either way, and the targets loop first asserts that the target list is not empty; shown red by widening isAllMultiSite() and lifting the two-step cap in nz-fungicides.js. The two in gh365 collect the DRIFTED fallback entries and assert that list is empty, which is the same statement for a file with a fallback and for one without; shown red by adding a 65/35 ternary beside a GAIP_GPStatus call in each of the two files. gh401 compares the SET of products whose application count exceeds their month count against the site's declared list, so the site with an empty list says "nothing moved" out loud; shown red by adding one to the accumulator's application count, which makes burns report three products that moved. The parity test now asserts which surfaces publish an annual delivered vector instead of skipping silently, and that is stated from measurement: on the NZ fixture `prog.delivered`, `prog.targets` and `prog.deliversSum` are all null while the Plan page prints a full Total Delivered footer (N 245.5, P 32.2, K 100.1) — the NZ programme (nutrition-nz-fertiliser-integration.js, which overwrites the standalone Prebble one on the shared global) carries neither vector, and delivery is computed at render time from the shared accumulator; on the AU fixture both are present and agree with the footer. NZ delivery is not missing, the vector is. Shown red by making the NZ integration publish one. Four of the eight then had their subject's unreachability ASSERTED rather than noted. Measured across all 18 diseases that have a rotation: Taratek 5F, Clarity and Fostonic appear in none of them, because selection takes one product per FRAC group over four steps and the two multi-site slots are held by Balear 720SC and Supamanz — so the classification could be wrong for those three products and nothing would notice. Each of the three tests now ends with `expect(rot.map(r => r.trade)).not.toContain('<product>')`, which fails the day the product enters that rotation and sends the reader back to the assertion above it, on a product the test can finally see. Pinning the absence is not a claim that the absence is right: whether these products belong in those rotations is a selection question, open with the owner and deliberately not settled here. Shown red on the new line specifically, with selection mutated and classification left alone — lifting the four-step cap puts Taratek 5F and Clarity in the dollar spot rotation, and giving each product its own FRAC group puts Fostonic in the pythium one (`Phosgard, Fostonic, Aliette WG, …`), in each case failing the `not.toContain` line while the reason assertion above it stays green. Fostonic is a pythium candidate all along (`P07`, `targets: ["pythium"]`); Phosgard simply represents P07 first, and Aliette WG is third — the unreachability comes from "one product per FRAC group", not from anything about the product. The fourth test, which sweeps Taratek 5F across its six targets, carries the same line over the whole list (`expect(present).toEqual([])`): it could already fail on its empty-target-list assertion, but its multi-site half was blind over all six diseases, and leaving one of the four half-blind would have rebuilt exactly what this entry removes. Shown red by the same step-cap mutation, which names all six targets at once. Three review findings on top of that. The gh365 scanner was lower-case only and growth-light-analysis.js writes its three fallbacks as `gp >= 70 ? 'High' : gp >= 40 ? 'Moderate' : 'Low'` — the labels it prints — so across four lines naming the module it returned nothing, and all three could be moved to 65/35 with the file's own test green. It looked covered because the lower-case fallback added to it for an earlier red proof WAS seen: that proof measured what the scanner can read, not what the file holds, which is the argument for the reviewer choosing the mutation rather than the author. Matching is now case-insensitive, and — the part that closes the class rather than the case — a file that yields no threshold must be named in `NO_LEVEL_FALLBACK` with a reason: "the scanner found nothing" and "the file has no fallback" are different statements, and reading the first as the second is what hid this. One file is listed: word-export.js, whose fallback decides a docx colour rather than a level string (`gpPct >= 70 ? '16A34A' : …`, word-export.js:6445) and is therefore not checked by this test at all. Both halves shown red: the three capitalised fallbacks moved to 65/35 now fail with all six numbers, and stripping daily-dashboard.js's fallback fails naming the file as unlisted. The three single-product fungicide tests promised "in none of the 18 diseases" in the comment while asserting one rotation, so Clarity entering the fusarium rotation would have dropped nothing; each now asserts both its own rotation and a sweep of every disease that has one, built from the database's target lists. Shown red on the sweep line by widening selection for the other diseases only, which names fusarium, anthracnose and helminthosporium for Taratek 5F and fusarium for Clarity while the line above stays green. For Fostonic the two lines cannot be separated: it targets pythium and nothing else, so its sweep is that same rotation, and it is there for the day that changes. And the caveat that pinning an absence is not a claim that the absence is right — the sentence that stops the next reader "fixing" the absence — is written out in all four tests instead of standing once with three references to it. Then the exemption itself turned out to be the same class a third time: word-export.js stood in `NO_LEVEL_FALLBACK` under the reason "no fallback", and it has one — `gpPct >= 70 ? '16A34A' : gpPct >= 40 ? 'D97706' : 'DC2626'` — which decides a docx colour rather than a level string. The thresholds in it are the module's, and nothing would have caught them moving. An exemption with a false reason is worse than a forgotten file: the file looks unexplained, this looked settled. The scanner reads colour ternaries now, in both spellings the module hands out (`getColorPct` for a page, `getColorDocxPct` for a document), with the colour-to-level map read back from gp-status.js rather than typed into the test, so a colour changed there changes the test with it. Every one of the nine files now yields at least one threshold — dashboard-init.js gains its page-colour pair, word-export.js its two docx colours — and the exemption list is empty, kept only as the place an assertion can point when a file yields nothing. Shown red both ways: the docx thresholds moved to 65/35 fail naming the file, the colours and both numbers (`file word-export.js, colour 16A34A, quoted 65, module 70`), and the same file with its real colours passes, so the form's presence alone does not fail it. One thing named and deliberately not taken: a FOURTH shape the scanner still cannot read — a fallback spread over several lines, where `GAIP_GPStatus.` sits on one line and its thresholds on the next (`growth-light-analysis.js:49-53`, a colour fallback at the module's own 70/40). This reader is line-based, so those thresholds are unchecked. That file yields six thresholds from its other three fallbacks, so it does not fall to the list-with-a-reason rule either; the multi-line shape needs its own decision. The empty list stays, as the place the assertion points when a file yields nothing, and a new rule guards it: an entry whose reason is missing, not a string, or shorter than a sentence fails a test of its own, asserted over the whole list rather than per file so it holds for an entry whose file still yields thresholds. Without it the list refills silently and the story repeats a step lower — first a false reason, then none at all. Shown red with three entries: an empty reason, a one-word one, and a non-string. The constant is renamed `NO_READABLE_FALLBACK`, since "no level fallback" stopped being what it means once colour ternaries were read. Finally the selection question behind the four fungicide tests is closed, not open: one product per FRAC group over four steps is deliberate, because resistance management turns on changing the GROUP rather than the trade name, so a second product from a group already in the rotation adds nothing (owner's decision, 16.09.2026; the rule has stood since the first commit, GH-188/GH-197/GH-200 having changed only classification and sequence checking). The caveat in all four tests now says that, and says what the line is still for — noticing a change in selection — instead of describing an open question. Offering the other candidates in a group is a thing to do on request, when the product on the shelf has run out. Comment text only: no assertion changed, so no red proof was run and none was possible. One more review finding after that, in the scanner again: it checked the THRESHOLD and never the COLOUR. A colour was only ever the signal for whether a ternary was worth reading, so a drifted one matched nothing and was skipped as somebody else's palette — dashboard-init.js's green moved from #16a34a to #22c55e at a correct 70 and all 27 tests stayed green. That is the half of the project rule this test exists for: "never hardcode a separate GP threshold/palette", and the palette half was unguarded. A colour ternary is now recognised if EITHER its colour is one of the module's band colours OR its threshold is one of the module's thresholds, and both are then compared against what gp-status.js returns for that level, in whichever spelling the call site used (`#16a34a` on a page, `16A34A` in a document). Shown red in both spellings with the threshold left correct — `file dashboard-init.js, quoted 70, module 70, quotedColour #22c55e, moduleColour #16a34a`, and the same for word-export.js's docx pair — and green with the real colours in place, so the presence of a colour does not fail a file by itself. The scanner was then rebuilt on structure instead of on values, which closed that gap and a second one with it. The second gap was the line: a fallback written over several lines was invisible even to a SINGLE drift — growth-light-analysis.js:49-53 held at 65 with a canonical colour and all 27 tests stayed green — and that file is also one of the three carrying a hardcoded GP palette, so the place a ticket is being prepared for was guarded in neither direction. And recognising a ternary by "canonical colour OR canonical threshold" reached into other scales: a disease scale at 70 is claimed by the threshold key and then fails on its colour, a DLI scale at #16a34a claimed by the colour key and fails on its threshold — #16a34a being Tailwind's green-600, an ordinary collision. A fallback is now the expression following the module call to the end of its statement — not a window of N lines, which is what dragged the neighbours in — and inside it ternaries are grouped by the variable they compare, so everything in a group is a GP decision by construction and nothing is recognised by its value. The band comes from position in the chain, the answer is compared against all four spellings the module gives (level, label, page colour, docx colour), and threshold drift, palette drift and both at once are equally visible. All fifteen fallbacks across the nine files are read, including the multi-line one that never was. Shown red on a single drift and on a double drift in that multi-line fallback (`line 49, subject pct, quoted 65, module 70, quotedAnswer #22c55e`), and shown green with a disease scale at 70 and a DLI scale at #16a34a planted beside the call — the two shapes that the value-matching rule claimed. The rule it replaced is deleted rather than left beside it. One more pass, and the last on this scanner by decision: the statement was still a position, and four shapes sat outside it — an assignment patched below the call, a fallback computed BEFORE it, one lifted into a helper, one further off than the window was wide — while a foreign scale inside the same statement was claimed, because grouping by variable called every group in the expression a GP decision rather than the one the module was given. What marks a fallback is the VARIABLE, not where it sits: the module is called with one, and the fallback decides the same band for the same value. The window is now the enclosing FUNCTION, and inside it only ternaries comparing the call's own argument — or a variable derived from it, since `gpPct = Math.round(m.gp * 100)` is that same number in the other unit — are read, following a fallback lifted into a named helper into that helper. Each of the four shapes shown red at 65/35, the foreign scale in the same statement shown green, and the fifteen real pairs still read. Two more turned up with them: `baseGpVal` and `todayVal` in growth-light-analysis.js:810,819 are GP fallbacks with no module call beside them, at the canonical 70/40 with the module's own labels — seventeen pairs now guarded where fifteen were. Recorded and not chased, the border being drawn here: an if-chain instead of a ternary (`gpToStressBand()`, growth-light-analysis.js:718-719 and 1311-1312, which compares GP at 70/40 but answers a different question — a stress band labelled Low at high GP — so whether it belongs to this test at all is a domain question); a helper reached other than by a bare name (`this.f(gp)`, `obj.f(gp)`, an arrow const); a subject this reader cannot connect to the argument (an object field assigned elsewhere, a value round-tripped through an array); a module call whose argument is an expression rather than a variable — measured: all fifteen calls in the nine files pass a plain variable; and thresholds held in a named constant — measured: none in these files. The reason for stopping: the scanner reads every fallback the code actually has and catches every real drift, and the shapes now being found are ones no file uses. One living instance out of that record was then taken, the border being about shapes no file uses rather than about a real one: growth-light-analysis.js:925, `normalVal` — the month's climate-normal GP, at the canonical 70/40 with the module's own labels, three lines under a comment saying it mirrors the guarded reading beside it. Moving its sibling failed a test, moving this one left 27 of 27 green: the file read as covered in four places and was blind in the fifth, which is worse than not being checked at all. Reaching it needed one step BACKWARDS from the argument — `gp = growth.weighted` and `normalVal` out of `monthlyNormal.c3` are two readings of the same quantity — and the step had to be narrow, because the first two attempts at it were the same false-positive class again: admitting the OBJECT pulled in everything else on it (dashboard-init.js reaches GP through `m`, which also carries the stress index and the forecast peak), and collecting field names off built-ins made `Math.round(...)` contribute `round`, so every rounded number in a function became the same quantity. So: the connection is the FIELD the argument was read from, off a real object rather than a built-in, and a DIFFERENCE of two readings is not a reading (`delta = Math.round(forecastAvg - todayGP)` carries the same unit and answers a different question, and its own 15-point scale was arriving as a GP band), while a scale change by a literal stays in, since `gpPct = Math.round(m.gp * 100)` is the same number in the other unit. Shown red on the drifted `normalVal` (`line 925, subject normalVal, quoted 65, module 70`) and green on the correct one. Eighteen pairs guarded now, from fifteen when this entry began. Two corrections to the plan, both measured: the config key is `setupFilesAfterEnv` (`setupFilesAfterEach`, which the plan names, is not a Jest option), and `expect.assertions(0)` does NOT satisfy `expect.hasAssertions()` — it fails with the same message — so the plan's proposed opt-out for a deliberate probe test does not work and needs a different answer. PHPUnit needs nothing: `beStrictAboutTestsThatDoNotTestAnything` defaults to true in PHPUnit 12 and the 164-test run flags no test as risky, though risky is not failing there unless `failOnRisky` is set.

**GH-458** The growth-potential palette is gp-status.js's and nobody else's. Three call sites kept their own copy of it beside the module call — the dashboard's GP bar (`dashboard-init.js:388`), the Word document's GP cell (`word-export.js:6445`) and the growth-light page's `gpColor()` (`growth-light-analysis.js:48-53`, written over several lines, which is why no check saw it until GH-457's reader was rebuilt). All three agreed with the module's numbers, and that is the point: this is not a defect on screen today, it is the same rule written down three times in places nothing keeps in step. When one copy moves, two scales on one page start contradicting each other in front of a client, and the page that generated a Word document stops agreeing with it. Each site now calls the module, and a missing module is reported rather than papered over: the GP bar keeps its own styling and logs, the document falls back to the muted grey it already uses for "no reading", and `gpColor()` returns the page's own no-reading grey — none of which is a GP band. The module already answered for a missing reading (`getColorPct(null)` returns its unknown colour), so that branch was a second copy too. Shown red per file and on both halves before the fix — threshold moved to 65/35 and colour moved to #22c55e at a correct threshold, each failing with the file named — and after it neither drift is expressible, because no site holds a threshold or a colour any more. `word-export.js` is now the first honest entry in the scanner's exemption list: it has no GP fallback at all. Seen on screen, not only in tests: the dashboard bar at 34% paints rgb(220,38,38) where the module says #dc2626, and the growth-light figures at 34% and 44% paint #dc2626 and #d97706 to match; the generated document still carries 31 green, 7 amber and 11 red GP cells in the module's own docx spelling. New `tests/e2e/gh458-gp-palette-live.test.js` (2) reads those colours off the rendered elements and compares them with what the module answers for the number beside them — `npm run test:e2e:palette`, and one of the 25 files `npm run test:e2e:all` runs, so it is not a suite only its author knows how to start. Separately, the GH-457 scanner was described more strictly than it behaved — the comment said the connection is by FIELD while a connection by OBJECT was still live, because `growth.anything` counted as a mention of `growth`; a band built on a field name that appears nowhere in the codebase was claimed as growth potential. Reading a field off a variable is not reading that variable, and it no longer counts.

**GH-459** A report is computed for the site of the sample it prints. The owner exported Test5 and got another site's climate: the monthly GP curve was the right curve on Christchurch temperatures, and everything downstream followed it — the nitrogen spread across the months, the products chosen for it, the delivery and balance. Only the Required column held: it is normalised to the target, so the annual figure the report asks for stayed 250 on both surfaces. Everything else moved. Measured on the owner's own scenario, screen against document: six products on the screen and three in the document, one name in common and that one with different figures (Pro Balance 1 x 60 L/ha against 3 x 210 L/ha), a product printing 450 kg/ha in the document that is not on the screen at all; delivered N 245.5 against 156.6, P 32.2 against 0.0; balance N -4.5 "On Track" against -93.4. An earlier version of this entry claimed the annual totals reconciled and the document therefore looked correct -- that was wrong, and it was wrong because the annual sums were checked on a run WITHOUT the leak and the conclusion carried over to a run WITH it, unmeasured. The owner said so before we measured it. `_buildEngineInputs()` took the coordinates from the `.gaip-lat` / `.gaip-lon` fields on the page (word-export.js:7234) and asked the climate service for normals at whatever they held. The combined export switches sites in a loop and calls that function once per sample, with a 300 ms pause between the switch and the read, against a repaint measured at 327 ms — the field is a race, and it belongs to whichever site the page last painted. The coordinates were one of three: a run on the same tree printed the previous site's SPECIES with correct coordinates, the mirror of the owner's case, and the overseed state is the third — a page-level global with no site stamp at all. All three now come from the sample's own site, resolved by id through the adapter's `getSiteConfig()`, which is the same per-site source the combined export's climate pre-pass already warms the cache from; the page-state fallbacks behind them (`GAIP_STATE.site`, `GAIP_STATE.location`, `GAIP_CANONICAL_STATE.turf`, the `.gaip-species` probe) are gone rather than demoted, since each is another site's answer wearing this one's name, and a site whose own config has no species keeps this file's existing hard-fail — a missing section, not a silent substitution. The scenario was run end to end on the stand: with a Christchurch site active, exporting one Test5 sample prints GP `100 100 99 86 63 41 29 33 44 58 77 95`, which is Test5's own. Not shown red on this machine — the race was won on every attempt here, including with the coordinate repaint deliberately delayed, so the mechanism rests on the code and on the reviewer's two reproductions rather than on a failure of mine; what is shown red is the structural guard (`tests/hoxton-combined-export-per-site-climate.test.js`, which itself pinned `.gaip-lat` and so guarded the defect: it now refuses any page-state read in that function and fails on the pre-fix file). New `tests/e2e/gh459-cross-site-inputs-live.test.js` (`npm run test:e2e:crosssite`) is that scenario. And the parity harness now compares the MONTHLY SERIES — GP, the temperature behind it and the nitrogen spread along it, month by month at 0.05 — which `summariseCalendar()` never carried: a whole year of another site's climate passed all 22 checks, which is why this arrived from a delivered report instead of from a run. Three fixtures at 23/23.

**GH-461 (PLAN-GH439 section 10, layer I — PART DONE, see the end of this entry for where to pick it up)** The export's site inputs are resolved by id, through one border. `resolveExportInputs({ siteId, soilSampleId, tissueSampleId, waterSampleId })` in nutrition-program-inputs.js returns a frozen object — site (id, name, location, timezone, areaHa), turf (type, subCategory, species, speciesKey, speciesDisplay, variety, construction, hoc, percentC3, warmBase, coolOverseed, overseedSpecies, overseedVariety, summerIntent, isC4 derived), program, samples by id, climate normals for those coordinates, and `sources` naming where each field came from. Absent is `null` with `'unresolved'`: there are no default species names in it, because a name printed by default and a name that leaked print identically, and this file produced both on the same page. `collectData(inputs)` builds the document's turf identity from it in one block and no longer reads `GAIP_STATE.inputs.turf` (measured on the reviewer's tape: cleared at 1,346 ms, refilled with the PREVIOUS site's values at 2,323 ms with the new site already active), the five-step turf-type chain (GaipTurfProfile.state, three DOM buttons, a legacy select — whose own comment said the controller state is "cleared during site-switch"), the overseed toggle and `GAIP_STATE.turf.overseedActive`, or the `.gaip-species` fallback; called with no argument it resolves the same object itself, so the single export and the combined one cross one border rather than two. `_buildEngineInputs()` now takes the same object instead of its own GH-459 read. The `'Couch'` default for the warm-season base is gone. New `tests/gh461-export-reads-by-id.test.js` (8): no page-state read in those functions except entries named in `EXEMPT` with a reason saying what lands there during a leak, a stale exemption fails, and the turf identity field list must come from the resolver — plus, added after this guard failed to catch its own mutation, the BINDING of the identity source is asserted, since repointing `_inTurf` at `GAIP_STATE` had left all seven earlier tests green while restoring the exact leak. Shown red by that mutation. One thing reverted rather than kept: deriving `isC4` from the species inside `computeProgram()` — section 10.3 declined a separate fix for that input, and the change moved westview's real numbers (gh403) besides pinning gh408; nutrition-calendar.js is back byte-for-byte at `13cfc21af07f63ab7429089eadf0a4ba`. **Still to do in layer I, in the order of section 10.5:** site name and location (`gaip-location-search`/`gaip-location-status`), zone area (`.gaip-soil-area-ha` — waits on question 2 of 10.8, resolver returns null today), variety and overseed variety (`GAIP_CLIMATE_V2_RESULT`, DOM selects), AA sample type and texture, the DOM ppm fallbacks for soil/tissue/water and the sample labels, construction at the Cross-Module block, and `word-export-combined.js:~2260` ("config OR page snapshot" → resolver). Each is listed in `EXEMPT` with what leaks there. Layer III (step B) is not started. Six printed default names remain (`'Perennial Ryegrass'` at 8211/8248/8255/9090, `'Couch'` at 9003/9656) — that is question 4 of 10.8 and is the owner's to answer.

**GH-462 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.10)** The export has a smoke test in the ordinary `npx jest` run. It exists because of one measurement: 2,639 green tests while the export was dead — a layer I change left a reference to a variable it had itself removed, `collectData()` threw `_collectSiteCfg is not defined`, and no document was produced at all. Nothing in the normal run executed the export end to end; the only full run was the parity harness's download, which is skipped without the stand, so the suite everyone watches could not see it. `tests/word-export-smoke.test.js` loads the page's own modules — the list read from `reports/export.blade.php` rather than copied, so a module added to the page and not here fails the test — then runs the real `GAIP_WordExport.export()` and asserts the cheapest things that are not nothing: a blob was produced and the link clicked, it is non-empty, it opens as a zip holding a non-empty `word/document.xml`, that document names the site and the species (the value that travels the whole layer I path, so its presence says the path ran), and nothing wrote to `console.error` or alerted. Getting there measured four things about the sandbox rather than assuming them: the libraries capture a timer at load and need a live one, the page modules reschedule themselves and need an inert one, JSZip's pipeline needs `setImmediate` and a `FileReader` (without it the export still writes a file but logs "Can't read the data of 'the loaded zip file'" from its own image-renumbering pass), and the export's error handler calls `alert()`, which without a stub buries the error that got there. Shown red on this morning's defect exactly — a reference to a removed variable fails with `ReferenceError: _collectSiteCfg is not defined` in the output — and on `buildSections()` returning `[]`, which fails only the "names the site" assertion. Blind spots named: a sandbox is not a browser, so chart capture, layout and the real Blob/URL are not exercised; the parity harness's download stays the browser-side smoke test. The loader is shared with the provenance guard through `tests/helpers/export-page-sandbox.js`.

**GH-463 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6 §2)** Where every identity value in a document comes from, read out of the code. The dynamic guard beside it poisons the page and checks that no sentinel reaches `data`, which is stronger but sees only the fields its one run fills: 25 fields are assigned into `data.turf`, 9 were compared, and among the 16 nobody checked were `isC4`, `effectiveIsC4` and `useC3Targets` — the three that choose the growth curve, which is the input the owner's report turned on. `tests/gh461-export-identity-dataflow.test.js` parses word-export.js and word-export-combined.js and, for every assignment into `data.site`/`data.turf`/`data.program` and every object property named after an identity field, walks the right-hand side back to its roots — following locals to their initialisers and helpers into their returns. Allowed roots are the resolver's `inputs`, literals and a named list of pure derivations; a call that answers by id (`getSiteConfig`, `getConfig`, `resolveExportInputs`) is allowed only when its id argument itself roots in `inputs`, because "reads by id" is not the guarantee — "reads by THIS sample's site id" is. Roots it cannot follow are listed separately rather than passed over, so the difference between checked and not checked stays visible. It sees code outside `collectData()`, which the function-body guards could not: the Cross-Module block builds `construction` from `GAIP_STATE.turf` around line 10769. Shown red on the reviewer's two mutations — `isC4` read from `GAIP_CANONICAL_STATE.turf.isC4`, and `subCategory` read through `getSiteConfig(activePageSiteId)`, by-id in form and another site in substance — and on a third: the read moved into a helper one line above the function. That third one passed silently at first, because the exemptions were keyed by file and field and the new leak of `species` was absorbed by the exemption for a different `species` read in the phytotoxicity block. Exemptions are now anchored to a fragment of their own line: one exemption covers one read, and the same field leaking from somewhere else is a failure. Ten reads are exempted with what lands in each during a leak, which is the remaining inventory of section 10.5 measured rather than copied.

**GH-464 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, as amended through the night)** Three things, all measured rather than declared. The overseed variety and its printed label come from the site by id: the resolver derives the label as a lookup in the variety table, falling back to the key when the table has no name for it (question 9 of 10.8), and the export's two reads — `GAIP_CLIMATE_V2_RESULT.overseedVariety` and a DOM select — are gone. They stood behind `if (!data.turf.overseedVariety || === 'generic')`, the "fill in what is missing" shape that is false exactly during a leak. Removing them made three exemptions in the dataflow guard stale, and the guard said so, which is the ratchet working as intended. `tests/gh461-export-turf-keys.test.js` (6) then takes EVERY key `data.turf` ends up with — 23 of them — and demands each is either equal to the resolver's field of that name or named in a list of derivations, each written as a function taking ONLY the resolver's object; a key in neither fails, so the list is complete rather than merely long. Two derivations are marked dead and their deadness is asserted as a fact of the run — `data.turf.c3Fraction` is undefined after collectData, and nothing in the codebase assigns it — so `overseedDominant` and `useC3Targets` stay reproduced rather than repaired while question 8 of 10.8 is open, and the day anything fills that field the test fails and the branch gets rewritten deliberately. Four values reproduce hardcoded defaults the export prints today and say in the list that they wait on question 7. The dataflow guard was widened with the same night's amendments: its scope is the whole `data` object rather than three containers; purity is a property of a body, not a name, so the list of "pure" function names is gone — six of the fifteen it held named functions that do not exist in the code at all, each an unchecked pass waiting to be claimed — and calls are unfolded by their bodies, across files; the file list is DERIVED by scanning every asset for identity writes and asserted equal to what is judged, so a third writer fails by appearing; result containers (view II) are blanketed per container with a reason each, and a blanket whose container stops reading the page must be removed. `GAIP_Sensor` joined the page-state roots because the guard's own untraceable list named it. The limit of the static half is written into it with the example that exists: export-metadata.js wraps collectData and holds the document object today, correctly invisible because it writes no identity — and the day such a wrapper builds its own document instead of adding to this one, only the sentinel run will see it. The two halves are not alternatives.


**GH-465 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, the second refinement of 17.09.2026)** What a document says about a site with no species is now pinned by a run rather than by a note. The reviewer measured what the note was worth: all seven occurrences of 'Perennial Ryegrass' in word-export.js replaced with 'Kikuyu', 6 of 6 key assertions green and 9 of 9 dataflow assertions green — a value the client reads changing with nothing to say so. The cause was that the guard's one run had a full site, so no branch printing a default was reached, and the defaults were checked for carrying a marker instead of for their value. `tests/gh461-export-turf-keys.test.js` now also calls `collectData()` with the resolver's shape and nothing resolved — species, variety, overseed variety and overseed name all empty — walks every leaf of the whole `data` object, and demands each non-empty one is either a documented default with its exact value or named as not being about the site's identity, with a reason. Ten defaults are pinned by value: 'Not specified' for the site name, its location, the effective species and the species line; 'generic' for the variety; 'cool-season grass' and `isC3Species = true` for the soil narrative, which also chooses the tissue table; 'turf' for what the tissue ranges say they are for; and the two the variety-traits table is looked up by. What they SHOULD be is question 7 of section 10.8 and stays the owner's. Shown red on three mutations: a literal replaced, a default introduced through a variable higher in the file, and a key that is not in the documented list. The seven literals themselves are answered by value rather than by argument: every one of them stands on the right of an `||` whose left side cannot be empty when the branch runs — six sit behind `overseedDominant`/`useC3Targets`, which read a `c3Fraction` nothing assigns, and the seventh's own guard requires the name it would supply. So no run can tell them from 'Kikuyu', and the two run-facts that make that true are asserted across five input shapes instead of being reasoned about: the printed overseed name and warm-season base are the site's own or absent, and `c3Fraction` stays unassigned even with an oversown sward carrying 40% C3. Shown red on a mutation that makes the substitute reachable, and on one that fills `c3Fraction` from `percentC3` — the connection between those two is question 8 of 10.8 and is asserted absent rather than assumed. One border closed on the way: `_buildEngineInputs()` called `resolveExportInputs({})` a second time instead of taking the object `collectData(inputs)` was given, so it answered for whichever site the PAGE was on. Both callers pass no argument today, so the two answers agree and no client number moves — but it made the border two places wide where its own comment says one, and it is why the empty-inputs run first produced a full 180 kg/ha/yr Perennial Ryegrass programme for a site the resolver said has no species at all. With the object threaded through, that run produces `engineInputs: null` and no nutrition section, which is the hard-fail b35fix313/b35fix314 put there and GH-459 gave the whole weight to. Two text guards anchored on the old signature (`gh383-input-contract-guard`, `hoxton-combined-export-per-site-climate`) had their anchor loosened to the function name.

**GH-466 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, third and fourth refinements)** The identity dataflow guard: exemptions are anchored by position (file, function, left-hand side, whole right-hand side) instead of by a fragment of the line; a cross-module call is judged by the called method's own body rather than by its module; and the ratchet pins five surfaces as recorded values, so narrowing one fails like widening it. The mechanism and the measurements behind it are in section 10.6 of PLAN-GH439-site-config-db-only-RU.md. Also repaired `tests/gh299-aa-ceiling-consumers.test.js`, whose anchor carried the old `_buildEngineInputs(data)` signature and had been asserting against a one-character string.

**GH-467 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, fifth and sixth refinements)** The fallback that let `_buildEngineInputs()` resolve by the page's site is gone, a call without inputs refuses, and `collectData()` warns when a site's config resolved nothing. The empty-inputs run now treats only null and undefined as empty, runs on a poisoned page and compares each table whole; the dataflow guard gained module state by property write, a marker for exhausted depth, roots as a fifth exemption coordinate, and method-before-module resolution. **GH-471 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, tenth and eleventh refinements)** A field's source is worked out from the read instead of being written beside it: `take(field, value, 'site-config')` is gone, each read goes through a path in `FIELD_PATHS`, and the reader refuses a field the table assigns to another store — which is what let `locationName` read a key no site config has while the provenance map called it a documented field, so a client's report printed coordinates instead of the place. The place now comes from `location.name`, and by the owner's decision (question 10.8(10), closed) a site with no name prints an empty Location line rather than a substitute. The sandbox's store stubs are built from `tests/fixtures/store-shapes.json`, recorded from a live page with key sets compared both ways and a live drift guard (`npm run test:e2e:shapes`), and the pliant reads that hid the drift — `row.name || row.label`, `values || payload || sample` — are gone. Mechanism and measurements: section 10.6 of PLAN-GH439-site-config-db-only-RU.md.

**GH-472** `sites.location_name` and `config.location.name` are one fact, so emptying the name in the config empties the column in the same write: the copy into the column sat behind `isset()`, which is right for "this write does not mention the name" and wrong for "this write removes it", and a PATCH empties a field through `clear`, which never reached the column at all — so the config could be emptied while the column kept its value and nothing said the two disagreed. Cleared rather than refused because the owner settled (question 10.8(10)) that a site with no name for its place prints an empty Location line, so an empty name is a legal state. `sites:repair-config` gained a report-only line naming sites where the column is filled and the config's name is empty; it repairs nothing, because the column is a copy that stopped being updated and writing it back would put a stale mirror into the source of truth.

**GH-473 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, twelfth refinement)** Every fact about a site has one owner and the resolver reads the owner: name, place, coordinates and time zone come from the `sites` row — reached by all three write paths, where the copy in `config.location` is reached by one, so a site created through `store()` has the column filled and the config empty by construction — and `FIELD_PATHS` carries no path into `config.location` at all, which a guard pins for the three files that build a document. `GAIP_SiteConfig` keeps the site row from `GET /api/sites` and answers `getSite(id)`; the `notInStore` mark is off `timezone` (twelve of twelve rows have one, zero of twelve configs do) and the two that keep it are checked against every recorded store rather than one. Read operations take an identifier, choose the record themselves and record which record they read, compared against the site and sample ids asked for; the store fixture now also carries the shapes of the method ANSWERS (`getSiteList`, `getAllSamples`, `getAllConfigs`, `getConfig`, `getSite`, `getActiveSample`) and the sandbox builds its stubs from them. Mechanism and measurements: section 10.6 of PLAN-GH439-site-config-db-only-RU.md.

**GH-474 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, thirteenth refinement as amended)** Ownership is declared per FIELD in one table (`App\Support\FieldOwners`, exported to `tests/fixtures/field-owners.json` and compared with the resolver's read paths in both directions): `location.name/lat/lon` and `timezone` belong to the `sites` columns, `location.elevation` to the config because no column exists for it — the other half of the rule, not an exception, and the reason the section-wide version with a 422 was dropped. Every write route splits a patch by that table, no input is refused and no sender changed; the derived copy in `config.location` is rewritten from the owning columns in one place after each write, at site creation too, and the repair command fixes drifted copies instead of reporting them. The three regional integrations, the spray log and the site dashboard read the owner through `getSite(id)`, and a guard holds the number of assets reading the copy at zero. Also: a sample's provenance records WHICH sample, checked against a basket holding more than one with the expected id stated independently (the previous check compared the key with the sample the resolver itself had chosen, out of a basket of one, and the tissue and water branches had never run); `notInStore` resolves a full path in the declared owner's shape; and the method enumeration is measured by wrapping the stores during a real export. Mechanism and measurements: section 10.6 of PLAN-GH439-site-config-db-only-RU.md.

**GH-475** The sentinel half of the poisoning guard had been asserting nothing: a poisoned value is a Proxy over a FUNCTION (a String wrapper's indexed properties are non-configurable and a proxy over one throws before the value reaches the document), so `typeof` said 'function' and the walker returned at the first poisoned value it met. It now reads a function's string form, and an inverted boolean the same way it already read a shifted number. Beside every assertion of absence there is now a positive control in the same file — a planted sentinel must be named in `data` and found in `word/document.xml` — and the whole-document check the third refinement specified and nobody wrote is in place, with the roots still able to reach a finished document named one by one (all of them view II results or section 10.5's remaining DOM reads) and a sentinel from anywhere else failing. The registry was re-run: repointing the turf identity at the page and copying a page object by enumeration are now caught by the sentinel itself rather than only by the key comparison; a read moved into a helper above collectData and a config read swapped for a page read stay red on the dataflow guard and the value comparisons — basis replaced, verdict the same. Also removed a dead `const loc` in the resolver, the last thing in that file that looked like a read of the config copy.

**GH-476 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, fourteenth refinement)** The region a client's product catalogue comes from is the site's own, derived by id from the coordinates the `sites` row owns — the owner's answer to question 10.8(11). `detectRegionFromHub()` is deleted rather than demoted: it read `.gaip-lat`/`.gaip-lon`, form fields in the hidden /hub runner holding whatever it last restored, and it was the first link of every region question in the product, so a site moved from Sydney to Auckland kept Australian products while its row, its config copy and the server's own injection all said Auckland.
