Ten files in the chain were converted and a guard holds their DOM coordinate reads at a recorded count, one of which is named as belonging to the seasonal question rather than the region one. Live scenario S9 moved from `PINNED, not approved` to an assertion: after a move to New Zealand the catalogue is New Zealand's while `.gaip-lat` still holds the previous site's number, which is what says the field is no longer the answer.


**GH-477 (PLAN-GH439 section 10.6, fifteenth refinement)** A reader of the config copy is now found by where its value came from rather than by the shape of the call standing beside it, which is how the site card on `/morning-briefing` was caught reading `config.location` out of a function parameter; four such readers were moved to the owning `sites` row through `getSite(id)`, with the import bundle's own location named as the single exemption. **GH-518** The GH-505 live guard no longer writes to the stand: its positive control generates a programme, which persists itself as six config PATCHes per run, and those are now caught in the browser by method and path while the rest of the page's traffic goes to the server untouched. The test also clears the annual-N field itself instead of requiring it to arrive empty — the programme it used to leave behind prefilled that field and destroyed its own precondition.

**GH-519** A run of the whole live suite no longer changes the state of existing sites. Eighteen live tests wrote to client data on the stand as a side effect of proving something else: they filled an empty Annual N field on whatever site they landed on, saved a whole site config to make a page recompute, or switched the active site and left it switched. Measured before the fix with a full stand snapshot (`scratchpad/stand/snapshot.sh`, eight site-bearing tables, per-row md5, each section checked against its own `COUNT(*)`) taken before and after a suite run. Three remedies, chosen per test: the GH-439 pattern, where a test creates and removes its own site; a narrow interception of the one write a test does not need; and capture-and-restore for the writes it does. The restore is SQL and puts back the bytes AND the `updated_at` (`CONVERT(FROM_BASE64(...) USING utf8mb4)`), verified against the database's own md5 — a restore that rewrites the timestamp is a restore that leaves a trace. New `tests/e2e/lib/stand-guard.js` carries `guardStand()`, `SITE_STATE_WRITES`, `fillOwnAnnualN()` (fills only an EMPTY field, and throws naming the site if neither the field nor `turf.nProgram` has a value, rather than inventing one) and `captureConfigsOnce()`/`restoreConfigs()`. **Measured after: 0 differing lines across 30+ runs.** Two defects found by the work itself and worth keeping: the first snapshot silently reported an empty `predictions` section because the query named `site_id` on a table whose column is `site_identifier` and `2>/dev/null` hid the error — the script is `set -e` and fails loudly now; and the first capture was taken one line too late, because opening the Plan page already writes, so the restore honestly returned what it had captured and reported success while the row differed. `tests/e2e/gh394-traffic-live.test.js` still calls the `PUT .../config/{id}` route, which the product retired (410) on purpose; it is named here rather than fixed, and it cannot report green silently because its helper throws on `!r.ok` inside `beforeAll`.


**GH-520 (PLAN-methodology-single-owner-RU, delivery A — server and data)** The soil-test methodology has one owner on the server: `config.turf.methodology`. It had four. `Controller::effectiveMethodology()` forced ammonium acetate for New Zealand coordinates; the same function then fell back to the literal `'mlsn'`; `sites.methodology_override` was read as a second store; and sample creation stamped whichever of those answered first. The consequence is the one the CLAUDE.md rule already names: a page printed a methodology the site had not chosen, and a sample was stamped with it. **Measured on the stand: the column is null on every live site and nothing writes it, while seven sites' stamps disagreed with their setting.** `effectiveMethodology(?string $saved): ?string` now returns the saved value or null — the coordinates are gone from its signature, so a caller cannot pass them by habit — and the NZ branch, the `?: 'mlsn'` tail and the `methodology_override` reads go with it, across `DashboardController`, `ReportsController`, `DataController`, `AnalysisController` (three sites, plus an NZ cache overwrite), `SettingsController`, `SampleAnalysisController` (which now reads the config rather than the cache) and `SampleController` (new `siteConfigMethodology()`; the stamp is taken from the config at creation). A site that has chosen nothing now prints "Methodology: not set" on Settings, growth-light, disease and the four report pages, instead of MLSN's name over MLSN's numbers. New `tests/gh520-methodology-has-one-owner.test.js` (9 tests); `tests/gh395-nz-methodology-gate.test.js` rewritten to the behaviour that replaced the rule it pinned.

**GH-521 (PLAN-methodology-single-owner-RU, delivery B — client)** The client reads the methodology from the site's own record, by the site's id, and offers Ammonium Acetate alone on a New Zealand site without rewriting what is stored. Six client reads answered for something other than the site being asked about, and each was a page-state read of exactly the shape GH-459 was: the hub store seeded `inputs.soil.methodology = 'mlsn'` before anything loaded (both copies, `gilba-hub-v2.js:387` and `:668`, now `null`); `nutrition-calendar.js` treated a bare `'mlsn'` as that seed rather than as an answer, and `resolveSiteMethodology()` folded an empty or MLSN setting to AA on New Zealand coordinates; `nutrition-program-inputs.js` took `sample.methodology || turf.methodology || GAIP_HUB_CONFIG.turfMethodology || 'mlsn'`, where the first link is the caller's own object and the third is whichever site the PAGE is standing on; `nutrition-prebble-integration.js` `getMethodology()` read that same page global and folded everything except SLAN to AA, so an NZ site saved as MLSN had its product selection scored against AA while the requirement engine branched on MLSN thresholds — the divergence `tests/gh393-prebble-methodology-source-divergence.test.js` was written to pin, now closed on both surfaces; and `hub-persistence.js`'s sample fallback read `.gaip-soil-methodology` off the page. That last read now goes to `GAIP_SiteConfig.getConfig()`, keyed by the same `GAIP_HUB_CONFIG.activeSiteId` the sample on that path was picked by — the first draft resolved the id from `GAIP_SiteContext`/`getActiveSiteId()` instead, which the comment three lines above it says can have been switched to `'default'`, so the methodology could have answered for a different site than the sample. On the NZ surfaces the list is Ammonium Acetate alone (the owner's decision; SLAN's carve-out was justified by the fold that is now gone) and a saved value the region does not offer is NAMED rather than swapped or rewritten: Settings shows the stored value with a note saying the site still computes on it, and both wizards CLEAR a disallowed preset instead of writing AA in the user's place. **Measured price, corrected against the first draft of this entry, which had it wrong: NO site reads as "not set", because no site on the stand has an empty methodology — all twelve carry one, and `sites.methodology_override` is null on every one of them, so delivery A's removal of that column read and of the `?: 'mlsn'` tail changes nothing for them. Settings and the wizards touch no site either (all four NZ sites are already AA). What the five stored-`mlsn` sites — Burns, Canberra, Test1 - Sports, Test6 - UK, Westview — gain is the opposite of a loss: their stored MLSN used to be indistinguishable from the store's seed and was reported as unresolved, and it is now read as the answer it is. Measured on the real stack, four readings per site, by `tests/e2e/gh521-methodology-per-layer-live.test.js`: the server page prints MLSN and no "Methodology: not set" pill anywhere; `collectFromState()` returns `mlsn` with `_methodologyDefaulted === false`; `resolveExportInputs()` returns `mlsn` sourced `site-config`; and `getMethodology()` returns `mlsn`. Test5 - NZ answers `ammonium_acetate` on all four.** And through the document: `tests/e2e/gh521-burns-document-live.test.js` builds a real .docx by the product's own "export current site" action on Burns (15 samples, 4.78 MB) and reads the methodology back out of `word/document.xml` rather than out of the objects that fed it — **"Annual Nutrient Requirements — MLSN methodology (Woods et al. 2016)", twice, with no "Methodology: not set" and no competing methodology claim; the single "Ammonium Acetate" in the file is the glossary's definition of the extraction.** Delivery A had put SLAN through this path (Federal Golf); 'mlsn' had never travelled it. Said plainly because the test says it too: this document proves the value ARRIVES and that the figures under it are MLSN's, and it cannot show which SOURCE won — Burns's config and all of its samples' stamps read 'mlsn', so the chain this delivery removed would have reached the same answer by any link, and no site on this stand has a config and a stamp that disagree and a sample to export. Nor can it show the 21/30 P threshold, which lives in the Prebble context and runs only for New Zealand sites. Five defects the work found in itself, two of them in this entry's own first draft: the wizards' note said "MLSN is not offered" whatever had been cleared, so a user who had chosen SLAN was told about MLSN (`_mlsnNormalisedForNZ` is now `_methodClearedForNZ` and holds the value); the calendar's DOM and hub-config fallbacks sat inside the `methodology === 'mlsn'` branch as its else-arm, correct while `'mlsn'` meant "not loaded" and a substitution once it meant MLSN, so they now fire on an unresolved methodology and nothing else; `isNZCoordinates()` was left with no caller once the fold went, which is a bounding box one line away from putting the fold back, so it is removed along with the coordinate plumbing that fed it in `site-config-persistence.js` (verified: zero declarations, zero callers, only a comment and a test asserting its absence remain); the bowls/cotula fold was widened to fire on an UNSET methodology as well as on `'mlsn'`, to preserve the answer an unset site used to get — which preserved the seed's behaviour under a new name, and is a substitution whatever justifies it. Narrowing it back was the first correction and it was not enough: the owner settled the general question on 18.09.2026, and **the rule is that coordinates determine exactly one thing — which options the Settings list offers, where a New Zealand site is offered ammonium acetate alone. Nothing else determines the methodology: not in the calculations, not on the pages, not in the document, not in the stamp, and neither the surface nor the sample nor a field on the page affects it.** So the fold is removed rather than narrowed, in all three places it stood: `nutrition-calendar.js` (read `GaipTurfProfile.state.turfType`, `GAIP_STATE.turf.turfType` and `GAIP_STATE.turf.cotula`); `prebbles-products.js` `generateProgram()` (`_isCotula`, from `context.surfaceType` and two turf-profile globals — and its `|| 'mlsn'` tail with it, which mattered more than it looks, because the stamp it wrote is what the staleness check compares a restored programme against later); and `cotula-bowling-green.js` `handleBowlsSelection()`, which wrote `ammonium_acetate` straight into the `.gaip-soil-methodology` select and dispatched a change — a surface answering the methodology question on the user's behalf, and one that reached the calculation, since the calendar still reads that select when a site's own setting is empty. What is NOT removed, because it is the setting answering for itself rather than the surface answering for it, is the mapping of the VALUE `'cotula_s78'`/`'cotula'` to `ammonium_acetate` — a methodology saved in a Hill Labs sample-type spelling. Two surface reads are deliberately left alone and named here rather than swept in: `ammonium-acetate-methodology.js` routing a cotula surface to the S78 interpreter, and `word-export-combined.js:2137` selecting the S78 sufficiency renderer for `surfaceType === 'cotula_bowling_green'`. Neither sets a methodology; both choose which interpreter renders a dicot surface the engine does not model, which is a different question and has not been asked; and the rewritten `getMethodology()` was broken twice over, found only by running it — it asked for `r.soil.methodology` when `resolveExportInputs` returns no `soil` key, and it required `GAIP_SampleManager.getActiveSiteId` to be a function on a page where sample-manager.js is not loaded, so each guard turned its own mistake into a quiet null and the panel's methodology was null on every site including the New Zealand ones it exists for. Both are the class GH-471 already recorded in `nutrition-program-inputs.js` (`cfg.locationName`, a key no site config has), and both now have guards that ask the MODULE rather than the source text: every `r.<key>` the function reads must be a key the resolver returns, and every `_npi.<fn>` it calls must be one the adapter exports. Eleven guard suites were rewritten rather than deleted, because each pinned an intention that survives — live beats stale, one value feeds both the number and its label, the region narrows the choices — under a source that did not: `gh262`, `gh263`, `gh265`, `gh266`, `gh273`, `gh377`, `gh379`, `gh383`, `gh393`, `gh395`, `gh407`, plus the two live NZ files. `gh262/263/265/266` now share one harness (`tests/helpers/sample-fallback-harness.js`) that runs the real block, instead of four copies of the same sandbox. **Red-checked three ways on the rewritten GH-265: restoring the DOM read turns 8 of its 12 tests red and 20 of the family's 39; reading the sample's stamp instead turns 5 red; resolving the site id from `GAIP_SiteContext` turns 6 red** — the third of those is what caught the id defect above. Offline suite after: 2,971 passed, 0 failed. Stand after the live runs: 0 differing lines, both marked rows byte- and timestamp-identical. **Named and NOT fixed, because it is latent today and outside this delivery's points: eight more `|| 'MLSN'` / `|| 'mlsn'` substitutions survive in the export layer — `word-export-combined.js:1578`, `:1595`, `:3646` and `word-export.js:1300`, `:3898`, `:11394`, `:11800`, `:12251`. A site with no methodology would have its document titled MLSN and its figures computed on the MLSN basis. Unreachable on this stand, where all twelve sites carry a methodology, and reachable the moment one does not.**

**GH-522** Five live tests that could not go red, and one blindness under all five. The reviewer mutated the product in four places and the suite stayed green: a monthly series rotated by one month with its annual sum intact (`nutrition-monthly-distribution.js:309-312`); `getSoilCEC` pinned to a constant 8 (`nutrition-prebble-integration.js:674`); the monthly temperature series raised 2 °C where the calendar re-indexes it (`nutrition-calendar.js:1495`); and the delivered N/P/K shifted ten per cent in the document alone (`word-export.js:2930-2932`). **The product was right in all five cases; the tests were blind, and the fix is in the tests.** The one shape behind them: each file asserts a RELATION between two things that both sit downstream of the mutation — the Plan page against the document, the printed trace against what the engine received, a header against a header — and a change made above the fork moves both sides equally, so the relation survives. The cure is the same in each: at least one assertion binding a value to a source outside the pair. `gh398-monthly-distribution-live` now reads each month's own growth potential off the programme (computed by `monthlyGP()`, which the mutation does not touch) and requires the months sitting at the cap to be the highest-GP months — **verified: the rotation turns it red, "months at the cap Jan, Mar against highest-GP months Feb, Dec", and the file is green again with the product restored**. `gh415-prebble-input-parity-live` compares the CEC handed to the recommender with the CEC recorded on the sample, instead of only comparing the two surfaces to each other — which is why a getter answering the same wrong number to both was invisible to a test whose own name is "not a hardcoded stand-in". `gh426-soil-temp-options-live` compares the months the calendar computed on against the NASA POWER normals in its own fixture, an anchor the file already carried and never used; its site lookup also matched on `x.id === s.id` where neither side has an `id`, so on a result without one every site matched the first entry. `gh409-product-table-units-live` now reads the figures under the N, P and K columns, which it previously asserted the HEADINGS of and captured on neither surface. `gh428-calc-trace-provenance-live` checks the row graded `entered` against the site's own climate normals rather than against what `computeProgram()` was handed, which is the row checked against itself-as-received; its existing drift control injects drift into the object the block READS, so it proves the checker and says nothing about the chain feeding both sides. Three items in the same delivery. **A witness for the stand guard**: 19 live tests use a GH-519 remedy — `guardStand` in 12, `fillOwnAnnualN` in 17, capture-and-restore in 7 — and not one asserted the guard had held anything, so all of them would pass unchanged if it intercepted nothing and every write reached the stand. New `tests/e2e/gh522-stand-guard-witness-live.test.js` asserts held > 0 with a negative control that reads still reach the server. Its own first draft opened `/plan` alone, on GH-519's note that opening that page writes, and held ZERO — a witness whose provocation never reached the path, the same class it was written to close; the walk is now recorded step by step and printed (**measured: growth-light 1, plan 0, reports/export 2 — three `POST /api/samples/sync` of 23 kB each, carrying `allSites`**). **Two tests no longer write into the working tree**: the calc-audit harnesses' output moves from `calc-audit/` to the OS temp directory. GH-437 had already moved it off a TRACKED path for the same reason; gitignored is not absent, and a harness that leaves artefacts where the source lives is the class of a live test that leaves rows on the stand. A duplicated final write in `calc-audit-all-sites-live.test.js`, indented as though it were still inside the loop it had left, went with it. **And the docblock at `tests/e2e/lib/stand-guard.js`** said the PUT config route "does not exist" two lines after saying both API paths "refuse on purpose", and a reviewer took the wrong half and relayed it as fact. The route exists — `app/routes/web.php:106` → `SiteController::updateConfig` (`SiteController.php:395`), refusing a whole-object write to `gaip` with 410 by decision GH-442, reasoning at `SiteController.php:407`, refusal at `:416-419`. The half that was right carried addresses and the half that was wrong carried a status code and an inference from it, so the rewrite is addresses throughout. Offline suite: 2,971 passed, 0 failed. Stand: 0 differing lines.

**GH-523** The GH-522 fixes, corrected: three of the five were red on a clean tree, before any mutation. `gh409` called `out(...)`, an idiom borrowed from three neighbouring files where `out` is a logger — in this one the name is taken twice by locals in other functions, so the call was a ReferenceError and the new assertion never ran. `gh426` looked the site back up in its own SITES list, first by `x.name === s.name || x.id === s.id` (neither side carries an `id`, so every record would have matched the first entry and checked Auckland's normals against Christchurch's calendar) and then by name alone, which failed outright because the record's key is `site`; the lookup was for something already in the record — `curves.air` IS that site's fixture normals — and is gone. `gh428` read a synchronous climate getter without warming it. **A new rule came out of this and applies to every red check from now on: the control run WITHOUT the mutation must be green first, and only then must the mutation turn it red. Under one red run these three would have been accepted — the same assertions were failing with and without the mutation.** Controls now green: gh426 4/4 (calendar months identical to the fixture normals on all four NZ sites), gh409 18/18. **The witness was witnessing nothing.** Breaking the `site_configs` pattern in SITE_STATE_WRITES — the row class the stand was actually moving on — left it 3/3 green with a byte-identical report, because the pages it walked never write a config. It now presses Generate on the Plan page, which persists the programme, and asserts the held list CONTAINS `site_configs` rather than that a count exceeds zero: **measured, four `PATCH /api/sites/{id}/config/gaip` held, keys `nutritionCalendarProgram`/`maxNPerMonth`/`nutritionProgramCoords` and `nutritionProgram`/`nutritionProgramCoords`**; with the pattern broken it goes red. **And the remedy needed a remedy.** This file's red check is performed by disabling the guard itself, so that run has no protection and the writes land: the first time it was done, Burns's config moved — md5 `3afdaffd` → `f1179119`, 19857 → 19862 bytes, `updated_at` 2026-09-17 07:13:28 → 2026-09-18 03:38:26 — and was put back by hand from the GH-519 content backup, bytes and timestamp verified by the database's own md5. The witness now captures and restores through SQL, which does not travel the intercepted routes, so the mutation that must turn it red no longer moves the stand: re-run with the pattern broken, `restored: [Burns~gaip], failed: [], unchanged: 23`, snapshot 0 differing lines. **Handed back, not fixed — a product finding, measured while making gh428 green:** `resolveExportInputs()` resolves NO coordinates on the Plan page, for every site. `FIELD_PATHS.lat` is `['site-row', 'latitude']` (`nutrition-program-inputs.js:682`) because GH-473 decided the site ROW owns the coordinates and the `config.location` copy is reached by one write path and deliberately not read; the Plan page carries no `GAIP_SiteConfig` store to serve that row and has only the server-rendered `GAIP_SITE_CONFIG`, whose `latitude`/`longitude` are null while `location.lat`/`location.lon` hold -36.85 / 174.76 for Test5 - NZ. So `climateNormals` is null and `climateReason` is `no-coordinates` there. GH-521's methodology read is unaffected — it takes `turf.methodology` from the config object, not from the site row. `gh428-calc-trace-provenance-live` is LEFT RED on purpose: passing it would mean reading the copy GH-473 chose not to read, or asserting nothing, and a green test over a hole is what this delivery exists to remove. **TWO MEASUREMENTS ADDED FOR THE ANALYST, both requested before the brief could be written.** *How old is it:* against the 08:51 copy of `nutrition-program-inputs.js` (commit 39ac6ee, before the day's methodology delivery) the coordinate path, `FIELD_PATHS`, `getSiteConfig` and the entire climate block are identical — the day's only change to that file is the methodology chain. `plan.blade.php` has never loaded `site-config-persistence.js`, so the store was never there to ask. **The defect is older than the work that found it.** *Who the consumer is, measured live on Test5 - NZ, sample "Soccer":* the resolver on the Plan page answers `climateNormals: null, climateReason: 'no-coordinates'` — and the Plan page prints twelve N cells anyway, on the temperatures `[19.8, 20.4, 19.1, 17, 14.7, 12.6, 11.4, 11.8, 12.9, 14.2, 16, 18.2]`, which are Auckland's NASA POWER normals to the tenth (checked against `tests/fixtures/gh426-nz-monthly-normals.json`, an independent record). The document builds too — 407 KB, Annual Nutrient Requirements and Monthly N Distribution both present. **So of the three outcomes named before the run — printed on the real normals, printed on substituted ones, or not computed — it is the first: nothing on the Plan page reads this resolver's climate.** The calendar takes its months from `extractMonthlyTemps()` and the live climate service. `climateNormals` has exactly one consumer, `NutritionCalendar.inputsForSite()`, and its only callers are in `word-export-combined.js` — the document path, which runs on `/reports/export`, where the store IS loaded and the coordinates DO resolve. **No client sees a wrong number from this today, and no figure is being computed on a substitution because of it.** What is broken is a resolver answering `no-coordinates` about a site whose coordinates are on the page, on a page where nothing currently asks — a trap rather than a live defect, and it is with the analyst. GH-521's methodology read is unaffected and was verified live: it takes `turf.methodology` from the config object, and `getMethodology()` answered `ammonium_acetate` on this same site while the climate beside it was null. Offline suite: 2,971 passed, 0 failed. Stand: 0 differing lines, 24 configs, 147 samples.

**GH-524** `gh394-traffic-live` sends the change, and `gh409` says what it does not guard. The traffic file was red with no mutation applied, for the reason GH-442 gives: its `putGaipConfig` sent a whole config object assembled in the browser to `PUT /api/sites/{id}/config/gaip`, and that route exists and refuses on purpose — `app/routes/web.php:106` -> `SiteController::updateConfig` (`:395`), 410, reasoning at `:407`, refusal at `:416-419`. **The product was right; the test pinned a behaviour the product had removed** — the same shape as the GH-262/263/265/273 family. Three writes went. The setup write for the golf control is now a keyed PATCH of `traffic` alone, shaped exactly as the product's own save shapes it (`settings-init.js` `patchGaipConfig({traffic: {schedule, savedAt}})`, body `{patch: {...}}`, with `savedAt` nested inside the key where it is allowed rather than at the top level where it is the documented 422): a setup write that differs in shape from the real one proves something else. Its previous form cloned the entire saved config to set one field, so a step whose subject is "does a golf site ignore a schedule" also rewrote every other field of that site from a browser's copy. The two whole-object PUTs that restored both sites at the end of the run are removed outright: they were a second restore through the API, on top of the SQL one, and this file's own teardown note says why that is wrong — a config put back through the API carries a fresh `savedAt` and `updated_at`, and the row then looks exactly like a row a user had just saved. **Two defects the control run caught, which a mutation run alone would have hidden under a red it was expecting:** the first draft sent the bare sections and got 422 "The patch field is required", because the route takes `{patch: {...}}`; and the assertion named "every site config this run touched was put back" was reading a state captured before anything was put back, since the removed PUTs were what used to restore before that read. It is split in two — one test named for what it actually measures, what the run LEFT on each site, keeping the identity-field half that still belongs to that moment; and one asserting the restore itself against the report of the instrument that performs it, `restoreConfigs()`, which writes the captured bytes and timestamp back through SQL and checks each row against the database's own md5. That restore moved from the teardown into the end of the run, because `afterAll` runs after every test and a test asking whether the configs were put back was reading a report that did not exist yet — measured, `restore report: null`. **Control run green, 8 of 8**, restore report `{restored: [2 sites], failed: [], unchanged: 22}`; the mutation half of the acceptance is the reviewer's. And a note in `gh409-product-table-units-live`'s header, written from the reviewer's own measurements, so the file's NAME is not read wider than its assertions: it GUARDS a one-sided divergence (proved by a mutation shifting Delivered in the document only — red on both NZ sites) and DOES NOT GUARD both surfaces moving together (proved by +2 degC on the temperature series handed to the programme: applications 3 -> 1, volume 90 -> 30 L/ha, granular 4 -> 5 and 61.6 -> 70.9 g/m2, test green). That class is Question 32 and is not being worked on now. Offline suite: 2,971 passed, 0 failed. Stand: 0 differing lines, 24 configs, 147 samples.

**GH-525** Three silent skips stated as assertions, and one stale baseline re-pinned beside the old one. **The skips.** `gh425:420/424`, `gh423:393` and `gh401:618` each declared a test wider than it asserted and returned in silence on the case it could not serve — `if (c.expect.P)` and `if (c.expect[n] !== 'removal-only-no-soil-data') return`, `if (products are equal) return`, `if (!site.multiSpray.length) return`. Until the 08:51 commit made an assertion-free test fail, each read as a pass. None is removed; each has a subject, only the declaration was not running. The emptiness is now said out loud, and said about the PRODUCT rather than the fixture: gh425 asserts both directions — a nutrient with no reading says so, and one WITH a reading does not, which is the half that was missing and would have let a trace claim 'no reading' for a nutrient the sample carried; gh423 asserts the agreement it used to return on, including that the products exist and are non-empty, so a replay that produced nothing no longer reads as harmony; gh401 asserts that a site whose fixture records no multi-application spray really has no liquid applied twice in the programme — `expect([]).toEqual([])` would only prove the fixture equals itself. A fourth of the same shape was found in `gh428-outer`'s RECORD branch and closed the same way. **Self-checked by inverting each declared state before delivery, which is how the reviewer will check them:** declaring a reading where there is none turns gh425 red; pointing the comparison at keys that do not exist turns gh423 red; counting every application as a repeat turns gh401 red on both sites. **The baseline.** `gh401`'s inline figures and `gh428-outer`'s recorded snapshot both expected 247.6 / 14.9 / 180.7 for Test5 - NZ; the product prints 245.5 / 32.2 / 100.1, and the Required K moved 136.1 -> 84.1, which the brief had not named. Nothing broke: GH-482 derives the certificate from the site's OWN soil texture, taking Test5's ammonium-acetate K range from 109.5-273.7 to 78.2-195.5 (`tests/gh482-certificate-follows-the-site.test.js:94`), which moves the requirement and with it the products chosen. Measured across all four NZ sites, the two with their own texture moved (test5 247.6/14.9/180.7 -> 245.5/32.2/100.1, russley 200.2/0/118.4 -> 143.8/0/81.8) and the two with `texture: null` did not — which is the shape GH-482 predicts. **The 2026-09-11 snapshot is kept unread and unwritten**, as the only surviving record of what these programmes were before this week; the current baseline is a new file beside it (`gh428-nz-plan-snapshot-2026-09-18.json`), RECORD mode refuses to write the older path, and the old file's md5 is unchanged (`a7491d78663baaac2eb768d48fb8f3fa`). **Controls green: gh425 and gh423 38/38, gh428-outer 5/5.** **HANDED BACK, NOT FIXED — two of gh401's four failures were not the stale baseline, and gh401 stays red on them:** (1) `Required is ONE quantity` — the document prints `84.1 ‡` against the Plan's `84.1`. The marker is deliberate (`word-export-combined.js:4327-4331`, GH-369 follow-up: a P or K figure derived from this sample's own tissue ratio while that tissue reading is below sufficiency) and carries its own legend, so the quantities agree and the STRINGS do not — this file's claim is wider than the product's contract, and which of the two should move is not a test decision. (2) `the caption is the sum of the rows printed above it` — caption 245.5 against rows summing to 245.6, **on both surfaces**, so it is not a divergence but a rounding inconsistency inside the product, found by the test doing its job. Offline suite: 2,971 passed, 0 failed. Stand: 0 differing lines, 24 configs, 147 samples.

**GH-526 (PLAN-samples-sync-FINAL, stage 1 — server routes)** Deleting a sample has one route, and the row says who did it. There was no per-record delete at all: the hub could only send its whole picture through `POST /api/samples/sync`, and the Data page had a second route of its own — `DELETE /api/data/entry/{id}`, `DataController::destroy()` — which resolved the row by (id, the user's ACTIVE site) rather than by the row's own, and left `site_summaries` pointing at what it had just deleted. Both are replaced by `SampleController::destroy()` on `DELETE /api/samples/{sample}`: rights checked against the SAMPLE's site; the summary re-pointed at a live sibling of the same (site, type, effective date) and rebuilt from it, or retired with the sample when there is none; `deleted_by_user_id` and `delete_source` written, the latter validated against a closed set (`hub`, `data-page`, `import-clear`) because a free-text column filled by whatever a client sent is not evidence. New migration `add_delete_attribution_to_samples`. **Four more server changes the plan asks for before the hub is rewritten:** `applyZoneMeta()` puts the display-zone map in one place for `sync()`, `store()` and `update()`, which used to give three different zone names for one row, and `update()` now registers a renamed sample on its site (D-6); a clearing `sync` may name ONE site and answers 422 for more, because said of several at once it stops being "replace this site with this file" and becomes the snapshot this whole plan removes; `index()` accepts a limit up to 2000 and returns `meta: {total, returned}`, so a client served a subset can tell — 200 was below what one site already holds; and `settings-init.js`'s `apiFetch()` stops returning `r.json()` for any status, which printed "0 records imported successfully" and redirected on a 422, a 403 or a 500. **D-3, decided by the owner:** an import that clears a site hides its `spray_logs` and `field_log_entries` instead of destroying them. Not "SoftDeletes on both models" as originally written — there are no Eloquent models for those tables, and all sixteen call sites are raw `DB::table()` queries — so a migration adds `deleted_at` and every one of the sixteen is taught to skip hidden rows by hand. `field_log_entries` carries unique(user_id, client_uid), so a hidden row still occupies the key: `FieldLogEntryController::store()` clears `deleted_at` when it finds one, and writing the same entry again brings it back rather than failing on the index. `SprayLogController::destroy()` keeps its hard delete on purpose — that is a user removing one of their own entries, outside this change's scope — and the asymmetry is recorded in the code rather than left to be noticed. **Open question carried to the owner, not decided here:** the import bundle contains no logs at all, so "import samples" clears logs it does not replace; the soft delete makes that reversible, but whether the import should touch them is a separate call. New `Gh526SampleDeleteRouteTest` (11 tests: viewer refused, the sample's own site rather than the active one, summary re-point and retirement, the closed source set, `meta`, the one-site rule and its accepted counterpart, logs hidden not destroyed, the same field-log entry written again). `Gh430SamplesNoSnapshotDeleteTest` re-pointed at the new route, and asserts the attribution nothing asked for before. **Live on the stack** (`tests/e2e/gh526-stage1-routes-live.test.js`, 4/4): the file creates its OWN sample on Test6 - UK — a site holding zero samples, so any row under it is the run's — deletes that one and nothing else, and never exercises `clearSiteData`, because the stand holds exactly three live spray_logs (ids 3, 13, 14) and nothing would replace them. **Measured: POST 201; `meta {total: 61, returned: 1}`; DELETE 200 with `delete_source: 'hub'`; the row still present with `deleted_at` set, `delete_source` 'hub' and `deleted_by_user_id` filled; the retired `/api/data/entry/{id}` answers 404.** The created row was then removed outright — taking back what the run added — and the stand matched its before-snapshot, 147 samples, 0 differing lines. PHPUnit 191 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,971 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-527** `methodology_snapshot` can hold "not set", in both tables that store it. GH-520 gave the methodology one owner and no default, so `siteConfigMethodology()` returns null for a site that has chosen none — and the column it is written into was `string(32) NOT NULL`. **Saving a sample for such a site was an HTTP 500.** Latent on the dev stack, where all twelve sites carry a methodology, and reachable by a user the moment one does not: create a site, import samples before filling in Settings. It surfaced as 13 red PHPUnit tests, and **the server suite had not been run since GH-520 shipped** — the defect was found only because the next piece of work stopped on the red suite. Fixed by making the column nullable rather than by writing something into it: the owner's rule of 18.09.2026 is that an unset methodology stays unset, so there was no choice of method here, only a consequence. `site_summaries.methodology_snapshot` is the same value copied onto the summary built from the sample and was NOT NULL for the same reason, so fixing only `samples` moved the same 500 one table along — measured, `NOT NULL constraint failed: site_summaries.methodology_snapshot` — and the migration covers both. `soil_texture_snapshot` beside them in both tables is deliberately untouched: it is owned by the site's own texture column and nothing here writes null into it. Three stale tests went with it: `GH482SiteTexturePayloadTest` ×2 read `sites.methodology_override`, the column GH-520 retired — that file's subject is the site's TEXTURE, which still has its column, and the methodology assertions rode along and are removed rather than re-pointed; `SiteApiTest` expected `'ammonium-acetate'` on a site created without a config, and now expects null. **Named and NOT closed:** the `default('')` is kept, so the column can express absence two ways — null and an empty string. Narrowing that is a decision about existing rows, not a side effect of making the write possible. Counted on the stand for that question: `samples` 0 null, 0 empty, 147 with a value; `site_summaries` 0 null, 0 empty, 71 with a value — so both representations are unused today and the ambiguity is latent. PHPUnit 191 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-528** Two tails of GH-526, both found by review; the product was right in both and is unchanged. **A docblock that was right about its decision and wrong about half its reason.** The migration making `methodology_snapshot` nullable explained that `soil_texture_snapshot` beside it stays NOT NULL "in both tables" — `site_summaries` has no texture column at all, measured against information_schema: it carries `methodology_snapshot` and nothing else of that pair. The decision does not move; the paragraph now says what was measured instead of what was assumed by symmetry with the column above it. **And a hole we knew about: resolution was covered, permission was not.** `Gh526SampleDeleteRouteTest` proves the row is found by its OWN site rather than by the user's active one — the defect in the route GH-526 replaced, which resolved by (id, active site) and answered 404. It could not prove anything about RIGHTS, because it gave both sites to one user: `canEditSite()` then answers true whichever site it is handed. **Measured: with the guard reading `canEditSite($request->user()->activeSite ?? $sample->site)` at SampleController.php:490, the whole server suite was 191 of 191 green.** The missing case is the one where the two answers differ — a user who MAY edit the site they are standing on and MAY NOT edit the site the sample belongs to — and the test asserts that difference about the user before it makes the request, so a future edit cannot quietly give them both sites again. **The refusal code is the subject and is printed by the test, not inferred:** correct product, `DELETE another account's sample -> HTTP 403`; under the mutation, `HTTP 200` — the deletion goes through. 403 is a request understood and refused on rights; 404 would be the row not found, which is the other claim, and a permission test going red with 404 would be guarding resolution again under a new name. Said plainly: the mutation was named to the author before the test was written, so it is a specification of the missing case and not an independent witness — what stands on its own here is which code the product returns, and that the user really can edit one site and not the other. PHPUnit 192 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,971 passed, 0 failed. Stand: 0 differing lines, 147 samples, 3 live spray_logs.

**GH-529** The caption over a list is the sum of what the list prints. The Annual Product Summary's Total Delivered row was the exact accumulated total rounded once, while each product row above it was rounded on its own — two different numbers, and on Test5 - NZ the caption read 245.5 kg of nitrogen over rows adding to 245.6. **The same on both surfaces**, the Plan page and the document, so it was never a divergence between them but a total that was not the total of the figures beside it, on a page a client reads. Owner's decision of 18.09.2026, variant A: the caption prints the sum of the printed rows and every month stays exactly as it was computed. The rule is stated once — `sumDelivered` and `formatSumDelivered` in `nutrition-delivery-core.js`, which is the module that exists to hold this kind of rule — and the three surfaces call it: `word-export.js`'s `_sumPrinted`, and `_sumPrintedDelivered` on the New Zealand and Australian panels. **This reverses a measurement, which is worth naming rather than discovering later:** GH-403 measured the sum-of-rounded-rows caption and rejected it, because at WHOLE kilograms six rows drift by up to 3 (`Test6 - UK K rows 127 true 125.4`). GH-403 then moved the rows to 1 dp, where each is off by at most 0.05, and what remained was the last 0.1. Both decisions are right at their own precision, and the reversal is written into `gh318-annual-product-summary-p-rounding.test.js`'s header, beside the measurement it overturns, because that file is kept precisely to record reversals. **The acceptance condition, and how it was met:** `gh401-delivery-volumes-live` carried a deliberately red assertion about this caption, under a frame saying it must go green from a product fix and naming two ways of making it green that were refused. The product was fixed with the test file untouched — md5 `67a10fc04954ea5aff0ea807fbf16eb0` — and the assertion went green on that same md5. Only then was the frame removed, md5 `ac5744224aa2d48ff9eade5d0d7a88ab`, and a diff of the two versions with comments stripped is EMPTY: not one executable line changed. A third, separate step re-pinned the fixture's `footer` from 245.5 to 245.6 (md5 `1bf257352052b4e19de38ee4fc5be2d8`) — the caption moved and `delivered`, the Annual Nutrient Requirements figure, did not, which is the change rather than a side effect of it. Five offline assertions pinned the rule that was replaced and are rewritten, with a behavioural check beside the structural ones: three rows printing 0.3 add to 0.9 where the exact total 0.75 rounds to 0.8. **Found and NOT fixed, named with its address:** the United Kingdom panel (`nutrition-uk-fertiliser-integration.js`) prints the same caption the same old way. How far the rule reaches was not part of the decision, which was taken on a measurement of two surfaces. The gap is not left quiet: `gh318-annual-product-summary-p-rounding.test.js` now asserts that panel's CURRENT shape, so fixing it fails this test and says why, instead of a third surface drifting unremarked. Live gh401 44 of 44. PHPUnit 192 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,971 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-530** A measurement, and it came out negative — recorded because that is an answer. GH-529 left the United Kingdom panel printing the old caption and named it as found-not-fixed; what was known about it was its SHAPE, read off the source, and a form is not a defect. Measured live on Test6 - UK (52.24 / 0.38, which is what makes `isUK()` true and that panel the one that renders): the site holds no samples, so the run created its own probe (`gh530-uk-probe`, no `_label`, since a label would reach `mergeZoneNameIntoSite()` and rewrite the site's attributes_json) and removed it afterwards. **Seven product rows, and the caption agreed with their sum to the digit on all three nutrients: N 203.6, P 18.1, K 67.0, difference 0.0 each.** The expectation was written down two-sided before the run — "either 0.0, or 0.1 on one or two nutrients" — so neither outcome could be read as confirmation afterwards. Said plainly rather than inflated: this panel did not print a wrong number, it simply did not land in the case where the rounding tails cross half of the last digit. `tests/e2e/gh530-uk-caption-measure-live.test.js` asserts that the measurement was taken and printed, not that it came out either way, and reports a panel that fails to render as a measurement that did not happen rather than as "no difference". The probe's own row was removed; the site's config, which the Generate press had rewritten, was put back from the 09:20 content capture by the coordinator, bytes and timestamp, verified against the database and against the whole 24-row table rather than the single row.

**GH-531** The fourth surface. The United Kingdom panel now sums the printed rows like the other three, through the same `sumDelivered` in `nutrition-delivery-core.js`. **Not because it was printing a wrong number — GH-530 measured it and it was not** — but because the shape was the one that produced 245.5 over 245.6 on the New Zealand and Australian panels, and whether the fractional tails cross half of the last digit depends on the site and the sample rather than on the panel. Three surfaces calling a rule and a fourth keeping its own way is one rule with two ways of not following it. **How the change was shown to have reached the panel, before any test was touched:** GH-529 had pinned the UK panel's OLD shape in `gh318-annual-product-summary-p-rounding.test.js`, deliberately, so the gap could not go quiet — "the day someone fixes it this line fails and says why". The product was changed and that test went red on an UNCHANGED file, md5 `63d6e2cc05bd44c64c1fd120abed64e7`, with `Expected pattern: /formatDelivered\(nutrientTotals\.N\)/` — the assertion that the old shape was still there. Only then was it rewritten, md5 `e318d156e8255c78bacb2c1da1301762`. A test written to record a gap and used, unaltered, as the proof that the gap was closed. PHPUnit 192 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,971 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-532** A live test may not exist without a remedy against moving the stand. GH-519 fitted seventeen of them with one and the same day a new one was written without any: `gh530-uk-caption-measure-live` presses Generate on a real site, the programme persisted itself, and Test6 - UK's configuration was put back by hand. The remedies existed; nothing REQUIRED them, and one file put right would have returned us here on the next new test. **The file first.** gh530 now captures before anything opens a page and restores at the end of the run — capture-and-restore rather than interception, chosen by what it needs: `guardStand` would hold the POST that creates its probe sample, and without that sample the picker is empty and the panel has nothing to draw, so the writes have to land for the measurement to exist. The probe sample is deleted through the product's own route (GH-526), and the restore's own verdict is asserted rather than printed, so a run that failed to put the stand back is a red test. **Then the requirement.** `tests/gh532-no-live-test-without-stand-protection.test.js` walks `tests/e2e` from the TREE — a new live file is in the universe the moment it exists — and every file either names one of the four remedies or stands in `EXEMPT` with a reason and an `until` date. Exemption keys are filenames and must match EXACTLY ONE file (the GH-517 rule: a key matching nothing is a stale exemption holding a door open, one matching several is a single reason covering several cases), and an exemption held by a file that has since gained a remedy is also red. The census prints what the walk found, file by file, with the remedies named in each and the count of `route()` interceptions — **measured: 35 live files, 21 carrying a named remedy, 14 without, all 14 exempted.** Three controls: gh401 must be found carrying `captureConfigsOnce`/`restoreConfigs`, gh433 must be found carrying none, and gh530 — the file this guard exists because of — must be found protected and NOT exempted, so "the guard is green" cannot come to mean "the guard stopped looking at its own subject". **What this guard deliberately does NOT do, because two drafts tried and failed:** it does not decide for itself whether a file writes. The first predicate counted the login click and flagged all 35 files; the second missed `gh526-stage1-routes-live`, whose writes go through a `call(method, ...)` helper rather than a literal `method: 'POST'`. A guard with an unreliable predicate would hand out false exemptions with its own authority, so it asks the question it can answer. **The fourteen exemptions are a named backlog with a date, not a finding that they are safe** — among them `gh459-cross-site-inputs-live` (twelve control presses, five non-GET calls, no remedy), `gh404-settings-location-required-live` (drives the Settings form), and `gh526-stage1-routes-live`, which deletes its own sample through the product but leaves the soft-deleted row behind. PHPUnit 192 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,979 passed, 0 failed.


**GH-533** The hub writes one record at a time, and the server stops resurrecting what a user deleted. Stage 2 of `PLAN-samples-sync-FINAL`, delivered as one piece because it cannot be delivered as two. **What it replaces.** Every sample mutation scheduled a 500 ms debounce, assembled a snapshot of every sample of every site out of the browser's own store, and sent the lot to `POST /api/samples/sync`. Adding one sample sent the whole collection — the shape the project rule names in one sentence: send the change, not the state. `scheduleSave`, `doSave`, `filterAutoGenSamples`, `syncSamplesToServer` and `forceSave` are gone, 124 lines, and `sample-persistence.js` no longer knows that route exists. In their place: `POST /api/samples` on an add, `PATCH /api/samples/{id}` on an edit, rename or turf-profile change, `DELETE /api/samples/{id}` on a delete, N of them on a clear. **Why it is one delivery and not three.** Three pairs are inseparable, and each was measured rather than assumed. (a) `store()` passed `null` for the trashed allow-list, which means "restore it", and stage 2 moves every per-record write onto `store()` — split them and the write arrives exactly where the resurrection still lives. (b) A restored sample carried its lab readings under `values` and nothing under `rawData`, and the old push read only `rawData`: that, and nothing else, is why the push was harmless on restored samples. Fill `rawData` before removing the push and every event starts overwriting the server's payload with a tab's copy, last-writer-wins across all samples at once. (c) `PATCH` and `DELETE` are addressed by the server's `id`; `client_uid` cannot be an address, because 27 of 147 rows on the stand have none and label-shaped uids like "Green 1" repeat between sites. **The server's third answer.** The plan said to drop `withTrashed()` from `saveSampleRecord()` outright. Applied literally that would have undone GH-431 for `sync()`: the ordinary push writes nothing and reports `skipped`, and three existing assertions depend on it. The plan predates GH-431 and its instruction is stale against it — said here rather than routed around silently. So the allow-list is untouched and `store()` gets a third answer of its own, `$ignoreTrashedMatch`: the soft-deleted row is not looked at, no match is found among the living, and a new living row is created. A push is a cache repeating itself and writes nothing; a `POST` is a person pressing Add and writes — into a new row, because the old one was deleted and its figures are not what the person just typed. `SiteApiTest::test_store_does_not_resurrect_a_deleted_sample` pins both figures: the deleted row keeps K=41, the new one carries K=47, and the list shows one. **A 500 found by writing a test for something else.** `GET /api/samples/{id}/analyse` threw `Argument #4 ($methodology) must be of type string, null given` for any site with no methodology chosen. The paragraph in `run()` already said what should happen — "Null means not set, and the nutrient classification that needs a methodology does not run" — and the parameter it passed to was typed `string`. The same shape as GH-527, one route further along: that was the write of the stamp, this is the read of the setting. Falling through to the MLSN branch was the smaller edit and is what the owner's rule forbids, so a nutrient keeps its measured value and says `No methodology set`; nothing is invented and no threshold applied. **Four traps, each closed by a line that says why it is there.** The site comes from the event, read at the moment of the action, not from the active-site pointer a request may outlive — GH-459 in the write direction. The live record is resolved synchronously, before the first `then`, because `getAllSamples()` returns a deep clone and a `serverId` written onto a clone reaches nothing. `gaip:sample-updated` carrying a `reason` is the b35fix411 migration announcing itself, and without that guard every page load would PATCH every migrated sample. `client_uid` is deliberately not sent on a PATCH: the route accepts and overwrites it, and it is the key a re-import matches on, so a rename would have moved it. **What deliberately writes nothing:** `gaip:site-changed` — looking at a site is not editing it — and `gaip:site-added/-renamed/-removed`, which the plan still routes to `syncSiteListToServer()`, a function GH-441 removed and for the reason it gave. **Rights, item 6.** `canEditActiveSite` travels on the page and a viewer sends nothing; the five header controls, the gear menu, the right-click menu and the double-click rename are not built for them, and the tooltip drops the line offering a rename. An absent flag is not a false — that is a page we have not taught to answer, not a page that said no. **Self-checked before delivery, control run green first: six mutations, each turned the intended test red** — dropping the `reason` guard, forcing the permission gate true, reading the pointer at handler entry, reading the pointer inside the request, sending a PATCH payload built from the visible fields only, and addressing a DELETE by the local key. The third one, the pointer at handler entry, passed the first draft and is the reason a seventh test exists: the event fires synchronously from the mutation, so that mutation preserves behaviour rather than escaping the test, and what neither version proved was the rule itself — that the event's word beats the pointer's. It is now asserted directly. **Live on Burns, expectation written into the file before the run and every line of it met:** 26 soil samples restored, first "Rye Nursery" `serverId` 53, `rawData` holding `K, Ca, Mg, Na, pH_Water, OM_Percent, CEC_meq100g` and none of the five envelope keys; add → 1 `POST /api/samples`; zone change → 1 `PATCH /api/samples/53`; delete → 1 `DELETE /api/samples/53`; two site switches → 0 writes; no held path is `/api/samples/sync` and no body names `allSites`. `guardStand` held all three and 8 requests reached the server, so the run measured the traffic without moving the stand. Stand before and after: 0 differing lines, 24 configs, 148 samples, 109 sites, 3 spray_logs. PHPUnit 195 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,991 passed, 0 failed.


**GH-534** The journals are cleared outright again. Owner's reversal of D-3, 18.09.2026: "hard for the journal only; leave the samples as they were." GH-526 had made a clearing Settings import hide `spray_logs` and `field_log_entries` instead of destroying them; a spray log or a field note is a record of something the user did and can be entered again, and the clear that removes it is one they asked for. **The samples are untouched and stay soft** — that distinction is the owner's and is what the whole change turns on: a lab reading cannot be taken again, and 88 of the 148 sample rows on the dev stack exist only because deleting one hides it. **What came out:** the soft-delete UPDATE in `SampleController::sync()` is a `delete()`; the ten `whereNull('deleted_at')` conditions on the two journals are gone from `DataController` (2), `DashboardController` (1), `FieldLogEntryController` (1) and `SprayLogController` (4), together with the revival in `FieldLogEntryController::store()` that cleared `deleted_at` on an upsert, and the note in `SprayLogController::destroy()` recording its hard delete as the deliberate exception — it is no longer an exception. `destroy()` itself is unchanged, checked and left alone. **And the column goes, not just the writes,** because a mechanism nobody uses reads as one in force: `2026_09_18_000003` drops it from both tables, guarded by `hasColumn` so a database built after the withdrawal still migrates, and the migration that added it is kept — it ran on a real database and deleting the file would leave that database's `migrations` row without a class — with a heading naming its own withdrawal. **Measured safe before running, and the measurement cannot be taken afterwards:** `spray_logs` 3 rows, 0 hidden; `field_log_entries` 0 and 0. Nothing was returned to life by dropping the column. Taken independently by the coordinator and the reviewer, who said plainly why he took his first — after the column is gone there is nothing left to tell a revived row from an ordinary one. **The coordinator's reading, that no further guard is needed because the missing column IS the mechanism, was required to be SHOWN rather than stated, and the showing changed it.** In the reviewer's own form, straight to the database: `select id from spray_logs where deleted_at is null limit 1` -> `ERROR 1054 (42S22) Unknown column 'deleted_at' in 'where clause'`, and the same for `field_log_entries`; the identical query against `samples`, where the column exists, returns a row, so it is the column that is missing and not the query that is malformed. Through Laravel on MySQL the same: `Illuminate\Database\QueryException`, `SQLSTATE[42S22]: Column not found: 1054`. **But the same statement on the engine this project's PHPUnit suite runs on does NOT fail — it returns 0, silently.** SQLite reads a double-quoted name that resolves to no column as a STRING LITERAL, and the query builder always quotes, so `where "deleted_at" is null` asks whether the text 'deleted_at' is null and matches nothing. Written bare it does throw; nothing in the product writes it bare. So the guarantee holds where the client is and is absent where we check: a soft-delete condition re-introduced on a journal would come back green from the suite with the log list empty, and 500 in production. Recorded in `Gh534JournalsHaveNoSoftDeleteTest`, two tests — the column is gone, and the silence is asserted as the dangerous property it is, so the day it becomes loud that test goes red and says the census can be argued down. A tree census was written to close the SQLite gap and **withdrawn on the coordinator's instruction**; its copy is in the delivery notes. The reviewer named the remaining boundary himself: the schema can be restored by one migration, so what stands between us and a quiet return is reading migrations at acceptance. **The walk, by four predicates rather than by memory, because the reviewer re-runs it with his own and compares:** `whereNull('deleted_at')` anywhere under `app/` — 4 hits, one on `sites` (`RepairSiteConfigs`, not a journal and never was) and three inside the GH-534 test, one of them the deliberate measurement; a journal name and a soft-delete word on one line — 6, all in the two migrations' docblocks, the test, and two changelog entries; the same words in the four controllers that touch these tables — **0**; and file-level, which catches what a line-level predicate misses when a statement spans lines — 8 files, every journal line in each of them read and none carrying a condition. Two GH-526 tests are rewritten rather than deleted, because their subject survives and only the answer moved: "hides the logs" is now "destroys the logs", asserted as an absence of rows rather than a value in a column, and the field-log re-entry test keeps its behavioural claim — the same entry written again after a clear leaves one row carrying the second write — with its reason replaced, the key being free rather than a hidden row being revived. Stand before and after: 0 differing lines, 24 configs, 148 samples, 109 sites, `spray_logs` 3 as it was. PHPUnit 197 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,991 passed, 0 failed.


**GH-535** Two corrections to GH-534, both in text, and one of them turned out to be a measurement nobody had taken. **A docblock pointing at a guard that does not exist.** `Gh534JournalsHaveNoSoftDeleteTest` referred four times to "the census below" — a tree walk written alongside it and withdrawn by the coordinator before delivery, which the file itself says two lines further up. The worst of the four was inside an ASSERTION MESSAGE, the text a person reads at the moment the test goes red on a non-sqlite engine, and it named that missing census as "the only thing standing between us and a silently empty journal list". All four now say plainly that the census was withdrawn and where the copy is; it is not brought back, which was the coordinator's call and not this fix's to make. **And a sentence the reviewer disproved by doing the thing nobody had done.** The same docblock said a soft-delete condition re-introduced on a journal "would come back green from this suite, with the spray log list empty, and 500 in production". That was a conclusion drawn from the engine difference — SQLite answering an unknown quoted column with an empty result where MySQL answers 1054 — and three people read the difference and built the same conclusion out of it without putting a condition back to look. The reviewer put one back. The suite does not catch the QUERY; it catches the EMPTY LIST, because the tests assert that rows are there. **Measured again here, one read point at a time rather than the two he tried, because the paragraph being replaced should not be replaced by another inference:** condition restored and `SiteApiTest` run — `buildFilteredQuery()` 2 red, the batch fetch by ids 1 red, `resolveOwnedLog()` 1 red, `FieldLogEntryController::index()` 1 red, and `SprayLogController::update()`'s re-read **0 red**. So four of the five read points GH-534 touched are already covered by assertions that existed before any of this, and the fifth is silent: its result is not looked at by any test, and on MySQL it would answer 1054 while here the update would save and the response would be a 404 from `firstOrFail()` on an empty result — visible to a user, invisible to the suite. The reviewer's boundary travels with the finding rather than being dropped: he did not walk every read point in the application and does not claim to, so what is established is the shape, an uncovered read point stays quiet, and not a count of them. This is Question 38's subject and Question 38 has been corrected the same way; the earlier wording is kept struck through beside it so it is not re-derived next week. **Third, offered as optional and taken because it is the same class:** `assertDontSee('Thing')` searched the whole response body for a substring — it passes today, would pass for the wrong reason the day that word appears in another field, and would also pass on a response that listed nothing at all. Replaced by the endpoint's own shape, `assertJsonCount(0, 'entries')` and `assertJsonMissing(['product_name' => 'Thing'])`, and self-checked: making the clear delete nothing turns that test red. **A rule of the day broken, named rather than left in the transcript:** a stray `git checkout` with no arguments went out in one of the mutation commands. It takes no path and changes no file — it printed branch status — and the tree and history are as they were, verified by md5 on the two controllers it could have touched. It should not have been typed, and it was mine. PHPUnit 197 passed, 0 failed. Jest 2,991 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-536** The browser stops keeping a copy of the samples, and a read that failed says so. Stage 3 of `PLAN-samples-sync-FINAL`. **The defect, in the three steps it ran in.** `fetchSamplesFromServer()` answered `onComplete(false)` for three different situations — no API on the page, an empty account, and a request that threw — so an empty account and a failed read were literally the same answer. `restore()` met that `false` with `restoreFromLocalFallback()`, which filled the store out of `gilba_samples` in localStorage. Samples from there carry no `serverId`, because only a server restore writes one, so every later edit stopped inside `writeUpdate()` at `if (!sample.serverId)` with a line in the console and nothing on the wire. The screen looked right for all three steps. That is the whole thing: the client kept working and lost the work without being told. **What replaces it.** Three outcomes — `server`, `empty`, `error` — and they are not interchangeable. An empty account is a SUCCESSFUL read of nothing: no banner, store open, the existing empty states already tell the truth. A failed read raises a banner in the db-shell content header with the plan's own words, “Samples could not be loaded from the server. Nothing has been changed.” and a Retry that calls `restore()`, and closes the store: `SM.setReadOnly(true)`, and `addSample`/`updateSample`/`deleteSample`/`clearSamples`/`clearAllSamples`/`importFile`/`importCSV` throw `Samples are not loaded — retry first`. `_gaipSamplePersistenceReady` is set on the failing path too, because `turf-profile-controller.js` gates its site switch on it and leaving it unset hangs a second defect off the first. `Generate & Download Word` and the iCal export are disabled with the reason beside them — GH-377's precedent, refuse rather than print an empty document; `Generate LED Report` is left alone because whether it reads the samples was not measured here. **The lock is set by a failed restore and is NOT the default,** and that is not a style choice: `morning-briefing.blade.php` and `stadium.blade.php` load `sample-manager.js` WITHOUT `sample-persistence.js`, so a lock that defaulted to closed and opened only on a successful restore would shut both of those pages permanently with nothing on them able to open it. Asserted against the manager loaded on its own, the way those two pages load it. **The fourth step, brought into the delivery on the coordinator's decision and not invented here.** The request is `samples?limit=200`; `meta: {total, returned}` has been served since stage 1 (GH-526) and **nothing read it — zero occurrences in the file, measured before the work started.** While the browser held a copy, 200 of 201 meant an incomplete cache over a complete local store. With the copy gone it means one sample the client cannot see and is not told about. `returned < total` is now an error with its own text, “Loaded N of M samples.”, and the rows that did arrive are KEPT and shown read-only rather than thrown away as well — a divergence from the plan's table, which puts partial in the “store empty and locked” row while its own banner text says “Loaded N of M”. Emptying the store would be a second loss on top of the first. `Gh536SamplesListMetaTest` pins the server half, including the one way to break it while the response still looks right: `total` counted AFTER the limit makes it equal `returned` always and the check can never fire. **Н3, the indivisibility that had nothing to do with samples.** `hub-persistence.js` kept the active-site handling inside `if (samples)`, where `samples` was that file's own copy under `gilba_hub_samples`. What the block does is honour `gilba_import_active_site` after an import and otherwise match the server's `activeSiteId`. Deleting the key without lifting the block would have stopped /hub setting its active site at all — silently, /hub being the hidden calculation runner. The 200 ms timer it ran on is replaced by the ready event, because the timer was a guess at how long a network read takes and what covered a miss until now was the copy underneath it. **A real defect found by a test that would not go green.** `enqueue()` chained with `prev.then(step)`, which runs only when `prev` RESOLVED; every write re-throws on failure, so one refused request left that record's queue permanently rejected and every later write to the same sample was skipped with no request and no word. The Retry could not have worked. Found by measurement — the retry test sent one request where it should have sent two — not by reading. Now `prev.catch(...).then(step)`: the address dependency the chain exists for still holds, a PATCH after a failed create still finds no `serverId` and says so, but the queue is no longer poisoned. **The unsaved marker, the second place the coordinator named.** `sample._dirty` has been stamped by `markFailed()` since stage 2 and read by nobody; `gaip:samples-persistence-error` had one listener and it skipped everything except `reason: 'sites-list'`. The sample's chip in the switcher now carries a red dot and a Retry calling `GAIP_SamplePersistence.retryRecord()`, with the plan's two named statuses in their own words — 403 “You don't have permission to edit this site”, 419 “Session expired — reload the page”, and no Retry on a 419 because the next request would fail identically. **A failed DELETE cannot be retried and that is structural, not an omission:** `markFailed()` is called with `null` for a delete, the sample is already out of the store, and there is no row left to hang a button on. **Everything else the copy touched:** `StorageAdapter`, `CONFIG.storageKey`, the `beforeunload` snapshot and the public `clear`/`getStorageSize*`/`StorageAdapter` out of `sample-persistence.js`; `collectSamples()`/`restoreSamples()`, the key and the export bundle's `samples` out of `hub-persistence.js`; the Re-run stamp out of `dashboard-ui.js` (`gilba_wb_water_override` beside it STAYS — it carries a choice the user made that the server has no record of); the pre-import cache wipe in `settings-init.js` re-sourced from the live store instead of localStorage; `b35fix268`'s one-time label repair and `CONFIG.storageKey` out of `sample-manager.js`; the key out of both `gilba-storage-migrate.js` lists. **`gaip-field-log.js` lost the most:** `SiteLoader._injectIntoStorage()`, `setActive()` and `_fromStorage()`, plus a fourth copy of the same read in `getSiteList()`. The fallback is NOT replaced by another guess — rebuilt from the copy it returned real sites, with the copy gone it could only ever have returned its own last resort `{id:'default', label:'Default Site'}`, a site that does not exist offered to the client as if it did, which is the shape GH-441 removed for the same reason. A failed read renders a disabled “Sites could not be loaded”. **A trap the coordinator's correction sharpened and the measurement then narrowed.** `StorageAdapter` is declared in TWO files — ours and `site-dashboard.js:73`, a different object under `GaipSiteDashboard` — so removal by name would have emptied the wrong one; pinned by a test. The correction added two more files reading the name through a global and warned they would break silently. **Re-measured, and they do not:** `gaip-decision-engine.js:61` reads `GilbaStorageAdapter || StorageAdapter` and `hub-header-bar.js:607,622` reads `window.StorageAdapter || GilbaHub.StorageAdapter` and then requires `getGlobal`/`setGlobal` — nothing in the tree assigns any of those three globals, `window.GilbaHub` has no `StorageAdapter` key, and `getGlobal`/`setGlobal` exist nowhere except the four lines testing for them. Both consumers already take their fallback branch on every load and did so before this change. The count of files was right; the consequence was not. **What did NOT come out, named rather than left to be found: the `values` alias.** The plan ends stage 3 with removing it. It is written in one place, the server restore, and every reader in the tree reads `rawData || values` — except `nutrition-calendar.js:701`, which reads `(sample && sample.values) || null` with no fallback, GH-471 having removed the chain on purpose. So the alias is load-bearing for the nutrition programme and removing it means moving a calculation path in a delivery whose subject is the browser copy. **A second reader of the same shape, and then a measurement that CUT THE FINDING DOWN.** `addSample` stores `rawData` and `normalized` and NO `values`, so both of those lines read `null` for a sample built through it rather than restored from the server. This entry first said that meant the calendar “reads null today” for every sample a user typed in. **That was true of the code and false of the product, and the correction is mine: the path exists and no client is on it.** Walked afterwards, every surface named: /data does not call `addSample` at all — it POSTs to /api/samples and reloads; /analysis has the manager but no manual-entry control and no soil form. The two callers that DO reach it are the switcher's “Save as Sample” and `lab-report-parser.js`, and `lab-report-parser.js` is loaded by four views only: hub.blade.php and the three /reports pages, where `legacy-hub-markup.blade.php` is included inside `<div id="rp-hub-runner">` (export :203-204, forensic :58-59, scenarios :76-77), which carries `display:none !important` and `pointer-events:none`. All five targets the parser injects its button into resolve inside that partial and nowhere else — `.gaip-header-controls` and `.gaip-run-btn` are declared there; `.gaip-sample-switcher-header` is built by the switcher, whose four mount points are each declared there and only there; `#gaip-dashboard-actions-slot` is built by `daily-dashboard.js`, which inserts into `#gaip-hub` before `.gaip-grid`, both declared there; and `.gaip-sample-toolbar` **does not exist in the tree at all**. The parser's OTHER entry, the delegated click on `#gaip-soil-pdf-import-btn` / `#gaip-water-pdf-import-btn`, is declared in the same partial, lines 418 and 575. `reports/accuracy.blade.php` is the one view holding a dashboard slot outside the runner, and it does not load the parser at all — nor is that slot visible, `style="display:none"` at :132. **So: the reading is real, the two readers are real, and the defect is out of a client's reach on every surface checked. Closed by measurement rather than by a fix, and not raised as a defect of its own.** Both facts about the shape stay asserted in `tests/gh536-browser-copy-removed.test.js` so neither can go quiet. **The boundary of that walk, stated because it is the same one another piece of work hit the same evening:** it was established by READING `assets/` and `app/resources/views/`, with no live DOM — the task forbade opening pages and the reading answered. Markup that only arrives at runtime could add a target, and nothing here rules that out. **Also not done, deliberately:** the orphan `gilba_samples` blob in the browsers of existing clients is not deleted. GH-442 set the precedent for a one-time cleanup in this exact file; the plan did not ask for one and it is a separate small item. **Self-checked before delivery, control run green first, five mutations.** Not locking on error — 6 red. Lock defaulting to closed — 1 red, and it is the morning-briefing trap. Short read not detected — 1 red. **The fourth stayed GREEN and that is why a sixth test file exists:** putting the /hub active-site call back behind a dead condition left the source pin untouched, because a pin on the strings in a block proves the strings. The block is now RUN in `gh536-hub-active-site-survives-the-key.test.js`, and against that the same mutation goes 2 red and deleting the block outright — the exact defect Н3 warns about — goes 3 red. Files restored and verified by md5. **Live on Burns — 019e96d8-97b7-714c-9bd6-d65b16ec7f2e, sample `Soil_1_y6pb` server id 28 — expectation written into the file before the run and every line met.** Ordinary load: source `server`, store open, 26 soil samples, the named sample at `serverId` 28, **no `gilba_samples` key in localStorage at all**. `GET /api/samples` aborted in the browser so the stand is never touched to produce the failure: source `error`, ready flag still true, store locked, `addSample` threw `Samples are not loaded — retry first`, 0 soil samples, banner on the page with the text to the character, still no key.
