**GH-537** A page loads the samples of the site it is open on. Owner's decision. **What it replaces.** Every page asked for `samples?limit=200` with no site at all — the whole account, first 200 rows, on a page showing one site. **The server needed nothing and was not touched:** `site_id` has been a `nullable` rule in `SampleController::index` since GH-526 and is applied to the query when present, so the request stays legal without it. We are not tightening the server; we are stopping asking it for everything. **And `restoreLimit` changes meaning:** it was a cap on the account, it is now a cap on one site. The most populous site on the stand holds 31 rows, 29 of them live. The partial-read detection stage 3 added is NOT removed — a truncated read is still truncated, the lock and the event stay — but the case where the truncation was caused by the SIZE OF THE ACCOUNT is gone. **THE RISK THIS CHANGE CARRIES, walked before a line was written, because it is the kind that goes quiet.** Something could depend on the store holding EVERY site's samples. It does. `word-export-combined.js`'s `enumerateSamples('all')` walks every site in the store and offers them in one picker — **measured on /reports/export before the change: 35 samples in 9 site groups.** Narrow the load everywhere and that becomes a one-site picker, silently: a client exporting several sites would get a document missing most of them and no symptom. So four views keep the all-sites load — /hub and the three /reports pages — and they are the same four that carry a control changing site WITHOUT reloading (`site-selector-ui.js`, `sample-switcher-ui.js`, `turf-profile-controller.js`). Everywhere else a site change goes through `dashboard-ui.js`, which PATCHes the pointer and reloads, so the next restore asks for the new site anyway. **The exception is read off the page, not declared by it.** No new flag: `window.GAIP_CombinedExport` exists on exactly those four views and no other. **What makes that safe is not the load order, which runs the other way:** `sample-persistence.js` is loaded BEFORE `word-export-combined.js` on all four (hub 200/205, export 276/287, scenarios 147/156, forensic 128/137), all of them with `defer`, so `init()` fires immediately and the global does not exist when this module loads. It exists by the time the question is ASKED — `restoreSiteId()` is read inside `fetchSamplesFromServer()`, itself inside the callback of `fetchSiteListFromServer()`, so the decision is taken after a network response and long after the deferred queue has run out. **This entry first said the opposite on both counts** — that the restore waits for DOMContentLoaded and that the module loads after this one — which would have told a reader the order protects them; the reviewer measured the real mechanism and the docblock carries the same correction. That the set is exactly those four is asserted from both sides rather than described, so a fifth view loading `word-export-combined.js` turns the pin red instead of changing the rule in silence. `stadium.blade.php` looks like a counter-example and is not: it loads the site-switching controls but NOT `sample-persistence.js`, so nothing restores there. **Everything else that reads across sites was walked too and none of it is reachable this way:** `settings-init.js` counts an imported BUNDLE, not the store; `site-data-transfer.js` indexes one site at a time; `site-dashboard.js`'s whole-account `exportAll()` sits inside the hidden `#rp-hub-runner` on every view that loads it; every other `allSites` read in the tree indexes by a named `siteId`. **The site REGISTRY is not narrowed with the samples** — it comes from `GET /api/sites`, which this change does not touch, and it is what the site switcher renders. Asserted, because narrowing it would be the same defect wearing a different hat. **The two numbers, asked for explicitly.** The path sees the LIVE count, not the row count: Burns by type is soil 26/26, tissue 4/2, water 1/1 — 31 rows, **29 live, and 29 is what the store holds**. Nothing on this path carries `withTrashed`. **Self-checked, control run green first, two mutations:** dropping the `site_id` from the URL — red; removing the cross-site exception so /reports asks for one site — red. File restored and verified by md5. **Live, expectation written into the file before the run, three sites named, every line met.** /analysis on Burns: **one** request, `samples?limit=200&site_id=019e96d8-…`, 29 samples in the store, **exactly one site with samples**, registry still 13 sites, ready event carrying `siteId`. /analysis on Westview: `site_id=019f7d28-…`, its single sample under `sample_118` at `serverId` 118 — the key its NULL `client_uid` forces. /reports/export: request with **no** `site_id`, 9 sites with samples in the store, and the picker still enumerating **35 samples across 9 site groups** — the capability this change could have removed, measured intact. The guard held 0 writes because nothing tried to write a protected table; 21 requests reached the server, GET and the two `PATCH /api/active-site` this run makes and puts back. **One assertion of mine went red on its own run and the assertion was what was wrong:** it compared Burns's SOIL count against 29, which is the count across all four types. Corrected to compare like with like and the per-type figures written into the file so the next reader does not repeat it. Stand before and after: 0 differing lines, 24 configs, 148 samples, 109 sites, predictions 1534, four marked rows intact. PHPUnit 200 passed, 0 failed — `app/` was not touched, run to show it. Jest 3,053 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-538** The stand-restore remedy can put back what it captures. Question 39, closed by two round trips rather than by a diff. **What was broken, and it was the half nobody checks.** `stand-guard.js`'s `sqlRaw()` passed the whole statement as one `argv` element after `mysql -e`. For the short SELECTs around it that is fine; for `restoreConfigs()` it is not, because that statement carries the row's entire content as base64 and every `analysis_cache` row on the stand is 209-234 KB of it. Linux caps a SINGLE argv element at 128 KB, so the exec never happened: `exec /usr/bin/mysql: argument list too long`. **The limit is on one ARGUMENT, not on the total** — the host's ARG_MAX is 1 MB and was never in the way, which is where the first guess went. **Detection kept working the whole time and only the repair failed, which is the worse half to lose:** a remedy that reports a failure it cannot fix still counts as “a remedy is named” to the GH-532 census, so the file reads as covered. **The fix, and the direction was already written in the question:** the statement travels on the child's stdin — `docker exec -i`, the same shape as `mysql < file`, which is how the one hand-repair of this kind was done. The payload never enters argv, so the ceiling is not in the path at all. Measured on the largest row present, a 468 KB statement: through argv it throws the message above, through stdin it answers. **A second defect in the same function went with it.** `stdio` discarded stderr, which is why a failed restore could say THAT it failed and never WHY — that sentence had to be recovered by re-running the command by hand. It is captured and attached to the error, with the statement's length beside it. **All five `sqlRaw` call sites moved together and all five were exercised by the round trip:** the capture's SELECT, the restore's two SELECTs and its UPDATE, and this file's own reads. Nothing else in the tree calls it. **What makes this the acceptance rather than the change.** Question 39 is done when a REAL row over the limit has been taken, damaged, put back and compared byte for byte, printed. `gh538-stand-restore-round-trip-live.test.js` does that on **Test1 - Sports** (`analysis_cache`, 168 100 bytes, **224 136 base64 — over the ceiling**, the case that could not be repaired at all) and on **Westview** (68 306 bytes, 91 076 base64 — under it, so the path that already worked is shown still to work). Chosen because neither is one of the four marked configuration rows, the Test5 - NZ trace, or Canberra, which was repaired by hand earlier; and neither appears in another live test's pair list. Both came back with their md5, their length AND their timestamp: `6e265e4a…` / 168 100 / 1786331199 and `a580c178…` / 68 306 / 1789655791, printed before and after. **The safety was not the remedy's own capture,** because that capture is the thing under test and trusting it to hold the only copy is the mistake this exists because of. An independent byte copy of each row is written to disk and verified against the database's own md5 BEFORE anything is damaged, and `afterAll` repairs from those files by the manual path if the remedy does not. **It fired, and that is the positive control:** with the old argv `sqlRaw` put back, the run went 3 red of 5 — Westview restored, Test1 - Sports failed with the 1054-shaped message quoted in the report — and the file repaired the damaged row from its own copy in the same run. A damaged row did not outlive it. **The open discrepancy inside Question 39 is closed, and by a date rather than by a method.** Eleven unrestorable rows against nine: both counts are right for their moment and both were taken the same way, base64 with the line breaks stripped. The eleven came from the 09:20:38 content backup; Federal Golf and Russley shrank from ~228 KB to 783 and 1 325 bytes at **11:26:16 and 11:26:24**, two hours after that snapshot was written. The coordinator's objection assumed the measurement's date was when the command ran; it was when the DATA was captured. The number is moot for the question either way — after this change the count of rows the remedy cannot put back is zero at any size. **And a smaller one settled in passing:** 1 768 against 1 791 and 1 044 against 1 057 was the method after all — `LENGTH(TO_BASE64(config))` counts the newline MySQL inserts every 76 characters, `REPLACE`-stripped does not. 1791−1768 = 23 with 23 expected breaks, 1057−1044 = 13 with 13. The stripped figure is the one that matters, because that is the form the remedy sends. **Not done, and named rather than assumed:** the fourteen live tests still under the no-run rule stay under it. Their remedy now works on their data, so the reason for the rule is weaker than it was, but lifting it is the owner's call and not a side effect of this change. Stand before and after: 0 differing lines, 24 configs, 148 samples, 109 sites, predictions 1534, four marked rows intact — across three runs, two of which deliberately damaged two rows. PHPUnit 200 passed, 0 failed — `app/` was not touched, run to show it. Jest 3,059 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-541** The Account site list shows each site's soil-test methodology. The owner asked for it as a checking place — “where I look to see what is set where” — and that is what settles how it is built: a column people come to in order to find out what is set cannot be quietly wrong. **The value is each row's own.** `AccountController::show()` already resolves `$turfMethodology`, for the ACTIVE site; `buildSitesTableData()` builds one row per site and now reads `config.turf.methodology` out of the `$gaip` it already holds for THAT site. Reaching for the first from the second would print the active site's setting under every other site's name — **GH-459's shape exactly**, one object's data beside another object's label, which cost a client another site's climate in his own report while the annual totals still agreed and nothing went red. Both tests are built against that specific failure and use sites with DIFFERENT methodologies, because with one site the right reading and the wrong one agree. **One owner, and it was not re-derived.** `config.turf.methodology` is the only place any surface may read it from — settled by the owner on 18.09.2026 and recorded in CLAUDE.md with “This has been decided once. Do not re-derive it from the code.” `sites.methodology_override` is not consulted; it is empty on all 109 sites and that is the expected state, not a defect. Nothing is derived from coordinates, from a sample stamp or from anything on the page. **An empty setting prints “methodology not set” and nothing is substituted** — not `mlsn`, not a default. The other columns use an em dash for “nothing here”; this column says “no setting” instead, because that is the distinction the screen exists to show. **The words are the Settings form's own**, `$methOptions` in `settings.blade.php`, shortened to what fits a cell: the select can afford “MLSN — Minimum Levels for Sustainable Nutrition” and a column cannot. **The case is deliberately NOT `strtoupper()`,** which `show()` uses for the single active-site line: applied to a column it yields `AMMONIUM_ACETATE`, the storage key shouted, sitting next to “Browntop Bent”. MLSN and SLAN stay upper because they are acronyms. An unknown key is printed as it is rather than hidden — a value the Settings form cannot produce is worth seeing on a screen whose purpose is to show what is set — and a PHPUnit test reads the key list OUT of `settings.blade.php` and goes red if a fourth methodology is added there without a label here. **Also stated rather than left off:** the row a freshly created site pushes into the table carries `methodology: null` explicitly. It renders the same today either way, and stops doing so the first time that cell reads anything but truthiness. **Live on the stand, expectation written into the file before the run, three sites named and every line met.** Active site Burns/`mlsn`, so a row taking the page's value would read MLSN everywhere: Burns **MLSN**, Test - GC - NZ - delivery **Ammonium Acetate**, Federal Golf **SLAN** — three distinct values, 12 rows on screen, column between Grass and Soil, no row printing “not set” because every site on the stand has one. The guard held nothing because the page only reads. **Two of my own assertions went red on the way and both were the assertion, not the product:** the active site lives in `users.last_active_site_id`, not `active_site_id`, and the view receives the rows as `sitesTableData`, not `sites`. PHPUnit 203 passed, 0 failed. Jest 3,059 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-543** The Account site list stops hiding its right-hand columns. The owner, on the methodology column shipped the same day: “now not all the information is shown, it is as if it hid under the panel” — and, asked whether to fix or revert, “no, fix it now. We need this column.” **Measured in the browser, because the markup could not answer it.** The ninth `<th>` was the only change, and the wrapper and the table's own widths were exactly what they had been when eight fitted. Three widths, and the same picture at all three: the table renders **1213px inside a panel of 1044**, with **Users and the row buttons past the right edge** — at 1024 the Last run column as well. **Not one cell was clipped**: `client` equalled `scroll` in all nine. Nothing was truncated; part of the table was simply not on the page. **And a wide window did not help**, which is the half that made it look like a cell problem: the panel measured **1044 at 1280 AND at 1680**, because `.stg-wrap` is capped at 1100px. **The 360px the Site column was holding was not the methodology's doing.** `.stg-st-name-wrap` forbade wrapping, and one site is called “Test - GC - NZ - warm season grass test” — 39 characters. A column is as wide as its widest row, and that row set it. **The fix is one declaration:** that class goes from `nowrap` to `normal`, plus `flex-wrap` so the type badge drops under a wrapped name rather than being squeezed against it. Chosen over widening the panel because `.stg-wrap` is shared with Settings, which nobody had complained about; `.stg-st-name-wrap` occurs once in the whole tree. **Verified at three widths: Site 360 → 124px, table 1213 → 1044, and at 1280 and 1680 nothing is past the edge at all.** At 1024 **30px remain, and they are the buttons column**, which the wrapper already scrolls — reported as a number rather than chased to zero with a re-layout. The longest name is shown WHOLE, wrapped across two lines, and is on the screenshot the owner was given, scrolled into view: the worst case, not a convenient row. **Three runs were used where one was budgeted and both extra ones were mine.** The first: my edit script failed on a mismatched anchor, wrote nothing, and the run went out against the unchanged file — I had not checked that the edit applied before starting it. The second: I asserted `getClientRects().length > 1` as a line count and it answered 1 for a name that cannot fit on one line in 124px; that measured the probe, not the screen, and was replaced by whether the name is clipped and how tall it renders. Jest 3,059 passed, 0 failed. PHPUnit 203 passed, 0 failed. Stand: 0 differing lines.

**GH-544** The panel is no longer capped on the right, on both screens that use it. The owner's decision, 19.09.2026: “can it just be the full page width, why are we limiting it on the right, and then we won't have the problem of site names and locations shifting.” That removes the reason the sites table had to choose between its columns at all, and it reverses a coordinator's call from the same morning that had refused this as scope creep — what looked like reaching into a second screen was the intent. **One declaration out:** `max-width: 1100px` on `.stg-wrap`. **There was no `margin: auto`**, checked before the change and not after: the block was left-aligned under a ceiling and is left-aligned without one, so nothing de-centred — asserted at every width rather than eyeballed. **The earlier fix is deliberately NOT reverted.** `white-space: normal` does not force a name to wrap, it allows one: with the panel wide the column takes the room and the names go back to a single line by themselves; on a narrow laptop they wrap instead of pushing the buttons off screen. Measured across the three widths on one row — the 39-character site — the name renders 96px tall at 1024, 32px at 1280 and **16px, one line, at 1680**, with the row 158 / 94 / **62px**. Neither change gives that alone. **Both screens were photographed, because both were touched.** Panel width tracks the window: 964 of 1024, 1220 of 1280, 1620 of 1680, on Account and on Settings alike. The sites table **fits with room** at 1280 (1164) and 1680 (1564); at 1024 the 30px remain, unchanged, because the cap was never what bound that width. **Settings was widened without a complaint against it,** so the run is the evidence rather than the argument: the form fields keep their own caps — 400 / 300 / 360 / 400px, each on the field and not on the panel — and what has no cap of its own and therefore does stretch is listed by name and width: `stg-page-head`, `stg-page-title`, `stg-panel` and the cards, all full-width containers doing what containers do. The owner was told Settings would change before it did; her answer came while the run was going: “you can make them the same.” Jest 3,059 passed, 0 failed. PHPUnit 203 passed, 0 failed. Stand: 0 differing lines.

**GH-545** A page waits fifteen seconds for live weather instead of five, and the number says of itself that it is a stopgap. **Written 22.09.2026 as a missing record: the change had shipped, the code carried the ticket number and a live test carried it too, and this changelog had no GH-545 entry at all.** **What was wrong.** A client could not get the daily average GP table to compute: `Weather fetch timeout after 5s`, then the fallback climate metrics, then `Schedule error: No forecast data available`. The weather did not arrive and **the calculation continued on substituted values** — the table vanished while everything else printed as usual. **What changed, and only this.** `weather-resilience.js`, the race that gives up on live weather: 5 000 ms → 15 000 ms. **The number is also built into the error text**, so the text is now assembled from the constant rather than repeating it — before this change the file said three different things in three places: `5000` in the code, `after 5s` in the message, and `12s` in the comment above them. The comment is corrected to match. **Why fifteen.** The author of this code intended TWELVE — that is what the comment said, though five went into the code — so fifteen is a value of the same order rather than an invented one. And the request is not small: Open-Meteo, `forecast_days: 16`, hourly, about ten variables, 384 points per variable, and on the failing run an archive call as well, both inside one race. **THE REAL CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the code says so where the number is.** Whether the request leaves the client's host at all, or leaves and is merely slow, is not known; the two need different fixes and can only be told apart from that machine. **Fifteen seconds help only in the second case, and the fact that it helped does not prove which case it was.** The owner confirmed the symptom is gone: the client's table computes. **The cost is measured.** When weather really is unavailable the page now waits 17 s instead of ~5, and for all of it the user sees a `Weather: Loading...` badge — not blank space and not stale figures. With an instantly unreachable provider the fallback still lands in 2.2 s: the fifteen seconds bite only a hung request. Live run 3/3, Jest 3 059 passed, PHPUnit 203 passed. The open unknown is Question 42 in `PLAN-remaining-defects-RU.md`.

**GH-546** The analysis result gets a form and an owner. Stages 0 and 1 of `PLAN-Q31-analysis-cache-intent-RU.md`. No live test was run and the stand was not touched — reads only. **Stage 0, the form.** `assets/analysis-result.schema.json` declares what a complete result is: 13 required `metrics` keys, two conditional (`companionDisease` on a companion surface, `vwc` with a sensor), two branch-dependent, and the 17 top-level `computed` keys consumers read. The numbers come from three sources that agree: the producer read from source (`collectDashboardMetrics` can emit 17 keys), the twelve rows on the stand read with SELECT, and the consumers. `gh546-analysis-result-form.test.js` compares schema and producer IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — a key added to the producer and not declared goes red, and so does a key declared that the producer cannot emit — with a guard that the extraction found the function at all, because an empty set agrees with an empty schema. Self-checked: adding a key to the producer turns it red. **The stage's finding, and it corrects the plan.** The plan says in section 4 that no run today emits `et` or `gdd`, and in section 1 that they come from `collectDashboardMetrics`'s `_cm` branch. **Section 1 is right:** Federal Golf's five-key row carries both. What the stand then shows is worth more than the correction — all eleven full rows went through the OTHER branch (`_cc`, no `gdd`/`et`), and the one `_cm` row is the thinnest on the stand. The branch is not chosen by whether the run completed, so a body built from this schema has to decide which branch is the contract instead of inheriting whichever fired. Declared, named, left to stage 2. **Stage 1, the owner.** `App\Support\AnalysisResults` is the only PHP that may name the result's storage: `record` / `forSite` / `forSites` / `statusMap`. Ten places named it before — one writer and nine readers, **eight of them assembling the identical three-key array by hand**. All now take one projection, which already carries the `lastRun` and `status` that stage 2 fills, so the readers are touched once rather than twice. `gh546-analysis-results-single-owner.test.js` walks every PHP file under `app/app` and allows exactly one exemption — the owner — in the shape of GH-447, and asserts the nine readers actually go through the projection rather than merely having stopped reading. **The permission that was not there.** `POST /api/analysis-cache` took `site_id` out of the request body and wrote it with no `canEditSite`, no `canViewSite`, no `authorize` and no `abort` — any signed-in person could replace any site's result by naming its id, while `SampleController` has carried the same check in six places all along. It stands at the service entrance, not in the controller, so the failure-report route stage 2 adds goes through the same check instead of a second copy. A viewer gets 403 and **the row is unchanged** — asserted by hash, because the refusal on its own is not the point. An unknown site is 404: `site_id` used to go straight to `SiteConfigWriter::mutate`, which creates what it cannot find, and the producer falls back to the literal `'default'`, so an orphan configuration row was one missing pointer away. **Question 43, in the same stage.** `SampleAnalysisController` no longer reads the analysis cache at all. It used to begin its answer with the whole `computed.soilNutrition` of the site's last BROWSER run and overwrite eight of its nineteen keys, so `zones`, `annualDemand`, `monthlyN`, `tissue`, `depthCm`, `bulkDensity`, `turfType`, `species` and `fromSample` reached the page from whichever sample was active during that run, under the requested sample's label — one object's data beside another object's name inside a single response. **And the dependency was hiding a wrong table:** the controller's own `MLSN_DEFAULTS` agreed with the product on the four macronutrients and disagreed on all five micronutrients — **Fe 49 against 2, Mn 5 against 1, Zn 2.2 against 1, Cu 0.9 against 0.3, B 0.5 against 0.3** — and it only applied to a site that had never had a Re-run, because otherwise the cached thresholds won. The same sample classified one way before a Re-run and another way after. The values now live in `App\Support\ClassificationConstants` with the canonical numbers, and `gh546-mlsn-thresholds-parity.test.js` reads both files and compares them nutrient by nutrient, naming the five old numbers so the fix cannot quietly revert. Where 49/5/2.2/0.9/0.5 came from is not established. **Four tests went red by meaning and none was made green by being weakened.** Five unit files call `computeNutrients` through reflection; four carried a helper whose signature lost two parameters, and the fifth never called it — the plan counted five. `NutrientOrderTest`'s “present cache wins over the fallback” lost its subject; the plan said delete it, and it was **rewritten instead** to assert the consequence — a cached list can no longer change the answer, so the ten canonical nutrients come back where the cache named one. `gh447` went red because `AnalysisCacheController` stopped calling `SiteConfigWriter`: its entry moved to `AnalysisResults`, and an assertion was added that the controller really did stop writing, so shortening that list cannot become a way past the guard. **Two places where the plan and the tree differ, reported rather than worked around.** Its stage-1 line says “`stand-guard.js` — new route”, but stage 1 adds no route: the failure report is stage 2's. Read as widening the guard, which was anchored at `(\?|$)` and covered the exact path and nothing under it — stage 2's `/api/analysis-cache/runs` would have arrived unguarded while the guard still reported that it protects that table. Widened to `(\/|\?|$)`, matching its own neighbours. And the composer's hand-built query fed a second block the inventory does not name — the “Analysis: <date>” pill — which broke when the query went and now takes the same projection. **Not done, by the brief:** stage 2 and beyond; no live test; no stand write; the divergence list is a list. Stand unchanged by this work — the 18 lines that differ from 19.09 are dated 19 and 20.09 and the plan records them. PHPUnit 212 passed, 0 failed. Jest 3,079 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-547** The analysis result is written once, by a runner that was opened as one. Stage 2 of `PLAN-Q31-analysis-cache-intent-RU.md`. No live test was run and the stand was not touched. **Three writers become one, and the two that go were never acts of a person.** `save()` posted the result on EVERY state save — every `input` and `change` inside `#gaip-hub` plus fourteen `gaip:*` events including a site switch — with a body of “everything the page holds at this instant”. The sensor re-sync posted a SECOND result for the same run; if a late reading changes the answer it belongs to the run and goes in the one send at the end of it. Both are gone, and `GILBA_REPORTS_EXPORT` with them: the flag fenced off `syncToServer` in ONE view of the four that load the bundle, which is exactly why /reports/forensic and /reports/scenarios wrote on every plain open. A prohibition is a permission turned inside out and it is forgotten on the next view that embeds the bundle. **Who writes is now an intention, not a circumstance.** The page decided it was the runner from `window.parent !== window` — true in any frame at all, a harness included, which is how a result was posted from /reports/export on a night when the weather hung. It writes only when opened as `/hub?rerun=<runId>&site=<siteId>`, both required, **and the site travels as a parameter rather than being read from the active-site pointer** — the pointer belongs to whatever the user is looking at now, and it can move in another tab between the press and the write. Asserted with the pointer deliberately set to a DIFFERENT site. **When it writes is three events, not a clock.** Weather ready, orchestrator complete, and the analysis reporting `gaip:analysis-complete` without `detail.error`. The three-second delay after the engines spoke and the ten-second path that fired whether they had spoken or not are gone; **the ten-second one is the likeliest author of the row on the stand carrying twelve keys instead of thirteen**, because it fires before the weather and `weatherSource` is written from the weather's own answer. If the three do not arrive inside the same fifteen seconds the weather fetch is allowed (GH-545), the runner **writes nothing** and reports `run-not-completed`. **A run that did not finish no longer looks like one that did.** The openers reloaded on ANY message and on a thirty-second timer besides, and `_signalRerunComplete()` was sent even when the POST failed — so a refused or empty run ended with the page reloading onto the PREVIOUS result while the button reported success. `gilba:analysis-complete` and `gilba:analysis-failed` are now objects carrying the run they are about, the opener matches on `runId`, and **a failure does not reload**: the dashboard restores the button and names the reason, the Settings import stays on Settings with “the import was saved, the previous analysis is kept” instead of sending the user to the dashboard to look at old numbers as though the import had produced them. A **403 is a failure too** — the code the viewer check from stage 1 now returns. **`alert()` is gone from the runner.** Two of them, in `hub-tissue-v3.js`'s cascade and top-level catch. They fired inside a hidden iframe, where a modal has nobody to dismiss it and stops that frame's JavaScript — its timers included — until somebody who cannot see it presses OK. The message travels on the event instead and reaches the opener as `calculation-error` with its text. **The disease copy stops being written** (K2 of the plan's browser-copy list): `gilba_disease_cache_<site>`. Its reader served a copy up to twenty-four hours old as current and, past six hours, served it “immediately … then triggered a silent background recalculation” — the old figures shown while new ones are computed behind them, which is the same copy with a delay. **The READER is not changed and that is a named boundary:** /field-log's own path without the copy is “recalculating with stripped-down hardcoded inputs”, a substitution of a different kind that belongs to `PLAN-no-substitution-surfaces-RU.md`. **A real race in the new code, found by its own sandbox and not by reading.** `_writeResult` awaits the bounded normals wait before posting, and two completion events can arrive inside that gap — the orchestrator's and the analysis's — so a latch that closed only on the server's reply let both through and sent the same result twice. The sandbox said 2 where it wanted 1. The latch is set synchronously at the top of the write. **Five tests went red by meaning; each says what it now bites on.** `gh251` — the bounded normals wait is asserted against `_writeResult` instead of the deleted `_doRerunSync`, and “the sensor call site is untouched” became **“there is no second writer”**: no listener for the sensor event, exactly one POST to the route in the file, and it is inside the completion path. `gh298` — the render-before-save ORDER moved intact, and its third clause became “the render happens once, on the one path that writes”. `gh539` — its verdict inverts: **no opened page writes, /hub included**, and a zero for /hub is the finding. `gh540` — the verdict survives and the reason does not: all four pages read zero, the two that used to write for a different reason than export's. `gh542` — “a press produces a write” became “exactly one write”, so a second POST from a late sensor is now a defect rather than normal. The three live ones are **rewritten but NOT run** — live tests are banned for this work — and each says so in its own docblock rather than leaving it to be discovered on the first run after the ban. **A new sandbox, 14 cases** (`gh547-runner-writes-once-on-completion.test.js`): a plain page and a framed page without parameters write nothing however much is fired at them; one parameter is not enough; a completed run writes once and files it under the site the opener named; weather alone is not completion; no weather means no write at fourteen seconds; `save()` no longer posts; a late sensor produces no second result; and the four failure paths report their reason without claiming success. **Not done, by the brief:** stage 3 — the pill, the panels and `dashboard-init` without `localStorage`. The failure reason reaches the console and `window.GilbaRerunOutcome` today; the screen gets it next. Jest 3,093 passed, 0 failed. PHPUnit 212 passed, 0 failed.



**GH-548** A re-run that did not finish says so, on every screen that prints the numbers it failed to replace. Stage 3 of `PLAN-Q31-analysis-cache-intent-RU.md`. No live test was run and the stand was not touched. **What the owner decided, 22.09.2026:** the previous result stays with its own date, and it is signed — "it needs to be written somewhere that this is an old calculation, and that the calculation did not happen for such-and-such a reason, and that it should be tried again". **Until now the reason existed for one tab and about thirty seconds.** A failed run reached a `console.warn` and `window.GilbaRerunOutcome` in the browser that pressed the button: gone on the next reload, absent on a second device, and absent for whoever opens the dashboard tomorrow and reads week-old figures as today's. The runner now files the failure — `POST /api/analysis-cache/runs` — and `AnalysisResults::recordFailure()` writes the reason into the same row as the numbers, so every reader of the projection gets it. **It writes the reason and NOTHING else:** `metrics` and `computed` are untouched and `synced_at` does not move, because `synced_at` is the date OF THE NUMBERS and a failure is not a fresher version of them. Asserted by hash rather than by looking. On a site with no result at all the stamp stays null, so a run that produced nothing does not date the nothing. `SiteConfigWriter::mutate` gained one parameter for that and it is the only caller. **The sign clears itself:** a completed result is a replacement and is now signed with its own `run_id`, so the mark from an earlier attempt goes with the numbers it was about — nobody has to dismiss anything. **One panel, one pill, one set of words.** The notification bar existed on three screens as three copies of the same markup, and its text was built twice in JavaScript out of `analyzedAt`, so the only thing it could ever say was how old the data was. It is now `partials/analysis-notice.blade.php` on six templates and `partials/analysis-pill.blade.php` on three, and the words come from `App\Support\AnalysisNotice` — a function of the projection and the site's own timezone, of nothing on the page. **The plan is diverged from here and it is named:** it put the reason-to-sentence map in `dashboard-ui.js` and the pill on the server, which is two maps in two languages, and the failure this whole question is about is one thing described twice drifting apart. The map is in PHP; the browser is handed it with the pill (`GAIP_ANALYSIS_TEXTS`) and looks codes up in it. A jest test reads the sentences OUT of the PHP and fails if any of them reappears in an asset. **The pill stops being rewritten after load.** `initAnalysisTimestamp()` in `dashboard-ui.js` and `populateTimestamp()` in `dashboard-init.js` both re-derived it from `analyzedAt` — the one label that cannot say a run failed — so the server's mark survived until the page finished loading and no longer. **The opener does not wait for a reload to speak.** A failed run still does not reload the page (GH-547), so the reason goes onto the panel there and then, from the same map; Settings' import box stops printing the bare code in brackets. **Two browser copies go.** K1: `gilba_hub_cache`, the browser's own copy of the whole result — the write, the read, and the key an older bundle left behind, which is now cleared on load rather than served as current for the rest of its twenty-four hours. The dashboard read it whenever the server had nothing, so an empty screen and a week-old screen looked alike; the server is now the only source and nothing is an outcome ("no analysis has been run for this site yet"). K3: `gilba_hub_state.turf.nProgram`, read by `soil-nutrition-analysis.js` to compute annual nutrient requirements the run had not produced — **and the substitute was worse than the copy.** `annualDemand` is produced by a run, not by a sample, so a site that had never been analysed printed kg/ha/yr in the same cards as one that had; and where the browser had no copy the formula fell back to a flat 150 or 180 kg N/ha, a default nobody entered, printed as this site's programme. `calcAnnualDemand`, `ANNUAL_RATIOS` and `readNProgramFromStorage` are gone and the section says what happened instead. **The sensor and weather copies on the dashboard are deliberately untouched** — a different object, items D1–D3 of the plan's list, carried in the main defects document — and a test says so, so that "left" is distinguishable from "missed". **Three tests went red by meaning.** `gh547` — its post filter was `/analysis-cache/`, which also matches the new `/analysis-cache/runs`, so a failure report would have counted as a result write; the filter is anchored and four failure paths now assert that the reason is FILED as well as announced. `gh251` — "save() calls cacheAnalysisResults without an await" lost its subject, because `save()` does not call it at all now; the assertion became "save assembles no result and touches no cache key", which contains the old one. `Gh546AnalysisResultsOwnerTest` — `run_id` is required on the result write, and the projection's `lastRun` is no longer empty. **Seventeen PHPUnit cases and sixteen jest ones are new,** and the screen ones render the pages rather than searching the templates: removing the panel from `plan.blade.php` reddens exactly one case and names it. **The plan counts six screens and four can be reached:** `/analysis/growth-light` and `/analysis/disease` are `redirect()`s to the SPA's tabs, so their templates are not rendered by any route today. Both were wired up anyway and a test states both halves, so reviving a route cannot quietly revive a screen that says nothing. **NOT DONE, and it is a red test rather than a silence:** `gh477`, the substitution ratchet, went red on `hub-persistence.js | label | || | POST | sid`. It is real and it is not new — `cacheAnalysisResults()` names a soil zone by its storage key when the sample has no label, and that goes to the server inside `computed.soilNutrition.zones` — but the guard had never seen it, because its own path to it runs through a computed member assignment. The new failure POST opened a second path by name aliasing and it surfaced. What an unlabelled zone should be called is the owner's (class 10.8), the ratchet allows the list to shrink and not to grow, and both narrow repairs to the guard were measured and cost real coverage (−5 entries including four genuine, or −3), so nothing was touched. **GH-549** A soil zone with no name is not given one. **The owner's decision, 22.09.2026, in two parts:** "do not substitute — on screen 'a zone with no name', and group by identifier internally without showing it", then, extending it to the report, "it must be the same as in the interface. If there is no name, there is none in the interface either, but the sample itself is displayed." Skipping unnamed samples was ruled out by name. **What was there, and the substitute was not even an identifier.** `cacheAnalysisResults()` keyed its zone map by `s.label || sid` and stored that same string as the zone's NAME — and `GAIP_SampleManager.getSamples()` returns `Object.values(...)`, an ARRAY, so `sid` is the array index. An unnamed soil sample was drawn on /analysis as a zone called **"0"**, the entry's `id` field carried the same index, and both went to the server inside `computed.soilNutrition.zones`. **The key and the name are now different things.** The key is `GaipZoneKey.derive()` — the zone identity this project already shares with the trend charts and the Word export (b35fix311_1) — so "Green 1 (June 2025)" and "Green 1 Q1 2024" stay one zone, which keying on the sample's own id would have broken by splitting every named zone into one bar per visit. The name is the label or nothing; `id` is the sample's own id or null. **What is printed is nothing, and the choice is argued rather than defaulted.** The owner offered two forms — an empty place or an explicit mark — and left the wording here. Numbering them was ruled out — a position number is a name nobody gave the zone and it moves when the sort moves — and grouping is unaffected, because grouping is the key. **Sorting changed with it:** an absent name sorted as an empty string put the unnamed zone at the TOP of the list, above every named one; named zones now sort above unnamed, with alerts still winning over both, so an unnamed zone with a deficit is not buried. **One word, two surfaces.** `GaipZoneKey.displayName()` is where the answer lives, because the Word export must give the same one and already loads that module; `/analysis` did not, and now does, before the file that uses it. **The report is NOT changed here** — `word-export-combined.js` carries the same substitution in its own words and is a separate delivery, Question 58, and so is `nutrient-trend.js`, whose surfaces are /hub and the three reports pages. **What the red test was really about, corrected by the reviewer.** `gh477` reddened on `hub-persistence.js | label | || | POST | sid` while GH-548 was being accepted. The substitution is real; the route the guard named is not. Turning the new failure POST's `method` to `'GET'` cleared the finding, so it hung on THAT request — whose body is `_fail(reason, detail)`'s parameters, and no call site passes a zone. The metric never travelled that way. Its real route is the one the guard cannot see: `computed.soilNutrition.zones` inside the RESULT write, reached through a computed member assignment the inventory does not follow. It went red on a true substitution by a false path. **The evidence for acceptance, both halves.** The inventory: `hub-persistence.js | label | || | POST | sid` is absent from the current scan, and no entry took its place — added: none. The code: `hub-persistence.js`, the zone block, where `|| sid` is gone from both `label` and `id`. Mutations, each with a green control first: restore `|| sid` in the producer → four cases red across `gh549` and `gh477`; make the screen fall back to `z.id` → red; make `displayName()` fall back to `subject.id` → three red. **The reviewer's required finding, closed in the same pass.** `run_id` was required in the code and held there by nothing — `nullable` on both ends left the suite green, because every case supplied one. Two tests, one per end: a result body and a failure body without `run_id` are each 422 and write nothing, and the producer's own sandbox asserts that every body it sends names its run. The mutation now reddens exactly those two. **And the reviewer's optional one, taken:** the plan counts six screens that print analysis numbers and four can be opened — `/analysis/growth-light` and `/analysis/disease` are redirects to the SPA's tabs. Named in `AnalysisController` above `growthLight()` and in section 8.1 of the plan, so whoever restores those routes learns it there rather than from two silent screens. Jest 3,124 passed, 0 failed.
