Mutation reached the subject and named it: restoring `parseFloat(_ions.B) || null` printed `boron measured as 0 -> null` and reddened two cases, including the one that states the whole rule; control green before and after. **ACCEPTED ON LIVE ROWS, both halves, two announced presses.** `Burns` (the only one of eight live water samples carrying boron, `payload.B = 0`): row 63 held `B = null`, the new row 64 holds `B = 0`. `New test - location` (five samples, no `B` key in any, iron present) as the control: row 65 holds `B = null` and `Fe = 0.33`, and its `traceIons` carry no boron — so the absence still says nothing and the repair did not catch the wrong thing. Jest 3346 passed, 0 failed; PHP 339 passed. **ПРИНЯТО, И ТРИ МЕСТА ПЕРЕПИСАНЫ ПО-АНГЛИЙСКИ.** Owner's rule: no Russian in the tree, only in our documents. Two of the three came in with this ticket — the owner's quotation in the producer docblock and the same phrase in the new case — and the third had been standing since the morning: `hub-tissue-v3.js`, the ninety-day quotation added by GH-597, whose own cleanup went through two TEST files and missed the PRODUCT one, so it was counted among the eighteen leftovers while in fact belonging to the same day's work. All three now read as `gh597:13` does — the decision stated, the quotation paraphrased, the meaning kept. Files carrying Cyrillic: 20 before, 17 after; the eighteen earlier ones are untouched, they are their own queue item. **NOTED, NOT REPAIRED, ADDRESS RECORDED:** the last DOM fallback at `hub-persistence.js:2439` still drops zeros — `if (_ik && !isNaN(_iv) && _iv > 0)`, where the `isNaN` guard is already present and it is the comparison that discards a laboratory zero. That path reads page state and belongs to the class already forbidden, so it is a separate subject rather than a second half of this one.

**GH-609** (пункт 3п) The restoration judge called a correct row wrong, and the case that proves it needs no press. The live probe of GH-591 compared the analysis page with the sample using `Number(a) !== Number(b)`, and on `New test - location` it reported eight nutrients disagreeing. The row was right. Measured, row 65 against sample 125: `P 19.6/19.57`, `K 18.8/18.84`, `Ca 240.8/240.77`, `Mg 39.4/39.38`, `S 13.9/13.95`, `Fe 115.7/115.71`, `Mn 30.4/30.35`, `Zn 7.2/7.18` — every one of them the page printing one decimal — and `Cu 2.0/2` agreeing only because `2.0 === 2`. `Burns` passed the same check because its readings survive rounding, so the fault stayed invisible until a site with longer numbers went through. The comparison is a pure function now, `tests/lib/row-vs-sample.js`, and the row's own text decides the precision: a value printed to one decimal is compared to one decimal. Nothing picks an epsilon — a surface that starts printing two decimals tightens the comparison by itself. Its boundary is named in the file: a genuine disagreement smaller than half the printed precision is invisible, which is the price of comparing a rendered number with a measured one, and a value DROPPED is a separate answer needing no precision at all. Moved out of the live file for the reason the defect demonstrates: the check that could only be exercised by pressing Re-run on the stand was the one that was wrong. Mutation reached the subject and named it: restoring `shown !== measured` printed `disagreed: P, K, Ca, Mg, S, Fe, Mn, Zn` and reddened three cases; control green before and after. **AND THE ITEM IT OPENED DOES NOT EXIST:** row 65 carries the sample's figures in `soilNutrition.nutrients[]`; the measurement that reported them empty asked for `soilNutrition.K`, a path the structure does not have — the same literal-path trap this probe's own docblock was written about. Jest 3351 passed, 0 failed; PHP 339 passed.

**GH-610** (пункт 3с) Russian cannot be added to the tree unnoticed. The rule was written on the morning of 23.09.2026 and broken three times the same day — by `gh601`, by `gh597`, and by the boron work, which put it into a product file and a test; files carrying Cyrillic went 18 after the morning sweep, up to 20, and are 17 now, and every breach was caught by a person, twice not by the author. A fifth case states requirement five outright — the comparison is of the LIST, not of its length: a set with one file swapped for another is the same size and must be reported in both directions, which is exactly what a count failed to show this morning when one of the eighteen was there not as a leftover but as that day's work, and the mistake lived nine hours covered by its own number. NO FILE IS EXCLUDED FROM THE WALK, this one included: the range is built from code points, so the file carries no Cyrillic itself — unlike `gh601`, which had to skip itself and said what that cost. AND IT CAUGHT ITS OWN AUTHOR ON THE FIRST RUN: the range had been written as literal characters, the census reported 18 files against a remainder of 17 and named this file. It does not clean the seventeen; that is its own queue item, standing last by the owner's decision. Jest 3355 passed, 0 failed; PHP 339 passed.

**GH-611** (пункт 3д) A row in the ion table now means the lab measured that ion. The eight rows were drawn on `if (ions.X)`, and `ions` is meq/L from `_meq`, which returns `(parseFloat(x) || 0) / factor` — so a carbonate the lab measured and found to be zero and a carbonate nobody tested for are the same `0`, and neither drew a row. Measured on all eight live water samples: `CO3` is the only genuine zero and it is zero on SIX of them (`Burns` 54, `New test - location` 136-140), so six rows the client never saw, with nothing to say whether the water had been tested. The producer now records `measuredIons` beside `ions` — what the sample carried among those eight, in its own units, DERIVED from the same `_mgToMeq` table that decides what `ions` contains, so an ion added there arrives with no second edit. `ions` is untouched and still answers 0 for an absent reading, which is correct: SAR, RSC and LSI need a number for every term, and a case asserts that it stays that way so nobody "fixes" it into agreement. The change is one-directional and that is checked, not claimed: six rows appear, none disappears. A row stored before the producer knew the difference carries no `measuredIons` and is read the old way — inventing an answer for those is worse than the silence they have. **TEXT DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN:** the badge ladder reads "Trace" at its bottom, which speaks of a small presence where the measurement says there is none; that is client-facing wording with a single author, so the number is shown and the badge omitted, and a case asserts the silence so it is not quietly filled in. Boundary named: `renderIons` opens with `hasIons = some(k => ions[k] > 0)`, so a sample whose every balance ion is zero would hide the section — no such sample exists on the stand and that gate is not this work. Three mutations, each reaching its subject: restoring `!!ions[ion]` dropped the carbonate row; badging the zero reddened the silence case; removing `measuredIons` from the record reddened the producer case in `gh586`. Control green after each. Jest 3361 passed, 0 failed; PHP 339 passed. **ACCEPTED ON A LIVE ROW, ONE ANNOUNCED PRESS.** Before: `Burns` row 64 carried `ions.CO3 = 0` and no `measuredIons` field at all. After the press, row 67 carries `measuredIons = {K 17, Ca 46, Cl 64, Mg 6, Na 47, CO3 0, SO4 9, HCO3 150}` — the sample's own units, carbonate among them as a measured zero. AND SEEN ON THE SCREEN, not inferred from the record: `tests/e2e/gh611-the-ion-table-on-screen-live.test.js` opens the Water Balance tab through the page's own tab link and reads the table — `["Carbonate (CO₃)", "0.00", "0.0", ""]`, the row present, the number shown, the status cell empty, while `Bicarbonate` keeps its `Moderate` badge and `Boron` shows the measured zero from GH-608. THAT PROBE PRESSES NOTHING and carries the stand remedy rather than an exemption: it only reads, so `guardStand` costs it nothing, and if the page ever starts writing site state while being merely looked at, the write is held and printed instead of the stand moving under a test that calls itself passive. Its held-writes list came back empty. The Word export is unaffected and that was checked rather than assumed: it draws no ion table — only an `EC / SAR / Na / Cl / HCO3` chart from a different object — and names no carbonate anywhere.

**GH-612** (пункт 3м) The two soil-sample states are told apart — in the record, where telling the truth needs no new words. A sample that is absent and a sample that arrived with columns the map does not know both produced `soil-sample-not-delivered`, and for the second that reason is untrue: it WAS delivered, it was not understood. Both places are changed under one decision, as the coordinator required: the gate `_gaipSoilSampleReadyOrGivenUp` (`hub-tissue-v3.js`) now files WHICH state it was as a `note` — level `info`, which `AnalysisNotice::warningLines()` does not print — and the runner's `_soilSampleHasArrived` (`hub-persistence.js`) became `_soilSampleState()`, returning `{delivered, readings}`, whose answer rides in the failure's `detail` as `delivered` and `readableColumns`. `detail` was chosen after checking `AnalysisNotice::detailText()`: it prints detail for four codes and this is not one of them, so the record gains a fact and the client gains no new words. **THE SCREEN HALF IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED** — the failure code is unchanged and the panel says what it said before, because a third state needs a third sentence, client-facing wording has a single author, and he has not written it. That half is the owner's open question. The two cases that PINNED the collapse are rewritten rather than repaired, as they asked to be in their own docblocks: each now holds both facts at once — the record tells the states apart, the screen does not yet — and each says it must go red again the day the screen half lands. One mutation per place, each reaching its subject: dropping `delivered` from the failure detail reddened the runner case; filing one note for both states reddened the gate case at 1 expected against 0. Control green before and after. Jest 3361 passed, 0 failed and PHP 339 passed WHEN THE WORK WAS DONE, on 23.09.2026 before the machine was restarted; this entry was written the next day, after the owner had committed the change without running it, so those two numbers describe the tree as it stood then and are not a claim about the tree as committed. They are restated by the next full run.

**GH-613** (пункт 3м, находка ревьюера) A live run writes its own transcript, so nobody presses twice to read it. On 23.09.2026 an unannounced THIRD press happened for a reason that had nothing to do with the stand: the second run's output had been filtered through `grep`, the failure reason was not in what survived, and the only way to read it again was to run the file again — which pressed the button again. What was then reported as closed was `tee` on the command line, and the reviewer found no trace of it in the tree — correctly, because there was none: it lived in how one person typed one command. That is a habit, and by the project's own test — what fills the rule — a habit is a wish. `tests/e2e/lib/transcript.js` writes from INSIDE the run: it does not depend on how the command is typed, on a `package.json` target, on a reporter, or on anyone remembering. Both live files use it (`gh591`, `gh611-live`); the path is printed at the start so it survives a filtered terminal; writing can never fail the run it records. Verified on the probe that PRESSES NOTHING, so checking the remedy for an unwanted press cost no press: the file came back with every line, ion table included.

**GH-614** (пункт 3м, обе находки ревьюера на GH-613) The transcript mechanism can now be shown red, and it says where it wrote. GH-613 was refused on two counts and both held. **There was no way to break it visibly:** deleting the `fs.appendFileSync` that does the writing left the whole suite green — 268 suites, 3361 passed, nothing failed — because the library is reached only by the two live probes and those skip without `GILBA_E2E=1`. A remedy against an unwanted press rested on nobody breaking it. **And the docblock claimed what was not done:** it said the path was printed "at the start and again at the end" while nothing printed it at the end and no caller read `file` at all — the closing line being the half the remedy exists for, since the opening one scrolls away and is what a filter drops, which is how the third press happened. The claim was DONE rather than removed: `close()` prints the path last, both probes call it from `afterAll` so it runs whether the run passed or failed, and it says plainly when there is no file. The cases live in `tests/gh614-…` and need NO STAND, which is the reviewer's own recommendation — no browser, no login, no press, so the guard against a stray press costs no press to run and sits in the ordinary suite where a deletion cannot hide. Three mutations, each naming its own subject: removing the append reddened the both-halves case; removing the closing print reddened the ending case; a probe that stopped calling `close()` reddened the case that reads the probes themselves. One trap met on the way and recorded in the file: `require.cache` does not reset a module under Jest, so the third case wrote into the first case's directory and failed for a reason that had nothing to do with the library — `jest.isolateModules` with an assertion that the directory really is this case's. Jest 269 suites, 3365 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 339 passed.

**GH-615** (пункт 3у) Organic matter reaches the run from the sample, not from the old hub's form. The owner settled it the same night — the row must carry it, "in the old hub it worked, so of course it should" — and there was no fork to decide. `pH`, `CEC`, `EC` and bulk density were already read from the active soil sample when the run builds its state; `LOI` and `OM_pct` still read `.gaip-loi`, a FORM FIELD OF THE OLD HUB, so the value came from the markup of the hidden runner and never arrived. One link of an otherwise complete chain, and the GH-459 class: a calculation fed from the state of a page instead of from the data of the object it is about. The `0` default went with the read — unmeasured organic matter is absent, not zero, and the recovery engine WAITS for this reading. Measured before the change: of 48 live soil samples 25 carry it (`OM` 22, `OM_Percent` 19), every value non-empty; none carries the stratified fields at all. **WHO RECEIVES IT NOW WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED**, because a number that was never there entering a calculation that expected it is how this class does its damage: the recovery engine and its verdict line, the thatch programs, irrigation, the soil-nutrition and orchestrator paths — and the soil-temperature model, which takes organic matter only for profiles marked `cecRefinable` (`native`, `pipe-drained`, `soil-field`), while all 11 live configs are `sand_profile`, so that one receives nothing new today. The analyst's claim that `om` reaches nothing was verified this way and holds for the same reason. **THE BORDER THE REVIEWER NAMED IS CLOSED BY EXECUTION:** "the reader answers `OM`" had been read, not run — Jest could not start that day — and `tests/gh615-…` now runs it against the PRODUCT's own normaliser, on both spellings, with the absent case answering null rather than zero. That file also caught its own author: the first run returned `null` because the fixture was handed pre-wrapped as `{id, values}` while `stubSampleManager` takes a flat lab row and wraps it itself — a bench failure that looked exactly like the defect under test, now recorded in the file with the shape taken from `gh577` rather than invented. **STRATIFIED `LOI_0_2 / 2_4 / 4_6` ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED** and a case pins that: the owner has not decided whether they are repaired or removed from the screen, no live sample carries them, and that case must go red the day she decides. Three mutations, each naming its own subject: the state reading the form again reddened the state case; the reader returning null reddened both reader cases; "repairing" a stratified field reddened the case that holds the open decision. Jest 270 suites, 3370 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 339 passed.

**GH-616** (пункт 3л) A zero the code produced is not a reading, and is no longer written down. `_meq` answers `(parseFloat(x) || 0) / factor`, so an ion nobody measured came out 0 and its key sat in the stored object all the same. Counted on the stand: across the ten rows carrying any ions there are 80 values and 62 are zero — TWO measured (carbonate on `Burns` and on `New test - location`) and SIXTY produced on the way, 56 of those on seven sites with no water sample at all. The record said "zero" where the truth was "nobody measured it". Owner's decision: write nothing. **THE REPAIR IS NOT WHERE THE ITEM SAID IT WAS, and that matters:** `_meq` is untouched, because SAR, RSC, LSI and the sodium percentage need a number for every term and they read the plain variables `_Ca`, `_Mg`, `_Na` — still numbers, still zero for an absent reading. What changed is the stored object: a key is written only when `_measuredIons` has it, and which readings those are is not decided at that line — it is derived from the same `_mgToMeq` table that decides what the object can hold. So the arithmetic and the record were told apart rather than one being sacrificed to the other, which was the reviewer's condition for doing this at all. **Nothing on screen moves, measured rather than hoped:** every reader takes `ions.X || 0` or asks `parseFloat(ions.X) > 0`, false for `undefined` exactly as for 0; the ion table has asked `measuredIons` since GH-611; and the sixty zeros were never on a screen, because with all eight zero `renderIons` returns nothing and the section is absent — which is why the first description of this item, rows of zeros a client could see, did not survive measurement. One existing case was REWRITTEN rather than repaired: `gh586` asserted that `ions` said 0 for both a measured zero and an absent one, which was true and is now false by decision — the meaning changed, which is the one reason a case may change. Two mutations, each naming its subject: writing all eight again reddened the absent-key case; `_meq` returning `undefined` reddened the arithmetic case at `SAR` being NaN. Targeted runs only — the full suite is held while the reviewer has the tree: gh616, gh586 and gh611 together, 22 passed.

**GH-617** (пункт 3т, находка ревьюера) What is missing is counted from the sample, not from the screen. `judge()` built `dropped` as a subset of `shared`, and `shared` is the ROW's vocabulary — so a reading the page has no cell for at all fell out of both answers and was named nowhere. Reproduced before the repair: `judge({K:'18.8'}, {K:18.84, Zn:5})` returned `{shared:['K'], disagreed:[], dropped:[]}` and the measured zinc vanished. A judge reporting "nothing missing" about a row that is missing a reading is worse than no judge, because its silence reads as a verdict. **AND ITS NAME PROMISED WHAT ITS VALUE DID NOT:** the caller states this as `measuredBySampleButNotInTheRow` while the value walked what IS in the row. Repaired by recount, so the name became true: the question is asked of the sample's readings, and a reading is missing when the row has no cell for it OR the cell is empty. Two cases added to the judge's own set; the mutation — `dropped` back to a subset of `shared` — reddens both. **PREDICTED ON THE LIVE ROW WITHOUT PRESSING:** on `Burns` the repaired judge will name `OM` and `Na`. `OM` is the owner's open question (3у). `Na` IS IN THE ROW under the name `soilNa`, so that one is a FALSE finding — the second half of item 3т, now visible: completeness rose and accuracy fell, and a judge that cries wolf is switched off faster than one that is silent. Three ways to settle it were named to the coordinator and none chosen alone.

**GH-618** (пункт 3у, находка ревьюера) The default was not removed, it was moved one layer down. GH-615 let an unmeasured organic matter stay absent in the run state; `gaip_transformToCascadeFormat` then wrote `domState.soil?.LOI || 0` and turned that absence back into a zero before any engine saw it — measured in a sandbox, `state.soil.LOI = null` arriving as `inputs.soil.LOI = 0`. A site with nothing measured was still computed at 0% OM, and the five cases of GH-615 stayed green because they measure THE STATE. Absence travels now (`?? null`), and the engines already treat missing as missing: the recovery engine asks `!e.soil?.LOI && !e.soil?.OM_pct`, true for `null` exactly as for `0`, while the thatch and irrigation paths take `safeNum(soil.LOI, 0)` at the point of use — a default belongs where a number is needed, not where a fact is carried. `tests/gh618-…` executes the converter and asserts WHAT THE ENGINE IS HANDED rather than what the state holds; mutation back to `|| 0` reddens it with the value printed. **NEIGHBOURS ON THE SAME LAYER ARE NAMED, NOT REPAIRED, and a case pins them so this file is not read as evidence the layer is clean:** `pH_water || 0`, `pH_cacl2 || 0`, `CEC || 0`, `bulkDensity || 1.4`, `water.ecw || 0`, `water.EC || ecw || 0`. `pH 0` is not a possible soil reading at all. **Border kept from the reviewer:** he measured the converter's output, not the stored row — whether absence survives into `analysis_results` is still open. Targeted runs only while the tree is held: gh618 + gh615 + gh609, 17 passed.

**GH-619** (пункт 3х) Five more defaults removed from the carrier layer, one left deliberately, and the whole layer listed rather than counted. `gaip_transformToCascadeFormat` holds about fifty `||` fallbacks; most are structural (`|| {}`, `|| null`, `|| ""`) or a genuine zero (no matches is no matches). Six were substitutions of a plausible value for an absent fact, and five are now gone: `pH_water`, `pH_cacl2` and `CEC` on the soil side, `ecw`, `EC` and `pH` on the water side. **THE INTENT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN IN THE TREE AND THIS LAYER WAS UNDOING IT:** the state sets these to `null` on purpose and says why — "Not measured → null, not 0 — a pH of '0' reads as real (implausibly acidic) data to disease models that use `??` to detect missing input". The readers that use `??` are real and named: `nutrition-calendar.js:1092-1093, 1154, 1163` and `nutrition-summary-integration.js:727, 737` all ask `soil.CEC ?? …` and `soil.pH_water ?? …`, for which `0` is a reading that happens to be zero. Everyone else was checked and is unaffected — the scenario engines take `|| 7`, the climate module `|| null`, engine confidence `if (soil?.CEC)` — all treating `null` as they treated `0`. `water.pH || 7` was the worst of the six: seven is plausible, so an untested water became a neutral one, and the synthesis reader now falls through to its next source instead of stopping there. Measured: 47 of 48 live soil samples carry a pH, 43 carry a CEC, 7 of 8 waters carry a pH. **`bulkDensity || 1.4` IS LEFT, NAMED, AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT:** NONE of the 48 live soil samples carries a bulk density, the field behind it is a form of the old hub, `input-range-validator.js:276` already calls it a structural default rather than a lab result, and 61 of the 65 stored rows carry 1.4 — so it is a constant of the model with no other source, and removing it would take a number out of a calculation that needs one. A case states that plainly so it reads as a decision rather than a miss. One case was REWRITTEN rather than repaired: it pinned that the neighbours still defaulted, which was true and is now false by decision. Mutation: `pH_water` back to `|| 0` reddens the new case. Targeted runs while the tree is held: gh618 + gh615 + gh609 + gh616, 24 passed.

**GH-620** (пункт 3ц) Both signs of one class, settled under one decision. Everything else this night removed zeros the code had produced; one place did the opposite and discarded zeros the laboratory had reported. **FORWARD SIGN:** `Na_ppm` began at `0` in the run state, sitting between `pH_cacl2` and `CEC`, both of which set `null` on purpose and carry a comment saying why — sodium was the one that did not; its twin in `cascade-orchestrator.js` flattened the same absence with `|| 0`. Both carry the absence now. **REVERSE SIGN:** the water DOM fallback kept a reading only `if (_ik && !isNaN(_iv) && _iv > 0)`, so a water tested for carbonate and found to have none arrived as a reading and left as an absence — the collapse GH-608 and GH-611 closed on the other two water paths, still standing on this one. `!isNaN` already separates "no number" from "a number"; the comparison added only the loss. **NEITHER WAS REACHABLE TODAY, WHICH IS WHY THEY WERE REPAIRED NOW:** of 48 live soil samples 44 carry sodium and NONE carries a sodium of zero; of 64 stored rows the water source is `null` on 49 and the sample store on 15, so the DOM fallback has not run once — while six live water samples do carry a measured zero, which is what the reverse sign loses the first time that path is taken. **ASKED OF EACH SUBJECT BEFORE TOUCHING IT, does it reach the stored row:** the forward sign does NOT — `soilNa: ppm.Na || Na_ppm || null` turns a zero back into null, and `assessSoilSodium` opens with `if (!e || 0 === e) return null`, so zero and absence already ended the same way; the change makes the carrier honest instead of relying on two readers to undo it. The reverse sign DOES reach the row, through `waterBalance`, the first time that path runs. **BOUNDARY NAMED AND LEFT:** `assessSoilSodium`'s own `0 === e` is a fallback AT THE POINT OF USE — a reader deciding what it does with a zero — and by the rule this night has worked to, a default belongs there rather than in a carrier. It does mean a measured sodium of zero still reads as "not tested", the same collapse one layer further in; a case states it so it reads as a decision. Two mutations, one per sign, each naming its subject: restoring `_iv > 0` dropped `CO3` from the kept ions with the list printed; restoring `Na_ppm: 0` reddened the forward case. Targeted: gh620 + gh616 + gh618 + gh611, 22 passed — the full run is the reviewer's this time.

**GH-621** (пункт 18) The item as stated does not reproduce; the other half of the same line did, and is repaired. **THE STATED SUBJECT, measured end to end: a non-numeric value does not reach the database.** `captureSoilForm` reads each field with a plain `parseFloat`, so anything unparseable becomes `NaN` and serialises to `null`. Counted across all 60 live samples: 812 readings, every one a number — 543 DOUBLE, 269 INTEGER — and the only strings are `_label` (60), `zone` (57), `_source` (46) and `_zone` (45), which are labels rather than readings. The importer itself already files an unparseable cell as "Not a valid number" instead of dropping it, and `lab-import.js` is loaded only by `/hub` and the report pages — the client Data page does not carry it, and nothing calls `LabImport.` from outside the file. **AND THE COORDINATOR'S QUESTION ANSWERED: the writer at `hub-persistence.js:1869` is NOT on this path** — it writes `analysis_results`, while the import travels into `samples` through `captureFromForm`. Two different roads. **WHAT WAS REAL:** the field was filled with `parseFloat(row[col]) || row[col]`, and zero is falsy — a laboratory that measured and reported `0` had its number discarded and the raw cell put in its place. The same collapse as GH-608, GH-611 and GH-620, this time on the way IN, in BOTH places that carried the line (soil and water). Six live water samples carry a measured zero today. A cell that does not parse still shows the raw text, deliberately: the problem is already reported, and an empty box would hide what the file said. **THE CASES ASSERT WHAT THE FIELD RECEIVES, by executing the function** — not what the source looks like, which is the trap `gh577` is red in today: it slices a fixed character window around an anchor, and a docblock written between two lines pushed the rest out of range. Two bench faults met and recorded in the file rather than worked around: a stub answering every selector handed the function an input as its container, and the maps the function reads are taken from the module instead of rewritten. Mutation: restoring `|| row[col]` printed `["mehlich3","0"]` against `["mehlich3",0]` and reddened the subject case. Jest 273 suites passed with one failure — `gh577`, a false red of the reviewer's own finding, product intact — 3392 passed; PHPUnit 339 passed.

**GH-622** (пункт «хрупкие тесты») A test that cuts a window out of source now says the window is real. **THE FAULT HAS TWO FACES AND THE SECOND IS THE COSTLY ONE.** `gh577` took `SRC.slice(at - 400, at + 1400)` around an anchor, and a docblock written between two of the lines it checked — GH-615's — pushed `CEC` to offset 2112 and `EC1_5` to 2179, both outside the window: the case went red with the product untouched. That face is harmless, somebody looks and fixes it. The other face is a window that shrinks past what it was checking while every claim about it is NEGATIVE: a negative claim is true of an empty string, so the case keeps passing over nothing and from outside looks exactly like one that works. **THE REMEDY IS NOT A WIDER WINDOW** — the next insertion breaks that too — but one positive claim beside each: not empty, and containing its own anchor, the pattern `gh299` has carried since GH-466, where an anchor stopped matching, `slice(-1, …)` returned the file's last character and three assertions passed over it. **SIZE, COUNTED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED: 101 source windows across the tree, 87 already making a positive claim, 14 not.** Four of those fourteen were repaired, chosen because ALL their claims were negative: `disease-forecast-unification` twice, `hub-tissue-analysis-writeback-merge-b35fix391`, and `gh305-aa-generic-range-ceiling-consumers` — which had NO ANCHOR CHECK AT ALL, the worse half, since `indexOf` returning -1 makes `slice(-1, 399)` hand back one character. Measured before repairing: that anchor sits at 4346 and the window is a full 400 characters, so the case was real — but nothing said so, and nothing would have said otherwise. **`gh577` ITSELF WAS FIXED AT THE CAUSE, not by widening:** its block is now cut at the closing brace of the object it belongs to, by brace matching, and asserted for length and anchor before anything is said about it — an insertion cannot break a boundary the code itself declares. The census holds the remaining ten by name and goes red in both directions, new and repaired. **THE MUTATION THAT MUST REDDEN IT, named because the reviewer cannot run one today:** add any window with only a negative claim — `const w = src.slice(at, at + 500); expect(w).not.toContain(…)` — and the census names the new file and binding. Shown: a probe file appeared as `tests/gh622-probe.test.js|w` and reddened the exactness case; control green before and after. Jest 275 suites, 3397 passed, 0 failed — `gh577` green again; PHPUnit 339 passed.

**GH-623** (пункт 15) The Russian is out of the code, all seventeen files, and the guard's remainder is empty. The list came from the census itself (GH-610), never from a list written by hand — a hand-written one goes stale the day the tree changes. **THE TWO PRODUCT FILES WERE OPENED FIRST AND THEIR CYRILLIC WAS IN COMMENTS ONLY**, each already carrying its English translation beside it: `nutrition-calendar.js` quoted the owner on methodology having no other dependencies, and `word-export.js` quoted her on not showing what belongs to someone else, plus a phrase naming the truthiness-versus-presence class. **GH-624** (пункт «хрупкие окна», остаток) The fourteen windows the census named are settled, and its unguarded list is empty. The list came from the instrument, not from a person: `gh622` prints what it inspected, and the fourteen were taken from that output. **NONE OF THE FOURTEEN WENT RED AFTER THE REPAIR, and that is the result rather than a disappointment:** every one of those windows is intact today — the anchors are found and the blocks hold their subjects — so there was no silent green among them. What the work buys is that the day one of them shrinks, it fails loudly instead of passing over nothing. **THEY WERE NOT ALL THE SAME THING, and treating them as one list was the mistake of the previous attempt:** ten were real windows of source and now carry an anchor check and a length floor beside them, in `disease-fusarium`, `gh250`, `gh298` (twice), `gh395`, `gh413`, `turf-type-bowls`, `hoxton-export` (three windows behind one helper) and `gh487`; three were never windows of text at all — `rowAfter(html, a).slice(off, off + 3)` takes three table cells and `lines.slice(idx, idx + 6)` takes six already-split lines, and nothing there can shrink past a subject; and one is a live probe whose window is cut INSIDE `page.evaluate`, where `expect` does not exist, so it throws on a collapsed window instead. **THE CENSUS LEARNED BOTH OF THOSE FACTS rather than having them worked around:** a measured span floor of 50 characters, taken from the tree (source windows run 120 to 4,000, array slices 3 to 6, nothing between), and the `throw` form as a positive claim alongside `expect`. `gh487` is the one that needed care: its window is conditional on purpose — the classifier answers `nowhere` for a document that has no such paragraph, which is a real outcome — so the claim is made INSIDE the branch where the anchor was found. **Two cases were rewritten rather than repaired**, both in `gh622` itself, because its remainder emptied as the work proceeded — the same shape as `gh610` an hour earlier. **THE MUTATION THAT MUST REDDEN THIS:** add any window with no positive claim; shown with a probe file that the census named as `tests/gh624-probe.test.js|w`, reddening the exactness case, control green before and after. From the other side, removing the length claim from any of the ten repaired windows does the same. Jest 275 suites, 3397 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 339 passed.

**GH-625** (пункт 16, находка по ходу) The site bundle neither exports nor restores the config, and no longer says that it does. `site-data-transfer.js` read `gilba_hub_site_configs` on the way out and wrote it back on the way in, logging "Site config restored for: …". Both halves were dead: GH-441 took that key out of service and `site-config-persistence.js` clears it — and its namespaced twin — UNCONDITIONALLY in `init()`, while nothing outside the transfer module reads it. So the export has been putting `null` into every bundle for as long as that has been true, and the import landed its write in a key wiped moments later while the log said the opposite. **REMOVED RATHER THAN REPAIRED, by the project's own rule for this exact case:** a control that stopped working because a write path was removed is removed, not wired back up. That write path went on purpose — a page pushing a whole held config is the defect GH-439 was opened for — and restoring it here would rebuild the browser copy that work took out. **REACHABLE ONLY FROM `/hub`, measured before deciding:** the bar these buttons mount into, `gaip-site-selector-top`, exists in `partials/legacy-hub-markup.blade.php` and nowhere else, and `/hub` is a calculation runner rather than a page a client opens. **WHAT IS NOT TOUCHED, and a case asserts it so the removal is not read as wider than it is:** the samples still merge through the sample manager, and the site's coordinates are still `PATCH`ed to the server, which is where they belong. **GH-626** (пункт 3т) The producer is asked what it calls each reading, and the judge stops guessing from spelling. Two kinds of rename were producing false findings: `Na`, the same reading the row calls `soilNa` — on `Burns` both are 11.5, and the judge called it lost from a row that carries it; and `EC`, which the row carries as `ECe`, that reading times a texture factor of five to ten, so comparing them for equality would have reported a sevenfold disagreement about a correct row. 41 of the 48 live soil samples carry EC, so the second was waiting for the first site that has one — `Burns` has no EC column, which is why nobody had seen it. **THE DESIGN IS THE ANALYST'S (9.6) AND ITS POINT IS THAT NOTHING IS WRITTEN DOWN:** a hand-written `{Na: 'soilNa'}` is a second place the name lives and second places drift, and it cannot express `EC` at all. So the correspondence is measured from behaviour — change one reading by a known amount, run the whole chain from sample to stored row offline, see which field moved and by how much: by the delta, the same reading; by something else, derived; not at all, not carried. **THE POSITIVE CONTROL THE ANALYST ASKED FOR EARNED ITS PLACE.** Two ways of joining the chain did not reach the producer: leaving the cascade's result where `runCascade` returns it, and handing it to `GaipOrchestrator.getState()`, each gave a surface of five scalars with an empty `nutrients` — every reading would have answered "not carried" for a reason having nothing to do with names. The producer reads `global.GAIP_STATE`; that is where it is joined, and the file says so. Measured: `pH -> pH` same, `Na -> soilNa` same, `K -> nutrients.K` same, `EC -> ECe` derived with a factor of 7, inside the texture table's range of 5 to 10. **A FIFTH OUTCOME, `derived`, joins the judge**, and a derived field is asked only for PRESENCE — equality is not asked of two different quantities — while a derived field the row does not state at all is still reported. **AND THE NAME BECAME TRUE, which was the other half of this item:** `measuredBySampleButNotInTheRow` now counts readings absent from the row UNDER THE NAME THE ROW USES, with derived fields excluded — before GH-617 it walked the screen, and before this it walked the screen's spelling. `tests/lib/orchestrator-bench.js` gained an optional `expose` hook so a caller can reach a module-private function; without it, default behaviour is unchanged for the four sets already using the bench. Cost named: one offline run of `/hub` per measurement, which is why this is a set rather than something the live probe does per press. Two mutations, each naming its subject: making the judge resolve by spelling again reddens the case that says a carried reading is not lost; treating a derived field as ordinary reddens the presence case. Jest 277 suites, 3407 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 339 passed.

**GH-627** (пункт 3т, находка ревьюера) The measured name map reaches the live probe, and the derived half is asserted instead of computed and discarded. His three addresses were verified and all held: `gh591` imported only `judge`, called it with two arguments, and `derived`/`derivedMissing` appeared nowhere. His measurement reproduced exactly — without the map, `Na` and `EC` are reported as readings the row has lost; with it, `Na` joins `shared` and `EC` becomes `derived`, both empty in `dropped`. **THE MAP IS BUILT, NOT COPIED:** `mapFor()` asks the producer about every reading the sample carries, and it carries NO hand-written list of where a reading goes in either — each is offered both doors, the scalar and the `ppm` one, and whichever moves the surface is the one the producer reads. So nothing in this work names a field of the row; the row's names come back as answers. Measured on a `Burns`-shaped sample: `pH -> pH`, `CEC -> CEC`, `Na -> soilNa`, `K -> nutrients.K`, all `same`. **A BORDER FOUND AND NOT PAPERED OVER: `EC` does not measure through this bench.** `ECe` arrives in the state ready-made rather than recomputed from `EC1_5`, so changing the input moves nothing; the earlier measurement that returned `derived` had `ECe` supplied by hand, which is exactly the second place this design exists to avoid. It is left unmeasured and named rather than hand-fed. **COST NOT HIDDEN AND NOT DECIDED:** several offline runs of `/hub` per reading, once per press; whether to build the map once and keep it is the analyst's question, asked and left open. **WHAT IS NOT PROVEN UNTIL MORNING:** the live probe was not run — the fourteen live sets are not run by anyone tonight — so what the map looks like against the real `rowSurface` on the stand, and whether `derivedMissing` is empty there, is unverified. Offline: Jest 277 suites, 3407 passed, 0 failed. Mutations that must redden this: remove the third argument at the `judgeRowAgainstSample` call and `Na` returns to `dropped`; drop the `derivedMissing` assertion and a derived field the row never states passes unnoticed.

**GH-628** (пункт 3я, устройство аналитика 9.7) The name map is measured from the sample's own lab row, over the whole declared universe, once per process — and the soil state gets a function of its own so that chain can run at all. **WHAT WAS WRONG WITH GH-626/627, measured by reading and confirmed by this work:** the shift happened on the READY soil state, so the test itself had to say which state field carries which reading — `{pH: 'pH_water', EC: 'EC1_5', OM: 'LOI', Na: 'Na_ppm'}` — and that is the second table of names the whole design exists to remove, one link earlier. Two things followed from it. `EC` could not be measured (the row's `ECe` is computed inside the assembly, which a hand-written state skips, so `EC` answered "not carried" — and 41 of the 48 live soil samples carry EC, so the live judge would have called it lost on all of them). And the universe was three readings chosen by hand out of fifteen. **THE PRODUCT CHANGE, 1 place, behaviour unchanged:** `gaip_build_state`'s inline soil block is now `gaip_soilStateFrom(sample, form)`, with the page read beside it by `gaip_readSoilForm(e)`. Every line is the line that stood inline, with its comment. Two consequences said out loud: the `|| "loam"` behind `soilTexture` and the `1.4` behind an unmeasured bulk density are now visible at the call site instead of buried in the assembly (unchanged, and whether the texture should come off the page at all is the analyst's separate finding); and `Na_ppm` from `ppm.Na` moved here from the end of `gaip_build_state` — it read `o.soil.ppm` and wrote `o.soil.Na_ppm` with nothing in between touching either, so the result is the same one, and the offline chain has to include it. **THE UNIVERSE IS DECLARED:** `readingKeysFor('soil')`, 15 readings, the same map `readingsOf` normalises against — a reading added to it is measured without anyone remembering. Measured, all fifteen: `pH->pH`, `CEC->CEC`, `Na->soilNa`, ten nutrients each under its own name, all `same`; `EC->ECe` derived with a factor of exactly 7, the loam entry of the product's own texture table; `OM` absent — the row does not carry it, which is the owner's open half of GH-615 and is now stated by name rather than being a hole. **A REAL DEFECT FOUND BY THE REDESIGN:** GH-626 flattened the nutrient cards as `nutrients.K`, a prefix this library invented — the row's card says `{nutrient: 'K'}` and the screen prints `K`, so the map sent the judge looking for a field nothing has. Handed the full map, the judge called all ten nutrients lost on a row that carries them. Names them as the row does now. **COST MEASURED RATHER THAN FEARED, and it decided the cache question:** 16 chain runs, 761 ms, once per process — so there is no map file in the tree and no cache outside it either. **THE LIVE PROBE NO LONGER WRITES A SOIL STATE FOR THE MEASUREMENT:** the hand-built state at the `mapFor` call, `bulkDensity: 1.4` included (Question 83), is gone; the measurement starts at the lab row and runs the product's own reader and assembly. **THREE MUTATIONS, control green first, each naming its subject.** Replace the product's `ECe` calculation with `null` — `EC` falls to `absent`, the derived case and the "what the row does not carry" case both redden, printing `["EC","OM"]`; this is the mutation that was INVISIBLE before, by the analyst's reading. Rename `soilNa` in the producer — the map prints `Na->soilNaRenamed` and the sodium case reddens. Remove `Na` from `SOIL_FIELD_MAP` — the universe measures 14 and the equality-with-the-declared-list case reddens. **NOT PROVEN UNTIL THE STAND:** the live probe was not run tonight, so what `derivedMissing` says about `ECe` against the real screen is unverified — `EC` used to be reported dropped there and will now be asked for the presence of `ECe` instead. Two sets were updated because the assembly's local was renamed from `_gaipSoilSample` to `sample` — `gh577` (its window, and the methodology claim, now EXECUTED against `gaip_soilStateFrom` instead of read off the source) and `gh615` (its window covers both halves, with an anchor and a length floor). **ТРИ МУТАЦИИ РЕВЬЮЕРА, ПРИМЕНЕНЫ ОФЛАЙН, контрольный прогон зелёным перед каждой — и его различение верно: мои мерили, ПЕРЕДАНА ли карта, его мерят, ВЕРНА ли она.** Чтобы их можно было применить без стенда, судья запущен против НАСТОЯЩЕЙ поверхности продюсера (`surfaceForRow`), а не против поверхности, написанной в тесте; граница названа: это сохранённая строка, а не экран. **M-1, карта возвращается пустой:** `dropped` получает `EC` и `Na` сверх `OM` — то есть карта на этих данных меняет вердикт, а не украшает его; `disagreed` остался пустым, как ревьюер и предсказал. **M-2, `EC` записан как `same`:** `disagreed` получает `EC` — строка 1.12 против пробы 0.16, семикратно; `dropped` не изменился. **M-3, `field` у `Na` подменён несуществующим именем:** `Na` возвращается в `dropped`; `derivedMissing` остался пустым. **НАХОДКА, НАЙДЕННАЯ САМОЙ M-1 и починенная в той же работе:** отчёт карты падал `TypeError` на неполной карте, и красное-по-TypeError неотличимо от «проверка до предмета не дошла» — печать переживает пропущенную запись и говорит `not measured`, а полноту утверждает отдельный случай. Jest 277 наборов, 3415 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-629** (пункт 3аа, задание аналитика — раздел 11 плана входов) A measurement, not a repair: what the onboarding wizard sends for a site that is not golf, and what the server does with it. Nothing in the product changed. **PART B, THE CLIENT** — a Jest sandbox on `onboarding-wizard.js` with the intercept at `fetch` rather than at `_api`, because the body is built on the way through and replacing that layer would measure the test: the PATCH to `…/config/gaip` carries `turf.subCategory: ""` for `sports` AND for `lawns`, the key present and the value empty. Positive control first, and it earned its place — `golf`/`greens` carries `greens` and two requests were intercepted, so a silent run could not be read as "the wizard sends no key". **PART A, THE SERVER** — a PHPUnit Feature test through the whole HTTP layer (calling the controller directly would skip the middleware that converts the empty string, and the measurement would be about something else), route `sites.config.patch`, the body `_save()` builds field for field. A1 `golf`/`greens` -> 200, so the measurement reached its subject. A2 `sports` with `subCategory: ""` -> **422**, `{"message":"null is not a value; empty these with \"clear\" instead: turf.subCategory.","invalid_keys":["turf.subCategory"]}`. A3, the discriminator, the same body WITHOUT the key -> 200, which is what shows the refusal is caused by that key and not by rights, route or anything else in the body. **ALL THREE READ LINKS EXECUTED: outcome 1 of the four the analyst named in advance — the defect is reachable in ordinary client work.** Any new sports or lawns site created by the wizard cannot be saved; the person reads `Could not save settings. Please check your connection and try again.`, which names the connection and not the cause, and a site with a provisional name is sent back into the wizard on every dashboard entry. **NUMBERS, read-only on the stand, with the boundary of the indicator named:** 75 sites carry `provisional_name = 1` with a type other than `golf` (68 `sports`, 7 `precinct`), and 67 of the sports ones have no `gaip` config row at all — the shape an unsaved wizard leaves. It is an upper bound, not a fact: this is a development stand, and "the wizard failed" does not follow from a missing config row until what created the site is checked. **WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, by the task's own frame:** the repair — the wizard not sending a key it never asked for, `subCategory` for golf only, 1 place — and the `alert` text, which is the owner's decision. The mutation for these two sets is the reviewer's to choose: they state observed behaviour, and no mutation of mine is claimed for them. Jest 278 suites, 3418 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 342 passed.

**GH-630** (пункт 3аа, решение координатора после замера GH-629) The wizard stops sending a key it never asked for, and a sports or lawns site can be created again. **ONE PLACE, and it is the one the analyst named:** `_save()` built `turf.subCategory: self.d.subCategory || ''` for every type, while the wizard asks for the sub-category of golf only and nulls it for anything else. The middleware turns that empty string into `null`, the config PATCH refuses a null inside a section, and the person read `Could not save settings. Please check your connection and try again.` about a site that could not be saved at all. The section is now assembled as `turfSection` and the key is added only when `turfType === 'golf'` and an answer exists — the project's own rule, send the change and not the state: a field nobody was asked for is not a change. **ASSERTED BY EXECUTION, not by reading the source:** the sandbox runs `_save()` and intercepts `fetch`, so the body measured is the body built. `sports` -> `{"turfType":"sports","species":"Perennial Ryegrass","methodology":"slan"}`, the key absent rather than empty; `lawns` the same; `golf`/`greens` still carries `greens`; **and a golf draft that never answered step 2 sends no key either** — the key travels because it was ANSWERED, not because the type is golf. The rest of the section is asserted beside it, or "no sub-category" would be true of a wizard that had stopped sending anything. **ABSENCE IS ALSO THE RIGHT VALUE FOR THE CONTRACT:** absent means untouched, so a site that already has a sub-category does not lose it. **THE MUTATION, control green first:** send the key for every type again (`turfSection.subCategory = self.d.subCategory || ''`) — three cases redden, printing the subject: `sports body.turf` regains `"subCategory":""`, and so do `lawns` and the unanswered `golf`. **WHAT IS KNOWN AND WHAT IS NOT, kept verbatim from the measurement:** the request now leaves correct; what the person SEES at that moment is confirmed only by the `alert` in the code, not by observation, and that stays until a live run. **NOT DONE, and named rather than done quietly:** the `alert` text belongs to the owner. **FOUND ALONGSIDE, MEASURED, NOT REPAIRED — Settings has the same shape:** `settings-init.js` sends `subCategory: document.getElementById('stg-turf-subcategory').value` and that `<select>` carries an empty `— select —` option, so saving the Turf tab with no surface chosen sends `''` to the same route and must draw the same 422. Numbers, read-only: of 12 `gaip` configs, 11 carry a sub-category value and 1 has no such key, so the field is empty on the stand for one site. Scope was held to the wizard on the coordinator's instruction; this is a queue item, not a silent fix. `Gh583CultivarAndConstructionAreRequiredTest` follows the section to its new anchor and now asserts its window holds its subject. Jest 278 suites, 3419 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 342 passed.

**GH-631** (пункт 3аа, решение координатора) The Settings side of the same question, and the answer is not the one either of us expected: **SETTINGS IS ALREADY RIGHT - WHAT IT LACKED WAS A GUARD.** My own claim that it sends `subCategory: ''` came from reading the ASSEMBLY (the Turf submit builds `turf` out of `document.getElementById(...).value`, and that `<select>` carries an empty option) and not the SENDER. Executing the sender says otherwise: `patchGaipConfig` filters the section before it goes - an empty ordinary field travels as `clear`, which is the contract's own way of emptying one, and an identity field that arrives empty is left out of the request entirely, neither patched nor cleared. Measured, the real body for a Turf tab with nothing chosen: `patch.turf {"species":"Perennial Ryegrass","turfType":"sports","methodology":"slan"}` and `clear ["turf.variety","turf.subCategory","turf.construction","turf.drainage","turf.hoc","turf.nProgram","turf.overseedSpecies","turf.companionSpecies"]`. **SO THE WIZARD WAS WRONG BECAUSE IT DOES NOT USE THIS HELPER** - it builds its own body and posts it, and that is the whole difference between the two forms. The reviewer's reading that they are one defect from two sides is not confirmed by measurement; his second half is, exactly: **a mutation on this side reddened nothing.** **WHAT WAS BUILT IS THE MISSING HALF: THE FILTER IS NOW EXECUTED, NOT READ.** The real `patchGaipConfig` is lifted out of its module and run with a captured `apiFetch`, and four cases state what the body contains - positive control that the sender reached the route at all, no empty field inside `patch`, the emptied ones said as `clear`, identity fields absent from both. **THE MUTATION, control green first:** remove the filter so every field travels as it is - the three claims redden and print the subject, `patch.turf` regaining `"variety":"","subCategory":"", ...` for all eight. **AND IT SHOWS WHY THE GUARD HAD TO EXECUTE:** with that same mutation in place, the whole rest of the suite stayed green, `gh371`'s textual check included - it asserts the line `GAIP_IDENTITY_FIELDS.indexOf(path) !== -1` is present in the file, and the mutation left the line standing and unreachable. **MEASURED ON THE SERVER, which is why an empty field matters at all:** a Turf save carrying nine empty fields answers 422 naming all nine; `clear` on ordinary fields answers 200 and removes them; `clear` on an identity field answers 422 "These cannot be cleared". No product code changed in this half. Jest 278 suites, 3423 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 344 passed.

**GH-632** (пункт 3аа, находка ревьюера) **HIS FINDING WAS RIGHT AND MY GUARD WAS NOT DONE.** It asserted `patch.turf[field]` is undefined for eight fields and that `clear` CONTAINS two of them, named by hand. That does not distinguish "the key is not sent" from "the key is sent empty and therefore cleared" - both leave `patch` without it. For the wizard the distinction does not matter; for Settings it IS the subject, because `clear` is the thing that actually empties the stored value. **SHOWN BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE REPAIR, and this is the number that settles it rather than an opinion:** dropping `turf.hoc` and `turf.construction` from the request altogether - neither patched nor cleared - left ALL EIGHT CASES GREEN, 8 passed. A guard that green cannot tell a working form from a form that has silently stopped emptying two of its fields. **THE REPAIR: the expectation is derived from the input, and the WHOLE LIST is compared instead of sampled.** For each field of the section exactly one outcome - a value goes into `patch` with the value the form held, an emptied ordinary field goes into `clear`, an emptied identity field goes into neither - and both lists are compared for equality, with the identity list read out of the file rather than written into the test. A field added to the Turf tab joins the comparison by itself. **THREE MUTATIONS, control green first, each printing its subject.** Drop two emptied fields from the request: `cleared` comes back six long instead of eight and the case reddens - the reviewer's own mutation, which the old guard could not see. Remove the filter so empty values travel: `patched` comes back eleven long and `cleared` empty, two cases redden. Clear an empty identity field: the case that says identity fields are left out of both lists reddens. **WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAYS ABOUT THE PRODUCT, unchanged from GH-631:** Settings does not send the key empty - `turf.subCategory` travels in `clear` - so there is no product defect on this side, and there was no guard. Now there is one, and it distinguishes the two states. No product code changed. Jest 278 suites, 3422 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 344 passed.

**GH-633** (пункт 17, стадия 1 плана аналитика) Stage 1 of `PLAN-config-patch-race-RU.md`: **BOTH LOSSES REPRODUCED BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT TO PREVENT THEM**, which is the analyst's condition for the rest of the work. **MEASUREMENT 1, THE CONFIG SECTION — the loss is real and section 1 of the plan stands.** Tab A loads with `construction: sand_profile`; B saves `native_soil`; A then saves its Turf tab the way `patchGaipConfig` does today, the section as its form holds it, changing only `hoc`. After A's save: `construction` is back to `sand_profile` and `hoc` is 12. B's change is gone and nothing said so — and it is invisible from A's side, because A's own edit landed. No concurrency was needed for this one: the loss comes from sending the section rather than the change. **MEASUREMENT 2, THE SITE ROW (plan section 2a) — the copy disagrees with its owner, so the second race is not theoretical and the extension is needed.** `sites.latitude = -36.85` while `config.location.lat = -41.29`: whoever reads the config sees a latitude the owning column does not hold. **HOW THE INTERLEAVING WAS PRODUCED, because two sequential requests cannot show this:** `ownedColumnValues()` calls `$site->refresh()` and only then takes the config lock, so the test listens for that very read — Eloquent's `retrieved` event, recognised by the value it brings back, A's own latitude — and runs B's whole request inside it, once. Nothing in the product is stubbed or modified; what the test controls is the ORDER, which is what a race is. A positive control asserts the interleaving fired at all, because without it the case measures nothing. **A DEPARTURE FROM THE PLAN, SAID OUT LOUD:** she asked for cases that are RED today and green after stage 3. A permanently red case would break the rule this team runs the morning suite by — expected reds are zero, any red is a finding — so each case states what happens TODAY and carries the line naming the repair that MUST turn it red, the shape `gh615` already uses for an open decision. The measurement is identical; only the colour convention differs. **My own Cyrillic guard caught me on the way:** the docblock quoted the analyst in Russian, and `gh610` named the file — nine runs, translated out. No product code changed in this stage. Jest 278 suites, 3422 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 346 passed.

**GH-634** (пункт 17, стадия 2 плана аналитика) Stage 2 of `PLAN-config-patch-race-RU.md`: the server side of the condition on each field, and one door for the site row and its copies. **THE CONDITION.** A writer may state the value it SAW, per field — `expected: {"turf.construction": "sand_profile"}`. The comparison runs INSIDE the same row lock that does the writing, because a comparison moved out from under it is a check with a gap between itself and the write, which is the race it exists to close. On disagreement: 409, naming the fields and their current values, and NOTHING is written — all or nothing, since writing the non-conflicting half would leave a state nobody chose. A field whose owner is a column is compared against the COLUMN, not against the config's copy of it: asking the copy whether the owner moved is asking the wrong thing. `expected` is compared and dropped — nothing stores it, so what the browser sends is still a change and not a state. Equality is lenient about SHAPE and strict about value (`25` vs `"25"` vs `25.0` came back differently depending on which column or client it travelled through; a condition failing on that would refuse every save on a site nobody had touched). **ONE DOOR FOR THE SITE ROW (plan section 2a).** `update()` now writes the row and derives its copies in ONE transaction, with the row locked FIRST, and `ownedColumnValues()` is read INSIDE the config lock rather than before it — the gap stage 1 measured was exactly between that read and the write of the copy. `patchConfig()` takes the site row before the config row whenever the patch touches a field a column owns, which makes the lock order the same on both paths; the deadlock was that one route took the config first and the other the row first. What decides is `FieldOwners::OWNERS` — no second list of "which fields are columns". **WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE, and it is a boundary, not an omission.** Both races are closed IN THE SERVER's device. In the product they are not yet closed for a client, because no writer sends `expected` — that is stage 3. So today the server can refuse a stale write and nobody asks it to. Plan point 2.6 ("a change without a condition is 422") is deliberately NOT switched on for the same reason: every writer in the tree sends none, and turning it on before stage 3 would stop every save in the product. A case states today's acceptance and carries the line naming the day it must go red. **No new text reaches the person: 409 and 422 are codes, and what a screen says about them is the owner's (plan stage 6). No migration, no data touched.** **NO NEW WRITE PATH CARRIES BROWSER STATE:** `expected` is a condition the server compares and discards, and no client sends one yet — measured by grep over `assets`. **THREE MUTATIONS, control green first, each naming what it breaks.** Never compare the condition: three cases redden, the two conflict cases and the reproduction of stage 1's loss, all answering 200 where 409 is required — the loss returns. Derive the copies from a read taken before the config row (the shape this work removed): the order case reddens, printing `read of the row for the copies @-1` — the read is no longer inside the lock. Stop taking the site row first on the config route: the lock-order case reddens, `row @4 config @2` — the deadlock order is back. **AND ONE OF MY OWN CASES WAS BLIND IN EXACTLY THE WAY THE REVIEWER FOUND AN HOUR EARLIER:** the lock-order case matched any read of `sites`, so it passed with the lock removed — three reads precede it (the access check, the pivot load, then the bare read by id) and it was counting the first. Sharpened to its subject, then re-mutated. **TWO THINGS MY OWN GUARDS CAUGHT:** `gh610` named Russian in the stage-1 docblock, `gh601` named a question number in a comment; both out. **WHAT NO OFFLINE TEST HERE CAN SHOW, said rather than left implied:** PHPUnit runs on SQLite, which has no `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, so the locks leave no trace in the query log — the order, the transaction depth and the executed lock decision are asserted, and the `lockForUpdate()` calls structurally. And stage 1's interleaving measurement stays green after the repair: it drives both writers through one connection, so it lands inside the lock rather than in front of it. A concurrent proof needs two connections and belongs to a live run. Jest 278 suites, 3422 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 356 passed.

**GH-635** (пункт 3с, находка по ходу) **A reference broken across two lines was invisible to the census that forbids references, and it was hiding real ones.** Found in the tree, in a comment I had written an hour earlier: `(Question` at the end of one line, `83).` at the start of the next. Every claim that guard made was true of the lines it read and false of the file. **Repaired by probing each line together with what follows it**, the next line's comment marker and indentation stripped — the reflow undone — and counting a match only where it STARTS inside the line, so a reference that fits on one line is still counted once, on its own line. **THE SHARPENED CENSUS IMMEDIATELY FOUND A SECOND ONE**, in the docblock of `gh538-stand-restore-round-trip-live.test.js`, which had been in its frozen remainder as a single hit while carrying two. Both are out of the code; the remainder lost the entry the tree no longer has. **A REPAIR THAT NEARLY REMOVED FINDINGS, caught and undone:** handing the silencing rules the probe instead of the line widened their context and silenced two real references in `word-export.js` — they get the line they always got when the match fits on it. **Mutation, control green first:** read one line at a time again — the new case reddens and prints the wrapped reference it no longer sees. Census after: 829 files, 89 references across 24 pairs, remainder in step with the tree. Jest 278 suites, 3423 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 356 passed.

**GH-636** (пункт 3я, остаток карты имён) The three things no offline set could answer are prepared so that ONE announced press closes all three, with both outcomes named before it runs.
