What gets printed: the row surface's key list and whether `ECe` is among them, beside what `derivedMissing` says; the verdict WITH the map and WITHOUT it, and a line stating in words whether the map changed the answer — with **outcome B named as a finding rather than a success**, because identical verdicts mean the names happen to agree on this site and the next may differ; and three lists for the third question — the readings the producer renames, those the screen states under their own name, those it states under the producer's name, and those it states under neither.

**GH-637** (пункт 17, стадия 3а плана) Stage 3a: **a field the person did not touch does not travel at all.** Settings sent its SECTION as the form was showing it, so a field somebody else had changed after the page loaded went back up at its old value and undid the later save — measured in stage 1, both tabs answering 200, tab B's `construction` returning to `sand_profile`. And with no race at all, an empty control nobody had touched travelled as a `clear` and erased a stored value. **WHAT IT SENDS NOW:** only fields that differ from WHAT THE SERVER GAVE THE PAGE — `D.gaipConfig`, rendered in by the server and replaced from the server's own answer after each save. **Not the form's state after autofill**, which the plan names as the trap: a form default would then read as a value the person had chosen. **THIS IS NOT A BROWSER COPY BEING WRITTEN BACK:** nothing of the baseline is sent, it decides what NOT to send, and what travels is still the change. Three outcomes per field, and the third is stage 3a's point: changed goes into `patch`, really-emptied goes into `clear`, untouched goes nowhere. An empty control whose stored value was ALSO empty is not a clear — there is nothing to empty, and asking to is the form asking for something nobody asked for. Nothing changed at all means no request is sent, since the route refuses a body with neither half. **MEASURED, one field changed out of eleven submitted:** `patched ["hoc"]`, `cleared []`, ten fields travelling nowhere. **NO NEW WORD ON SCREEN and no 409 is possible — no condition is sent.** Stage 3b (the condition and the conflict) is NOT done: it needs a new thing said to the person and waits for the owner. **THE ANALYST'S ANSWER TO THE REVIEWER'S OPEN QUESTION, taken as the decision it is:** `turf.subCategory` is NOT added to the client's `GAIP_IDENTITY_FIELDS` — that list means "this can never be emptied", a sports surface may legitimately be absent, and adding it would settle an open owner question by the back door. The class the finding belongs to is closed by 3a itself: an untouched empty field no longer travels, so the request to erase it never arises. **THE SAFE FALLBACK, named:** a page with no server config reads every field as changed and behaves as today. **FOUR CALLERS ARE COVERED BY THE ONE DOOR** — Turf, Site, Traffic and the settings import all go through `patchGaipConfig`; the import's behaviour changes with them, and it changes for the better: a field absent from the imported bundle no longer erases the stored one. `traffic` still travels on every save because its own `savedAt` is new each time, which is section data and not a condition. **THREE MUTATIONS, control green first, each printing its subject.** Let untouched fields travel again: `patched` grows from one field to six and four cases redden — the loss is back. Make an empty control with nothing stored a clear again: `cleared` gains five paths and two cases redden — the form asks to erase what nobody touched. Lose the server baseline: five cases redden, everything reads as changed. Jest 278 suites, 3428 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 356 passed.

**GH-638** (пункт 5, звено 11, устройство аналитика 4.13) Link 11, first delivery: the two server inputs the composer of an emptiness sentence needs, and nothing on screen yet. **THE ANALYST'S CORE FINDING, and this closes it: the composer had no input about the numbers a person is looking at.** `lastRun` describes the last ATTEMPT, and `runShape()` carried its skipped steps and journal entries only when that attempt was `partial`. Measured in the database this night: 45 complete rows hold 59 journal entries between them, and the projection discarded every one — a complete row reached the screen with no account at all. A sentence built from `lastRun` would then describe one run while standing under another's figures, which is GH-459's shape inside a single screen. **SO THE PROJECTION NOW CARRIES `numbersRun` BESIDE `lastRun`**, taken from the row whose numbers are shown, on EVERY outcome: `{outcome, skipped, notApplicable, notes, assumptions}`. `notes` are the `level: 'info'` entries THAT CARRY A REASON CODE — prose with no code is a line for a log, not a cause a sentence can be built from. **GH-573's `continue` is untouched, and that is the point of this door:** the panel still does not print `info`, and the composer reaches those entries without it being removed. `runShape()`, `warningLines()` and the panel are unchanged. **THE SECOND HALF: A REASON CARRIES ITS CLASS, and the class decides whether pressing again is offered.** `NOTHING_A_RETRY_CAN_FIX = ['no-soil-sample']` was a second list beside the reasons — a second place to remember, which the section composer would have had to remember too, so panel and section could have disagreed about the offer. Each of the 22 codes now carries `class` beside `text` in the one table, `retryCanHelp()` derives the offer, and `classOf(null)` is the honest fifth class `not-recorded` rather than a guess. Behaviour is unchanged: `no-soil-sample` is `input-absent` and offers nothing, every other existing code is `run-incomplete` and offers the press, exactly as the hand-written list did. An unclassified code falls to `run-incomplete` — the safe side, since telling someone nothing can help when it can leaves them stuck. **THE BROWSER IS UNCHANGED:** `clientTexts()` still hands it a flat code-to-sentence map, built from the same table; the classes stay on the server, because sending them would make the browser a second reader of a server decision. **`producedSomething()` IS PUBLIC NOW, as plan 4.13b point 2 requires:** "is this section empty" gets ONE answer, on the server. Four pages have four conditions today and they disagree — `computed.pgr` without `gdd` is produced to the server and empty to `/plan`. **NO TEXT WAS WRITTEN AND NO TEST COMPARES ONE:** every claim is about the class, the offer or the input, which is what the plan asks at this stage; the words are the owner's. **THREE MUTATIONS, control green first, each naming what it breaks.** Take the account from the last attempt again: the case that keeps the two rows apart reddens — the section would describe a failed attempt while standing under complete numbers. Carry notes only on a partial row, as `runShape` does: the complete-row case reddens with `size 0 matches expected size 1` — the 59 entries are lost again. Stop reading the class in the offer: the `no-soil-sample` case reddens — a site with no sample is sent round the loop again. **TWO GUARDS OF OTHERS CAUGHT THE CHANGE AND WERE FOLLOWED, NOT LOOSENED:** `Gh546AnalysisResultsOwnerTest` asserts the projection's exact shape and named the new key; `gh586` parses the reasons table out of the PHP and needed the new entry shape, and now also asserts its parser matched something. **DELIVERED IN PARTS, and this is part one of three:** the composer's `section()` with the key-to-step map from the graph is next, then the pages (`renderEmpty`, `renderPGR`) and the two watchers. Jest 278 suites, 3428 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 366 passed.

**GH-639** (пункт 5, звено 11, вторая часть) `AnalysisNotice::section($key, $projection)`: one sentence per empty section, or nothing when the section is not empty. **THREE THINGS DECIDE IT, AND NONE IS A PAGE.** Whether it is empty: `AnalysisResults::producedSomething`, the server's own predicate — four pages have four conditions today and they disagree, `computed.pgr` without `gdd` is produced to the server and empty to `/plan`. Which run to ask: `numbersRun` (GH-638), the account of the row whose numbers are on screen, never `lastRun`. What happened: the cause recorded against the step that writes the key, looked for in `notApplicable`, then `skipped`, then the journal notes — **which is the door GH-573's `continue` does not have to be removed for; the panel still never prints `info`.** **THE STEP IS DERIVED FROM TWO DECLARED SOURCES, NOT RESTATED BESIDE THEM, and measuring that took two attempts. The graph names ENGINES (`pgr-module`) and the run warns under STEP NAMES (`pgr`)** — my first reading returned `pgr-module` and every case went `not-recorded`, which is how I learnt that a "key to step" table would have been a third spelling of the same fact. So: the graph is asked whether ANY engine writes `computed.<key>`, `STEP_NAMES` is asked whether that step exists, in either of the tree's two spellings (`stressTrajectory` is warned under `stress-trajectory`), and a key both sources do not confirm gets NO step. Nothing is written down twice, and a key nobody declares gets an honest `not-recorded` rather than a plausible guess. **THE GAP IS MEASURED AND NAMED RATHER THAN FILLED:** of the 17 consumer keys the schema declares, 10 get a step; 7 do not — `applicationWindow`, `confidence`, `forecast`, `soilNutrition`, `soilTempPhysics`, `tissue`, `waterBalance`. Six of them are assembled by the row's producer and are nobody's graph output; `tissue` is warned under `tissue-corrective`, a spelling neither source derives from the other. **`soilNutrition` IS IN THAT LIST, so the soil section — link 11's main case — answers `not-recorded` until that gap is closed, and where it should be closed is the analyst's decision, reported rather than patched.** **NO WORDS WERE WRITTEN.** `text` is the sentence the one reasons table already holds; `UNWORDED` (plan 4.13b point 3) decides what stands in for a code with no sentence, and the tree is effectively `code`, so that is what it holds; a cause never recorded returns `text: null` and its class, because the words for that case are the owner's. Not one test compares an English phrase — every claim is about the class, the place, or the offer, exactly as the plan asks at this stage. **THE COMPOSER READS SOMEBODY ELSE'S FILE WITH A PATTERN, so both sides watch it:** in JavaScript the graph is RUN and the consumer keys that get a step are printed; in PHP the composer's own reading is compared against an independent count of every `'computed.X'` in the same file — 21 against 21 — so a reformat that hides an engine collapses the count and reddens instead of quietly turning sections into `not-recorded`. **FOUR MUTATIONS, control green first, each naming what it breaks.** Read `lastRun` instead: four cases redden — the section would describe a failed attempt while standing under complete numbers. Put the page's own emptiness condition back: the predicate case reddens — two readers of one question again. Stop letting journal notes reach a sentence: `engine-produced-nothing` comes back null — GH-573's `continue` wins and the note is lost. Give a key with no declared step one anyway: the boundary case reddens with the wrong list — a guessed cause. Jest 278 suites, 3430 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 376 passed.

**GH-640** (пункт 5, звено 11, третья часть) The pages stop writing their own emptiness, the delivery door carries the composed sentences, and two watchers hold it. **THE DOOR (plan 4.13 point 4):** `clientTexts($projection)` gains `sections` — an answer for EVERY consumer key the schema declares, `null` where the section has numbers — and `analysis-pill.blade.php` passes the projection. The texts ride in the same HTML response as the figures, so "the numbers arrived and the words did not" cannot happen. The universe comes from `AnalysisResultSchema::consumerKeys()`, the declared list, not from a list of "sections that can be empty" written beside it. **THE PAGE (`plan-ui.js`, PGR section and PGR card):** both now ask the server two things they used to answer themselves — whether the section is empty, and why. The page's own condition was `!pgr || !pgr.gdd`, and the server's predicate disagrees: that shape is a produced result to it. Two readers of one question, and the page's answer was the one a client read. Its literal was false twice over on `Burns` — it said no PGR application was recorded when one was (TE250, 99 days against a 90-day window) and it invited a re-run that gives the same answer every time; both sentences are gone from the file. **NO WORDS WERE WRITTEN FOR THE SCREEN.** Where a cause was recorded, the page prints the composer's sentence; where none was, it prints the class and the code plainly, because the words for that case are the owner's. **THE SOIL SECTION IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED, and the address is named so her answer lands in one place:** `soil-nutrition-analysis.js`, `function renderEmpty()` and its call at `if (!sn || (!sn.nutrients && !sn.tissue))`. The composer cannot place `soilNutrition` on a step yet (GH-639's measured gap), so moving it over would print "the cause was not recorded" over a row that records `no-soil-sample` — a new untruth on screen, produced by this very work. A case asserts the literal is still there and MUST go red the day the gap closes. **WATCHER ONE, POSITIVE — the opposite direction from `gh548`.** That guard is negative and narrow: it looks for the server's phrases inside assets, so a page writing its OWN different sentence is invisible to it, which is how about fifteen such literals live at a green suite. This one hands the renderer a sentinel through a sandbox and requires that the sentinel is what appears, plus a positive control that the renderer wrote anything at all. **WATCHER TWO, COPIES — built from what `clientTexts()` OUTPUTS**, every string it hands the browser, whatever constant it was declared as. `gh548`'s pattern matches `=> '…'` and cannot see `FAILURE_FRAME` or `UNKNOWN_REASON`, whose copies therefore live in the tree unnoticed. Measured: 40 composer strings against 235 assets, 2 copies, both in `dashboard-ui.js`, named as the remainder with their reason (the opener composes the failure sentence at the moment of failure; switching it to the server's changes what a client reads and is the owner's). **AND THE SIGN'S OWN LIMIT IS WRITTEN DOWN:** the analyst names three copies, this finds two — the third is assembled from a fragment in `settings-init.js` rather than copied whole, so a search for whole strings cannot see it. **THE REVIEWER'S CHECK, RUN: break the source and see whether the map follows.** `stepsFromGraph()` takes a path so a broken graph can be handed to it: with `computed.pgr` removed from the graph the map no longer holds `pgr`, and an emptied graph raises rather than answering with an empty map that would turn every section into "cause not recorded". Nothing in the tree is touched — the broken copies are temporary files. **FOUR MUTATIONS, control green first.** Let the page decide emptiness again: three cases redden. Put the literal back: four redden, including the one that reads the file. **GH-649** (пункт 3ж, устройство аналитика 4.12а, в её порядке) The note about an exhausted PGR window survives the pass, because it is now BORN inside it. **HER ORDER WAS KEPT, and it is not decoration: the two composer changes come FIRST, or there is a tree in between where a code reaches a screen.** (1) `UNWORDED` stops being `code` — the value is REMOVED from the allowed set, not merely unselected — so a cause with no words gives the page nothing and the page keeps the sentence it has. The server now reads both shapes (`AnalysisResults::reasonOfNote`, `AnalysisNotice::reasonOfEntry`), and a truncated string that no longer parses yields null rather than a guess. Without this the note would have reached the composer as prose with no cause, and link 11 would have said "not recorded" over a row that records it. **HER PREDICTION ABOUT `gh597` HELD TO THE LETTER:** two cases of five went red, exactly the two she named, with exactly the failure she wrote down — `Expected length: 1 / Received length: 0`. **GH-663** (пункт 3ак, устройство аналитика раздел 29) THE RUN FRAME IS BUILT FOR THE SITE IT WAS ASKED FOR. `/hub` took its site from `users.last_active_site_id`, so a frame opened as `/hub?rerun=r&site=<A>` while the pointer stood on B rendered B's config, B's coordinates, B's species, B's turf type and — through `GAIP_HUB_CONFIG.activeSiteId` — B's samples, while `?site=` decided only the address the row was filed under. **MEASURED, NOT ARGUED (GH-660, GH-661):** with the pointer on `Westview` and the frame opened for `Burns`, a write that was HELD instead of sent carried `site_id: Burns` with Westview's soil sample 118, its sample date `2026-07-27`, its soil temperature 18.5 °C and its warm-season `Large Patch` — four independent witnesses, none of them the coordinate check, which I had written wrongly and said so. Rows in the table: 74 before, 74 after. That is the GH-459 class with a second address: the right curve on another site's temperatures, and the annual totals still agree because the annual figure is normalised to its target. **THREE LAYERS, EACH CATCHING ITS OWN THING, in the analyst's order.** (1) `App\Support\PageSite` is the ONE place that decides which site a page is rendered for, and both `layouts/app.blade.php` and `hub.blade.php` ask it — they read the pointer separately before, so repairing one would have rendered half of one site and half of another (her 29.6). A request carrying BOTH `rerun` and `site` is a frame and is rendered for the parameter; everything else follows the pointer exactly as before, including the report pages she put out of scope. Access is the API's own rule, and **an unreachable or unknown site is refused rather than replaced by the pointer — falling back is the defect itself.** The pointer is never moved: a frame that wrote it would switch the site under the user's other tab. (2) The runner refuses to file when the document disagrees with the run's intent, or when `gaip:site-changed` fired after the start, and reports `site-mismatch` — a cause that had a sentence and no writer until now. (3) The server refuses a body whose `inputs.site` names another site, or whose `inputs.samples` carry a sample belonging to one, `422 site-mismatch`. **AN ABSENT DECLARATION IS NOT A DISAGREEMENT**, and that distinction is the one my own predictions measurement turned on (GH-662): reading those bodies for `site_identifier` — the COLUMN's name — instead of `site_id` returned nothing, and "the field is empty" would have read as "the server decides the site". There is no such outcome, so `PredictionController` now NAMES the record it drops — `skipped` with `site-missing` and a count — instead of swallowing it, where silence was indistinguishable from no write. **`gh547` CHANGED MEANING, AND THAT WAS ITS WORK.** Its harness set the document to another site for EVERY case, on the grounds that the address must not come from the pointer; half of that is still true and still asserted, the other half — that a frame may compute one site and file the numbers under another — is the defect. The default is now a document that agrees, and the divergence is set deliberately in the one case about it, which asserts no row and a `site-mismatch` report. **FOUR MUTATIONS, CONTROL GREEN BEFORE AND AFTER EACH.** The helper returning the pointer regardless of the parameter: three cases red, including `To contain: 01a0d0d6-…` — the site asked for, absent from the page. The runner's comparison removed: the new case red, `Expected - 1 / Received + 72` — the whole body it should not have sent. The server's check removed: two cases red, `422` became `200`. The named skip renamed: the predictions case red. **NOTHING A CLIENT SEES CHANGES ON A SITE THEY ARE LOOKING AT;** what changes is that a frame cannot compute one site and file under another. Jest 3459 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 422 passed.

M3 — the absent construction substituted with clay again — reddens the third case, which builds its state itself rather than relying on a live site, because all twelve have a construction today. M2 is a property and it holds: every expected word is a literal, never taken from the dictionary, so no case compares the dictionary with itself. **AND THE CASE A COPY COULD NOT SATISFY:** the same value resolved twice, the cell saying sand then clay, and the engine follows both times. **`gh656` LOST A CLAIM AND SAYS SO:** its `structurePathway` row compared the dictionary against the engine's table, and there is no table any more — comparing the dictionary with a reader that reads the dictionary is a mirror that cannot redden, so the row now asserts only that no table survived and points at `gh664` for the rest. **THE LIST IS PRINTED, not only the verdict** — twelve sites with their construction and pathway — because nine of them shared one wrong answer and a green without the list is indistinguishable from never reaching the subject. **What a client sees: nothing today** — no page and no export reads `soilStructure`, and stress takes only `suarezSAR` from it, which does not depend on the pathway. Comments are stripped with the line numbers kept true, since a shifted address is worse than useless in a census whose whole output is addresses. **THE PROBE IS PLANTED IN A NEW FILE, which was the reviewer's condition:** planting it in a file the census already names would show only that it re-reads what it knows, so the case creates a file that did not exist, watches both censuses name it by path and line, and deletes it whatever happens. **Both censuses print the files they examined and every match BY NAME before any verdict**, because "nothing found" and "never reached the subject" are otherwise the same output; and what is allowed is allowed BY NAME WITH A REASON, with the other direction asserted too -- an allowance whose file no longer exists is an open door nobody is watching. **A SIXTH PLACE WAS FOUND BY THE CENSUS ON ITS FIRST RUN and it is recorded as a finding, not as a permission:** `word-export.js:10991` MANUFACTURES a CaCl2 pH from a water pH by subtracting 0.5, in a document a client reads. It is the same class in the opposite direction and it is not among the five the analyst named; it is carried to the coordinator and the entry goes when it is settled. Jest 3495 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-675** (пункт 4, срез 1, устройство аналитика 22.7) A MISSING INPUT IS JUDGED AGAINST WHAT EXISTED WHEN THE RUN STARTED, NOT AGAINST THE DATABASE AT THE MOMENT OF WRITING. The owner named two cases and they get different sentences -- "the data was there but did not get into the calculation, that is our problem" against "there was no data, so that part was not calculated" -- and telling them apart needs to know what existed WHEN THE RUN BEGAN. **WHY NOT THE DATABASE AT WRITE TIME, and this is the reviewer's condition carried into the device rather than answered with a caveat:** a sample created between the start and the write is absent to the run and present to the server, so judging by "now" writes "it did not arrive" -- a true statement on a false premise. That is the GH-459 class stretched over minutes, and it flips with no defect in the code at all. The two readings are made SIMULTANEOUS by recording one of them. **WHERE AND WHEN:** the first thing the server does for a run is render its frame, so `App\Support\RunStart` records the set there -- the live samples per type and whether each key of the inputs list is filled -- under the run's own id, with `Cache::add` so the FIRST write wins and reopening the frame cannot move the start forward. The store is the database on this stand (`CACHE_STORE=database`), so **no column and no migration**; at write time the set is copied into the row's `detail` so the judgement can be read back later instead of recomputed against a database that has moved. The set is never handed to the frame: that would be browser state written back to the server, which this project forbids. **THREE ANSWERS, AND THE THIRD KEEPS US HONEST:** absent at the start gives `input-not-entered`, present at the start gives `input-did-not-arrive`, and NO RECORD of the start gives `run-start-not-recorded` -- our side too, because a client cannot be blamed for a fact nobody wrote down. `input-not-entered` deliberately carries NO TEXT: its sentence needs the human name of the input, and the `label` field of the inputs list is the owner's draft, so a section with this cause keeps the phrase the page already prints. **THE ANALYST'S MUTATION FOR O-14 REDDENS EXACTLY ITS OWN CASE:** the server consulting the database at write time turns the sample-created-after-the-start case red while the it-was-there-and-did-not-arrive neighbour stays green. **AND A SILENT DROP WAS FOUND BY THE FIRST RUN OF THE SET:** the row filed an EMPTY judgement while the body carried a full one, because `detail.notApplicable` was not named in the validation rules and Laravel hands back only the keys the rules declare. It is declared now; without the printed row beside the verdict that would have looked like a device that simply does nothing. **Slice 1 is the two server halves.** The run's own writer of `notApplicable` lives in the orchestrator and is not in this slice. PHPUnit 455 passed; Jest 3495 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-676** (пункт 6, остаток стадии 0б; устройство аналитика 59.2, 59.4, 59.5) THE DEPENDENCY GRAPH BECOMES DATA, AND THE TEST'S FIRST RUN IS THE WORK ITEM. The graph data file is TRANSFORMED out of the definitions that already lived in `dependency-graph.js` -- 26 nodes, all with outputs -- never retyped, because a retyped list is the class this repository spent the day removing. `runner`, `handle` and the split of the old `inputs` into `requires`/`uses` are left EMPTY on purpose: whether an input is required or merely used is a judgement about what a module does without it, and the test prints every hole so the data is filled from that list one line at a time. `App\Support\DependencyGraph` reads it, a graph that did not load is an OUTCOME rather than an empty graph, and the page is handed it as data so the browser copy stops carrying its own nodes. **THE FIRST RUN FOUND THAT MODULES WITHOUT A NODE ARE SEVEN, NOT THREE.** Beyond `soilStructure`, `water` and `soilTempPhysics`, which the plan named, real passes also write `soilNutrition`, `salinityPenalty`, `wearRecovery`, `waterBalance`, `forecast`, `confidence` and `mlsnRows` with no node declaring them; all seven are recorded with what they appear to be, and an EIGHTH reddens. **AND IT FOUND TWO FAULTS IN MY OWN COMPARISON BEFORE IT FOUND ANYTHING ABOUT THE PRODUCT:** I compared the roots a row writes against the nodes' DOTTED declarations, so sixteen modules looked like orphans when each has a node speaking at a different depth; and I had not separated the pass's own bookkeeping -- `attempted`, `skipped`, `warnings`, `passInputs`, `passStartedAt` -- from a module's outputs. Both are repaired and both are named in the file. **UNIVERSE (c) TAKES THE RECEIVER FROM THE FUNCTION'S OWN SIGNATURE, and it has TWO forms, the second found by the positive control failing.** A cascade delegate takes the state as its first parameter -- `gaip_firmness_engine(e, t)` reads `e.turf.drainage`, which is the read `GH-644` cannot see -- while an orchestrator builder takes NO parameter and reads the module-scope `_hubState` THROUGH LOCAL ALIASES. The parameter sign alone reported zero reads for `buildWearRecoveryInputs`, which is exactly what a census must never do quietly; with one declared hop of aliasing it reads seventeen, including `turf.construction`. Results of other modules (`computed.*`) and the state's own section names are separated out with a reason: they belong to `after`, not to `requires`. Reads through deeper aliases stay outside the sign and are PRINTED — `r = e.soil` in the firmness body — rather than swallowed. **THE PROBE IS PLANTED IN A NEW FILE, through the parameter `e`**: a delegate and a wrapper in a file that did not exist, found by path and by both receivers, deleted whatever happens. Jest 3510 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 455 passed.

**GH-677** (пункт 6а; устройство аналитика 59.2, 59.4, 59.5, 59.7 и 60.6) THE GRAPH'S DEVICE IS FILLED IN FROM THE TEST'S OWN OUTPUT, AND UNIVERSE (a) CLOSES. `runner` and `handle` are measured at the CALL SITES -- the cascade's run loop and the orchestrator's two pass bodies -- never from the plan's tables, which had already drifted from each other. **MODULES WITH NO NODE WERE TEN AND ARE NOW NONE.** Only ONE of the three the plan named was genuinely missing a node, `soilStructure`; the water engine already had one under a different id (`water-blender` IS `executeWaterEngine`, the same class as `mlsn-engine` <-> `mlsn-calculator`); `mlsnRows`, `salinityPenalty` and `wearRecovery` are SECOND KEYS of existing nodes, and `salinityPenalty` is one module written under two spellings by the two passes. `computed.forecast` was not a missing node at all: `disease-forecast` declared `computed.diseaseForecast`, a key NO pass has ever written. `confidence` moved to the pass account -- it is handed the pass, reads no input, and its `after` would be the whole graph -- and `soilNutrition` and `waterBalance` into a new class named with its reason, sections the ROW PRODUCER assembles out of other modules' results. An eleventh reddens. **`runner` AND `handle` ARE A LIST WHERE TWO PASSES RUN ONE MODULE.** Four do, and a single string would have had to drop one of them with its reads unchecked; the two lists are pairwise and the test holds their lengths equal. **A HANDLE MAY BE QUALIFIED `file:function`, because `generateForecast` is declared in THREE files** and a bare name resolves to whichever the listing reaches first -- the silent first match this repository has spent two days removing. An ambiguous bare name reddens instead of choosing. **FIVE NODES KEEP `runner: null` AND SAY WHY**, in the data: no pass writes their output, they are libraries or page modules, and a node with neither runner nor reason reddens. **THE SPLIT IS A JUDGEMENT AND IT IS MADE ON PRINTED EVIDENCE.** For every read the test names the code line it stands on and whether that line SUBSTITUTES, which is the analyst's own sign: 171 reads, 162 substituting, 9 bare. So `uses` carries 144 names and `requires` carries ONE -- the salinity engine's `water.ecw`, which is a GATE in both passes rather than a substitution. Under-declaring `requires` is the safe direction: an optional input moved into it stops a module computing where it computes today, and that changes a client's numbers without a decision. **FIVE FAULTS IN MY OWN SIGN, EVERY ONE FOUND BY ITS OWN OUTPUT RATHER THAN BY RE-READING IT:** (1) universe (c) took `handle` as a string, so the four nodes that declare two reported ZERO reads and nothing said so; (2) bodies were read WITH THEIR COMMENTS, and a docblock naming `soil.pH` and `soil.Mn_ppm` invented six reads `buildDiseaseInputs` does not make -- the same prose-as-code fault as census 1 of `GH-674`; (3) the result class was taken from the graph's own output roots, but the state's INPUT sections share those names, so forty real inputs -- `water.ecw`, `pgr.applicationDate`, `tissue.N` -- were reported as results; (4) an alias was matched anywhere in a chain, so `climate?.temperature?.soil?.mean` produced a read `soil.mean` out of a substring; (5) a WRITE was counted as a read, so the irrigation builder appeared to require the sensor value it writes. **THE CASCADE RENAMES SECTIONS AND THE MAP IS PARSED FROM ITS OWN ASSEMBLY:** `traffic` is `schedule` and `shade` is `site`, so `state.traffic.restDays` IS `schedule.restDays`; a census reporting the local name would invent two inputs and miss the one that exists. **`after` NOW EARNS ITS PLACE:** a read of an upstream node's output root is a result, decided from the graph rather than from a list of spellings, so a result read from a node NOT declared upstream still reddens. **THE INPUTS LIST GAINED 52 NAMES AND NOT ONE NEW QUESTION TO A CLIENT:** 37 spellings as `readAs` of inputs that exist, 6 as `derived`, 3 as `notInputs`, and 6 new rows whose place of entry was MEASURED in the Settings form (drainage, the three Clegg readings, the two grow-light fields, soil moisture, irrigation method). Both directions of the list are claims now: an input no node reads is a spare, and the three that remain are allowed BY NAME with what each is, with a stale allowance reddening too. **ONE SIDE OF `GH-644` MOVED HERE BECAUSE ITS UNIVERSE COULD NOT ANSWER IT** (59.5 item 7): it demanded that every name the list excuses be read, over a universe of cascade engines only, so `site.country` and `pgr.gddThreshold` -- both read by an orchestrator builder -- looked like excuses for reads nobody makes. It was right to exist and wrong about the facts. Asked here over every script, it holds; and my own first form of it was the SAME fault pointing the other way, asserting over the nodes' handles alone and failing on fourteen names read by page modules, so it is narrowed to a universe that is complete. **SIX INPUTS ARE READ THAT NO SURFACE FILLS -- not a form, not the wizard, not the API -- and they are recorded against their nodes rather than declared.** Where such an input belongs in the list is the analyst's decision; the measured cost of the question is `fertility.monthlyN`: it gates the nitrogen engine, and all 37 stored rows that carry `computed.nitrogen` hold the skipped stub, so N-opt has never computed on this stand. **AND THE CHANGELOG ITSELF WAS FOUND BROKEN BY ITS OWN GUARD'S REPAIR.** Entries were being appended before the FIRST literal `## Backlog`, which appears inside the `GH-669` entry's own prose: that SPLIT the entry, left its tail standing at the start of a line looking exactly like the heading, and put every entry from `GH-670` on INSIDE it. The guard read the section only up to that false heading and stayed green over it. The entry is one again, the section end is an exact heading line, the glued-entry sign now means NOTHING BETWEEN rather than any mid-line marker -- it was reddening on legitimate prose mentions of `**GH-461**` -- and its line numbers are counted from the file instead of from the section, which is how it named line 1090 for text on line 1316. Jest 3517 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 455 passed.

**GH-678** (пункт 6, место 3 — ворота; устройство аналитика 59.5, 59.6, 77.4, 77.10, 77.12, 77.20–77.23) THE GRAPH'S DATA COMES FROM THE PAGE, ITS ABSENCE IS AN OUTCOME, AND WHO EXECUTES A MODULE IS ANSWERED FROM A PARSE. `dependency-graph.js` carried twenty-six engines of its own beside three other hand-written declarations of the same facts; it now reads `window.GAIP_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH` and **335 lines of literals are gone** -- not retyped elsewhere, because the data file was transformed out of that block and then filled in from the test's own output. **GIVEN NOTHING IT INSTALLS NOTHING.** A graph built from nothing answers every question with "nothing": `getAffectedEngines('soil.CEC')` returns `[]`, and the coming warning would read "changing this affects nothing" -- a false statement wearing a correct answer's clothes. Two absences are told apart (no injection against an injected graph with no nodes), every caller already falls back to recomputing EVERYTHING, and a case measures the cost: with the gate removed the same module answers `[]` where the real graph names eight engines. **THE GATE'S FIRST RUN FOUND A LIVE HOLE ON THREE PAGES A CLIENT CAN OPEN:** `reports/export`, `reports/scenarios` and `reports/forensic` load the module and were never given the data -- the global was injected in `layouts.app` and they extend `layouts.db-shell`. Until the gate they used the literal copy silently. One injection per layout. **AND IT FOUND THAT THREE OF OUR OWN GUARDS WERE GREEN AGAINST A STALE COPY:** `gh572`, `gh584` and `gh639` read the module in a sandbox, so while it carried the literal they compared with that instead of the data. The moment the data became real they disagreed -- two engines outside every bucket, six keys outside the pinned list, two dead aliases (`forecast` pointed at `computed.diseaseForecast`, a key no pass has ever written; `water` was listed as having no engine although `water-blender` IS the water engine). Two surfaces drifting together, which is the class this repository has a name for. **A LIVE 500 WAS CAUSED AND REPAIRED IN THE SAME WORK:** `AnalysisNotice::stepsFromGraph()` parsed the JS file's TEXT with a regular expression over those literals, found zero outputs, threw, and every page printing a notice answered 500. Found by the PHP suite, forty-six failures deep, not by a client. The composer reads the data through its reader now, and the reviewer's own check survives the move -- the path is still a parameter, so breaking the SOURCE still breaks the answer. **WHO EXECUTES A NODE IS A FIXPOINT OVER CALL SITES, NOT A WALK ALONG PATHS.** The kind of a call site comes from the FUNCTION it sits in, never from the file: the call to `buildIrrigationInputs` is inside `executeEngine`, which lives in the orchestrator's file and is reached only from a dead export -- deciding by file said `orchestrator`, coherent and false. A value is the union of its callers' values, iterated to convergence; the limit is computed before the count from the shape of the problem (4922 functions x lattice height 10397) and printed with the actual number, and a run that has not settled fails with its own word rather than hanging. A non-monotone update is caught where it happens. The unresolved is a VALUE, not an absence, so a branch this device cannot follow cannot vanish from a complete-looking answer. **SIX FAULTS OF MY OWN DEVICE, EVERY ONE FOUND BY ITS OWN OUTPUT, AND FOUR OF THEM CAME OUT GREEN:** (1) `handle` read as a string, so four nodes with two handles reported ZERO reads; (2) bodies read WITH their comments, inventing six reads out of a docblock; (3) the result class taken from the graph's output roots, which share their names with the state's input sections, so forty real inputs were reported as results; (4) an alias matched anywhere in a chain, making `soil.mean` out of a substring; (5) a WRITE counted as a read; (6) **EXPORT-AS-EXECUTION** -- `global.GaipOrchestrator = { populateCanonicalState }` is a reference at a file's top level, and counting it as an execution collapsed EVERY chain to `page` and hid the registry roots entirely. Not emptiness: a coherent, plausible, entirely wrong answer. **AND THREE MORE IN THE RESOLVER, each of the same family as the bare key:** the object dropped from a member call, so `hub.orchestrator.computeSelective` resolved to the same-named function of another file with a different body; the third form of an export (`global.NAME = NAME` with the literal declared apart) left two nodes looking unexecuted; and AMBIGUITY DECIDED BY FILE ORDER -- 32 member signatures have more than one candidate, and the `gilba`/`gssh` twins resolved differently when the universe was listed in reverse. Ambiguity is declared now, not chosen, and the walk's output is byte-identical under a permuted order. **THE PARSE REPLACED A LIST OF PATTERNS**: the six function forms come from `@babel/types`' own alias, callers are every reference to a binding (so a callback handed to `addEventListener` is a caller without any list of places one can be handed over), and `getFunctionParent()` decides the enclosing function -- with anonymous told apart from none, because treating an anonymous callback as the file's top level made a config write inside `bindEvents` a page entry point of six views. Two written lists remain and both are on the surface: the node types that carry a `callee`, checked against the PARSER's schema rather than against what appeared in the files (declared: this catches an incomplete list BEFORE a case exists, and the parser's set is FIVE, not the three first written), and the rule for resolving a member across files. **WHAT CANNOT BE RESOLVED IS RATCHETED BY NAME, NOT COUNTED:** 196 places by kind, and DEAD CALL SITES in a list of their own -- 37 -- because the two mistakes are not equally reversible. In the ratchet blindness costs a spare link; in the dead list it would invite deleting live code, the one irreversible act here. So every dead entry says HOW the absence was established (a bindings parse, which covers an alias) and none claims confirmation while a call on a property of a property goes unresolved. Both lists are ratcheted in both directions, under a fingerprint of the resolution rule -- and that fingerprint had a hole of its own: the list moved 198 to 207 while the version stood still, because it covered one function and resolution depends on the collection of exports as well. **GRANULARITY OF THE BOUNDARY, AND IT IS A NUMBER:** 262 files parse, 21 only in part -- all of them views' inline `<script>` carrying Blade, NONE in `assets`, asserted from both sides. A partial parse must be visible or it drops a piece of the universe silently, so `ast.errors` is read after every parse, and a PERMANENT case plants a file whose syntax Babel RECOVERS from (`break` outside a loop, chosen by measuring eleven candidates) -- a probe on the thrown road would have guarded the `try/catch` and left the check bare. Jest 3544 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 455 passed.

**GH-679** (замер к пункту 6а, заказан ревьюером) DOES THE NUTRITION CALENDAR'S `init()` WRITE WITHOUT A HUMAN PRESS, AND DOES ANYTHING LEAVE THE PAGE WHEN IT DOES. The calendar starts itself when its file loads and that file is loaded by five views including the run frames, so if it writes state with nobody touching anything it belongs to the class of state written without a human action -- and this would have been its third case. **TWO QUESTIONS WITH DIFFERENT ANSWERS**, because answering only the first would make a page being filled from its own site's saved data look like the defect. **IT DOES WRITE `program` WITH NOTHING PRESSED, in a run frame as well as on `/plan`** -- through `restoreFromPersisted()`, from `GAIP_SITE_CONFIG.nutritionCalendarProgram`, which `site-config-persistence.js` sets from the server's config. **AND NOTHING LEAVES THE PAGE:** `GAIP_SiteConfig.mergeConfig` 0, `localStorage.setItem` 0, `fetch` with any method but GET 0, in both states. Server to page is the direction this project wants; page to server without a human is the defect, and it does not happen. The two roads that DO persist are behind a human action. **BOTH STATES ARE BUILT AND THE CASE SAYS WHICH IT MEASURED** -- the reviewer's condition, and his reason is the measurement's whole value: on `/plan` this same write is ORDINARY WORK, so "it writes" alone answers nothing. The pair makes the frame result a statement about WHERE. **THE PROGRAMME IS A REAL ONE OFF THE STAND** (8KB, twelve months) rather than a shape I imagined -- the first form of the test used an invented programme and the render threw on a field it had never heard of. **A READ IS NOT A WRITE**, and the first recorder did not tell them apart: the plan state fetches its own site's tissue samples, a GET, and that counted as something leaving the page. **AND THE ATTRIBUTION DEVICE WAS ABANDONED RATHER THAN PATCHED:** brace matching over JavaScript without a parser is not sound, it named a nested helper, then a method closed a hundred lines earlier, then nobody at all -- so the claim moved onto EXECUTION (zero writes on a load, recorded) and the attribution stayed as a print with its unsoundness written beside it. Jest 3544 passed, 0 failed.

**GH-680** (пункт 6а, данные; устройство аналитика 60.6, 77.19, 77.22, 77.23) THE THREE NODES THAT ARE NOT PASS MODULES, AND `page` AS AN ADDRESS RATHER THAN A LABEL. The graph gains `nutrition-calendar` and `scenario-engine` with `runner: 'page'`, and `nutrition-summary` with `runner: 'producer'` -- the row producer calls it immediately before the one write. **THE ADDRESS IS A VIEW**, the template the server renders; a partial's and a layout's scripts belong to every view that uses them, so both the `@include` and the `@extends` chains are followed. Resolving a page root to the ASSET FILE instead gave eighty-five "addresses" for one node, which is noise; resolved to views it is 73 pairs, and each carries HOW the node got there -- `top-level`, where code runs when the view loads the file and the address is exact, against `listener`, where a listener was only put in place and whether it fires is unknown. **ONLY THE DECLARED INTENT GOES INTO THE GRAPH: `plan` for the calendar, `reports/scenarios` for the scenario engine.** Writing what the guard found into the data would make the graph check itself. The other **72 pairs are DIVERGENCES** (54 `top-level`, 18 `listener`) in a ratcheted list of their own with this ticket, and the batch has a declared closing condition -- a `top-level` pair leaves by being declared or by leaving the code, a `listener` pair by narrowing what reachable means -- because 85 entries under one ticket is one reason for eighty-five subjects. Nothing is added to the batch: a new divergence reddens by name. Both directions hold, as in the other ratchets: a pair that became declared or left the found set reddens as `resolved, remove from the list`. **EQUALITY IS DECLARED PLUS KNOWN DIVERGENCES EQUALS FOUND**, and a declared pair that is NOT found is split in two rather than read as a wrong declaration: with no unresolved edge it is `never calls it`; with one it is `not confirmed`, with the count. `scenario-engine : reports/scenarios` is the second -- `gaip-whatif-ui.js` takes `const scenarioEngine = global.GAIP_ScenarioEngine || …` and calls through that LOCAL ALIAS, so the member resolves by a name that is the alias. **AND THE HANDLE WAS WRONG UNTIL THE WALK SAID SO:** `buildState` is an internal step; the entry a human reaches is `compareScenarios`, which that UI names as its primary call. **TWO NODES' RUNNERS WERE TOO NARROW BECAUSE I DECIDED THEM BY FILE** -- `climate-engine` and `ambient-dli-engine` are reached from both passes through the shade engine's handle. Widening them killed the rule that runner and handle must be pairwise: one function is run by two passes, and I duplicated the handle for a minute to satisfy the rule before taking it out. Data written to satisfy a rule is worse than the rule being wrong; what holds is that every handle resolves and the declared set equals the found set, which contains pairwise as a special case. **THE CONDITION FOR SUBMITTING THESE NODES IS IN THE SUITE, AND IT COULD NOT BE WRITTEN EARLIER:** "no `page` root falls on a block the parse cannot read" would have run over an empty set and been green by emptiness. With two addresses declared it has a subject, its universe is the DATA rather than a list, and the evidence it will be compared against is printed whole -- including the zeros: 17 views carry an unreadable block, and of those only `data.blade.php` (2 of 5 readable), `reports/scenarios` (1 of 2) and `reports/export` (1 of 2) yield anything at all. **THE BOUNDARY, MEASURED:** the member resolution rule's found case is closed -- `hub.orchestrator.computeSelective` no longer produces a coherent wrong link, it produces `member-unresolved`, which is the safe direction -- but **275 resolved member links rest on the object's NAME matching** against 155 through a global's, so a local variable named like an exported object would give the same coherent wrong link. Every chain resolved that way counts as UNCONFIRMED until item 3bzh compares the static resolution with the run's own stack. Jest 3544 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 455 passed.

**GH-681** (пункт 6а, место 2; устройство аналитика 4.9 п. 2, 59.5 п. 6) THE CASCADE'S ENGINE LIST IS DERIVED FROM THE GRAPH, AND THE THIRD PLACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN CONVERTED. Three places declared the same engines by hand. TWO HAD ALREADY DRIFTED, each in its own direction: the adapter's `engineMap` carried `climate-engine`, `dew-prediction-engine` and `disease-engine`, none of which this adapter has a branch for, while `GAIP_CASCADE_ENGINES` named `mlsn-engine` and `water-engine` -- the graph calls those nodes `mlsn-calculator` and `water-blender`. Nothing compared either with the code, so neither could be wrong out loud. **BOTH COME FROM ONE PLACE NOW:** the cascade's engines are the nodes whose handle is declared in the adapter's own file, and the `computed` key each writes is the root of its first declared output. The handles are QUALIFIED with their file for this -- a bare name does not say which file it belongs to, and guessing by the `execute` prefix would be a rule about spelling rather than a fact. Thirteen engines, and the derived map reproduces every old value while the three stale entries simply are not there. **THE RENAME HAD TO COME WITH IT OR THE PASS WOULD HAVE GONE QUIET:** the run loop tested `engines.includes('mlsn-engine')`, so with the list derived and the loop untouched MLSN and the water engine would stop running while the list looked right. Every id the loop tests is now an id the graph declares, and that is a case. **NO GRAPH, NO PASS:** with nothing injected the engine list is empty and the adapter refuses instead of running an empty pass that reports success. **AND THE REFUSAL DOES NOT INVENT A CODE** -- the first form returned `reason: 'dependency-graph-unavailable'`, and `Gh644NoIdentifierAnywhere` caught it: a code the runner reports must carry a sentence a client reads, and the words are the owner's. The fact goes to the pass's journal instead. **THE THIRD PLACE IS LEFT ALONE, AND THE REASON IS A NUMBER.** `detectEnginesUsed` emits ids that are keys into the CITATION REGISTRY, not the graph's vocabulary. On a real stored row of 34 keys, a graph-derived detector would ADD FOURTEEN engines to a client's document and REMOVE THREE -- among them `water-quality`, which is a citations key carrying `ayers-westcot`, while `water-blender` is a key in the VERSIONS map. Deriving it would silently drop a reference from a document a client reads, which is not a rename and not mine to decide. **THE GATE'S FIRST FULL RUN TOOK SIX SUITES DOWN AT ONCE, and all six were the same shape:** the orchestrator bench loads the adapter without the graph, so the adapter refused and the passes produced nothing. A bench that stands in for the page has to give what the page gives. **AND TWO GUARDS HAD PINNED THE DRIFT IN PLACE:** `GH-644` read its universe out of the `engineMap:` literal that no longer exists, and pinned the count SIXTEEN -- the number of the stale map. Its universe is the graph now and its pin is the LIST of thirteen, because a count says only that a number changed. **AND MY OWN REPAIR THERE COST COVERAGE UNTIL IT WAS MEASURED:** locating an engine's body through the adapter's delegate is righter about WHICH file and landed on the wrapper where the old lookup landed on the body -- bodies with reads fell from six to three. Both roads are scanned now, distinct reads went from 41 to 42, and the floor moved off "how many bodies held reads", which turned out to be a fact about traversal order, onto how much the scan sees. Two inputs the better lookup exposed are placed: `climate.historical` and `turf.ambientDLISource`, both results the run produces rather than anything a client enters. Jest 3551 passed, 0 failed; PHPUnit 455 passed.

**GH-682** (серверный замер, форма аналитика 70.2) WHAT EVERY PAGE BEHIND THE LOGIN DOES FOR A USER WITH NO SITE. An account with no site is an ordinary state -- the first minute of every account -- and the question was which pages FALL OVER or send the person somewhere unintended. It needs no browser and no live stand: the suite has its own `sqlite :memory:`, so the user is created there and lives until the test ends. **THE UNIVERSE IS THE ROUTE TABLE**, not a list written in the test: every GET route whose middleware requires a login, with a parameterised route NAMED as skipped rather than left out, because a skipped route and a route nobody thought of look identical in a list of results. **THIRTY ROUTES WALKED, TEN NAMED AS SKIPPED, AND NOT ONE VIEW FELL OVER: 5xx is zero.** So the answer to "do the pages break on an empty site" is no, and the question of a client-side measurement does not arise. **ONE FINDING, AND IT IS TOLD APART BY A PAIR:** `/dashboard` answers 302 to `/no-access` for a user with no site, while for a user differing in EXACTLY ONE THING -- having a site -- the same page answers 200. So the cause is the empty site and not the state of the account, which matters because `/no-access` is the same door for both. Every other route answers for the same user, `/settings`, `/plan`, `/hub` and `/data` among them: exactly one door closes, and it is the first one a new account arrives at. The words on that door and where it should lead are the owner's, so they are not written here. **TWO FALSE PICTURES WERE TAKEN OFF THIS MEASUREMENT BEFORE IT WAS SUBMITTED, both mine.** Every route appeared to redirect to the PREVIOUS one in the walk -- that is `back()` reading a session shared across requests, so the session is flushed and the referer fixed. And **six `/api/*` routes appeared to answer a REDIRECT to a JSON caller**: they do not, I had asked an API for HTML. Asked with `Accept: application/json` the same route answers 422 JSON with a site and without one, which is a missing parameter rather than anything about an empty site. Submitting the first reading would have sent the owner a question about six defects that do not exist. PHPUnit 457 passed; nothing on the stand was touched.

Every read now carries `wasNull`, so a read of a key that was not there stops looking like a read of a key that was, and every site gets an execution class from the two together: `in-both` is a client's behaviour, `only-under-fabrication` is POSSIBLE for a client and not shown, `only-without-fabrication` is our own values stopping something a client does. **THE PAIRED PLANT SITS INSIDE THE DEVICE:** `probe_both_key` is read unconditionally and must come out `in-both`; `probe_onlyfab_child` is read only when its parent is present and the parent is seeded only under fabrication, so it must come out `only-under-fabrication`. Either one failing makes the device unfit. **A SITE THAT RAN IN NEITHER PASS GETS A REASON** from facts the journal shows elsewhere, and a silent `NOT EXECUTED` is gone. `ROUTE` lines carry the requested URL, where it actually landed, the status and the reads, per pass and for the run frame; `PASSED` names every non-GET that reached the stand with body and answer (exactly two, the declared pointer switch there and back), the distinct GET paths of each pass, and `GET /hub?rerun` with what the server writes for it; `HELD` ties each kept-back write to the page it came from through `req.frame().url()`. The output carries the DATE and a `READS-BY-SITE` block by `file:line`, so after the cache work removes some of them it can be said which it removed and which were never found. **AND THE ARITHMETIC IS TESTED WITHOUT THE STAND, because this device gets one press and no second:** the execution class, the reason, the control block and the header are pure functions, and layer 1 shows that one substituted expected value turns the header into `INSTRUMENT NOT VALID` and every reading into `UNTRUSTED`. Layer 1: 5 passed. The file's md5 is now `83c5869eda33575926daef62a758f877`.

**GH-692** (Вопрос 79, часть 0) WHICH NODES REALLY CANNOT COMPUTE WITHOUT AN INPUT, MEASURED — AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE THREE THIS BENCH CAN JUDGE ALL COMPUTE WITHOUT IT. `requires` was empty on every node but one, so the `requires`/`uses` split had never been made from evidence. What they produce is not an empty shell, which is why the shape is printed and not just the presence: with no soil sample at all `computed.mlsn` prints "Rootzone depth: 10.0 cm; Bulk density: 1.40 g/cm3", and with no water analysis `computed.water` prints "Salinity class: Low salinity risk" and "Sodium hazard (SAR): 0.00 - Low sodium hazard". The controls now assert that the input left the state and the engine ran without it; the verdict is printed as the finding. The control keeps its expectation and the header still says `INSTRUMENT NOT VALID`; a `DRY-REACH` line now states, per key, whether it was read, what kind was found, and that no Re-run frame and no `/hub` were opened. **TWO MORE THINGS THE ARTEFACT ITSELF FOUND:** the `WRITES` line said "2 RunStart rows, one per pass" on a pass that pressed no Re-run and wrote none -- it counts the actual `GET /hub?rerun` requests now, because a journal naming a write that did not happen is the one thing it must never do; and a `COUNTS |` line was added because every reading is prefixed `UNTRUSTED `, so a search anchored at the start of a line finds no `ROUTE` at all, which is how this journal was read as having none. Layer 1 covers the journal's assembly now: the four parts by POSITION, an empty control list forcing `INSTRUMENT NOT VALID: no controls were assembled`, and a dry journal stamping every reading while the header still says the instrument is fit. Both of the reviewer's mutations redden -- `controlsMissing = false` and dropping the `dry` stamp.

**GH-697** (3бд, шапка безвредного прохода) FOUR NUMBERS AND A LIST OF NAMES, SO "LOOKED AND FOUND NOTHING" STOPS LOOKING LIKE "NEVER LOOKED". The reviewer read the previous journal as "there was a file, there was no sight", and he was right that nothing in it could tell the two apart. Five conditions, all computed over reads WITHOUT the plants -- a device proving itself with its own plants proves only that it can plant: intercepted > 0 and bound to a census LINE > 0 in each pass; a marker reaching a sink in P; reads naming a census FILE and no census line = 0 in both, because the file is known and the tree did not move, so such a read is a broken binding rather than a gap in the census; and the views opened where one was asked for, BY NAME, since an empty list and "no ROUTE lines" are the same fact. **CONDITION 3 IS ASKED OF `P` ALONE, and that is the analyst's correction rather than a convenience:** `O` does not fabricate, so it has no markers, and the condition applied to it would make the device unfit on EVERY press -- a condition that cannot be met is indistinguishable from one that was not met. It is kept as a case so nobody restores the symmetry by reading the table. Layer 1 grew to ten cases: one per way of being blind -- nothing intercepted, reads that bind to nothing, the file recognised and the line not, an empty `ROUTE`, no marker reaching a sink -- each asserted to make the device unfit AND to name which condition failed, because "unfit" without the reason is what sent the last journal back.

**GH-698** (3бд) THE INSTRUMENT PRINTS WHICH FRAMES IT ENUMERATED AND WHEN, AND AN EMPTY ENUMERATION MAKES IT UNFIT. The reviewer's diagnosis was the same shape as the empty `ROUTE`: "there were no frames" and "there were frames and we looked later" were one silence, and the reading that decides between them is which. A frame is created, runs and is gone; a single enumeration after a twenty-second wait sees what is left. Now the lifecycle is recorded as it happens -- attached and detached, each with its moment and URL -- every enumeration is recorded with its moment, its reason and what it saw, and the frames ATTACHED and never enumerated are named on their own line. That line is the verdict the reviewer asked for: a frame enumerated and holding no marker means the CONTROL is wrong; a frame never enumerated means the INSTRUMENT is; and the honest third possibility, that the value reaches nothing and the expectation is wrong, stays open and is now separable from the other two. **THE SIXTH CONDITION:** no enumeration at all, or every enumeration empty, makes the device unfit, exactly as an empty `ROUTE` does; a run frame attached and never enumerated does too. **BEYOND WHAT WAS ASKED, and said so rather than folded in:** the pass now enumerates ten times during the Re-run wait instead of once after it, because printing alone would tell the NEXT press that a frame came and went unobserved without collecting what it read -- the point of the press is data, and the press happens once. Layer 1 grew to ten cases; the three new ones cover the two frame silences and the attached-but-never-enumerated run frame, and the sixth condition reddened the existing cases the moment it existed, because their fixture carried no enumerations -- a fixture short of a condition cannot judge it. Rehearsal: two enumerations per pass, one distinct frame, nothing attached and unseen.

**GH-700** (пункт 3ар) THE COMPARISON STOOD BEFORE THE RIGHT TO WRITE, AND MOVING IT CLOSES ONLY HALF. So the list does not leave: the body returns what the caller themselves sent, the type and the key that disagreed and the site it was filed under, and the owners are written to the journal with the `run_id`, where only an administrator sees them. The diagnosis is moved, not deleted, and a case holds that. **WHAT STILL LEAKS IS NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN:** the refusal itself says a sample with that key exists somewhere; it cannot go, guard 3ak rests on it, and it carries no identifier and no name. **AND ONE CODE CARRIED TWO MEANINGS:** the runner reported every `422` as `incomplete-result`, so a `site-mismatch` reached the failure report under the name of a different fault -- one asks the person for missing data, the other says the run must not be filed at all. The server names its refusal in `error` and that name travels; an unnamed `422` stays `incomplete-result`, and the pair is asserted together because a repair that renamed every `422` would be the same defect facing the other way. The measurement in `Gh666…Test` becomes a claim, since the decision it was waiting for has been taken. **THE UNESTABLISHED POINT IS SETTLED BY READING:** `recordFailure` inserts, so failure records with one `run_id` do NOT merge -- each report is its own row. Four mutations, each red on its own case: the early check removed (403 becomes 422), `belongsTo` restored, the journal silenced, the runner ignoring `error`. `owner` as a role needed nothing: it cannot be assigned since the June migration and the one row left is an administrator's. PHPUnit 487, jest 3589.

**GH-701** (пункт 3бд, три правки ревьюера) THE CONTROL WAS WRONG, NOT THE PRODUCT; THE KEY IS EXACT AND DERIVED; AND THE JOURNAL SAYS WHERE IT WAS WRITTEN. The control on the hub state expected `decides-input` and the instrument answered `inert`. Which of the two was wrong had been decided BEFORE the press: if the run frame is enumerated and no marker is found in it, the control is. The third press settled the premise -- the frame IS enumerated on a live pass, six markers issued inside it with sinks in it -- so the expectation becomes `inert`, with the reason beside it, because an expectation that moves without one is the thing this instrument exists to prevent. **THE KEY CARRIES A SUFFIX AND THAT WAS HALF THE REASON IT FAILED:** `hub-persistence.js` builds it as `'gilba_hub_state' + (userId ? '_' + userId : '')`, so the control now asks about ONE EXACT KEY, derived from that rule rather than matched by prefix or written as `gilba_hub_state_1`, which would bind it to whoever user 1 is on this stand. Both forms stay, because the two questions differ: the control asks about a key, the dry pass's choice of views asks which census sites read a key of that FAMILY. **AND THE SENTENCE ABOUT WHERE THE REHEARSAL WRITES WAS THE OPPOSITE OF THE CODE:** it promised "outside the repository unless told otherwise" while the default writes inside, beside the real journals. The instrument does what its code says; the sentence was wrong and is fixed, the journal now names its own path and whether it is inside, and `3bd-DRY-*` is ignored by git -- because a rehearsal artefact lying in the record beside real ones will one day be read as a measurement, and a name alone does not stop that. Three mutations, each red with its own signature: the expectation restored (`expected "decides-input" | got "inert"`), the base name instead of the exact key (`got "NOT MARKED"`), and the rehearsal no longer saying it is one. The rehearsal now comes back `INSTRUMENT valid`. **THE REVIEWER RETURNED IT AND HE WAS RIGHT: NOTHING GUARDED TWO OF THE THREE.** He put the suffix back and the expectation back and the suite noticed neither, because both lived in the live half, which the ordinary run skips — a repair no run can see lasts until the next person edits that line. So the key's rule and the control's construction are pure functions now, and two cases over clean data hold them without a stand: the key derives from the user and the rule is asserted against the product's own expression in `hub-persistence.js`, so a product that stops building it that way says so instead of the control quietly asking about a key nobody writes; and the control's name and its expectation are one claim, checked against a table where the BARE name carries a different value, which is what makes the exactness of the name a claim rather than a spelling. His own mutations redden them on the ordinary run: the suffix removed gives `Expected "gilba_hub_state_7", Received "gilba_hub_state"`, the expectation returned gives `Expected "inert", Received "decides-input"`.

**GH-703** (пункт 3аф) A LIVE TEST THAT NAMES A STAND SITE IS ONE THE OWNER'S OWN EDIT CAN BREAK, AND THE CLASS NO LONGER GROWS. `tests/gh703-live-tests-name-stand-sites-only-where-listed.test.js` walks `tests/e2e` (61 files, printed by name) and finds stand sites by UUIDv7 literal and by the site names the fixtures declare; the census must equal `tests/fixtures/gh703-stand-site-references.json` both ways (38 files, 113 references today), so a new reference is red with its file and a vanished one is red until the inventory shrinks. **GH-704** (пункт 3ас) THREE COPIES OF THE PREDICATE THAT DECIDES WHETHER A PASS PRODUCED SOMETHING, AND THE TWO IN THE BROWSER BECOME ONE. They agreed on every input, which is exactly why repairing one of them would have moved nothing any run could see and the two would have parted company in silence. `hub-orchestrator.js` defines it and hands it over; `cascade-orchestrator.js` asks for it and REFUSES rather than judging when it is absent, because a private fallback there would be the copy coming straight back, quietly. **ONE INPUT TABLE, READ BY BOTH LANGUAGES, WITH THE ANSWER DECLARED IN IT.** Comparing two of our own surfaces proves nothing -- after the repair the browser pair cannot disagree at all -- so each copy is checked against the declared answer instead, and a change in either language reddens that language's own case. The table lives under `app/tests/fixtures/` because that is the one place both runners can read: the container mounts only `assets` and the Laravel app, so PHPUnit cannot see `tests/`, while jest runs on the host. **THE SERVER KEEPS ITS OWN AND ASKS ONE THING MORE,** and that difference is declared rather than discovered: asked WITH a key it also consults the result form's `emptyWhen` marker, which is about the REASON a section is empty -- and this item does not consolidate the reason. A case names it, with the marker's value read FROM the form after the first version of that case invented one (`no-soil-data` against the declared `NO DATA`) and failed on a value of mine. **THE CENSUS OF COPIES TAKES ITS SIGN FROM THE FORM OF A BODY**, not from two words appearing in a file: the first version asked only that, and it named the cascade -- which carries those literals for its own refusals and no longer holds the predicate. The boundary is named: a copy spelling them through an extracted constant is NOT caught. Two files carry it now, by name. **AND THE LOAD-ORDER CLAIM WAS NARROWED BY A MEASUREMENT:** `stadium.blade.php` names the cascade BEFORE the hub, and that is not a fault, because the predicate is looked up when it is CALLED, from the run loop. Three mutations, each red with its own signature: the browser definition losing the status check (`declared false, got {cascade: true, hub: true}`), the server's losing it (`declared false, got true`), and a private copy returning to the cascade (the one-implementation case and the census, which then names three files). `gh644` and every test that drives the cascade stay green: 60 passed.

**GH-708** (пункт 3бк, часть 3) THE WIZARD LOCK IS WIRED: A SITE IS NOT LOOKED AT OR CALCULATED UNTIL THE PERSON HAS ANSWERED WHAT THE CALCULATION NEEDS. The owner's decisions of 24.09.2026 are what it holds — the wizard cannot be left until the required answers are in, refreshing the page brings it back, there is no calculation before it is finished, and `/hub` is under the lock because what she excluded was the old hub's INTERFACE, not its route. **IT READS THE SITE OF THE PAGE, NOT THE POINTER.** It asked `$request->user()->activeSite`, and a run frame is opened as `/hub?rerun=…&site=<id>` about THAT site: a lock reading the pointer waves a calculation through for an incomplete site whenever the pointer stands on a complete one, which is one object judged by the state of another. `?setup=0` does not bypass it, because it reads no parameter at all; the dashboard, logout, the no-access and pending doors, the account page and everything under `api/*` pass, each with its reason written where the exception is — a lock with no door is a broken product rather than a strict one. **WHAT IT HOLDS IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED:** required for the turf type AND collected by the wizard, so an input added to the list with a wizard step brings its own case; `traffic.schedule` is required for a sports site and asked by no step, so it does NOT hold a page, and that has a case of its own because "not held" and "never required" read the same otherwise. **WIRING IT CHANGED THE PRECONDITION OF EVERY PAGE TEST AT ONCE:** 31 cases in 10 files were drawing pages for sites their fixtures had left incomplete. Those fixtures were preconditions and not subjects, so the answers come from a helper on `Tests\TestCase` that ADDS and never overwrites, and takes the seven from `CalculationInputs` rather than writing them out — a fixture cannot fall behind what the product requires. The two tests whose subject IS an absent methodology were not touched. **AND TWO MUTATIONS REDDENED ONE CASE, WHICH WAS A GAP IN THE MEASUREMENT AND NOT IN THE CODE:** reading the pointer, and excusing `/hub`, both showed up on the same line with the same output. `PageSite` honours `rerun`+`site` on ANY route, so a frame parameter on `/plan` now separates the first, and `/hub` reached by the pointer alone separates the second — each mutation reddens a case the other leaves green. Three mutations shown red: the wiring removed (the first input answers 200), the pointer read instead of the page's site, and `hub` taken out from under the lock. PHPUnit 506 passed.

It walks every text-like column of every table, decodes JSON, and names each value that equals the id of a site other than the row's own, with no field name known in advance; the result is compared both ways with `database/data-audit/known-violations.json`, whose entries each carry a `GH-NNN` decision.
