Not seen, said in the command's header: a trace carried by values rather than an id, deletions, the right address with foreign content, and a trace overwritten by a later legitimate write. PART 2, the relations declared by code: `copy-differs-from-owner` (every field `FieldOwners::derivedCopies()` names against its owning `sites` column) and `sample-of-another-site` (every key in an analysis row's `inputs.samples` against the row's site, through `App\Support\SampleOwners::sitesOf`, now the one lookup the write path in `AnalysisCacheController` also calls, behaviour unchanged). On the stand both find 0 violations (14 configs, 31 rows with samples), so their red is shown on the test database only: `same()` forced true reddened the copy case, the sample check disabled reddened the sample case, both restored by undo, md5 unchanged; 14 cases. `gh546` gains a third exemption, by decision: the audit reads the stored rows rather than the owner's projection, and only reads.

**GH-710** (пункт 3ац) A SITE NOBODY HAS CONFIGURED CARRIES NO KEY NOBODY ENTERED — AND THREE OF THEM WERE WRITTEN BY THE SERVER BEFORE THE PERSON HAD ENTERED ANYTHING. Measured on the stand, read-only: `GH-671 wizard press 021831` has all three location columns NULL and a config of exactly `{"location": {"lat": null, "lon": null, "name": null}}`. **THE WRITER, ESTABLISHED RATHER THAN NAMED:** `FieldOwners::deriveCopies` wrote the leaf whatever the column held, so a site created with no coordinates came out of its own creation holding three keys of the server's making. A copy of nothing is not a copy. An empty column now REMOVES the copy, and the section goes with it when nothing is left — the second half matters on its own: a column a person CLEARS must not leave the old copy standing, which would be the stale-copy class this file exists to close, and an empty section is still a key nobody entered. **THE VERIFIABLE FORM IS THE ANALYST'S THIRD ATTEMPT AT IT**, and the earlier two are why it is worth quoting: "the config does not exist at all" was factually wrong, and "a site created and not finished in the wizard" was still about the config's existence instead of its contents. What is wrong is a KEY. One case per copied field, taken from the table's own accessor rather than a list written in the test, so a field added to the table brings its own case — and the value offered is of both kinds, because the first version fed a string to every column and the coordinate's cast rejected it, failing the case on a value of mine rather than on the rule. Two mutations, each with its own signature: writing the null again returns exactly the measured `{"location":{"name":null,"lat":null,"lon":null}}`, and leaving the emptied section returns `{"location":[]}`. PHPUnit 515 passed; the owner's sites were read and never written. **TAIL, 25.09: THE RED THAT WAS REPORTED AS ORDER-DEPENDENT IS NOT.** Seven orders were run — the declared one and six random seeds — 518 tests green each time, so the order is not what decided it. What decided it was the MOMENT: `FieldOwners.php` stood mutated in the tree inside an acceptance window (the pre-mutation copy is stamped 23:33 on 24.09), and a run falling inside it reddens exactly the case the mutation was chosen to redden, with exactly this subject, and never again after the undo. A red taken against a mutated file is correct at that moment; what was wrong is that its output could not be told from a red against the tree, so the only reading left was "it comes and goes". The class now prints the subject it exercised — path from the class rather than written down, sha1, size, last written — on green runs as well, because a witness that appears only on failure has nothing to be compared with. Shown rather than argued: clean runs print `sha1 f81ade6c…` and the derivation mutated back to writing the null prints `sha1 ddf34f27…` beside the failure. Restored by undo, md5 unchanged, 4 passed.

**GH-711** (пункт 3ба) THE WRITE PATHS ARE COUNTED FROM THE REGISTRY, NOT FROM THE FOUR LAYERS THAT GUARD THEM. Sign A (`app/tests/Feature/Gh711WritePathsTest.php`): every route of the framework's registry answering a write method, with where its site comes from read off the handler's source (`url`, `body`, `pointer`, `none`), equals `app/tests/fixtures/gh711-write-paths.json` both ways — 48 write paths of 92 routes. Sign B (`tests/gh711-page-write-calls.test.js`): every `fetch` / `XMLHttpRequest.open` / `sendBeacon` write in 276 scripts and view templates, tied to a route by the literal parts of its address, equals `tests/fixtures/gh711-page-write-calls.json` both ways — 18 routes with a found caller, 13 calls unresolved by file, 29 routes without a found caller. Both lists carry the sign they were measured under; a sign changed without a new version is red, and growth by a wider sign is printed apart. A route registered in a new place and a caller in a new file are both named without editing a list. Mutations, each red then restored by undo, md5 unchanged: sign A narrowed with the version kept; the `pointer` source no longer read (five paths named as `site source changed`); sign B reading only double-quoted methods (every caller named as declared but not found). Not built here and said so: the frame invariant by behaviour, which alone would see a write through a computed name or a wrapper, and whether a path's site really comes from where its source says.

**GH-712** (пункт 3ах, половина по `drainage`) THE EQUALITY GUARD COULD NOT SEE THE READ ITS OWN LIST DECLARED. `turf.drainage` was already in `calculation-inputs.schema.json`, carrying a `$comment` that it is read by the firmness engine through the cascade delegate — a claim nothing could check, because `gh644`'s scan matched a read only when the receiver was spelled `state`, `inputs` or `s`, and the engines in `hub-tissue-v3.js` are declared `gaip_firmness_engine(e, t)`. The body was IN the universe and the read was not, which is this file's own failure one level down. **THE RECEIVER NOW COMES FROM THE SIGNATURE**, so renaming a parameter cannot quietly empty the scan, and **THE UNIVERSE WIDENED TO THE ENGINES' DELEGATES AND THE STATE ASSEMBLY, NOT TO EVERYTHING THAT READS:** the assembly is located by following `runCascade`'s first argument to the function that built it (`gaip_transformToCascadeFormat`), never by naming it. The wide variant — every function's first parameter over whole files — was measured and rejected: it drew in rendering functions, calendars and the weather fetch, 48 new names of which 19 were declared nowhere. **UNION, NOT REPLACEMENT,** because the narrow scan alone drops three names the whole-file pass sees outside any delegate (`climate.historical`, `turf.ambientDLISource`, `turf.turfType`); a sharper attribution that loses reads is not an improvement. Distinct reads 42 -> 83, engines with reads 3 -> 11 plus the assembly, entries in the list read by nothing 22 -> 7, and `drainage` is attributed to `firmness-engine` — asserted by name, because the old floor cannot tell the widened universe from the old one. **ELEVEN NAMES THE WIDENING EXPOSED, EACH DECLARED FROM ITS READ SITE AND NOT FROM A GUESS:** `climate.lon` is `location.lon` under the climate spelling, which `location.lat` already declared and its twin did not; five `traffic.*` are the schedule fields the list had declared only as `schedule.*`; `water.SAR`, `water.adjSAR`, `soil.meq` and `turf.growthMultiplier` are results, and where each is produced is written beside it (`soil-structure-engine.js` Suarez, `sample-manager.js:1058` from the sample ppm, the stress engine's combined growth modifier). **AND A HOLE IN THE EXISTING CHECK:** `derived` carries leaves and dotted keys alike, the lookup read leaves only, so `turf.grassType` came out as an input nobody declared the moment a universe read it. Both directions shown red: the list losing `drainage` names `turf.drainage (read by firmness-engine)`, and an entry nobody reads and nobody fills names itself; each restored by replacement, md5 back to the clean value. **FOUND INSIDE THE WORK AND FIXED INSIDE IT:** a full-suite run of this file died on `ENOENT ... assets/__gh716_probe_delete_me.js` — somebody else's probe file, created and removed while the directory-listing scan was walking — and the whole suite then failed to run, a red with no subject. Reads driven by the listing now name what vanished and print it. The irrigation half of the item is the owner's (Вопрос 108) and is untouched; `drainage` is empty on two of fourteen stand sites and stays empty. `gh644`, `gh667`, `gh676`, `gh630`, `gh656`, `gh658`, `gh664` green. **RETURNED BY THE REVIEWER AND REPAIRED IN THE SAME TICKET: A REASON MUST CARRY AN ADDRESS, NOT A WORD.** His finding: "the method is right, the entries are unverifiable" -- he opened all 18 `notInputs` and 14 `derived` and found no file, function or line in any of them, and measured five himself to confirm the classification was at least honest. The check asked only that a reason contain `result` or `derived`, which a guess containing the word also satisfies. Every reason in BOTH maps now names at least one pair `` `path` / `anchor` ``, and the check opens the file and looks for the anchor: 37 pairs found, printed one per line, because "37 reasons checked" and "the loop never ran" read the same otherwise. `derived` was under no requirement at all before, so it is held to the same rule and the case asserts that both maps were reached. **FILLING THEM CAUGHT FOUR ENTRIES THAT WERE WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY UNVERIFIABLE, and one of the four was written by me the same night:** `turf.pgrActive` is produced nowhere -- every occurrence reads it, there is no form field, so the engines that consult it always see false; `site.country` is set only as `country: null` in the state shape and its reader always gets null; `water.SAR` is a declared water-lab column (`assets/lab-import.js`) as well as a computed value, so calling it purely a result was wrong; and `derived.purpose` excuses a read nobody makes -- nothing reads a purpose in any section and the only trace is an open question to the owner about whether the wizard should ask for one. Each now says what was measured instead of what was assumed, and which class those four belong to is a question rather than a repair. **AND A MEASUREMENT MISTAKE OF MINE, CAUGHT BEFORE IT REACHED THE ENTRIES:** the first sign I used for "who writes this" was `key\s*=`, which matches `===`, so reads were coming back as writers; with the sign corrected to an assignment, almost none of these keys is assigned into the state at all -- they are properties of returned objects, which is what the addresses now name. **GH-716** (пункт 3щ) A RUN NOW SAYS WHICH TREE IT SAW, AND REFUSES TO BE READ AS GREEN WHEN IT SAW TWO. The occasion was measured, not supposed: a full run taken while a developer was mid-edit named five suites red, and a re-run of the same five gave 48 cases and 0 failures — nothing in the output distinguished "the product is broken" from "the tree moved under the run". `tests/lib/tree-fingerprint.js` walks the WHOLE tree minus declared exclusions and returns content hash, newest ctime, file count and the exclusion list itself, so a verdict always arrives with the subject it looked at. `tests/lib/tree-fingerprint-setup.js` prints `[tree] <hash> start`, `tests/lib/tree-fingerprint-teardown.js` prints `[tree] <hash> end`, the verdict as the LAST line (measured: Jest prints its summary before the teardown, so anything earlier is scrolled past) and sets a non-zero exit code. Content alone is not enough and this was shown rather than argued: an edit reverted INSIDE the run leaves the hash identical, so the newest ctime is compared too — `content is back: true | verdict: "TREE MOVED DURING RUN: content is back but a file was touched at 13:51:54"`. End to end with the hooks connected, `tests/gh676` running 129 s and the tree touched mid-run: 31 passed, then `TREE MOVED DURING RUN: content changed, 5fb45421a6fcea4a -> 2e9b300e7de14d60`, exit 1 — a green suite that still cannot be accepted, which is the whole point. Four boundaries are named rather than left to be discovered: a run falling BETWEEN two edits sees one tree at both ends; the database is not in the fingerprint; Laravel caches change behaviour without changing the tree; and a file created and deleted within a run is invisible to it (both reads lack it, content agrees, no surviving file's ctime moved). NOT DONE AND NOT COVERED OVER: the PHPUnit half (bootstrap), and the connection itself — two lines in `jest.config.js` — which is held by an operational decision while three people are editing the tree by design, because a marker that fires always stops being read. THE PHPUNIT HALF (place 3 of the plan) is written too: `app/tests/Support/TreeFingerprint.php`, `app/tests/bootstrap-tree-fingerprint.php` and five cases in `app/tests/Unit/Gh716TreeFingerprintTest.php`. Its universe is everything the container can reach — the parent of the app root, discovered rather than listed — which is `app` and `assets` only, so the two halves describe different trees and each print names its root. The verdict is printed from a shutdown function because that is the only place after PHPUnit's own summary, and it calls `exit(1)`: a hook that throws instead gives a PHP fatal error and code 255, which shows a stack trace where a sentence about the tree belongs. Measured before excluding anything: a run moves exactly one file of the universe, `.phpunit.result.cache`, and a mark that fires every time stops being read. Shown: 523 tests passed and exit code 1, with `TREE MOVED DURING RUN` as the last line, against a file that appeared while the run was going. `RefreshDatabase` and Laravel's caches do not move the tree — the database is in memory and the caches are under `storage`. NOT CONNECTED, by the coordinator's decision: `bootstrap="vendor/autoload.php"` in `app/phpunit.xml` becomes `bootstrap="tests/bootstrap-tree-fingerprint.php"`, one edit, and it is not made.

Five misses found on the first run are recorded with reasons in `tests/fixtures/gh717-known-misses.json`, both ways, as a separate case. Pair of mutations: the bare-key rule back reddened the witness with `climate-engine-v2.js:962 … static -> hub-orchestrator.js:5532 | observed -> gilba-hub-v2.js:970`; with names recorded instead of places the same line agreed and the witness case went green — the blindness of a name-based witness, shown; restored by undo, md5 unchanged. RETURN FROM THE REVIEWER, answered: that `disagreed` line on `climate-engine-v2.js:962` was measured before GH-718 removed the `computeSelective` of `hub-orchestrator.js`, its static target; on today's tree the same mutation leaves `:962` `declared unresolvable` and reddens the witness on the other twin it finds, `GilbaStorageNS.get` (static `climate-normals-service.js`, observed `gilba-storage-ns.js`), and with names recorded that line agrees. The docblock no longer promises a `resolved, not observed` verdict the code does not print, and the universe is asserted, not printed: every script `/hub` loads instrumented, no parse error, no load failure — dropping one script reddens it by name. Weaker than the plan by one axis, said: the live case is `declared unresolvable`, so its presence is checked and agreement on it by nothing.

**GH-718** (пункт 3бз) TWO EXPORTS OF `GaipOrchestrator` THAT NOTHING REACHED ARE GONE, BY THE STACK. `tests/gh718-orchestrator-exports-by-the-stack.test.js` runs the bench over a full pass and the live climate path with the place-identifying record of GH-717: `computeIsolated` had no call site and was never entered; `computeSelective` of `hub-orchestrator.js` had one call site by name, `climate-engine-v2.js` `hub.orchestrator.computeSelective(...)`, and execution from it enters the method of `gilba-hub-v2.js`, never this one. **GH-719** (пункт 3ау, часть 1: сторож блока) THE UNIT IS THE BLOCK, AND THE BLOCK'S DEFAULT TURNED OUT TO HAVE TWO HOMES. The item is reported as "the wear load is a markup default", and the reviewer's condition M4 is that a guard about the matches-per-week field alone stays green the week the same defect arrives through `matchDuration` or `trainingRotation`. `tests/gh719-the-wear-block-fields-and-their-readers.test.js` derives the field list from the runner's own markup — the `data-card="traffic"` section of `legacy-hub-markup.blade.php`, cut by its declared attribute and its matching close — takes each field's default from the markup (an input's `value`, a select's `selected` option: two different reads, and only one of them failing is invisible in a count), and censuses readers across `assets` by directory listing, because the reviewer said plainly that a list in the task would hide a third place. **TWO OF THE ITEM'S NUMBERS ARE CORRECTED BY THE CENSUS:** the block holds **18 fields, not 15**, and **10 files name them, not 2** — `hub-orchestrator.js`, `mlsn-progressive-disclosure.js`, `nutrition-program-inputs.js`, `turf-profile-controller.js`, `site-config-persistence.js`, `hub-persistence.js` and `gaip-clear-data.js` beside the two that were known. **AND THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE REPAIR:** `assets/wear-recovery-integration.js` is not a reader of this form, it BUILDS a second copy of it in a script, with the same `value="2"`, the same `1.5`, the same `selected` options — so the default has two homes and **16 of the 18 fields have more than one**. Repairing the blade card alone would have moved nothing. The census therefore covers every place across the views and `assets` that DECLARES one of these fields together with a default, recorded by file and value and deliberately without a line number, since a line moves on the next edit and a pinned census goes stale in silence. Both sides of the ratchet compare LISTS, not lengths. Control green, 3 cases; two mutations, each reddening its own home and leaving the other's list untouched, which is what makes them distinguishable: `gaip-session-duration` moved to 2.5 in the blade reddened `markupDefaultsChanged` by name (a field that is NOT matches, which is M4's shape), and `gaip-matches-week` moved to 4 in the script reddened `declarationsChanged` with both values printed while `markupDefaultsChanged` stayed empty. Each restored by replacement, md5 back to the clean value. **NOT DONE AND HELD, NOT COVERED OVER:** the repair itself — the run taking the schedule from the server instead of the form — changes the number on screen for nine named sites, so it stops at the boundary for the owner. Boundaries of the instrument, named rather than left to be found: a read through a computed class name or a variable holding it is not seen, and neither is a default assigned in code rather than declared in markup.

**GH-720** (пункт 3е) THE RUNNER'S SAFETY NET AGAINST A MID-RUN SITE CHANGE HAD NEVER ONCE FIRED, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED. `hub-persistence.js` registered `window.addEventListener('gaip:site-changed', …)` in the bubble phase, and all three senders -- found by directory listing, not from a list -- dispatch on `document` with a plain `CustomEvent` and no `bubbles`. **THE CLAIM IS ABOUT BEHAVIOUR, SO IT IS MEASURED AS BEHAVIOUR**, and neither easy road would have done: a DOM stub written in the test would encode my own belief about propagation and then agree with it, and the analyst's form says jsdom, which this project does not have (`require.resolve('jsdom')` throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). So `tests/gh720-the-frame-hears-a-site-change.test.js` opens a real browser -- and it is NOT a live test: a blank page, no login, no press, no site. The shapes it uses are read out of the product's own sources at run time rather than transcribed. Measured: dispatched on `document` without bubbles, heard by window in the bubble phase **false**, by window in the capture phase true, by document true. The positive control is asserted first, so three falses cannot be read as "nothing was dispatched". **THE REPAIR, AND WHY IT NEEDS A CONDITION AND NOT JUST A MOVE:** a listener on `document` also hears the frame's own legitimate first settling, and a bare flag would make every run refuse itself. The flag is raised only when the event names a site OTHER than the one the run is for, and an event naming no site has not spoken -- the same rule the site reporters beside it already follow. **THIS IS WHAT MAKES THE ORDER OF THAT FIRST EVENT AND THE RUN'S START STOP DECIDING ANYTHING:** `_runIntent` is read from the address when the script loads, so the comparison exists before any listener can fire, and the condition is about WHICH site rather than about WHEN. The condition is a function of its two arguments so that the wiring and the condition fail separately; the test lifts it out of the source and runs it over seven shapes, then drives the real thing in the browser: settling on its own site leaves the flag false, `A -> X -> A` raises it -- the case nothing else can catch, because by the time the result is filed both reporters name `A` again. One assertion turned over rather than deleted, and it is marked as changing with the decision: it read `window` before this ticket and reads `document` now, while the propagation facts stay asserted so that putting the registration back on `window` still costs a red. 4 cases green.

**GH-721** (пункт 3ав) A CLAIM WITH A NUMBER CARRIES THE TREE IT WAS TAKEN ON, AND A TOOL SAYS WHETHER THAT TREE IS STILL OURS. The mark is `[tree <fingerprint> | <command>]`: both parts are machine parts, the fingerprint copied from `npm run tree` or any run's `[tree]` line (GH-716), the command the one that repeats the claim. `npm run marks -- <file>` (`tests/lib/claim-marks.js`) lists every mark in a document as current, stale (the tree moved since; repeat the command) or incomplete, and exits non-zero on the last two. It is a tool run on demand, not a guard in the suites: the live document is edited by four people at once. It does not find claims that carry no mark, does not check the human part "what was measured", and a claim wider than its measurement is not stale — those stay with acceptance by someone other than the author. `gh721` (texts written in the test, never the live document): mismatch read as current and a mark without a command read as complete each reddened; restored by undo, md5 unchanged.

**GH-722** (пункт 3м, сдача 1 из нескольких: карта написаний) HOW A LAB WRITES EACH READING OF A SAMPLE IS DECLARED ONCE, IN `assets/lab-reading-names.json`, AND THE RUNNER BUILDS ITS TABLES FROM IT. NOT IN THIS DELIVERY: the upload itself (server-side, all rows, outcome with numbers), the Settings import, the upload page taking the map, and code that reads payload keys directly with its own chain of spellings, which neither side of the equality test can see. DELIVERY 3, THE SETTINGS IMPORT: A FILE WITH NOTHING RECOGNISED IN IT IS REFUSED BEFORE ANYTHING IS CLEARED. The clearing import wiped the site's samples and journals first and then wrote whatever came, silently skipping a sample with no data, so a file with no readings emptied the site and reported success. Now the whole file is checked first by `App\Support\LabReadingNames::recognise` -- the runner's resolution, reimplemented on the server and held to the runner by one recorded contract, `app/tests/fixtures/gh722-recognition-contract.json` (445 rows including every column set in the six site files under `files/`; the runner and the server each agree on all 445). Nothing recognised in any sample: 422, nothing cleared, the owner's words from `App\Support\SampleUploadOutcome`, the one place the Data page upload will take them from. A sample with nothing recognised is not written and is named; the answer carries `outcome` (`saved`/`partial`/`rejected`), `rowsRead`, `rowsSaved` and `notSaved`, and the page draws `partial` in the warning style without a check mark and clears its own copies only after the server has answered, no longer before. Manual entry and the ordinary push stay unchecked, by her decision. Four mutations, each restored by replacement with md5 back to the clean value: `partial` reported as `saved`, the refusal before the clear removed, `partial` drawn as a success, and the page clearing before the answer -- each reddened its own case and no other. Three `Gh526` cases sent an empty file expecting a clear; that is now a refusal, so they send one readable sample. Found in the census while delivering: `gh477` follows values by NAME, so a new local `text` was joined to an unrelated `text` elsewhere in the file; renamed, and the census's scope-blindness is named rather than fixed here. The sentences for `saved` and `partial`, and the sentence with the numbers after her refusal, are drafts awaiting her words. DELIVERY 4, PART 1: THE CODE THAT READS A SAMPLE PAST THE MAP IS FOUND, LISTED AND HELD. `tests/lib/sample-payload-reads.js` follows a value taken from a sample's `payload` or `rawData` into its variable, by binding rather than by name, and lists every column read off it; `tests/gh722-direct-sample-reads.test.js` holds that against `tests/fixtures/gh722-direct-sample-reads.json` both ways, each read with a state and each place with what it is and what happens next. It found 16 places reading a lab reading past the map, not the 5 named at delivery 1 -- that number was a text search of spelling chains, and the census refutes it. They are listed, not moved: pH in ten of them disagrees with the map about `pH_CaCl2` (an open owner decision), CEC in five would gain a value for four stored samples (an owner decision on numbers), and `ECe`, `EC_paste`, `Texture`, `ESP` and `SAR_ppm` are read though the map does not declare them. Two mutations: a new `K_ppm` read in `PageController` reddened as not listed; a listed `K` read changed to `K_ppm` in `nutrition-calendar.js` reddened both as gone and as not listed; each restored by replacement with md5 back to the clean value. DELIVERY 4, PART 2: ELEVEN READERS MOVED ONTO THE MAP, AND NO STORED VALUE MOVED WITH THEM. The server gains `LabReadingNames::readingsOf`, the counterpart of the runner's; the topbar's tissue N/P/K, the analysis card's ten nutrients, range check, Na and the EC behind ECe read through it, and the samples API hands every sample its `readings`, so the Plan page -- which does not load the runner -- stops spelling columns: its soil nutrients and its tissue list read from there. In the runner, the zone table's nutrients, the second door's Na, both nutrient-trend charts' water EC, the active tissue N/P/K and the soil sync's nutrients and OM read through `readingsOf`. THE PROOF IS AGAINST THE STAND'S OWN VALUES, not synthetic ones: `tests/fixtures/gh722-stand-sample-readings.json` holds the reading columns of all 148 stored samples, live and deleted, read once with SELECT; each removed chain, recorded as it was, and the map give the same value in 3955 comparisons out of 3955. The first form of that proof used synthetic values and reported differences that were only the order of two spellings holding equal numbers -- the order matters only when the values differ, which is a fact about the data. HELD, because the stand's values say it would move a number: the second door's EC for ECe (three live samples carry only `EC1_5` and would take ECe from the sample instead of the page field), besides CEC and pH which wait for the owner. Found while delivering: the census had not listed PHP reads by a variable key (`$payload[$nut]`); it does now. `readingFieldsFor`, a function added in delivery 1 that only tests called, made the caller-walk list it as a function with no caller -- a suite not in delivery 1's run; it is data now (`readingFields`). Three mutations, each restored by replacement with md5 back to the clean value: the topbar back on the bare key reddened its case and the census; the Plan's K back on the payload reddened the census; ECe taken from the wrong reading reddened the analysis case. DELIVERY 5, THE PART THAT NEEDS NO DECISION: THE LAB SAR AND TDS ARE FOUND THROUGH THE MAP. The two places that read a lab SAR -- the water named for the run and the row's own fallback when the ions cannot give one -- and the TDS stand-in for EC spelled `SAR || sar || SAR_ppm` and `TDS` themselves. The rule of the row is unchanged and shown on the producer itself (`tests/gh722-the-lab-sar-is-read-through-the-map.test.js`): with no ions a lab SAR arrives on both roads in either case of its name, with ions the ions decide (1.64 against a lab 9.9), with neither SAR stays empty. `SAR_ppm` is declared nowhere and no stored sample carries it; no stored water sample carries SAR or TDS at all. The first mutation on the named road stayed green, because the row's fallback found the same sample in the store; a case where the store's active water has no SAR isolates that road, and the same mutation reddens it. WHETHER A LAB SAR SHOULD REACH THE RUN'S INPUT, and win over the ions when both exist, is the owner's and is not done.

**GH-723** (пункт 3би) EVERY PAGE DIVERGENCE NOW ANSWERS FOR ITSELF, AND REACHABLE MEANS THE VIEW LOADS THE HANDLE'S FILE. Eighty-five entries, later fifty-four, all carried `ticket: 6a` and then `GH-680` — one reason for a whole batch, so a month later nothing could say why a given pair was on the list. Two things changed. `pagePairsFound` in `tests/helpers/gh678-caller-walk.js` paired a node with every view loading the file of its ROOT, and a root is often a shared file such as `dashboard-ui.js`; a view that loads the root but not the file where the node's handle is declared cannot run that node at all, because the function is not on the page. Narrowing it dropped 80 edges and 32 of the 54 entries — the analyst's number, measured rather than taken on trust. Those dropped edges are a defect OF THE WALK and are printed by the run under `[gh723]` with the root and the handle file named, because narrowing the definition without recording them would hide the symptom; they need a ticket of their own. The remaining 22 each carry `why` built from facts of the code — which file the root is, which file declares the handle, on that view — plus a `state`: 5 are `internal-accounting` (the view is `hub`, the run frame no client opens) and 17 are `candidate-not-established`, the GH-459 family, where a report or analysis page loads an engine file itself and a reader could be seeing numbers computed ON THE PAGE instead of read from the stored result. WHETHER THEY ACTUALLY EXECUTE IS NOT ESTABLISHED: proving it needs a wrapper in place on a live page, and no live run was taken. AND THE SHAPE OF AN ENTRY IS NOW HELD BY SOMETHING. The reviewer of this ticket took `why` and `state` off all twenty-two entries and put the batch ticket back, and the suite gave 31 green: the defect this item removes could return without a single red, and that is how it returned. `gh676` now asserts, per entry rather than as a count, that `why` exists and is DIFFERENT from every other entry's, that `state` is one of the declared words, and that `ticket` is present. Distinctness is NOT required of `ticket`, by her reasoning: several entries may honestly close under one ticket, and it is the REASON that answers for the entry. Measured: taking `why` off reddens with both the missing-reason list and the shared-reason list; an invented `state` reddens by name; putting the batch ticket back on all twenty-two stays green, which is the named boundary.

**GH-724** A TISSUE SAMPLE NEVER REACHED THE CALCULATION, BECAUSE THE RUN ASKED FOR AN ACTIVE SAMPLE AND A RUN FRAME HAS NONE. Measured on the stand, read only: `computed.tissue` is empty in 66 of 66 stored rows while `Burns`, `Russley` and `Test5 - NZ` each hold live tissue samples. The mechanism is not a missing engine: the runner read `getActiveSample('tissue')`, and nothing in a freshly opened frame makes a tissue sample active -- the browser copy that used to carry one went with the move to the database as the only source, and soil survived only because GH-588 had started naming it in the address. **THE OPENER NAMES THE SAMPLE, BY THE SERVER'S OWN RULE**, the one it already applies to soil (`COALESCE(lab_date, sample_date) DESC, id DESC`), asked before the frame starts -- awaiting anything inside the runner's handler stops the weather from ever arriving and the run dies having written nothing (GH-587). The question is now asked for any kind, so `&soil=` and `&tissue=` travel together. **AND THE SECOND OPENER ASKS IT TOO:** `settings-init.js` passed neither parameter, so a run started from Settings computed on whatever the frame happened to hold; both call one builder in `dashboard-ui.js`, and a kind added there reaches both. **THE RUNNER COMPUTES ON THE SAMPLE IT WAS NAMED,** which is the GH-459 rule one layer down -- what a result is about comes from the data of the object it is about, not from the state the page is in. `none` is an answer and nothing is substituted for it; a named sample that is not in the store is an outcome of its own rather than a quiet fall back to the active one. The row records what the run was told, and the server now reads `none` as the stated absence it is instead of looking it up as a key, resolving nothing, and filing it as a sample nobody could find. **WHICH SAMPLE EACH SITE GETS, MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED:** `Burns` 121 -- it holds two tissue samples dated the same day and only `id DESC` separates them, which is why the server-side case is built on a tie and not on two different dates -- `Russley` 142, `Test5 - NZ` 144; the other eleven sites have no tissue sample and stay without one. Control green then mutations: the runner put back on the active sample reddened three cases including the positive control; the `none` skip removed reddened the server's own account with `unresolved: [{"type":"tissue","sample":"none"}]`. Each restored by replacement, md5 back to the clean value. **FOUND WHILE DELIVERING AND REPAIRED IN THE SAME PASS:** `Gh642TheOneListOfInputsTest` asked that a `derived` reason contain the word `from`, the same word-check GH-712's return had just removed from its neighbour; it is held to a `path` / `anchor` pair now, shown red on a reason stripped of its address. **NOT IN THIS WORK AND NOT COVERED OVER:** what the calculation does with tissue once it arrives -- the tissue corrections are an open owner question -- and `/plan`, which picks a tissue sample per green by zone (GH-414) and is untouched. **GH-725** (пункт 3бо) FOUR ENTRIES OF THE INPUT LIST THAT WERE WRONG ABOUT THEMSELVES, EACH MEASURED FOR WHAT IT COSTS A PERSON BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED. The four came out of GH-712's return, where filling every reason with a checkable address is what exposed them. **THE FIRST STEP WAS REACHABILITY, NOT REPAIR**, because a list entry that moves nothing on a screen and one that hides a wrong number are different jobs, and the distinction the coordinator set is three ways an unwritten entry can be wrong: the input is not needed, the input is needed and is not asked, or the input is asked and goes somewhere else. **TWO ARE ASKED AND GO NOWHERE, AND BOTH ARE TRAPS RATHER THAN LIVE DEFECTS.** `turf.pgrActive`: the person answers the PGR switch, stored as `pgr.enabled` in the site's own config, and the shade engine asked a state field nothing fills, so it always saw `false` -- it decides only `currentlyActive` and `conflictDetected`, and the second one prints a line of screen text (`hub-tissue-v3.js`, on the surfaces `stadium` and three report pages load). Measured: PGR is off on all twelve configured sites, so the line would have stayed invisible after the repair too, and no site's numbers move. It now comes from the config the SERVER delivers to the frame rather than from a field on the page, and silence is not read as `off` -- `|| false` was a substitution. `water.SAR`: a water report may carry SAR (`assets/lab-import.js` recommends the column and gives it a range) and the converter answered `|| 0`, which is the safest-looking sodium hazard there is -- GH-707's manufactured zeros in another place. Measured: none of the eight live water samples carries a SAR, so again nothing moves; absence travels as absence now, as it does for the soil neighbours settled under GH-619. **THE DELIVERY OF A SUPPLIED SAR IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NAMED:** the water reading map that would carry it lives in another item's file. **ONE ENTRY WAS STRUCK AND ONE COULD NOT BE**, and the difference was the guard's to make rather than mine: `derived.purpose` is produced nowhere and read nowhere -- it excused a read that does not exist -- and it is gone. `site.country` I had classed the same way on a census of ONE reader; striking it reddened `gh676` with a second, `buildPreEmergentInputs`, which keys a New Zealand branch on it. The record is back with a measured reason: read by two engines, filled by nothing, both treating it as a fallback behind coordinates. **AND WHAT THAT SECOND READER SHOWED IS BIGGER THAN THE ENTRY:** its region starts at a hardcoded `"au"` and its coordinates are read off the PAGE, which is the named GH-459 class; that is item 3bt and is not touched here. Control green, then both substitutions put back in one mutation: `water.SAR — absent: 0` and `turf.pgrActive — config silent: false`, each case red on its own value and distinguishable from the other; restored by replacement, md5 back to the clean value, copies taken first. **GH-726** (пункт 3бп) WHAT MAKES THE DROPPED PAIRS HARMLESS IS NOW HELD BY SOMETHING. GH-723 narrowed `reachable on a view` to "the view loads the handle's file too", and 32 node x view pairs left the batch. Measured before writing anything here: the call chains from the root to those handles DO exist, so the graph was not lying — the PAIR was wrong, not the edge. Which makes this an incomplete account rather than a false edge, and 80 edges needed no ticket of their own: they are gone, not filed. What the pairs rest on is that every caller on the way to such a handle stands behind a check that the global is loaded, so on a view without the file the path does not run. NOTHING HELD THAT: removing the check at `ambient-dli-integration.js:36` left four suites and 42 cases green. `gh676` now asserts it — the handle files come from the walk's own dropped edges, the names from what each file publishes, and every call through such a name must sit behind a presence check in its enclosing text. Six calls are guarded today (`ambient-dli-integration.js:41`, `hub-orchestrator.js:3073` and `:5022`, `hub-tissue-v3.js:7337`, `disease-ui.js:33`, `hub-persistence.js:507`). Measured: removing either check reddens naming the exact line. The check found its own case on the first run — a docblock `@param … DiseaseForecast.generateForecast()` read as an unguarded call — so comment lines are dropped, which is one of two named boundaries; the other is that a guard made further up the stack is invisible to a text window. Only the `page` kind is in scope here; whether other kinds rest on the same widened answer is Question 115. THE WINDOW IS NOW THE ENCLOSING FUNCTIONS, not 120 lines above the call, after the item's reviewer showed what the line window bought: delete the guard, leave a `typeof AmbientDLIEngine` standing anywhere in those lines, and the call read as guarded. Same shape as `gh580`'s anchored text window. The functions containing a call are found by parsing and each is asked from its own start down to the call — every level, not only the innermost: `disease-ui.js:33` calls inside `setTimeout(function () { … })` while the guard protecting it stands in the function around that one, and asking only the innermost called it unguarded, which is a false finding. Prose is not a guard either: the comment lines were dropped when looking for the CALL and not when looking for what protects it, so a deleted check whose words survived in a comment still counted — measured, and both sides are code now. Boundary that remains, and it belongs to the language rather than the window: a sister function declared above the call inside the same enclosing one is in that window. Measured after the change: six guarded calls, none unguarded; removing a check reddens naming its line, and so does leaving only its words behind.

**GH-727** THE PRE-EMERGENT WEED SET FOLLOWS THE SITE'S OWN PLACE, AND THE WEED TABLES SPEAK ONE LIST OF REGIONS. Two faults hid each other. The builder handed the engine a region identifier from the regional profiles, while the weed tables answered to four short codes of their own, so no site ever matched and every one of them was served only the seven species tagged as growing everywhere: six weeds missing in Australia, five in New Zealand, two in the UK. The eleven records carrying those codes now carry the declared identifiers, with no translation table between the two spellings, and a tag outside the declared list reddens a case that reads the list from the one file that declares it. Separately, the place itself came from the page's coordinate fields, which hold whichever site the hidden runner restored last, so a pass for one site could be computed for another's place — four Australian sites held New Zealand in their last stored row. The builder now asks the site by id through the same function eight other files already use, and the branches on country and region that went with the page fields are gone. A site whose row carries no coordinates gets no region, and the run declares the gap by name instead of computing for Australia; the engine refuses such a call as well, the way it already refuses one with no soil temperature, rather than answering with the everywhere set. Stored rows keep what they hold until the next run.

**GH-728** (пункт 3бс) THE SUBSTITUTION CENSUS FOLLOWED A NAME, SO TWO VARIABLES THAT SHARED ONE CARRIED EACH OTHER'S ANSWERS. One map keyed by identifier name for a whole file: a substitution recorded against `name`, `label` or `species` was inherited by every sink in that file mentioning the same word. The analyst hit it from inside another item — a new `text` of hers picked up what a different `text` carried — and renamed her variable rather than repairing the census, which is what this item is for. **THE TECHNIQUE WAS NOT INVENTED HERE:** the sample census already resolves a variable by its BINDING (`tests/lib/sample-payload-reads.js`), and a Babel `Binding` is unique to one declaration in one scope, so `text` in two functions is two keys. It transferred whole. **OBJECT FIELD PATHS STAY KEYED BY NAME AND THAT IS SAID IN THE CODE:** `data.site.location` names a field, which has no scope to resolve it in; the two stores are kept apart so the difference is visible rather than implied, and an identifier with no binding keeps the old behaviour and is counted in `unresolvedNames` — a census that quietly stopped following a name looks exactly like one with nothing to follow. **THE NUMBER FIRST, THE REPAIR AFTER, and the two were separated because the first comparison I made was against the RECORDED list, which confounds two things:** taken now, the census finds 176 by name and 107 by binding — 69 gone, 0 new — while the recorded list held 184, of which 8 were already stale, found by neither. Verified by hand rather than inferred: in `account-init.js` the substitution `u.name || u.email` lives in `function userInitials(u)` and the `PATCH` sink is inside `tbody.addEventListener('click', …)` — different functions, glued by the shared word. **WHAT IS NOT A FINDING, checked before it was reported as one:** the ratchet's one-directionality is declared on purpose — its own case states that a removed substitution does not redden and that the list may shrink and not grow — so the shrink was recorded with the writer that exists for it. Control green, then the mutation: the census re-glued by name re-adds 71 entries, each named in the failure; restored by replacement, md5 back to the clean value, copies taken first. **AND A MISTAKE OF MINE ON THE WAY:** the boundary report was attached to the returned array as an ordinary property, which broke two negative controls comparing the whole return with `[]` — an empty array with an own property is not deeply equal to one without; it is non-enumerable now. Jest 126 across the suites that touch the census. **THE REVIEWER'S RETURN, AND SHE WAS RIGHT THAT THE REPAIR HAD STOPPED HALF WAY: the map of CALLEES was still keyed by name.** The values moved onto bindings and the parameters of a called function did not, so two functions of one name in different scopes shared one entry and the last one parsed won. Her planted case, reproduced before the change and now standing in `gh477` in both arrangements: a substitution that reaches `innerHTML` through `fill(place)` is NOT FOUND when a silent `fill` is declared BELOW it, and IS found when the same twin is declared above — the census answered by the order of the file, which is the one thing a ratchet may not do. A callee is resolved by the binding the CALL site sees now, the same lookup the declaration used. Measured: the census does not move (107 entries, unchanged), which is why the planted case rather than the number is the evidence; mutation, keying by name again, reddens it with `silent twin BELOW -> []`. **AND THE BOUNDARY IS NAMED IN FULL, which was the return's second position:** it was said to be object paths and unbound names, and there is a third — a function that is a KEY on an object literal has no binding to be keyed by, so it is matched by name; those names travel out beside the result as `callsKeyedByNameOnly` and a case prints them, so where the scope-aware matching stops is read off a run rather than remembered. Jest 23 in `gh477`.

**GH-729** (пункт 3ал) A STORED PREDICTION NOW NAMES THE RUN THAT PRODUCED IT. The logger stamped every batch with `generateUUID()` — a number invented per call, equal to nothing else in the tree — so a prediction and the run that computed it had no way of being about the same attempt. Measured on the stand and worse than the item said: it travelled under `cascade_run_id` while `PredictionController` reads `cascade_id`, so it never arrived at all — `predictions` holds 1718 rows and the column is filled on NONE of them. Two faults under one symptom. `hub-persistence.js` now publishes `GilbaPersistence.currentRunId()` — it is the one place that reads `/hub?rerun=<runId>&site=<siteId>`, and a second reader of that address would be a second answer waiting to disagree; the logger takes the id from there in both places it stamped one, and sends it under the name the server reads. OUTSIDE A RUN FRAME IT IS `null`, never a stand-in: a page opened without `?rerun=` is not a run, its predictions belong to no run, and an invented id there is the same defect renamed. `tests/gh729-…` runs the logger in a sandbox and asserts the pair rather than either half — the value is the run's id, and the name the browser sends equals the name the controller reads, each taken from its own source. Mutations: minting an id again, letting the name drift back to `cascade_run_id`, and substituting a UUID when there is no frame — all three red, naming the case. Not in scope and named: `generateUUID` is now called by nothing and is left standing; whether the server stores what it is sent belongs to the controller's own cases. THE LAST LINK IS NOW ASSERTED TOO, after the item's reviewer closed it by reading: `app/tests/Feature/Gh729PredictionKeepsItsRunTest.php` writes through the route and reads the column back. Reading is how the first fault survived — the logger sent `cascade_run_id` while the controller reads `cascade_id`, and 1718 rows carried an empty column without one line looking wrong. Three cases: the id arrives in the column; no run keeps it null rather than a stand-in; and two predictions of one run share an id while the next run's does not — the point of the id is that it GROUPS, which a per-call id satisfied only in form. Mutations: the server reading the old field name, the server substituting `unknown-run` for an absent one, and the column not written at all — all three red.

**GH-733** (пункт 3э) SETTINGS STOPPED TELLING THE DATABASE AN ANSWER NOBODY GAVE — AND THE CONDITION THAT HELD THE ITEM TURNED OUT TO BE MET ALREADY. Measured now, all three ARE in the list — `filledIn: ["settings.turf"]` on each, and `turf.summerIntent` declaring its second name `readAs: ["turf.overseedSummerIntent"]`, which is the analyst's find that the writer and the reader use different names. The condition is asserted by a case of its own, so it no longer rests on anybody's reading. **WHAT IS STILL SILENT, named rather than quietly fixed:** ten places substitute `'transition'` when the value is absent, and the disease readers take only the second name while `irrigation-scheduler.js:218` takes both. That is a readers' class, not the writer's, and it is not in this item. **SCOPE IS ASSERTED, not just respected:** the block holds eight stand-ins, and the five that are a different family — `|| '0'` on the two percentage fields, `|| ''` on the two species keys and the companion — are left, with a case saying so, so a later reader does not take them for an oversight. Boundary in the code: a field the person CLEARS cannot be cleared this way, because a key absent from a patch means "unchanged"; sending an explicit emptiness is a separate shape and the analyst's decision. **AND A MISTAKE OF MINE THE CASE CAUGHT:** the explanation went INSIDE the object literal and quoted the three removed values, so the assertion that the literal no longer contains them went red on my own comment; it lives above the literal now. Control green, then the mutation: the guard rewritten to fall back to `'transition'`/`'none'` reddens the group case with the whole rewritten block printed; restored by replacement, md5 back to the clean value, copy taken first.
