**GH-734** (пункт 3аз) THE SOIL TEMPERATURE IS COMPUTED ONCE, IN THE RUN, ON THE RUN'S OWN INPUTS — three deliveries, in an order that was itself the subject. One model was being called twice with different inputs: once by the rendering panel, once by the canonical step, and the number the database kept was the PANEL'S, because the producer copied it out of `GAIP_SOIL_TEMP`. **TWO PRECONDITIONS WERE CHECKED BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE ANY WORK WAS PAID FOR THEM, and both had expired:** the reviewer's condition that `soil.CEC` be declared in the inputs list first — it is, as a `readAs` alias of `samples.soil`, whose readings are declared once by the lab-name map, so a separate entry would be a second place for one fact; and the owner's open question about CEC appearing on four samples — the three thermal profiles that CEC refines are `native`, `pipe-drained` and `soil-field`, only `Westview` has one, its single soil sample carries no CEC under any name, and the four samples of that question belong to two `sand_profile` sites, so her answer cannot move a soil temperature. **DELIVERY 1 — the calculation, its inputs and its refusals.** The profile was `construction || profileType || "usga"`, so a site whose construction the server could not resolve was computed as a sand profile; it comes from the resolved construction the server delivers. The moisture was `climateMetrics?.moisture?.soilMoisture?.mean || 0.25`, and the `0.25` was the value that actually travelled because that wrapper has two writers and one gives no key; it is the mean of the non-empty `soil_moisture_0_to_7cm` of the same hourly series the air temperatures come from, kept as a function of its argument so the rule can be measured apart from the wiring. An absence is an outcome with a reason — `setting-missing`, `soil-moisture-unavailable`, each with its result key — and **the model is not called without moisture**, because it carries a third substitution of its own that would fire on a null. The result travels with the inputs it was computed on, so "which moisture was it computed on" is answered by the row. **DELIVERY 2 — six readers, not the four the task named:** the census by directory found `cascade-orchestrator.js`, `disease-forecast.js`, `disease-engine-pure.js`, `overseed-climate-integration.js`, `large-patch-model.js` and `soil-temp-logger.js`, and each takes the run's result through the orchestrator's own accessor now. Comments are stripped before counting, because every repaired place names the global in its own explanation and a count over the raw text reports the work as not done. **DELIVERY 3 — the global ceases to exist**, 0 mentions in code: the panel draws instead of publishing, the last live-session fallback is gone, the producer's third home for the measurement is gone, and three entries left the site-switch cleanup list — `GAIP_SOIL_TEMP` plus `GAIP_MLSN_RESULT` and `GAIP_WEATHER_DATA`, which cleaned globals nothing in the tree assigns. **THE ORDER IS HELD BY A GUARD RATHER THAN BY CARE, and that guard exists because the one I promised did not:** I told the coordinator twice that `GH-606`'s census would redden if the cleanup entry went before the global, and measured, it does not — delivery 1 had already taken that global out of the row's construction, which is the only universe that census has. The protection was real when I named it and my own first delivery removed it. `tests/gh734-the-cleanup-list-and-the-globals-agree.test.js` reddens on a name that is cleaned and assigned nowhere, so the entry must go first; it found its own case on the first run, naming the two dead entries above. It holds ONE direction and prints the other as a number: 193 globals of the family are assigned, 15 are cleaned, 178 are not, and nothing in a name separates a per-site result from a module namespace, so a list of 177 would be a blanket. **FOUR CASES TURNED OVER WITH THEIR REASONS, not deleted:** two of `gh559` (the orchestrator's state "never" carries the physics result; the panel's global is read when the climate carries nothing) and two of my own delivery-2 controls, each of which expired with the subject it named. `gh568` was red on a count of skip-recording steps pinned at three; the subjects are asserted as a named set now, because a count is a fact about the batch and this case is about which steps record a skip — the third time tonight an assertion counted where it should have listed. **BOUNDARY, written into the item before the work and unchanged by it:** the 24.4 measurement — panel, canonical number and transfer on one run's weather, site by site — was NOT taken, so this delivery does not mean "checked against live data". Jest 69 across eight suites, PHPUnit 542. **RETURNED BY THE REVIEWER, and the return's own work found two more places of the night's class.** The two refusals were filed under the step they run INSIDE — `noteSkipped("climate", "soil-temp-physics", …)` — while a recorded cause is found by the step it is filed under and a section asks for the step the graph names for its key: measured, the reason reached NO section and the panel said nothing at all about the missing soil temperature, and where the climate was empty too it printed the soil temperature's sentence under the climate's name. Filed under its own word now, and `gh568`'s pair census asserts over the LIST that no pair's step and module differ. The module also had no word in `STEP_NAMES`, so `gh572` was red in the tree naming it; it takes the label the graph already carries for that engine, `soil temperature`, and `soilTempPhysics` therefore leaves `Gh639`'s list of consumer keys with no step — it stood there because nothing recorded a cause for it and nothing had a word for it. `Gh644`'s universe was narrowed from the whole client payload to the sentences in it, because the payload legitimately carries `step`, `class` and `cause` identifiers beside the words, and the first three-word step identifier to reach a section made a working payload look like a defect. PHPUnit 557, jest 138 across thirteen suites. **THE RETURN ITSELF: A READER RECEIVES A NUMBER, and until now nothing said so.** "Six readers take the run's result" was held by the TEXT of the call, so the reviewer's mutation — one reader asking for `raw.T_5mm` instead of `raw.T_50mm` — stayed green. `tests/gh734-the-reader-receives-the-number.test.js` measures the result's shape by RUNNING its producer and reads the top level off the orchestrator's own assignment; the six readers are taken from the code with comments stripped, because a comment quoting the accessor made prose look like a reader on the first full run. Four of the six are followed in: each is given two results differing only in the physics numbers, and its own answer has to differ — the reviewer's mutation now reddens two cases, the executed one printing the air-temperature average on both runs. The two that are not followed in are named with their reasons, and the list is asserted, so a new reader is red until it is classified. **IT FOUND ITS OWN CASE:** `soil-temp-logger.js` asked for `depths.d50mm`, `d100mm`, `d10mm` — the canonical state's spelling — while the producer returns `'50mm'` and the like, so its "priority 2: the run's result" was `undefined` on every run and it fell through to the canonical copy. Both spellings are accepted now. Its boundary is stated rather than implied: the only caller keeps sensor readings and discards the rest by source, so nothing a person sees depended on that read. Two stale comments naming the panel's global as the source were brought to the tree, and the delivery line "one calculation" was corrected to "one calculation in the run", the widget remaining as the named remainder. PHPUnit 562.

**GH-736** (пункт 3бш) A SITE WITH NO WATER SAMPLE NO LONGER CARRIES A CONDUCTIVITY OF ZERO. `gaip_build_state` assembled the run's water as `ecw: sample ? (sample.ecw || 0) : 0`; the zero died at the row's last gate in `hub-persistence.js` until GH-731 made a zero a reading there, after which the next run would have stored `ecw 0` and `leachingFraction 10` for every site without water and the water page would have printed "Leaching fraction required 10%". Absence now travels as `null`; a measured zero is still a zero. The water `pH` of the same block (7 when there is no sample) is left as it is, pending the owner (GH-735). `tests/gh736-a-site-without-water-carries-no-conductivity.test.js` runs the real assembly into the real row producer.

**GH-737** (пункт 3бц) A SODIUM THE LAB MEASURED AT ZERO REACHES THE ROW AS ZERO, THROUGH BOTH DOORS. `soilNutrition.soilNa` is written by the pass door (`_si`) and the sample-store door (`fromSample`) of `cacheAnalysisResults`; both were `||` chains, so a measured zero fell to `null` (the second door via the page Na field first). A value that parses is now a reading, the rule GH-731 settled for conductivity; a sample with no sodium behaves as before, including the second door's page-field read, which is a different class and is left alone. No stored sample carries a zero sodium today. `tests/gh737-a-measured-zero-of-sodium-reaches-the-row.test.js` runs `gaip_build_state` into the first door and the sample store into the second.

**GH-738** (пункт 3бщ) WHICH KEYS OF THE ROW A RUN ASSEMBLES ARE EMPTY, DECLARED AND COMPARED. The case that called for it is not hypothetical: GH-731 repaired the choice of sample and passed its acceptance, and a neighbouring item then measured that the stored row had gone from `ecw null, leachingFraction null` to `ecw 0, leachingFraction 10` — a stand-in from another place stopped being blocked and began to arrive. Every case was green throughout, because each looked at the subject of its own item and 'a repair here woke a default there' is nobody's subject. What is compared is NOT the values: those move lawfully with weather, sample and season. What must not move quietly is whether a key is EMPTY — `null -> filled` means a number appeared where the row said 'not known', which is a different sentence to the reader. `tests/gh738-…` takes the map from what the run ASSEMBLED, before any write, which is what lets it answer a case where no row had yet been stored. 422 keys today, 59 null and 363 filled, DOWN TO THE LEAVES: a map of top sections would have missed `ecw` inside `computed.waterBalance`, and a device that cannot find the case it was built for is not a device. Two facts the bench forced and they are conditions rather than tricks: the schema is handed in as the page is handed it, and the bench is made a RUN FRAME, because `_bodyMetrics` and the write live in the branch taken only when the address carries `?rerun=&site=`. Measured: substituting a zero for `ecw` in the assembly reddens with `computed.waterBalance.ecw: null -> filled`. Boundary, named: the map covers the ONE path the bench executes — the same substitution written into `hub-tissue-v3.js`'s DOM assembly passed green, because the bench does not take that road; and a key that only appears on another branch is not in the map at all.

**GH-739** (пункт 3бэ) THE EUE ENGINE NO LONGER READS A GLOBAL NOTHING WRITES. `assembleChemInputs` took `soil1to5EC` and `soilKStatus` (Pathway A) from `GAIP_MLSN_RESULT`, which no code in the tree assigns. Measured in a browser rather than read: the `/hub` page's own 206 scripts loaded into a blank page with no login, no site and no press, every request answered locally — the bridge initialises and never runs (`GSSH_EUE.calculate` 0 calls, no `gssh:*` event, no assignment of the global, no non-GET request), while one `gssh:shadeOrchestratorComplete` sent into the same page makes the same channels see it run, so the watch is not blind. The agreed outcome for "not executed": the read goes, both inputs stay null as they always were. `tests/gh739-is-the-eue-bridge-executed.test.js` holds the measurement and the consequence.

**GH-740** (пункт 3бы) A RATCHET KEY NAMES THE CALL, NOT THE LINE IT SITS ON. `gh678-caller-walk.js` states a few hundred lines above its own key-builder that a key carries no line number, because a line lives until the next edit — and three keys carried one anyway: for an edge the walk could not resolve, `callee` was the address `<file>:<line>`. Measured rather than predicted: a delivery that added 89 lines to `hub-orchestrator.js` moved `:5022` to `:5111`, and the ratchet reported one edge RESOLVED and another NEW — the same call read as two events, which is noise where a ratchet should be a statement. The call's own text is used instead, taken from the use already recorded at that place: `scenarioEngine.compareScenarios`, `DiseaseForecast.generateForecast`. The twins `gaip-whatif-ui.js` and `gssh-whatif-ui.js` write the identical call and stay apart because the FILE is the first part of the key; two identical calls in one file are told apart by the ordinal the key already carries; the line travels beside the key, printed and never compared. When the text cannot be found the address is kept, so an entry is never lost and that case stays visible. Shown as a pair: forty-nine lines inserted above the call leave the suite green, and renaming the call itself reddens.

**GH-741** (пункт 3бч) A SUMMER INTENT NOBODY SET STAYS UNSET. Fourteen readers turned an absent summer intent into `'transition'` and four objects asserted it for a sward with no overseed; since GH-733 the Settings form no longer writes it, so the readers were the last place the guess was made. Nine readers and the four objects now carry `null`; every reader compares the intent only with `retain`/`maintain`/`perennial`/`keep` inside an overseed branch, so each decision is the one made on `'transition'`, and `disease-integration.js` still consults the overseed window copy when the intent is unset. Five readers in files another item is editing are listed in the census and removed there; the profile lookups (`profiles[intent] || profiles.transition`) are the next part. `tests/gh741-an-unset-summer-intent-stays-unset.test.js` runs the readers and holds the census both ways.

**GH-742** (пункт 3ад) THE PANEL NAMES THE SOIL PART OF THE ANALYSIS AFTER THE SITE'S METHODOLOGY, AND THE NAME HAS ONE OWNER. The word was `STEP_NAMES['mlsn'] => 'MLSN'`, keyed by the name of the STEP, so every site read `MLSN` whatever its settings said; eight of thirteen sites say something else. The methodology now travels to the panel's projection from the single owner `config.turf.methodology`: `AnalysisResults::forSites` reads it in one query and puts the key in the projection, and nothing derives it from coordinates, from a surface, from a sample's stamp or from a field on the page — a site set to `slan` whose sample is stamped `mlsn` reads `slan`, and the mutation "take it from the stamp" reddens on that. **THE NAME'S OWNER IS THE INPUTS LIST**, the analyst's decision: `turf.methodology` carries `values: {mlsn|slan|ammonium_acetate: {label}}` beside its keys, the way `turf.construction` does, and `CalculationInputs::methodologyLabel` is the single server reader. `AccountController::methodologyLabel` delegates to it, so the second copy of the names on the server is gone. **THE REVIEWER'S CONDITION WAS THAT BOTH READERS OF THE STEP'S WORD BE NAMED, not one:** the section's module and the sentence the incomplete-run panel prints are both routed through one new `AnalysisNotice::stepName`, so they cannot drift apart, and the mutation of the second reader back to the fixed word reddens with the sentence printed. An absent methodology is an outcome: the key is present and `null`, the step keeps its own word and nothing is substituted; a key the list does not declare is not printed as itself either, because a client never sees an identifier. **ONE COPY IS LEFT AND NAMED rather than quietly fixed:** the wizard's `_METHOD_LABELS` — the list is read by the server only, so the wizard's name has to be delivered by the server, which is the same surface move as Settings and belongs with it. **MEASURED BEFORE THE WORK, because the second case would have been a question rather than an execution:** all eight sites change for ONE reason, the hard-wired word giving way to the setting, and none because the methodology was read from somewhere else. Boundary: what is PRINTED ON THE SCREEN is not measured — what is guarded is what the assembler returned. PHPUnit 549, jest 29. **RETURNED BY THE REVIEWER: AN ABSENCE WAS NAMED AFTER A METHODOLOGY.** With no methodology, and with a stored value the list does not declare, the step kept its own word — and that word is `MLSN`, so a site set to nothing was told a methodology, which the owner's rule forbids outright. The word for those two cases is now held beside the names it stands in for, `labelWhenUndeclared` in the inputs list's `turf.methodology`, read by one server function (`CalculationInputs::methodologySoilStepLabel`) as the names themselves are: both readers of the step's word print `soil nutrition`, the projection's methodology stays `null`, and nothing is substituted for the setting. The word is a DRAFT — the developer's, standing on the screen marked as one, for the owner to accept or replace. Taking it out of the list reddens three cases with `MLSN` back on the screen, which is the defect returning. Three assertions in two files asserted that defect as correct and were turned over with their reasons written in; one of them, in `Gh639`, was not named in the return and was found by the full run. PHPUnit 557.

**GH-743** (пункт 3ае) THE PANEL'S `Details` BLOCK IS FOR AN ADMINISTRATOR ONLY, the owner's decision: the run's own records are for diagnosis. `partials/analysis-notice.blade.php` renders the block only when `auth()->user()?->is_admin` — the admin type in this product, the one `Gate::before` and `User::roleOnSite()` already use; a site manager and a signed-out page get the warning sentence and not the lines, which are not in their HTML at all. `Gh743DetailsAreForAdministratorsTest` renders the partial for an administrator, a manager and nobody; `Gh653` now takes its measurement as an administrator.

**GH-744** (пункт 3бю) EVERY WORD A SCREEN PRINTS FOR A METHODOLOGY COMES FROM THE INPUTS LIST, AND NO SCREEN CHANGES. Four kinds of text lived in four places: the name, the topbar's abbreviation (`AA`), what the Settings chooser adds to the name (the full name of MLSN and SLAN, the lab of ammonium acetate) and the wizard's explaining sentence. They are now `label`, `short`, `fullName` / `lab` and `description` in the `values` of `turf.methodology`, verbatim from the screen, read by `CalculationInputs`; Settings builds its chooser and its New Zealand conflict note from them, the topbar its pill, and the wizard gets them with the setup state the server already sends it, beside the constructions. There is no `labelLong`: "Hill Labs NZ" is a lab, not a longer name. One thing changes on purpose: a value the list does not carry was printed `MLSN` by the topbar's `default` and is not printed now; no stand site carries one. `Gh744MethodologyWordsHaveOneOwnerTest`; `gh395`, `gh407` and `Gh541` take their anchors from the list rather than from the old literals. RETURN, closed: the wizard's last step still made the word out of the key (`toUpperCase().replace('_', ' ')`, `AMMONIUM ACETATE`, and a made-up word for an undeclared key); it takes the list's label now, and `Gh744`'s census counts a word built from the key as a copy, which it missed. `tests/gh744-the-wizard-names-the-methodology-from-the-list.test.js` draws the step. SECOND RETURN: the wizard's lookup still printed the key when a declared value had no label (`label || id`), which `gh477` caught; the list declares a label for every value and `Gh744` holds it to that, so the label is taken as it is.

**GH-745** (пункт 3бм) THE RUN FRAME'S INVARIANT, WATCHED RATHER THAN READ. The census of GH-711 finds the ways a run can start by reading call sites as text, which is why the item says a fifth path — one the frame takes with no person behind it — is not established by it. First the item's own open measurement was closed: a bench run DOES reach the write, once the page is given the schema it is normally given and a document rendered for the site the address names. Three refusals were met on the way and none was a limit — `schema-unavailable`, then `site-mismatch`, then the write went through; the second of them is the invariant itself at work. `tests/gh745-…` now runs the frame three ways: an agreeing frame writes and the row carries the site and the run id; a frame rendered for ANOTHER site does not write and names both disagreeing signals; a site change arriving mid-run stops the write, which is GH-720's net seen from the far end — there it was measured that the listener hears, here that hearing has an effect. TWO THINGS THE REVIEWER'S OWN MUTATIONS EXPOSED IN IT: switching off one of the two site comparisons left the case green because the other carried the refusal alone, so the LIST of disagreeing signals is asserted rather than the refusal; and writing `site_id` from the page's config instead of the address also left it green, because a frame only reaches the write when the two AGREE — so this says the row carries the right site and does NOT say which source it came from, which is written into the case as its boundary. What it does not see: it exercises the paths the bench executes, so a fifth path only a real page can take is not proven absent — this narrows where one could hide. ON THE REVIEWER'S RETURN, A FOURTH CASE TELLS THE TWO SOURCES APART. The boundary written into the third case was real but wider than its subject: a frame reaches the write only when config and address agree, so `site_id` read from one looked identical to `site_id` read from the other. There is a lawful state where they differ and the write still happens — the config carries no site (`activeSiteId: null`, which the disagreement check passes over because an absent value is not a disagreement) while the context agrees with the address. In that state the address says `site-A` and the config says nothing, so the case can name the source. Measured: the same mutation that writes `site_id` from the config leaves the first three cases green and reddens the fourth with `site_id null`.

**GH-746** (Вопрос 128) A GUARD COMPARES THE LIST, NOT ITS LENGTH — MADE A MECHANISM. `tests/lib/length-claims.js` finds every place a test compares a length with a number (`.length` against a literal, `toHaveLength(n>0)`, PHP `assertCount`), keyed by file and the assertion's text; `tests/gh746-a-guard-compares-the-list-not-its-length.test.js` holds them against `tests/fixtures/gh746-length-claims.json` both ways. A new site is red until declared `multiplicity` (the members are indistinguishable and the number is the claim, with its reason) or `pending-list` (to be rewritten to compare the list); the 210 sites found on 25.09.2026 are recorded `unclassified`, a state that may shrink and not grow. Floors, `toHaveLength(0)`, counts through a variable and printed-only counts are outside it and said so.

**GH-747** (пункт 3бя) THE FOURTH SHAPE JOINS THE CENSUS, AND THE FIRST BATCH IS JUDGED. Accepting GH-746 measured its named boundary and found a hole with a size: a count carried through a variable (`const occurrences = matches.length; expect(occurrences).toBe(2)`) was invisible to the census, and six real sites were written that way — that is how people write, not how they evade a guard, and a guard exists so a site reddens by itself. So the shape joined the census instead of the six being repaired by hand: two steps rather than one pattern, the names given a length and then the assertions made about those names. Prose was dropped at the same time and had to be: this module's own comment carried an example, and one recorded site turned out to be an example inside a docblock of `gh490` rather than a site at all. The census went from 210 to 215 over 469 files. Batch 1 then judged twenty-one: nineteen `multiplicity` — writes and requests of one kind, where the members tell nothing apart and a second one IS the defect (`gh547` writes once, `gh533` one write per record, `gh552`, `gh251`, `gh537`, `gh542`, `gh526`, `gh490`) — each with its own reason, and two `pending-list`, where the members differ and the run already prints the list beside the count (`gh678`, `gh679`). Left unclassified: 193. BATCH 2 judged fifteen more — thirteen `multiplicity` and two `pending-list` — leaving 178 unclassified. The two are the telling pair: `expect(REQUIRED.length).toBe(13)` counts the schema's required metric keys, which are the most distinguishable members a list can hold and whose loss the number cannot name; `expect(bodies.length).toBe(2)` counts two request bodies the same case then reads DIFFERENTLY, so the members are told apart three lines later and the count says nothing about which arrived. The thirteen are events and requests of one kind — one completion, one failure, one restore call per surface — where a second of the same is the defect, each with its own reason. And the census's own number was corrected: the three original shapes give 210 without dropping prose and 209 with, the extra one being an example written inside a docblock of `gh490`; 215 today is 209 real sites of the old shapes plus 6 of the new. BATCH 3 judged nine — five `multiplicity`, four `pending-list` — leaving 169. The four again count members that carry identity: zones the producer groups BY IDENTITY rather than by name, where two unnamed samples must stay two zones, and the twelve months of a stored programme, where losing March and gaining a second April leaves the number at twelve. The five are a pass's own outcome — one failure, one result, or none at all — and there a second of the same kind is the defect. BATCH 4 judged fifteen — three `multiplicity`, twelve `pending-list` — leaving 154. The twelve are the clearest case yet for why a number is not a claim: nine of them count what a DETECTOR found, and the case standing beside them already asserts the members' own properties (`sites[0].timerBetween`, `sites[0].enclosingFunction`), so a count of one says a site was found and not that it is the planted one; the other three count nutrients and result keys, which are named members. The three `multiplicity` are one add, one delete and one patch per record on a live page, where a second of the same kind is the duplicate that item exists to prevent. BATCH 5 judged thirteen — two `multiplicity`, eleven `pending-list` — leaving 141. ELEVEN OF THEM COUNT TWELVE MONTHS, on four different roads: the plan's own rows, a calendar row, the published series and the exported table. A month is the most named member this product has, and every one of those eleven says `12` about a list whose members are January to December — lose March, gain a second April, and all four roads still say twelve. The two `multiplicity` count values identical by construction (two empty strings, two copies of '200'), where nothing distinguishes the members and the number IS the statement. BATCH 6 judged nine — six `multiplicity`, three `pending-list` — leaving 132, and it drew a distinction worth keeping: three of the six count ONE whose single member is read by the very NEXT line (`assertCount(1, $lines)` followed by `assertStringContainsString('Rootzone Profile is not set', $lines[0])`). There the number completes a list assertion rather than standing in for one, which is not the same thing as a bare count and should not be rewritten as though it were. BATCH 7 judged five — one `multiplicity`, four `pending-list` — leaving 130, and three sites were PUT BACK to unclassified rather than judged. Those three, with two more found in batch 7, are a THIRD kind the device does not declare: a count of one whose single member the next line reads (`assertCount(1, $lines)` then `assertStringContainsString(…, $lines[0])`). Classifying them either way would record a decision nobody made, so they wait for the device's own author. The one `multiplicity` is the case where the number IS the subject — a list limit, whose own message says `the limit was not applied`. THEN THE THIRD KIND ARRIVED AND IT CANNOT BE DECLARED. The analyst's `members-asserted`: beside the count stand assertions about every member by index, 0..n-1, on the same receiver, so the count together with them already IS a list comparison. The guard INFERS it — no entry is written, and an entry for such a site now reddens as `DECLARED BUT INFERRED`, so the ratchet cannot keep an excuse the guard no longer needs; 55 entries left it that way. Nothing bare can wear the kind, because losing the per-index assertions makes the site an undeclared bare count again: measured, removing all three assertions about member 0 in one case dropped the inferred set from 51 to 50 and reddened that site by name. THE FEATURE FOUND TWO FAULTS IN ITS OWN IMPLEMENTATION, which is the only reason to trust it: a hyphen written `'"->` made a RANGE from `"` to `>`, so a PHP receiver parsed as `$lines);` and the whole PHP side of the kind silently did nothing — caught by the analyst's own check that five deferred sites must close by themselves; and the per-index assertions were looked for across the WHOLE FILE, so a site held the kind on a neighbouring case's assertions — narrowing the window to the enclosing case returned four sites to unclassified. State, measured from the fixture: unclassified 99, multiplicity 24, pending-list 41, 164 entries, 51 inferred.

**GH-748** (пункт 3ва) THE EUE ENGINE, ITS BRIDGE AND THE OPERATIONAL SUMMARY LEAVE THE FOUR PAGES THAT NEVER RUN THEM — `/hub`, `reports/export`, `reports/forensic`, `reports/scenarios`. Measured in a browser before the change, each page's own script list in a blank page with no login, no site and no press, every request answered locally: no call into any `GSSH_EUE` method, no summary container, no LED button, no non-GET request, no page error; planting the element each script waits for made the summary appear on all four and the LED button on the export page, so the watch was not blind. After the change the same pages load with no error and no call. `gssh-led-export.js` stays on `reports/export` as the handler of the "LED Lighting Report" card, which waits for the owner. `tests/gh748-the-eue-scripts-leave-the-pages-that-never-run-them.test.js`; `gh739` now rebuilds the pre-GH-748 `/hub` list so its measurement stays reproducible.

**GH-749** (пункт 3аы) A SITE WITH NO METHODOLOGY IS NOT GIVEN ONE: THE RESOLVER REFUSES. Two places filled it, both spelled `|| 'mlsn'` — `nutrition-program-inputs.js` `resolveSufficiencyRanges()`, where the sufficiency ranges are decided, and `nutrition-calendar.js` `computeProgram()`, which is what hands the methodology to that resolver on the Plan page, so repairing only the first would have left the second deciding. Measured before the work: GH-521 took this same substitution out of `resolveSiteProgramInputs()` one function below and its comment names it — that function resolves an absent methodology honestly as `null`, and the next call turned the null back into `mlsn`. The analyst's decision, executed literally: it REFUSES and writes no reason, because a reason would admit the case as an allowed one; the form is the one this file already uses for a config it cannot resolve for the site it was asked about. The numbers the item is about: with no pH the MLSN P floor is 21 instead of 40, and the label, the citation and the source stamp are identical in both cases, so nothing distinguishes “the ladder was applied” from “there was no pH”. THE REFUSAL NARROWED ITSELF AFTER A MEASUREMENT: calling the range resolver unconditionally made the whole site resolver throw, and three cases of `gh383` — about clipping and about the GH-521 rule, neither about a range — went red; the ranges are simply not resolved now, and the field that says why was already there (`sources.methodology: 'empty'`). A banner with drafted words was written first and removed entirely: the words were the developer's and the decision is that this case gets none. A THIRD ASSERTION OF THE DEFECT AS CORRECT was found by the full run, after the two of GH-742: a case named “no methodology at all still defaults to MLSN, as before”, turned over with its reason, and a `gh369` fixture that carried no methodology got the one its site has. Boundary, and the item does not close on it: what a person sees on /plan in that state is measured by nothing here — the error reaches a `console.warn` and leaves the panel empty, and measuring the page needs a site selected. PHPUnit 562, jest 3742. **AND THE THIRD LINK ITSELF, FIRST HALF: A GUARD OVER PAIRS.** The analyst's device is over `{input, effect}` pairs rather than over modules: the pairs are declared in `whenAbsent` beside the reading they are about (`samples.soil` declares two — a phosphorus floor left unadjusted by pH, and a certificate band held as a proportion of the CEC that cannot be computed), the pairs the code records are held against them BOTH WAYS, and each declared pair has a case that runs the module and reads the pair back, the case naming which module records it so no list of modules is kept. A module writes only HALF a pair — the reading it did not have — because the inputs list is read by the server alone and this resolver is a browser module; the effect is completed where the words live, so the halves cannot drift. THE DEVICE FOUND A FALSE PAIR IN ITS OWN FIRST VERSION, which is the only reason to trust it: it recorded `soil.CEC` whenever a nutrient's band came out empty for any reason, and on `S277` that is Sulphur, which the certificate does not print — an absence recorded where nothing was lost, the very defect the item exists against. The condition asks the producer now: only a threshold held as a proportion of the CEC counts, which is K, Ca and Mg on `S81` and nothing on `S277` or `S279`. MEASURED ALONGSIDE, and it changes the item's fourth row: the run never passes CEC to the soil-temperature model at all (`{ profileType }` against the panel's `{ profileType, cec, om }`), so there is no absence to record there and the stored row's `inputs.cec` names a value that did not enter the calculation; the refinement moves the number by 0.07 °C and exactly one stand site of fourteen has a refinable construction. Left at a boundary by the owner's order to finish reviews first: two pairs declared and guarded, the run side and the summary's water still to come. PHPUnit 565, jest 3760.

**GH-750** (пункт 3бг) THE SITE IMPORT IS REMOVED; THE EXPORT STAYS. The import's one write to the server PATCHed the file's coordinates into the site the page had open (`GAIP_HUB_CONFIG.activeSiteId`) rather than the site the file described — the class of GH-459. Without that write it would only have put the file's turf profiles into localStorage and merged its samples into the sample manager, which is a browser copy the project rule forbids, so the control goes rather than being repaired. Its button lived only in the `/hub` markup: `/hub` itself (reached by typing the address, linked from nowhere), the hidden Re-run frame, and the three report pages where the markup sits in `#rp-hub-runner` with `display: none !important`; the stadium page includes the markup but not the script. No stand site carries coordinates that differ from its config. `gh625` now holds that the import is gone and, by running the module against a planted selector bar, that only the export button is added. RETURN, closed: the removal had left its caller in `tests/fixtures/gh711-page-write-calls.json`, so `gh711` was red by name; the entry is gone. That nothing here writes to the server is `gh711`'s claim — its census sees a write however the verb is spelt, measured with `var verb = "PATCH"` — so `gh625` no longer carries a text check for `method: 'PATCH'`, which only looked like a second guard.

**GH-752** (пункт 3бл) ONE GRADE FOR A SAMPLE, BY THE SITE'S METHODOLOGY, IN THE RUN AND ON THE SERVER — delivered in parts. PART A, DELIVERY 1: the run takes the site's construction and methodology from the site, not from `/hub`'s form. `gaip_build_state` read `.gaip-construction`, and `gaip_readSoilForm` read `.gaip-soil-methodology` with `|| "mlsn"` when it was empty; both come from `GAIP_HUB_CONFIG` now — the construction resolved by the one dictionary (GH-664), the methodology from the site's `config.turf.methodology` — and an absent one stays absent. `layouts/db-shell.blade.php` now carries the resolved construction too, as `layouts/app.blade.php` did, because the report pages run the engines in a hidden frame of that layout. `tests/gh752-the-run-takes-construction-and-methodology-from-the-site.test.js` runs the assembly with each field empty, contradicting the config and agreeing; `Gh752TheShellCarriesTheSitesConstructionTest` renders a db-shell page. PART A, DELIVERY 2: the two interpretations the Word export prints — the soil interpretation and the synthesis — and the export's own soil block take the methodology and construction from the site (`GAIP_HUB_CONFIG`, the export's inputs), not from the form field, the page's `GAIP_STATE` or `'mlsn'`; `gh461` loses the exemption that named the export line's leak. Two readers named in the plan are `/hub` interface only and are left: `mlsn-progressive-disclosure.js` (a tooltip and a field warning) and `gaip-evidence-ui.js` (its panel, which the export does not read). `tests/gh752-the-interpretations-take-the-sites-methodology.test.js` runs both collectors with the page contradicting the config. PART A, DELIVERY 3: the server's soil interpretation no longer puts MLSN where the page sends none — `?? 'mlsn'` where the value was read, the fallback to the MLSN config, and `normalise_methodology` answering MLSN for anything it did not recognise, the empty string included. Without this the substitution the page stopped making would only have moved to the server. An absent or unknown methodology is refused with its reason, before the service check; a known one is interpreted as itself. `Gh752TheSoilInterpretationIsWrittenForTheSitesMethodologyTest`. RETURN ON DELIVERY 1, closed: every site in `tests/gh752-the-run-takes-…` carried a methodology, so a `|| "mlsn"` put back at the root of the run's methodology was never reached and the cases stayed green; a site with neither methodology nor construction is now run with the field empty, contradicting and agreeing, and prints that it has neither before it is judged. PART B, DELIVERY 4: the SLAN ranges leave the engine for one file. `assets/slan-ranges.json` carries the ranges by soil type (`sands`, `others`) and the pH adjustment of Fe and Mn, moved without edits from the literal in `mlsnEngine`; `App\Support\SlanRanges` is its one reader, and `layouts/db-shell.blade.php` hands it to the report pages, which load the engine. No JavaScript copy. `tests/gh752-the-slan-ranges-have-one-file.test.js` holds the file equal to the literal and finds, from the views themselves, every view that loads the engine; `Gh752TheServerReadsTheSlanRangesTest` renders a db-shell page. PART B, DELIVERY 5: the soil type the SLAN ranges are chosen by is a property of the construction dictionary, `resolves.slanSoilType` on every value of `turf.construction`, moved as the engine applied it (`sand_profile` is `sands`, every other construction `others`). The dictionary is compared with the engine's rule run on each value, and `gh656` holds each type to a key of the ranges file, with the other consumers' tables; every value now declares seven properties. PART C, DELIVERY 6: the server's analysis of a sample (`SampleAnalysisController`) grades a SLAN site as the run grades it — the SLAN ranges of the site's soil type, resolved from its construction by the dictionary, Low / Sufficient / High on lo and hi, Fe and Mn adjusted by the sample's pH — instead of by MLSN's thresholds, which it applied to every site that was not AA. A SLAN site with no construction, and Fe or Mn with no pH on the sample, are not graded rather than graded by a guess (the run puts pH 7 there; not copied). The engine and the server meet in a fixture recorded from the engine (`app/tests/fixtures/gh752-grade-grid.json`, two soil types by three methodologies): `tests/gh752-the-server-grades-a-sample-as-the-engine-does.test.js` holds the engine equal to it, `Gh752TheServerGradesASampleAsTheEngineDoesTest` the server, grade and threshold apart. MLSN is printed, not asserted: the run grades it against a target built from the annual uptake, which one sample does not carry. AA micronutrients are printed, not asserted: the server's AA table has no Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu or B, so those fall to MLSN's thresholds. RETURN ON DELIVERY 6, closed: that Fe and Mn with no pH on the sample say so, rather than taking the run's pH 7, was held by the code alone; a sample with no pH is now a case of its own, and it prints that the sample carries none before it is judged. PART D, DELIVERY 7: the soil page names the site's methodology, not the run's stamp. `soil-nutrition-analysis.js` labelled every threshold "AA:" for AA and "MLSN:" otherwise, so a SLAN site's ranges read MLSN; and seven places decided the methodology from `sn.methodology` — the stamp of what a run used, which is not read back to interpret anything — three of them with `|| 'mlsn'`. The page takes the methodology from the site's config and the word for it from the inputs list, which `layouts/db-shell.blade.php` now carries as `GAIP_HUB_CONFIG.methodologyShort` (null for a value the list does not declare); a site with none is told "No methodology set". Seven older page tests gave the methodology through the stamp and now give it as a site, through `tests/lib/soil-page-site.js`, which reads the word from the list. `tests/gh752-the-soil-page-names-the-sites-methodology.test.js` runs the page with the stamp contradicting the site; `Gh752TheShellCarriesTheSitesConstructionTest` renders the word. The page's own word tables for a methodology's name and description are left as they are: replacing them with the list's words would change what a client reads. RETURN ON DELIVERY 7: the header's badge and the verdict rebuild their word from the key rather than take the delivered one. The owner decided the page keeps its own words ("leave it as it works now"), so both stay as they were — an AA site's verdict still reads `(AMMONIUM_ACETATE)` — and a change made to them before her answer was reverted.

**GH-768**: Implement GH-768: Centralize AA nutrient ranges and enhance analysis consistency

**GH-769** A construction the site already holds is shown in Settings instead of being blanked. The form offered five values while the setup wizard offered the whole declared list, so a site stored with any other one rendered an empty field that read as "the wizard did not save it" when the database held the value. The offered set now has one reader, `CalculationInputs::constructionChoices()`, driven by an `offered` flag on the declared list; Settings and the wizard take the same identifiers and labels, the hard-coded array and literal labels are gone, and a stored value outside the offered set is rendered as its own selected option with the label the list declares. All eleven values stay declared, so the resolutions the server reads for already-saved configs are untouched.

**GH-770** A MISSING WATER pH WAS PRINTED AS 7.0 AND CALLED SUITABLE. The tissue state assembly stood a 7 in when no water sample existed, beside the zero removed under GH-736, and the water page turned it into "pH 7.0 - Suitable - No adjustment required". The stand-in is gone and the value is absent, so nothing is stated about water a lab has not seen. RSC is no longer produced when none of its four ions arrived.
**GH-771** THE PGR APPLICATION A RUN COMPUTES WITH NOW COMES FROM THE SPRAY LOG. The calculation read a date out of settings that the new hub has no screen for, so an application entered in the log never reached it. The server answers the last PGR as its own query, without the 90-day window and without the 200-row limit, so an application older than the window is named instead of being reported as none; the window still governs every other field of the context, and the 90 days are applied once, in the engine. The run takes the date from that answer and only for the site the run is about, checking `site_id`. The settings branch, the `GAIP_STATE.pgr` read, the `gilba_last_pgr_*` copy in browser storage and the two config helpers that wrote and restored it are gone, leaving only the sweeper that clears the old keys.
**GH-772** A PGR APPLICATION OLDER THAN THE WINDOW IS NAMED INSTEAD OF BEING REPORTED AS NONE. A site whose last application fell outside the 90-day window was told "no PGR application is recorded" while the log held one, which is a different fact from having none. The panel now says which product was applied, on what date, and that its growth-regulation effect has ended and is not part of the analysis. All three values are data rather than text: the product and the date travel from the spray log through the server, and the length of the window comes from the engine's own constant, so a window of another length changes the sentence by itself. This is the only cause whose sentence is composed per run; every other one keeps its fixed text, and a cause with no words still leaves the page the phrase it already prints.
**GH-773** A SAMPLE IS STORED UNDER THE CANONICAL NAME OF EACH READING, WHATEVER THE LAB CALLED IT. Columns arrived in the payload spelled the way the laboratory spells them, so the same reading sat under `pH_Water` on one site and `pH` on another and every reader had to know both. The reading names map gains one function that lays a row out under its canonical keys, and it lives in the map's only reader, so no second list of spellings exists; both write paths call it, which covers upload, store and the sample editor. Only the unambiguous is renamed: a column recognised only after a method suffix is peeled, a second column claiming the same reading with a different value, and water phosphorus stay under the names they arrived with, because each of those is a different measurement rather than a different spelling. Samples already in the database are left as they are, and the one reader that knew only the old spelling was moved first.
**GH-774** WATER PHOSPHORUS IS CALLED PHOSPHORUS ON EVERY SCREEN. The value a laboratory reports as phosphorus was labelled "Phosphate" on the data page, the sample switcher and the water blender, while the form that collects it has always called it P and described it as phosphorus as reported by the lab. The five labels now read "Phosphorus (P)". Nothing else changed: the stored keys, the spellings the reading map accepts and the values themselves are untouched, so no sample was rewritten, and a column arriving as PO4 or phosphate still lands in the same field it always did. No conversion factor is involved, because no formula uses this reading.
**GH-775** WHEN ONE SAMPLE CARRIES TWO COLUMNS FOR THE SAME READING, ONE OF THEM IS STORED. A laboratory file that spells a reading twice used to leave both columns in the payload, so the same sample held two answers to one question. The declared order of spellings decides, which is the rule the product has always followed when filling a reading from a form: the more specific column wins, and the other is not stored. Nothing is said about the column that lost. What a run computes with does not change, because it read the winning column before this too, and samples already in the database are left as they are.
**GH-776** A SITE WITH NO PLAY SCHEDULE NO LONGER CARRIES A WEEK OF SOCCER. Where a site had entered no schedule, the wear inputs fell back on the hidden calculation form, whose fields ship with defaults, so golf courses and lawns were analysed as if they held three hours of matches and four and a half hours of drills every week. The fallback is gone and the defaults are removed from the four schedule fields in both places that declare them, so an absent schedule reaches the engine as absent; the engine already answers no matches and no training for that, which is the right outcome rather than another invented number. Nothing is substituted in its place. Stored rows keep what they hold until the next run. The root depth keeps its default, which is a separate question and has its own case holding it in place.
- Introduced `AaRanges` class to read ammonium acetate sufficiency ranges from a single JSON file, replacing the previous hardcoded constants in `SampleAnalysisController`.
- Updated `SampleAnalysisController` to utilize the new `AaRanges` class for nutrient range calculations, ensuring consistent methodology across analyses.
- Modified tests to reflect the new input structure and validate the correct application of AA ranges, enhancing test coverage and reliability.
- Improved documentation to clarify the changes in AA nutrient handling and the rationale behind the new structure.
- This change significantly enhances the accuracy of nutrient grading for AA samples and aligns server behavior with the underlying engine's logic.

**GH-777** A SECTION THAT WAS NOT CALCULATED NOW SAYS WHY, AND THE RUN JUDGES THE REASON AGAINST WHAT THE SITE HELD WHEN IT STARTED. Four modules produced nothing and declared nothing, so an empty section on the plan page was indistinguishable from one whose engine had failed, and the client was left to guess. The pass now takes its modules on from the dependency graph in one walk instead of eleven hand-written gates, and a module whose declared inputs the site does not have is recorded as not applicable, with those inputs named, rather than left silent. The server judges each named input against a record of what the site held at the moment the run began, so "you have not entered it" and "it was there and did not reach us" are told apart and never swapped; where an input lives is declared beside where a person enters it, because several are kept in a column or in the spray log rather than in the site's settings, and one of them at a path of its own. From those facts the server composes one sentence — what was not calculated, what is missing and where to enter it — with the words taken from the list rather than written in code, so they can be changed without touching it; an input with no name, no reachable place, or a place a site of that kind is not shown gets no sentence at all, because an address that is wrong is worse than none. The plan page prints what the server composed for the sections it draws and keeps its own words where there is nothing to print. Separately and measured: a run computes on the sample the server named for it, which until now it never did — the frame carried the row's id while the browser's store was keyed by the client's own name for the sample, so no named sample was ever found and the tissue analysis was empty in every stored row. The sample is found by the row id now, and a run told a site has no sample of a kind does not wait for one.
**GH-778** A RUN COMPUTES ON THE SAMPLE THE SERVER NAMED FOR IT, AND ONE FUNCTION DECIDES WHICH THAT IS. The server chooses a site's sample and names it on the address of the frame the calculation runs in, but four places in that frame asked the browser's sample manager for whichever sample the page had selected instead: the block that builds the soil readings, the field recording which sample a run computed on, the check on whether the soil had arrived, and the water sample a laboratory sodium ratio was read from — the last with a third rule of its own, the selection or else the latest by date or else the selection again. The selection is set in several unrelated places and knows nothing of the server's rule, so a stored row could carry one sample's numbers while saying it was about another, which is the class of defect that once printed one site's climate under another site's name. All four now read the one function that answers what the frame was told, and the field recording the sample carries the row id of what the calculation actually received, while what the run was told stays recorded separately, so a disagreement between them is visible from the row itself. Nothing changes on a screen today and that is measured rather than assumed: on every stand site holding more than one sample the two answers agree, and on two of them they agree only because a tie of laboratory dates happens to be broken the same way on both sides. Where a named sample carries no reading, the row keeps the absence instead of filling it.

**GH-779** THE EFFICIENCY OF A SITE'S IRRIGATION SYSTEM COMES FROM ITS SETTINGS, AND A SITE THAT HAS ENTERED NONE GETS NO RUNTIME. Settings saves the system efficiency with the rest of a site's irrigation block, and the run read a field of the old hub's form instead -- a field whose markup carries a hardcoded 75 and which nothing ever fills from the site. So every schedule was computed at 75 per cent whatever the site had entered, and the figure was not a stale value but a literal, taken off a page rather than from the object it was about. The run takes the site's own value now and nothing else, and where there is none the scheduler answers with no runtime, no cycles and no gross depth rather than minutes computed on a number nobody chose: a default in a calculation is a measurement the reader cannot tell from a real one. Three fields that were read off the same form beside it -- the irrigation method, the rainfall effectiveness and the cost per kilolitre -- are gone rather than moved, because no engine read them and a dead read with a default in it is the next such literal waiting to happen. Nothing already computed from a site's own setting changes: every site on the stand that carries a value carries exactly the figure the form held, so what goes are the minutes of the sites that never entered one.

**GH-780** A SITE IS USING A PLANT GROWTH REGULATOR WHEN ITS SPRAY JOURNAL SAYS SO, AND THERE IS NO SWITCH TO SET. The old hub's form carried a PGR checkbox, and the flag the calculation read was filled from it; the new hub has no such control and nothing had written the setting for a long time, so the shade module and the morning briefing behaved as though no site anywhere used a regulator. The owner decided on 29.09.2026 that the question is answered by the journal: a site is using one when an application is recorded within the last ninety days. The window is declared once, by the PGR engine, and the two other places that used to hold the number now read it from there. The answer is produced once, in the state both passes are built from, rather than derived again wherever it is wanted -- the first attempt computed it in the converter, which the cascade saw and the pass did not, so a stored row went on saying the same false. Three answers are kept apart: a journal that said nothing leaves the flag unset, a journal with no application answers no, and a dated application is measured against the window with the day itself inside it. Where two runs happen in one frame the answer of the run that just finished is the one published, because the publish otherwise lets the earlier run's conclusion win. The checkbox is gone from the old hub's page by this project's rule for it -- a control whose write path has been removed is removed rather than repaired -- and the product, date and rate beside it stay, because other readers fill them.

**GH-781** THE ACCOUNT OF A RUN BELONGS TO THE PASS WHOSE NUMBERS ARE IN THE ROW. Everything a pass said about itself -- what it skipped, what it warned about, what did not apply here -- lived in one shared list that the next pass cleared, and the writers outside a pass had no name in it, so their records were taken for the orchestrator's own and removed without a trace: the note about an exhausted plant-growth-regulator window reached 0 of 108 stored rows, and both rows mentioning an unusable water sample carried the problem with an empty list of skips beside it. Every record now names its producer and the pass it belongs to, the four public doors refuse a record that names neither, and a pass is settled at its end rather than at its start: a pass that finished accepts its own account and drops that producer's older one, a pass that threw or finished without a result drops its own and leaves the previous account standing. The row's marks and fingerprints are taken from the accepted pass rather than from the last attempt, so a repeat that produced nothing can no longer put its own stamp beside another pass's numbers. What the row's own assembly discovers travels in the body of that one write instead of through the shared list, because a list with no name has no moment of cleanup to get wrong. A module that does not apply to this site is recorded with the inputs whose absence made it so, which no stored row carried before. Two guards hold the shape: every writer of the journal is either met in a stored row or declared with the condition under which it must write, and a writer whose condition never occurred is reported as open rather than green; and a run's body is checked for any value of a pass that was not accepted. The annual nitrogen figure of 200 that stands in when no programme has been entered is kept -- the owner decided on 30.09.2026 to restore it -- while a programme entered as zero stays zero, which is a different case and was not part of that decision.

**GH-782** THE SOIL TABLE OF AN AMMONIUM-ACETATE SITE IS COMPUTED BY THAT METHODOLOGY, AND ITS RANGES COME FROM THE SITE RATHER THAN FROM THE PAGE. The converter that hands the page's state to the engines carried a hand-written list of fields and dropped three of the eight the soil engine reads -- the methodology, the soil texture and the depth -- and the engine filled the first of them with `|| "slan"`. So every site set to ammonium acetate was computed on the SLAN table while its stored row declared ammonium acetate from the state taken before the converter: 43 rows of such sites since 23.09, 41 of them labelled that way. The converter now carries what the engine reads, and no methodology is an outcome rather than a reason to choose one -- a run that reaches the engine without one computes nothing and says so, which puts the cause in the row and the owner's sentence on the page instead of an empty section. Separately, the ranges of that methodology were resolved from the species in the `/hub` form field, which is the page and not the site, and on every ammonium-acetate site that field is empty while the species lives in the site's own configuration; potassium on sand therefore stood at 50.0-116.0 ppm where the certificate gives 78.2-195.5. One function now answers which species a site is, for the soil table and for the input-range validator alike, and it reads the configuration of the site the run is for and never the form -- the validator had been right in the same run only because a merge let the store's keys win. Which table each nutrient's range came from is recorded per nutrient in the stored row, so a certificate-backed range and the texture-only fallback are no longer indistinguishable after the fact: a nutrient whose numbers happen to match the fallback is labelled as the fallback.

**Engineering backlog (internal, not a client comment)**

- **Check whether SLAN's `targetPpm` gets misread as a ceiling in `renderAnnualRequirements()`.** Found 2026-08-21 while explaining the "Annual Nutrient Requirements" panel's methodology differences to the user, unrelated to the AA fixes in this session. `mlsnEngine()`'s SLAN branch (`hub-tissue-v3.js:2765-2770`, explicitly "unchanged" and untouched by all of GH-258-277) sets `targetPpm: range.lo` — the **floor** of the SLAN range, by design (comment: "For SLAN, target is the low end of range"). But `renderAnnualRequirements()` (`soil-nutrition-analysis.js:891-896`) reads `nObj.targetPpm` for every non-AA methodology and uses it as if it were a **ceiling**: `isHigh = actual >= targetV`, zeroing the displayed kg/ha requirement whenever `actual >= targetV`. For SLAN this means `isHigh` can trigger the moment a nutrient merely reaches the *floor* of its sufficiency range (i.e. as soon as it's SUFFICIENT, not just when it's genuinely HIGH) — the Annual Requirement would show 0 far too early for SLAN sites, unlike MLSN (whose generic PACE-style `targetPpm = mlsnThreshold + uptakePpm` or `×1.5`, `hub-tissue-v3.js:2836-2839`, is a genuine ceiling-ish value, not a floor) and unlike AA (which correctly uses `rangeMax`, GH-260). Not yet confirmed live on a real SLAN site — found by reading the three branches side by side while answering an unrelated question, not from a bug report. Before fixing: reproduce on a real SLAN site/sample (SUFFICIENT-but-not-HIGH nutrient) to confirm the panel actually shows 0 kg/ha incorrectly; if confirmed, the fix is presumably to give `renderAnnualRequirements()` a SLAN-specific ceiling source (SLAN's own `range.hi`, analogous to AA's `rangeMax`) instead of reusing the floor-shaped `targetPpm` field, mirroring the `isAA` branch's shape.

- **Remove `methodology_snapshot` (`samples`/`site_summaries` columns) entirely.** Investigated during D07/GH-265: this field is computed at sample-creation time (`site.methodology_override ?: account.methodology`, `SampleController.php:373`) and returned in several API payloads, but as of GH-265, nothing in the live codebase actually reads it to make a classification decision — both the JS side (`ammonium-acetate-methodology.js`, region-based auto-select) and the PHP side (`Controller::effectiveMethodology()`, same NZ-bounds check) independently recompute the effective methodology live from site coordinates every time, ignoring this stored value. GH-263 was the only place that ever tried to use it for a live decision, and that turned out to be wrong (GH-265): the snapshot goes stale the instant a site's methodology changes after a sample is saved, while the live geography-based computation doesn't. Contrast with `soil_texture_snapshot`, which stays — `SampleAnalysisController.php:52` genuinely depends on it (no live geography-based fallback exists for rootzone texture). Before removing: grep for `methodology_snapshot`/`methodologySnapshot` across `app/` and `assets/` to confirm no other consumer appeared since this note was written, check `Sample`/`SiteSummary` model fillable lists and the initial-schema migration, and decide whether a DB migration to drop the columns is worth it or whether leaving the (now definitely write-only, never-read) columns in place is lower-risk — this is cleanup, not a bug fix, so no rush.
